TITLE: Driver unscrews unloading hose while under pressure
CASE_DESCRIPTION: An incident occurred while unloading a wagon of extinguished lime. The driver of the Zijderlaan company unscrewed the unloading hose while it was still under pressure. TITLE: Unit 7 TIT LPT temperature unauthorised change.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
It was observed that U7's load was lower than expected. 
Upon investigation it was discovered that the TIT LPT was at 1270 Degrees with the GT relative power at 100%; this temperature should be at 1290 Degrees in normal operation.
It transpired that the TIT LPT had been reduced using a simulation that hadn't been authorised, there was not a PEM 109 recorded for any simulations on the firing temperatures. This firing temperature simulation is still in force awaiting a Unit two-shift for removal.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
An immediate investigation was undertaken to find out why the firing temperature was reduced.
The cause/reason for the application of the simulation needs to be discovered.

TITLE: Leakage of ammonia water UHA 72m

The gate valve upstream of the pressure measurement was closed. The plant fire brigade was informed and emptied the sump.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The gate valve upstream of the pressure measurement was closed. The company fire brigade was informed and emptied the sump.
1. the drip tray has no leakage monitoring, this should be retrofitted.
2. the gas detector is in an unfavourable position. It did not recognise this leakage. The thermals in the boiler house have driven it in the other direction. The gas detector should be relocated.

SAP message: 50238076

16.12.2022 Marco Mäder

TITLE: Oil entering the sewerage system
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
As already described in Synergi Life case no. 31480 (The Buchholz relay triggered the transformer's fire extinguishing system. At this point, the oil collection pit had been drained to the oil separator.  The triggering caused the oil collection pit to overflow after a certain period of time.  As oil is lighter than water, an unknown quantity of oil was able to leave the oil collection pit and wet the neighbouring footpath and road), the overflowing of the oil collection pit caused a mixture of oil and water to spill onto the power station road. Despite the measures taken, an obviously not inconsiderable amount of oil entered the power station's sewerage system.
As a result, the oil alarm at the control centre for the Rapphoffsmühlenbach was triggered and the system was immediately switched to emergency operation so that the surface water was channelled towards the company sewage treatment plant. In addition, there was considerable oil contamination in the surface drainage channels that lead directly to the company sewage treatment plant, which in turn led to an oil slick floating on the 33 metre circular tank in the sewage treatment plant.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The pumping station to the Rapphoffsmühlenbach was immediately switched to emergency operation. Subsequently, the pump structure was completely cleaned on 3 and 4 February 23.
The water surface in the 33-metre basin was suctioned off on 03/02/23 and the inflowing channels were flushed.

TITLE:
Oil spill to surface water due to overturned cube containing oil and flushing away due to process water leakage.

Oil spill to surface water due to a tipped over IBC with oil and the wash away due to a process water leakage.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Sequence 1
While moving a cubel (mounted on a undercarriage with wheels) on the forks of a forklift by a contractor employee, the cubel with undercarriage fell over while being set down. This allegedly happened because the tyres of the undercarriage of the cubel were too slack, making it unstable. After the cube with undercarriage fell over, +/- 300L of oil leaked from the cube through an unsealed opening at the top of the cube and spilled onto the tiled floor.

Actions taken immediately: immediate report to Uniper by contractor employees. Spill contained and covered with absorbent gravel. Also put the cubel with undercarriage back upright.

Sequence 2 ( case 40361)
After the incident had occurred and was made safe, the contractor company resumed its operations (clearing the hall). While moving a pallet containing material, a contractor employee (while making a turn with his forklift) 30-60 min after sequence 1 hit and damaged an in-service process water pipe (7.5 bar). This involved a capped branch of a GRE process water pipe that protruded +/- 1.5 m straight up from the floor. This process water pipe transports process water from the Brielse Meer and is supplied by Evides.

Immediate actions taken: immediate report to Uniper by the contractor employees. The shift operators on duty blocked the process water pipe locally, stopping the leakage.

Sequence 3
Due to the large amount of water released from the process water pipe, the oil spill drifted away, ending up partly in an HWA gutter next to the hall. This HWA drain discharges via underground sewers directly into the Europa harbour.

Immediate actions taken: immediately placed floating oil beams in the harbour by Uniper employees, as a result of which the oil spill from the HWA sewer was contained as much as possible.

General note:
- Unclear whether work permit procedure was followed. The incident investigation should show whether it was applied.
- Unclear whether loss of process water could have caused Trip. The incident investigation should show what the possible consequences could have been.
- Current case 40353 will be used as the main case for cases below. Only this case will be filled after the investigation.

TITLE: Oil radiator fire
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 12:40 pm, smoke developed in the 110kV single-phase switchgear house WKW. The smoke was coming from a floor shaft between the circuit breaker cells and the office building.

The flap to the floor shaft was opened carefully and at a distance by the operating personnel. The smoke was dense and could not be assessed by the operating personnel, so the fire brigade had to be notified. The internal reporting chain was also triggered.  
When the emergency services arrived a short time later, they were informed and briefed by the plant personnel. The fire brigade then climbed into the floor shaft with breathing apparatus and brought an oil radiator outside through a window. It had leaked oil and was smoking heavily. A technical defect in the oil radiator was identified as the cause of the fire. The RCD on site tripped and switched off the oil radiator circuit. This presumably prevented greater damage.

An emergency doctor and the police were also on site. No persons were injured and the operation was over after approx. 1 hour.

This shaft and the room below it were not marked on the construction plans. This room had not been used in recent years.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Emergency call plan processed, then emergency call made.

TITLE: KWIr, unit 3; HEL leakage at burner level 5
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On 14 June 2022, a trial run of unit 3 was carried out from 4:00 am. The first burners were ignited with (extra light heating oil) HEL at 4 a.m. The grid was switched on shortly after 6 a.m.
The entire HEL route from tank 4 to the boiler house was monitored by the shift with regular inspection rounds. The last inspection round was completed by around 8.15 am. No abnormalities/leaks had been detected by then. At around 8.25 a.m., an employee noticed HEL leaking down to zero metres in boiler house 3. He immediately informed the control centre. An intensive search for the cause/leakage was carried out immediately. At the same time, the oil spill was stopped with oil binding agent.
The oil was escaping from a leaking three-way valve on burner 5.1. The burner was immediately taken out of operation and the oil supply stopped.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Water (Inc. excess volume, lack of, uncontrolled release or excess use)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
- Oil supply stopped by burner off
- Oil binding agent in the area of the oil pool to zero metres
- Opening of a floor drain, which had obviously been penetrated by HEL, leading into the boiler drain pit block 3
- Boiler drain pumps were secured in the "Off" position; no boiler drain water was pumped into the cooling water pipe leading to the Danube. A hazard to the water could thus be safely ruled out.
- Submersible pumps were set up to ensure stable plant operation and pumped into the substance-tight sinks.
- The pumped water, which is obviously slightly contaminated with HEL, is sampled. Environmentally friendly disposal is then arranged.

Thanks to the high level of experience and qualification of the shift workers (reinforced by two additional people for the trial operation), action was taken quickly and purposefully.
This prevented a fire and/or environmental damage to the Danube!

TITLE: Oil leak UST storage facility Krummhörn
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Tuesday, 12 January 2020, the operator OGE pumped machine oil into the intermediate oil tank for repair work on the ME 1 gas transport compressor.
After the repair work was completed, the oil stored in the intermediate oil tank was to be pumped back into the ME 1 machine.
The dismantled Uniper ME5 and ME6 injection compressors and the OGE ME1 and ME2 machines share a machine oil pressure line in this context.
During the dismantling work in the storage compressor hall, the pipeline in the hall was disconnected and not resealed in a pressure-tight manner. The cut machine oil pipes were only provisionally sealed inside the supply shaft of the compressor hall.
As a result of the pumping process, the oil did not return to the ME1 as intended, but instead emptied through the open pressure line in the supply shaft of the compressor hall due to the lower resistance.
The shortfall in the ME1 was compensated for by the OGE employee carrying out the work with fresh oil.
It was not until Friday, 15 January 2020 that the shortfall was discovered during a regular gauging of the oil quantities in the tank. The person responsible for the plant was informed of the shortfall on Monday 18 January 2020.
Immediate measures to contain the damage were initiated without delay. The responsible authorities and the plant operator Uniper were informed and the immediate measures were supported by the Aurich district authority.
There was no oil contamination of outdoor areas or public waters.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Oil (Inc. contamination of land or water)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Securing the tank farm systems against recommissioning.
Carrying out extraction and cleaning measures for machine oil at the supply shafts, the surface drainage system up to the central oil separator system / rainwater retention basin.
Damage assessment in the presence of all the above-mentioned authorities and the environmental expert Dr Spange.
Determination of further expenses for damage elimination (cleaning, soil sampling, replacement of contaminated soil if necessary, paving).
During the damage assessment, the discharge point of surface water after the oil separator into the public watercourse (Erbsenbinderschloot) was also examined. There was no discharge of machine oils / hydrocarbons.

TITLE: Heavy release of ash following lorry loading Loading lane 1 new ash loading.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

Due to this blockage, the flow of ash towards the lorry could not be stopped. The employee of the partner company who was present then activated the emergency stop of loading line 1. After successfully simulating the position feedback of the dosing roller, the programme could then be cleanly transferred to the exhibition. The lorry was able to leave the loading area.
During the activation of the emergency stop, the loading of the neighbouring loading line 2 was in operation at the same time. This had to be put back into operation. Due to the fact that loading line 2 also drew the product from silo 1 (just like loading line 1), conveying air got under the dosing roller of loading line 1 (simulated), which was still in operation, causing a backward flow of ash via the ventilation of loading line 1.
This could only happen because the corresponding shut-off valve of the conveying air system in the direction of loading line 1 was leaking in the closed position. This resulted in the uncontrolled escape of ash via the corresponding ventilation of the loading chute on loading route 1.
The estimated amount of ash is approx. 5 tonnes of E-filter ash.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Upon noticing the ash leakage via the loading bay on route 1, the partner company's employee immediately activated the emergency stop again. The lorry driver was able to escape unhindered into the open, the partner company's employee immediately went into the loading shed on loading route 2 and immediately informed the control room about the incident, as he was unable to escape into the open due to the poor visibility. The control centre immediately activated the alarm chain and activated firefighters with self-contained breathing apparatus to rescue the affected employee of the partner company. The employee of the partner company remained unharmed and was able to make his way outside under his own power. After the ash dust in the atmosphere had settled, rough cleaning was started immediately.
In consultation with the maintenance department, a concept was developed as to how to start identifying/rectifying the cause after the rough cleaning had been completed.
Actions were also drawn up for this case.

TITLE: Unintentional/unnoticed activation of the sprinkler system (fire extinguishing water) in the NH3 station.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the late shift on 5 June 2024, the sprinkler system (fire extinguishing water) in the NH3 station of the Heyden power plant was triggered unintentionally.
Due to an imminent internal test of the air receiver (see photo "Air receiver NH3 vaporiser station") for the HSX10 BB001 instrument air, it was activated by the late shift on duty. During this activation, the air receiver, which is fed by the plant air system, is shut off by corresponding ball valves and an associated bypass (see photo "Air receiver bypass fitting") is opened for continuous supply to the valves of the sprinkler system. During the disconnection measures, the bypass was neglected to be opened, as a result of which the fire extinguishing valves (see photo "Manifold valves for NH3 sprinkler system"), which were held in the CLOSED position by air support against the spring force, lost their CLOSED end position and fire extinguishing water was released. Due to the gradual drop in pressure in the system, the employee who had carried out the activation on site was unable to notice that the sprinkler system had been triggered. At around 7.00 p.m., the control centre received a message via the PBS message sequence that the air pressure in the air vessel had dropped below a certain level. However, this is normal and desired in the course of activation, so there was no need to take any action as a result. There is no message via the process operating system (message sequence) about the opening of the fire extinguishing valves or the triggering of the sprinkler system.

The activation was finally noticed by an employee on the night shift at around midnight during a tour. The first thing he did after making sure that it was an unintentional activation was to close the upstream manual valve of the fire extinguishing water supply line. After the sprinkling ended, the previously mentioned bypass of the air receiver was also opened. Once the necessary system pressure (air) had been reached, the previously closed manual valve for the fire extinguishing water was opened again so that the sprinkler system was/is available again.

It can therefore be assumed that fire extinguishing water was released/sprayed from approx. 19:00 to approx. 24:00.
The following areas were sprinkled:
-evaporator station
-Waggon refuelling
-Tank 1 & Tank 2

The majority of the fire extinguishing water collected flowed through the channels provided into the HSQ00 BB001 collection tank provided for this purpose (see photo "HSQ00 BB001 collection tank"). The accumulated water was then pumped towards the neutralisation tank in the VE/KA system. This is neutralised at a sufficient level and pumped towards the precipitation tank.
However, as the capacity of the HSQ00 BB001 collection tank is limited,
the channels in the evaporator station area overflowed. The overflowed water reached the outside through the building doors and flowed into the gullies of the external drainage system. The water flowed into the rainwater retention basin via the existing drainage system. As a precautionary measure, the pumps of the rainwater retention basin were switched off electrically so that the water could not be pumped towards the overpumping station without prior sampling by the power station laboratory.

Parallel to the measures taken on site, the on-call manager of the Heyden power plant was informed of the incident by the shift supervisor on duty. The incident was also documented in the electronic shift log (SAP).

On 6 June 2024, the water in the rainwater retention basin was sampled by the power plant laboratory. An ammonia concentration of 0.3 mg/litre was detected, which is well below the limit value of 10 mg/litre. As a result, the collected water can be pumped towards the pumping station as usual, which led to the pump being switched off.

It should be noted that at no time was there a risk from the release of ammonia or any other hazardous energy in terms of process safety.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Immediate measures:

-temporary interruption of the fire extinguishing supply
-Restoration of the air system pressure
-activation of the rainwater retention basin pumps
-informing the on-call officer
-Documentation of the incident

Recommendations:

-Sensitisation of staff
-Check whether alarm signals can be retrofitted when the sprinkler system responds.

TITLE: Transformer oil released onto Uniper land
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

TITLE: Oil leaking from machine
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the test run following the conversion of the control technology on machine set E3 (new flow monitors for the bearing oil supply were also installed here), an oil leak occurred at a screw connection that had not been tightened. As a test run of this system had already been carried out the previous week (approx. 5 minutes), during which no problems occurred, the ALV decided to carry out a longer test run. This resulted in an oil leak, which was not immediately noticed as the affected part of the system in the upper generator area had not been checked. When the leakage was noticed after a few minutes of the test run (during which the turbine bearings in the lower machine area and their oil supply in particular were inspected), all oil pumps were immediately deactivated and an attempt was made to collect the oil using appropriate means. Due to the structural conditions, there was no oil leakage into the underwater; the leaked oil volume was approx. 30-40 litres. All screw connections were then checked again, a test run of the system was carried out and no further leaks were found.
The provision of large quantities of binding agent and oil fleece proved to be very helpful in this situation.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Oil (Inc. contamination of land or water)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Switch off all oil pumps, use binding agents, clean oily components

TITLE: Environmental incident: Pollution from diesel fuel during mobile ship unloading
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
For mobile ship unloading, coal ships are brought into position by a floating pontoon

A mobile hydraulic unit is located on the floating pontoon to supply oil to the fastening jacks. A mobile power generator is used for decentralised power generation.

TITLE: Internal environmental incident: Contamination due to leaked hydraulic oil
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Internal environmental incident: Contamination caused by leaking hydraulic oil on the Sennebogen dredger used for mobile ship unloading.
On 6 May 2024, a hydraulic oil leak was detected on the dredger during unloading of the MV Nordwind.
The dredger was shut down immediately and the damaged area was localised.
It was a defective seal in the hydraulic system, from which approx. 20-30 litres of hydraulic oil had leaked and was collected in the mobile drip tray under the dredger.
The defective seal was replaced by a specialist company in the course of the afternoon and the dredger was ready for use again from 16:00.
The catch basin was cleaned by the service provider for ship unloading. The resulting oil-water mixture was disposed of.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Oil (Inc. contamination of land or water)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The prudent behaviour of the operator, the immediate shutdown of the excavator and the installation of the mobile collecting basin under the excavator prevented major damage and thus pollution of the immediately neighbouring body of water.

Tijdens de start van MPP3 is er gasolie terecht gekomen in het stoomsysteem. Uiteindelijk is deze gasolie via de ontspantank in waterdamp/gasolie-vorm over het Uniper-terrein verspreid met de windrichting mee. Start incident investigation.

TITLE: Hydraulic oil leak due to burst hydraulic hose - Eschenfelden borehole Esch 7
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
After completion of the loading work at the Esch 07 well, the crane from Baier Kran was about to leave the site.
The crane travelled from Esch 7 to the storage area at Esch 05. Shortly after leaving the Esch 7 well, a hydraulic hose burst on the crane, causing an oil leak. The damage to the mobile crane was only noticed before the Esch 05 storage area. As a result, a drop-shaped oil slick formed on the road.

The oil spill was covered with oil binding agent and swept up by hand after a short time. The oil spill was then covered twice with special oil binding agent

TITLE: Accident during the transport of ammonia water tanks
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
IBCs containing ammonia water were being loaded in the area of the NH3 transfer station. When manoeuvring a forklift truck, an IBC was damaged at around 10:30 in the morning (see photo), causing approx. 1m³ of ammonia water (approx. 35%) to escape. Work was interrupted immediately, employees on site put on a protective mask and the area was cordoned off. Work in the surrounding area was also stopped as a precaution. The smell of ammonia was clearly perceptible in the immediate area of the incident. With a light wind from the east, the smell of ammonia spread westwards towards Scho A and the power plant administration. In the direction of dispersion, ammonia was no longer perceptible at any time, even at the level of the power plant administration, not even in the west car park and not in the neighbourhood. This means that any odour nuisance or even danger to residents or people outside the power plant site can be completely ruled out.
	
The ammonia water ran via a paved surface (double-T interlocking paving, so-called "bone paving") into the sewerage system to the 33 m basin of the company sewage treatment plant. A very strong dilution with approx. 2,000 m³ of industrial wastewater takes place here. No odour of ammonia could be detected at the 33 m basin, nor was the pH value exceeded at the HMP1. As a precaution, the Emschergenossenschaft was also informed of the incident.
	
Immediately after the incident, the leaked ammonia water was absorbed with plenty of water as an immediate measure, and surfaces wetted with ammonia water were also rinsed free with plenty of water. The rinsing water was also discharged via the sewage system to the 33 metre basin of the company sewage treatment plant. Puddles in the area of smaller unpaved surfaces were checked with litmus paper. In some cases, high pH values were found, so that the soil was absorbed and replaced depending on the depth of penetration of ammonia water. Similarly, the paving is recorded and the penetration depth of ammonia water is determined. If the soils beneath the paving or the paving itself also exhibit ammonia findings, these soils are also removed, disposed of and replaced.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Immediate measures according to case description

  driver must be instructed and again instructed in accordance with the work authorisation on site.

  forklift truck before carrying out the work. The equipment must be

TITLE: Aggreko Hiab hydraulic hose failure (LX73 AVL)

1. Hiab isolated and made safe, with hydraulic oil system taken out of service to prevent further leakage.
2. Local oil spill containment deployed by working party and area made safe.
3. Hydraulic hose repaired by Aggreko sub-contractor Pirtek.
4. Suspended load safely loaded on to transport and despatched from site.
5. Oil spill cleaned by Aggreko sub-contractor RSK RAW.
6. Aggreko site personnel shared event information with Aggreko regional office.

TITLE: HCl tanker leak developed in offloading point.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During pressurisation of a delivery tanker of HCl to the WTP, a loss of fluid was observed from the foot valve area on the underside of the Brentag delivery tanker.  The tanker was immediately depressurised to reduce leak to a low flow. The fluid produced some gassing which was damped down using a fine spray from a washdown hose. The area was immediately barriered off to avoid unprotected persons entering the area. All forwarding systems for wash down residues was stopped and site surface drains closed. HVAC systems for adjacent buildings was stopped. Security informed to block access to site. Brentag driver requested assistance from Brentag emergency response team as per company procedure. Decision by Emergency Controller, in consultation with exec team, to ask site personnel to leave in a staggered approach to minimize risk of mass egress of 200+ staff (station on outage), rather than initiate sitewide evacuation. All persons confirmed off site by 15:03. External pump used to transfer product from tanker to designated delivery point. Leak flow decreased during transfer period and finished upon full transfer to tank. Tanker off site 17:30. Boiler Clean Drains Tank contents monitored and measuring 1.8pH. Advice sought from site chemist who approved use of Sodium Bicarbonate to neutralise contents of site chemically contaminated drains tanks. Tanks neutralised and monitored – in compliance with discharge permit. Discharged in purge.
No harm to persons or risk of as all control measures for delivery being followed as per approved operational procedure.
Full report to follow.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Hazardous substance, which is non-toxic, non-CMR substance (carcinogenic, mutagenic, reproduction toxic)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Immediate actions are covered in case description. Awaiting investigation from Brentag.

TITLE: External damage to manhole structure and DN300 pipeline, Herne, Am Böckenbusch
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Severe damage to a UWG district heating shaft and considerable damage to the DN300 FW pipeline. During demolition work by the external company Hofschröder, a large part of a FW shaft was torn off. The FW pipe and gate valves were in operation at the time and, in addition to the material damage caused, posed a considerable risk to the people working there.  No district heating water escaped.

A planning enquiry was carried out and the external company was provided with all the necessary planning documents by UWG. The external company started work without further consultation.

The unauthorised demolition of the shaft and the damage to the district heating pipe only came to light during a UWG inspection.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Immediate interruption of the external company's work. Damage assessment and instruction of the external company regarding the failure to comply with the legally prescribed planning enquiry and the associated obligation to notify work in the area of the supply systems, stating the location, type and expected construction time and the requirement to coordinate the construction project with UWG on site.
Written request for acknowledgement and liability for the damage with involvement of Uniper Legal and setting of a deadline.

Update: 10.8.22: Reminder sent to civil engineering company. This in clarification with insurer.

Update: 24.4.24: Civil engineering contractor is still clarifying with insurer whether the damage can be settled by V.

Update 7.6.24: Civil engineering contractor passes the claim on to subcontractor Bernemann

Update 22.01.2025: UWG has issued an invoice to Bernemann as part of the annual accounts in December.

Final update 02/02/2025: Bernemann in criminal proceedings, settlement is no longer expected. UWG claim must be written off.

TITLE: Organisation for network reconstruction
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
As part of the catalogue of measures for the grid restoration plan, functioning and blackout-proof or blackout-resistant communication between all partners involved - control centres of the TSOs, DSOs and the generation plants relevant for grid restoration - is essential.
 
The specific technical design and implementation of the measures is the responsibility of each person responsible for implementation within their own area of responsibility.
 
To this end, the TSO TenneT and Uniper (Dispatch & Grid Solutions) have drawn up specific process documents for dealing with blackout-proof communication and for KNK (power plant grid coupling).

Assessment for KW Franken:
For incidents L or XL according to Annex_05_ext_South, it would be necessary to disconnect the grid transformers. This can usually be done by the shift via the control technology system. However, the level of training must be ensured in the event of reduced staffing with the system switched off.
After disconnection, the power station is de-energised and the mains transformers must be switched manually. According to BA17, this may only be done by appropriately authorised persons. In the event that communication is also unavailable, it should be ensured that standby services are still available for restart operation.

CASE_DESCRIPTION: After rebuilding the SIRA block 4, we have increased vibrations on both lines of the injection pipes after the IBN.

Boiler house shut-off from 31 to 55m
Reduction of the output to 480MW net until the weld seams of the injection pipe are inspected 27.1.25
Labelling of all access points in the boiler house that it is closed during block operation
Staff information
Vibration measurement of the output with MUST RUN up to full load 15 and 16.1.25
Result was available on 24.1.25
Utilisation of weld seams 50% with the critical seams remaining less than 30%
Weld seams are checked from 4.2 to 12.2.25 after 23 starts
Risk assessment has been prepared and distributed
Thermal imaging camera and camera are placed and images are transferred to the control room
Additional vibration specialist has been requested
Process engineering investigation has been initiated and driving programme with tests is being defined and will then be implemented
Further analysis of the pipework with regard to changing the suspension and damping

TITLE: Oil store flooding due to Mulsifyre system discharge
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the electrical works conducted on weekend of 15th/16th Feb the supplies to the oil store were isolated.  The mulsifyre system was still live and the loss of supplies to the store included loss to the mulsifyre compressor which primes the air sensing lines.  When the pressure in the lines dropped the fire system was discharged in the oil storage area.  This deluge caused damage to several boxes of grease cartridges and also allowed oil drip trays to overflow.  The contents of which went down the station drains.

Oily water also proceeded to pass through to the office area and into the switchroom and down a cable tunnel.

This was not discovered properly until Tuesday 18th Feb as the Altrad oil supervisor was working in the main stores on Monday 17th Feb and didn't go in to the oil stores.  Legacy issues with the fire alarm system prevented the Operation teams from identifying where the mulsifyre system had been discharged and led them to believe there was a significant leak.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Oil (Inc. contamination of land or water)

TITLE: Block 1 failure during shutdown due to UL 1/1 opening too late
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Due to the incorrectly set monitoring of the "CLOSED" end position of pressure control valve 1 UL 1, injection valve 1 UL 1 opened too late and the turbine was disconnected from the grid at 40 MW via fast shutdown. The reason for this was that the "CLOSED" feedback signal from the pressure control valve was only cancelled at > 21%. However, the temperature control valve only opens when the "CLOSED" position of the pressure control valve is no longer present. As a result, the vapour flowing via UL 1/1 was not cooled and the temperature downstream of UL 1/1 increased inadmissibly. This caused the turbine to shut down.

TITLE: Leakage Bearing oil GeneratorBlock 2
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
An uncontrolled leakage of bearing oil occurred at the generator bearing of unit 2 on 11 July 2023 at 3:43 am.
The bearing was opened as part of maintenance work on 10 July 2023 at around 13:00 and the upper bearing shell was lifted off.   This dismantling state was left at the end of the working day in order to continue the work the following day.
When the automatic oil heating system went into operation during the night, the oil was able to escape from the generator bearing. This was not switched off during the maintenance work.
Approx. 47mm of level was missing in the storage oil tank. This corresponds to a quantity of 1142 litres that escaped. The leaking oil was distributed below the generator in the nacelle over a distance of 14m, 8m to -4m.
The leakage was detected and stopped on 11/07/2023 at 04:24 during a walkabout.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Oil (Inc. contamination of land or water)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
-The pumps were immediately stopped manually via the control system and secured against restarting (take-out), thus preventing further leakage.
-The oil leakage was checked and it was ensured that no contamination of the environment was possible.
-The oil accumulation 8 metres below the generator was bound with oil binder
-An SAP fault message was created 50276459.
-A disconnection was carried out on the storage oil system

TITLE: Oil store flooding due to Mulsifyre system discharge
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the electrical works conducted on weekend of 15th/16th Feb the supplies to the oil store were isolated.  The mulsifyre system was still live and the loss of supplies to the store included loss to the mulsifyre compressor which primes the air sensing lines.  When the pressure in the lines dropped the fire system was discharged in the oil storage area.  This deluge caused damage to several boxes of grease cartridges and also allowed oil drip trays to overflow.  The contents of which went down the station drains.

Oily water also proceeded to pass through to the office area and into the switchroom and down a cable tunnel.

This was not discovered properly until Tuesday 18th Feb as the Altrad oil supervisor was working in the main stores on Monday 17th Feb and didn't go in to the oil stores.  Legacy issues with the fire alarm system prevented the Operation teams from identifying where the mulsifyre system had been discharged and led them to believe there was a significant leak.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Oil (Inc. contamination of land or water)

TITLE: HCl tanker leak developed in offloading point.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During pressurisation of a delivery tanker of HCl to the WTP, a loss of fluid was observed from the foot valve area on the underside of the Brentag delivery tanker.  The tanker was immediately depressurised to reduce leak to a low flow. The fluid produced some gassing which was damped down using a fine spray from a washdown hose. The area was immediately barriered off to avoid unprotected persons entering the area. All forwarding systems for wash down residues was stopped and site surface drains closed. HVAC systems for adjacent buildings was stopped. Security informed to block access to site. Brentag driver requested assistance from Brentag emergency response team as per company procedure. Decision by Emergency Controller, in consultation with exec team, to ask site personnel to leave in a staggered approach to minimize risk of mass egress of 200+ staff (station on outage), rather than initiate sitewide evacuation. All persons confirmed off site by 15:03. External pump used to transfer product from tanker to designated delivery point. Leak flow decreased during transfer period and finished upon full transfer to tank. Tanker off site 17:30. Boiler Clean Drains Tank contents monitored and measuring 1.8pH. Advice sought from site chemist who approved use of Sodium Bicarbonate to neutralise contents of site chemically contaminated drains tanks. Tanks neutralised and monitored – in compliance with discharge permit. Discharged in purge.
No harm to persons or risk of as all control measures for delivery being followed as per approved operational procedure.
Full report to follow.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Hazardous substance, which is non-toxic, non-CMR substance (carcinogenic, mutagenic, reproduction toxic)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Immediate actions are covered in case description. Awaiting investigation from Brentag.

TITLE: Several anomalies found with regard to the lifting plan Sarens DFB-1
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
5-9-2024 During the lifting work of the DFB1 ducting parts and in the run-up to this work, several things did not go as they should.

On the morning of 5 September, the hoisting specialist made an appointment not to hoist the ducting parts because the wind speed was too high.
After this, it was decided to start hoisting without the hoisting specialist being present (in violation of the WMS).

Other issues on which adjustments were made earlier:
- During the installation of the scaffolding, there was an apprentice machinist who did not hold a TCVT certificate who was actually not suitable to carry out this kind of high-risk work.
- Lifting certificates of rigging only made presentable by Sarens at the very last minute. Work was temporarily halted by the lifting specialist until the certificates were present.
- 700T crane set up without azobe bulkheads under two legs (on the sand). During preparation, not properly looked at by Sarens
- and at the time of lifting, a complete barrier was not set up and people were not removed from the lifting area during lifting.

- When placing the ducting parts, no thought was given to bracing the load before the load (bracing was also not prepared) was detached from the crane. Response of the foreman Sarens is very defensive.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Striking into an object (Non-vehicle impacts with fixed objects)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
06-09 A meeting was held with the foreman and management of Sarens by the management of the DFB-1 project and HSE.
No hoisting will take place without preparation and only if the hoisting specialist is present.

The pre-alarm installed as a result of this activated this time, but did not allow the technician much time to de-ice the cooling air fan inlet. So whilst a SIS activation was avoided this time, it could have occurred if the technician were not immediately available.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The ice build-up on the cooling air fan inlet was removed using a spray bottle of antifreeze.

Golden Hour recorded, to detail the nature of the incident

TITLE:
Stationary extinguishing systems for electrical / control / switchgear / IT technology (rooms and objects)
Note from Safe.on audit from 28/07/2022, No. 1.35
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Stationary extinguishing systems for electrical / control / switchgear / IT technology (rooms and objects)

The rooms for electrical, control, switching and IT systems and the central control room are not equipped with fire extinguishing systems. The control room is manned around the clock.

Lack of fire extinguishing systems in the rooms and cabinets for the electrical/switchgear/server and IT technology

The site should identify the most important and non-redundant rooms and cabinets containing electrical/switchgear/control/IT equipment. These facilities should be equipped with automatic fire suppression systems. A risk/cost analysis for protection should be carried out, including the cost of replacement and the potential time and cost of business interruption if the short operating time per year is not met.

As effective firefighting in rooms with electrical/switchgear/control/IT systems is not possible by employees or the fire service (response time, access only when de-energised), an automatic protection system is the only chance for safe, fast and reliable extinguishing. In addition, the fire brigade would use water/foam as an extinguishing agent, which would destroy all assets. In any case, a total loss of the room must be assumed.

Recommendation: Installation of an inert gas extinguishing system with automatic activation, at least for the rooms or cabinets that are most important in terms of material value and business continuity.

Please note that closed cabinets require fire detection and extinguishing in the cabinet, as fire detection on the ceiling and flooding the room with inert gas is not an adequate protection objective.

As these rooms are usually unmanned, room protection with nitrogen or argon is possible, but the HSE requirements must be taken into account (CO2 should therefore not be considered).

Another option is non-toxic inert gases such as "Argonite" (Minimax) or "Inergen" (Tyco / Johnsson Controls), which can be kept fully active when people are present and therefore do not require organisational shutdown / impairment and monitoring systems for fire detection or extinguishing systems.

Synthetic gases such as Novec 1230 or FM200 are currently not accepted by Uniper. Neither 3M as the manufacturer of Novec 1230 nor the companies offering it are willing or able to issue a genuine test authorisation for electrical equipment. Even within the manufacturing companies there are different opinions about the possibility of using the product in switch cabinets, as requested by Uniper (in 2022).

Costs: Around 25,000 euros per room for the inert gas system, depending on the type of room and the number of closed cabinets.

Another option for individual properties are direct object protection systems (inert gas flooding of individual cabinets) for the most important systems / cabinets, or 19'' plug-in units for individual cabinets, consisting of a detection and suppression device that could be installed directly in the cabinets. Of course, this only makes sense if the important cabinets are closed units in which a necessary inert gas concentration can be maintained for a certain period of time.

Costs: Approx. 400-1500 euros per cabinet, depending on how many cabinets are to be protected. The more cabinets are protected with a system connected in series, the cheaper it is per cabinet.

Probability of a fire on "non-rotating electrical appliances": Expected during the service life of the system (1:1.00)
Uniper Risk Consulting can provide you with further detailed information and support in planning efficient and sensible fire detection and suppression for "non-rotating electrical equipment".

TITLE: Heavy dust generation during unloading work on a construction site
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During a delivery to a construction site using a silo trailer, a considerable amount of dust was produced when a gritting vehicle was being filled. The technical condition of the construction site gritting vehicle was inadequate. There was no gate valve, pressure release lever, filling level indicator or functioning ventilation system to ensure that the material could be blown into the spreader virtually dust-free.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The vehicles were positioned in such a way that the wind direction carried the dust outside and no employee could inhale the dust. In addition, the BauMineral drivers controlled the unloading process so that as little dust as possible was produced.
A standard for the safe delivery of binding agents to construction sites is being developed for the future.

An asphalted area has already been provided specifically for the requirements of BauMineral for the regular blow-out processes at the silo.

TITLE: Hoist work DFB 1
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
While working in the demolition area E2, we saw from a distance that lifting operations were taking place at the DFB, with no obvious demarcation. We then decided to go and have a look on site. On arrival, we saw that the barrier, consisting of three plastic posts, was lying flat on the ground. At that time, lifting operations were still in full swing.

As we surveyed the situation, we saw someone coming towards us from the other side under the barrier. I introduced myself and asked him why he was entering the hoisting area. He replied that he was the supervisor and gave the impression that he thought (thought) this was permissible.

In addition, I noticed that the rigger had regular hand contact with the load, posing a potential risk. There were also three employees on the platform directly under the load, which the supervisor did not see as a risk.

We further noted that the work permit was not fully completed. Specific risks, such as proximity to an operating boiler and steam pipes, were not included in the work permit/TRA. The TRA lacked the names and initials of who took the necessary measures and which ones. This poses a significant safety risk that should not be overlooked.

I would like to stress that these observations indicate that the current safety measures are inadequate during this work and that action must be taken to ensure the safety of all employees.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Incorrect posture or insufficient work environment
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Incident discussed with various stakeholders

TITLE: U6 HP Bypass failed to operate correctly and boiler safety valves operated
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
When taking U6 off load the HP bypass spray wasn't controlling properly causing high after bypass temperatures and tripping the HP Bypass.This is a known issue so we were expecting this to happen. Due to the Bypass trip the HP header pressure rises as the steam has nowhere to go. When the bypass was reset it was noticed that the process value on the HP bypass was struggling to meet the set point and was lagging behind quite a bit. This caused the HP header to rise significantly and the safety valves lifted. At this point the unit was off load but it was noticed that the GT EV burners were still lit adding to the high steam pressure situation. We tried to put an 'OFF' on the GT sequencer but this didn't work so we used the emergency trip button located on the unit desk. Once the flames were out the pressure started to subside but the HP bypass was still clearly not controlling as it should.Due to the significance off the HP bypass the unit was MEL'd to 0MW until 12:00 01/10/24
There are x3 issues here:
1. HP Bypass spray water control not controlling well enough to stop the HP Bypass tripping on high temperatures
2. Hp Bypass process value not following the set point as it should.
3. The GT not shutting down correctly and taking the flames out when the Circuit breaker was opened.

TITLE: Loss of Containment while returning U42 Sync Comp Cooling Pump 2 To Service
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
When returning to service a closed cooling circulation pump following maintenance, the operator didn't see the vent valve on the discharge pipe had been left open and process fluid was released into the area. The operator managed to shut the valve and minimise the release of fluid.
Following the incident it was also realised that the closed cooling system had lost system pressure and was in alarm. No-one on the shift had been trained to repressurise the system and there are no operator procedures are in place for the Sync Comp units to refer to. The location of the O&M manuals are also unknown.
The Uniper commissioning Engineer was contacted for advice on how to repressurise the system but the equipment didn't work.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Immediate Action
1.An email was sent to all SAP's to request that when vents and drains are left open and not part of the isolation, a note is left within the Key Safe to alert the person returning the plant to operational state.

Recommendations
1. As above, circulate best practice guidance to SAP's for logging of drains and vents not part of the isolation
2. Produce operational procedures for Sync Comp units
3. Ensure Sync Comp O&M manuals are accessible for both operations and engineering personnel.

TITLE: Oil leakage from lower guide bearing at KW Niedernach
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
After coordination between Uniper (referred to as the client) and Stellba-Hydro (referred to as the contractor), the oil required for the bearings was filled into the machine's guide bearing at the Niedernach power plant.
At this point in time, the contractor's executing personnel were not aware that filling aids (filler pipe, funnel and oil dipstick) were available at the power plant.
The information on this had been exchanged between the client and the contractor. Due to a partial change of personnel, this information was not known at the time of execution.
The oil was filled directly from the 200 litre oil drum into the filler opening of the storage facility using the electric oil pump provided.
The filling process was interrupted several times to check the fill level in the housing using a torch. The visual fill level check was also carried out via the filler opening. A clear view is only possible up to the upper surface of the bearing carrier marked in blue.
The oil was filled in until the oil level was visible above the bearing bracket for the first time. The quantity filled in was estimated at approx. 20 to 25 litres.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Oil (Inc. contamination of land or water)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The client and contractor have visually inspected the impeller for oil leaks via the access to the opened impeller casing.
Cleaning the oil traces on the outer casing of the impeller Oil traces.
Oil binding cloths in the suction pipe to bind any oil present.

TITLE: Improper use of a solvent in the new demineralisation plant

Improper use resulted in vapours that were briefly inhaled by several employees without protection. To rule out any damage to health, all those involved were taken to hospital for a check-up. All those involved were released after a thorough examination without any findings.

According to the SDS, it should only be used in well-ventilated rooms, preferably only outdoors

TITLE: Black smoke from PKM pipe 24
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Totalis reports black smoke entering the boiler from burner nozzle 24 (photos added). Totalis is carrying out work, immediately next door, on burner 23. Wait went to the scene and also saw the black smoke. It comes out slowly, at the bottom of the boiler, and falls slowly down the wall, some of it rising/diffusing.

Cause is from cutting fire work PKM20 bends. After stopping this work (and partly opening pipework), it can be seen that smoke is still forming from this duct. See photos/video.

Subsequent inspection (photos added) shows that fuel is present in the pipes, this is pulverised coal. The pipe always contains several millimetres of dust, but in many places centimetres thick. The cutting burners give open fire to this fuel + liquid metal on the fuel.

The licence does not mention presence of fuel, working in ATEX zone, and specific measures to mitigate this.
HSE revision spoken to. They will discuss this further within revision team.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Boiler cleared. PKM20 operations halted.
Fire-fighting equipment put on standby on site.
Conducted further inspection and consultation with HSE man this evening: Add to TRA that combustible material is present, ATEX zone active. And discuss what measures are needed. For example, grinding or cutting instead of cutting fire, open section, clean pipe, then cut fire, or use inert gas in ductwork.
This is taken to revision team.

TITLE: EKSP2 protective tripping defective
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
When filling the boiler on block 2, the EKSP 2 fell out via protective tripping.
(Bottle >13.5m and capacitor not ready for pick-up)
The UGS wanted to shut down but stopped in step 53 because the 6kV drive of the EKSP 2 had not yet switched off. It could not be switched off either.

The electrical standby team was informed and it was communicated by telephone whether the drive could also be switched off in the switchgear. The manual switch-off did not work, so the control fuse was removed manually and the drive was switched off. Further investigation by the electrical department revealed that the contactor K12 in the switchgear had tripped, but had not passed on the command, so that the drive did not switch off because a contact of the contactor was bent.

With this fault, the signalling of the T3000 was somewhat opaque, as the backing pump and the main pump (grey background) signalled switched off, but the drive continued to run. When the UGS was switched off and then switched on again and sent to standstill, nothing changed.
The EKSP2 was not damaged by this fault, it ran at the minimum flow rate of 109 bar for approx. 10 minutes. The engine air temperature was 42 degrees. The oil supply was also guaranteed.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The drive was switched off manually, the electrical department investigated the cause and found the fault.

TITLE:
Sharp false fire alarm

False fire alarm
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
2024-05-16 at 20:35 The fire alarm centre received a fire alarm. The heat detector on the steam turbine bearings has been activated.
No abnormalities were noted during the inspection, so the firefighters were called off.
The smoke outlets and telescopic gates were closed back. The empty CO2 cylinder was replaced.
Please seal the lockers.
The incident has been reported to the SBT. The incident has been entered into Synergi.


17.05.2024 SBT investigated the incident, cause unknown, sensors tested, OK

On 16.05.2024, at 20:42, an automatic fire alarm was received from the collective line 13206 (3db FDOOT241-A9 detector). No actual fire occurred. No specific cause was found during the review. We measured the instantaneous ambient temperature of all three detectors with a certified thermal imager. The low pressure bearing was measured at 30°C and the clutch assembly environment at 43-43°C. Consequently, the mode of operation of the two sensors at the clutch assembly remained as thermal sensors, but their parameter set was changed from thermal speed monitoring and thermal maximum 60°C to thermal speed monitoring and thermal maximum 80°C, adapting to the ambient conditions. Testing was carried out to ensure that the sensors were working properly.

TITLE: U1 OUTAGE - FLT Transporting Generator Casing Steel Plate
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A near hit incident occurred involving a forklift and a stack of heavy steel plates. The incident took place at outside Unit 1 turbine hall at approximately 14:05

Details of the Incident:

Forklift Operator:  PES 
Equipment Involved, Steel Plates

Sequence of Events:
The forklift was transporting a stack of heavy steel plates.
As the forklift took a corner, the plates began to slide off the forks.
The sliding plates posed a significant risk of falling and potentially causing injury or damage.

Immediate Actions Taken:
The forklift operator immediately stopped the vehicle to prevent further movement of the plates.
The area was cordoned off to ensure safety until the situation was stabilized.
Additional personnel were called to assist in safely repositioning the plates.

Root Cause Analysis:
Load Securing: It was identified that the steel plates were not adequately secured before transport.
Forklift Speed: The speed at which the corner was taken may have contributed to the instability of the load.
Corner Handling: The angle and method of turning the corner were reviewed for safety compliance.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Provide additional training for forklift operators on safe handling practices, especially when transporting heavy and potentially unstable loads.
Emphasize the importance of reducing speed and careful maneuvering when taking corners.
Conduct regular safety inspections to ensure compliance with load securing protocols.

TITLE: Misuse of 'Man Down' feature on Site Radios
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the evening of 16th July 2024 around 20:00, the night security guard set off the ‘Man Down’ alert on his site radio, which was subsequently reset. Later, whilst undertaking the 22:00 site tour, the security guard failed to take the Gatehouse radio & site security mobile phone.
The Gatehouse radio was left in the Gatehouse and set to ‘Man Down On’ and thus activated an alert on the Gatehouse, CDC & KPS Control Room radio base stations.
Operations personnel in the CDC Control Room attempted to contact the security guard on the radio & site security mobile phone, to no avail.
Fortunately, operations personnel in the CDC Control Room were able to spot the security guard walking around site, which negated the need to escalate the matter. Operations personnel in the CDC Control Room were able to speak to the security guard on his return to the Gatehouse and instigated additional contact protocols to ensure there were no repeat occurrences that night.
The following morning, upon his arrival to site, the day security guard reset the Gatehouse radio base station which was still in alarm. The night security guard simply turned off the Gatehouse radio and turned down the volume on the Gatehouse radio base station to silence the audible alert, as he did not know how to reset it.

On the evening of 22nd July 2024, the same security guard once again set off the ‘Man Down’ radio alert and was given instruction on how to reset it by Killingholme operations personnel. However, at the start of the morning shift on 23rd July 2024, Killingholme operations personnel found the KPS Control Room radio base station in alert, so it would appear the security guard had triggered the alert again at some point during the night.

These are serious matters of concern, which highlight the security guard’s lack of understanding and discipline, repeatedly creating unnecessary work for numerous Uniper personnel.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The security guard has been instructed to take with him the Gatehouse site radio and security mobile phone each time he leaves the Gatehouse to perform a site tour. He has also been instructed several times on how to use the 'Man Down' feature on the site radios.
A meeting has been arranged on 14th August 2024 with his regional manager to ensure there are no more 'Man Down' incidents which are concerning and extremely disruptive to Uniper operations personnel.

TITLE: GT Fire detection trigger
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
GT Fire operated at approx. 08:30 today. 
Investigations identified that a Smoke detector within the Turbine Hall HVAC extraction ducts had triggered the alarm.
The associated filter on the detector was today identified with what appeared to be oil residue The other 2 detectors in the ducting’s also where in a similar condition however still functioning. 
On external visual inspection of the GT it was identified that some browning around the turbine bearing vents at the 11 and 2 o’clock positions and this has caused lacquer formation This is believed to have been gradually increasing since 2022.
Some of this material was removed for analysis and to determine if it was as suspected oil or charring. -  from this it was determined that the residue appeared to be a mixture of oil vapor and dust . Not charring
Checks where made on the GT start bearing rodding point which appeared to be clear from Coking.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The fire detector filters in the HVAC ducting were cleaned and put back in service, the original operating one still showing a fault but functioning
Siemens have been contacted for advice on the issue which they have referred to engineering . The fire detection contractor is due to service the units next week
The cause and effects matrix for the fire detection system is being checked to ensure does not trigger the GT protection system.An area was cleaned on blow offline to determine future fouling rate.

TITLE: Low voltage cable found under concrete.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Whilst carrying out surface civil works associated with Gatic cover replacement, an AWC was discovered. No contact was made with cable - discovered as concrete slab lifted. Insulation appears damaged but judging from buried state appears to have been in this condition for some time. Site drawings checked prior to starting work did not show any buried cables, cat scans were carried out which did not detect cable (most likely dead), and removal of the thin layer of surface concrete was being carried out using hand tools as a precautionary measure as per SSOW.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Work stopped immediately and area secured pending further investigation.

TITLE: PSO - Main Control Block Fire Alarm
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The control block fire alarm sounded at 07.48hrs. A full sweep of the building commenced and the various fire panels were checked to identify the source of the alarm. The area identified was zone 1 ground floor. A burning smell was evident on entry to the area. When opening the Inverter Room switchroom door thick smoke and burning smell was evident. The switchroom was ventilated and checks of adjacent areas of the switchroom annex confirmed that the source of the smoke was from the Inverter Room. As the smoke cleared, on inspection none of the equipment in the associated switchroom appeared to be in distress! With the support of the electrical team each panel was inspected and it was believed that EML4 lighting inverter was the most likely source although it was still operating apparently normally.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Fire watch set up. Further discussions with the electrical team as to what further actions required. EML4 put on hard bypass and isolated for inspection by the OEM and routines on EML's 1, 2 & 3 also planned. Consider thorough inspections of all apparatus within the Inverter Room

TITLE: Work Firma Boels halted and removed from site
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Frima Boels was building an arched tent on behalf of the Newes firm on the backfiring field (this had been allocated as a workshop area).
What preceded.
Last Tuesday, 18 June, saw the Boels company working on the refuelling field and noticed in cycling past that these people were not using the proper PBMS (no safety glasses, short sleeves and not all wearing the proper work clothes prescribed by Uniper.
I approached these people and pointed this out to them and they immediately adjusted it.
I then asked them who they were working for, which was the company Newes, so I asked if they had had a work start meeting and where the permit was.
The permit was at the office and there had been no start work meeting, which surprised me because there was an aerial platform (in my opinion, a high-risk permit should always be explained to the group), so I took it upon myself to explain the rules that apply on the site when work is being done.
After this, I called the supervisor and permit holder and shared with him what I had observed.
He immediately wanted to speak to the men, to which I replied that this was no longer necessary as I had already done so.
The men understood and promised better here. This is how we parted company.
Today, 20 June, I went back to check on the work and found the men again without safety goggles and wearing short sleeves.
I spoke to them directly and a discussion ensued about now and then and because they were almost finished and hot anyway.
I then stopped the work and called in the relevant people from Newes and said that we could not use this attitude on the Uniper site.
I then contacted the safety people at the project and Uniper to ask them to remove these people from the site.
I also immediately checked the work permit, which I found listed below:
- Permit was not in place
- No start-up meeting had taken place
- Permit was at the office and valid for this work
- Work started on the second day without physical contact between the holder and the party carrying out the work
- Permit had not been signed by the holder
- TRA had not been signed (i.e. apparently not discussed)
- No additional comments had been made and the contact person was not on the permit
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Incorrect posture or insufficient work environment
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Work halted and affected people removed from site in consultation with security

TITLE: Hire car not delivered on time
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Monday 22nd January at 08:40, I raised a request for a Hertz hire car which was accepted in 30 minutes. I received my confirmation and reservation booking: K7450329419. The delivery address was in Lincoln.
On Tuesday 23rd January at 08:32 I received a phone call from the branch in Nottingham, stating they could only offer me an electric car, would I be okay with this. I said yes and awaited the delivery of the vehicle later that day.
I then received a phone call from the branch stating the delivery drivers were having trouble charging the car, they were going to have to head back into Nottingham to charge the car and they would be an hour or so late delivering the vehicle to me, to which I said was okay.
By 9pm on Tuesday 23rd I decided that the hire car was not going to be delivered that night. I woke up on Wednesday 24th and called the branch at 08:00 when they opened to find out what had happened. As I was explaining the situation, I was rudely interrupted and told to stop talking as they knew who I was. I have now been informed, the delivery drivers continued to have issues trying to charge the vehicle and eventually had no option but to abandon the delivery as the car had no charge. They have vehicles being collected this morning and they will get one to me as soon as possible but that wont be until around 11:30am.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Informed business support and Exec.

TITLE: U1 OUTAGE - FLT Transporting Generator Casing Steel Plate
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A near hit incident occurred involving a forklift and a stack of heavy steel plates. The incident took place at outside Unit 1 turbine hall at approximately 14:05

Details of the Incident:

Forklift Operator:  PES 
Equipment Involved, Steel Plates

Sequence of Events:
The forklift was transporting a stack of heavy steel plates.
As the forklift took a corner, the plates began to slide off the forks.
The sliding plates posed a significant risk of falling and potentially causing injury or damage.

Immediate Actions Taken:
The forklift operator immediately stopped the vehicle to prevent further movement of the plates.
The area was cordoned off to ensure safety until the situation was stabilized.
Additional personnel were called to assist in safely repositioning the plates.

Root Cause Analysis:
Load Securing: It was identified that the steel plates were not adequately secured before transport.
Forklift Speed: The speed at which the corner was taken may have contributed to the instability of the load.
Corner Handling: The angle and method of turning the corner were reviewed for safety compliance.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Provide additional training for forklift operators on safe handling practices, especially when transporting heavy and potentially unstable loads.
Emphasize the importance of reducing speed and careful maneuvering when taking corners.
Conduct regular safety inspections to ensure compliance with load securing protocols.

TITLE: Activation not carried out correctly
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The control oil system was to be temporarily normalised for a test run on MDRV 2 Block 2. There were 2 isolations for the order 76143194. Firstly, the turbine activation 30762294, in which the auxiliary control oil pump and the shut-off valve after the control oil fire valve were activated. These were temporarily normalised. The second enabling circuit was 30762295, which enabled all drains on the control oil side and the oil pump bypasses. This activation was for draining the control oil system and was not temporarily normalised.
During the shift handover from the night shift to the morning shift, it was announced that the control oil system was ready for the test run. During commissioning of the control oil system, it was determined that the leakage oil tank, to which all control oil drains go, was rising rapidly. After the leakage oil tank rose faster than it could be pumped out, the test run was cancelled.
When activating the FS 30762294, only the control list from SAP was used and the status was not set to ITNM (Is temporarily normalised).
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The early shift has cancelled the test run and temporarily normalised the activation of 30762295.

TITLE: Leaking transmitter Height level measurement HCl tank
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On 20 March 2024 at around 02:00, the shift personnel noticed a slight hydrochloric acid leak on the hydrochloric acid tank in the chemical storage room during their tour of the water treatment plant. After closer inspection by the laboratory staff and M-Werkstatt, it turned out that there was a slight leak of HCl at the transmitter of one of the two old level measurements of the HCl tank - see picture no. 1.
Approximately one litre of 30% hydrochloric acid leaked from the leak. The leaking hydrochloric acid was diluted with water and rinsed into the clean tank. The chemical room is designed as a catch basin and is connected directly to the neutralisation basin. After shutting off the local level measurement, the leaking measuring transducer was replaced. The work was carried out by the M workshop wearing a chemical protection suit and a full face mask with a breathing filter for hydrochloric acid vapours.
After inspecting the defective transmitter, it was determined that there was an internal leak inside the transmitter at the intermediate piece for separating the hydrochloric acid and the transmitter - see Figures 2 to 4. External damage during the current replacement of the existing height level measurement by the scaffolding can therefore be ruled out.
The level measurements were installed in 2008 during the modernisation of the demineralisation plant; a radar measurement system for chemicals was not yet on the market at that time or the acquisition costs were too high.
Measures that were already in the implementation phase before the hydrochloric acid leak
The newly installed level measurement (radar measurement) is attached to the top of the local level measurement. The new measurement is therefore no longer directly exposed to the liquid medium like the previous measurement - see Fig. 5.
The new radar measurements on the NaOH and HCl tanks were purchased because in the event of leaks at the measuring transducers, the leakage of chemicals and the associated risk of the chemical tanks leaking via the local level measurement is avoided (safety risk).
The old level measurements on the two chemical tanks will be dismantled in April 2024 - see Fig. 6 and Fig. 7. The local level measurements will then be sealed at the bottom with a blind flange - see Fig. 8.

TITLE: Superheated steam from oil burners enters light oil leak tank
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
As a result of blow-through steam valves of the stove burners, superheated steam enters the leak tank, by chance I discovered that the joint drain valve was closed, after opening this valve (30HJF98AA301) was closed, it only closes at maximum level of the leak tank.
After opening this valve (normal operating condition), the temperature of the leak tank rose and the drain line to the tank felt very hot.
This leak tank contains light oil with a flash point of >55grdC and a self-ignition temperature of >250 grdC.
The atomising steam can reach a temperature of 280grdC.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The overfill valve 30HJF98AA301 closed controlled and mbv forcing in composer blocked on open control and secured by order with B6 notification.
Recommendation to check all steam valves and hand valves for forcing during overhaul.
Also investigate whether the situation as currently connected is safe and may need to be rerouted to a safe location.
Current situation is unacceptable.

TITLE: Forklift Truck Transporting Generator Steel Casing Plates
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Forklift Operator: PES

Equipment Involved: Forklift, Steel Plates

Sequence of Events:
The forklift was transporting a stack of heavy steel plates from the turbine hall on U1.
As the forklift took a corner whilst reversing backwards, the plates began to slide off the forks.
The sliding plates posed a significant risk of falling and potentially causing injury or damage.

Immediate Actions Taken:

The forklift operator immediately stopped the vehicle to prevent further movement of the plates.
Additional personnel were called to assist in safely repositioning the plates.

Root Cause Analysis:

Load Securing: It was identified that the steel plates were not adequately secured before transport.
Forklift Speed: The speed at which the corner was taken may have contributed to the instability of the load.
Corner Handling: The angle and method of turning the corner were reviewed for safety compliance.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Supervisor informed
No further lifting with fork lift truck. 
Movement operations between turbine halls
Correct mobile plant
Banks man

TITLE: PEM 120 - Grain - Gas Ignition Block Overpressure Integrity Risk
CASE_DESCRIPTION: GT Ignition block gauge is being subject to gas pressure potentially beyond its design pressure. This synergi is captured as per PEM120 exclusion zone requirements. Please see GE Help case 20240222-0255 for further details and Depp Data.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
1) Exclude access to the auxiliary skid top of lube oil tank from unit ignition through to shut down as risk is present at many and uncertain running conditions particularly the TRIP risk. 

2) If integrity was breached the purge credit system would likely fail due to leakage in the system while it’s applied. 

Monitoring Action: Operations team to monitor purge credit system status across all units and if the system fails, the operations team should carry out a gas leak check in the area local to ignition block as soon as possible after shutdown. If the atmosphere is safe, then carry out a local leak check of the ignition block assembly with leak detection spray to see if any leak persists. Additionally the assembly should be visually inspected for any signs of damage or leakage. 

3) Plan to remove the gauge and replace with a plug to eliminate risk of leakage via the gauge until a full solution is developed to reinstate the gauge. GE recommended and confirmed with ignition block OEM. Once plugged the exclusion zone is no longer required.

The files had been scanned prior to use and transfer onto the dedicated USB storage device for the zone. The initial Microsoft defender scans did not detect any malicious software.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: A quick online research via-a-vis the compromised software was conducted, revealing  several articles detailing that the software was able to be modified with injected malware but then re-digitally signed with stolen manufacture signature certificates. This bypasses many of the simpler window’s installation and execution warnings that may deter use.

TITLE: Forklift Truck Transporting Generator Steel Casing Plates
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Forklift Operator: PES

Equipment Involved: Forklift, Steel Plates

Sequence of Events:
The forklift was transporting a stack of heavy steel plates from the turbine hall on U1.
As the forklift took a corner whilst reversing backwards, the plates began to slide off the forks.
The sliding plates posed a significant risk of falling and potentially causing injury or damage.

Immediate Actions Taken:

The forklift operator immediately stopped the vehicle to prevent further movement of the plates.
Additional personnel were called to assist in safely repositioning the plates.

Root Cause Analysis:

Load Securing: It was identified that the steel plates were not adequately secured before transport.
Forklift Speed: The speed at which the corner was taken may have contributed to the instability of the load.
Corner Handling: The angle and method of turning the corner were reviewed for safety compliance.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Supervisor informed
No further lifting with fork lift truck. 
Movement operations between turbine halls
Correct mobile plant
Banks man

The side protection in the area of the system-free scaffold planking must be installed at the edge of the planking (no gap between scaffold planking and side protection).
-
The scaffolding components of the UW-side scaffolding along the wings that have been removed for technological reasons (laying / tamping under the cover plates) must be replaced immediately, otherwise these scaffolds must be blocked.

Unauthorised modifications to the scaffolding are prohibited for scaffolding users.

Contacted Mitsubishi HSE Duisburg.

TITLE: Leakage of district heating water when filling the new Rentfort-Nord project section
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During filling work on the newly built section in the area of the new customer AWO in Gladbeck-Rentfort, there was an unintentional leakage of district heating water. The flanges shown in the photo were not sealed with flange covers at the time of the water leak. The pipe section was filled with approx. 20-25 m²/h from the return flow from the Talstraße station. The leaking water was discovered by the caretaker of the AWO. The water escaped from the flanges in a 20-30 cm high fountain inside the closed construction fences. After overflowing the excavation pit, the water ran down a meadow following the slope. A citizen saw vapour clouds and therefore informed the fire brigade.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Temperature Extreme (Inc. Hot or cold surfaces, gases and environments)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The fire brigade called EVNG (gas supplier) before arriving at the scene. They immediately closed the nearby FW ground valves, stopped the water from escaping and pumped out the pit. The partner company employees then arrived.

Further commissioning work will only be carried out by specialised Uniper Wärme employees.

Recommendation for further measures:
Review transferability of plant responsibility to partner companies during commissioning

TITLE: FGD Ops Van Rear Light Cluster Damaged
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The CPO was asked to check the status of the towns water tank inlet pipework which had previously been identified as leaking, the CPO drove the van up Redhill tanks on  the  track, which was muddy. When the CPO arrived he parked the van and went to check the leaking pipework.  After the check was completed the CPO had to turn the van around to go back to the the track, upon reversing the van he slid on the mud into the undergrowth and damaged the rear drivers side light cluster.

The CPO used his mirrors (as the reversing camera didn't initiate - see below) but because he'd slid on the mud he couldn't avoid the 'bushes'. A point to note was that the reversing camera did not initiate whilst in reverse gear and it appears that if you are below a couple of mph then it doesn`t initiate the reversing camera.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Returned to supervisor to report incident
