TITLE: Foreseeable temporary reduced capacity extinguishing system due to maintenance on 19 June (6-24h).
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
We are required to report this in advance to DCMR and Fire Service (Meldposter), this has just been done by phone.
Incident number from DCMR control room: 1153955.
Scope of maintenance and measures:
Two ground valves are being replaced near the UCML cooling water pump building.
This will require part of the system to be blocked and depressurised. This means that the entire extinguishing system in that area will be unavailable during the repair period of about 8 hours. See attached P&ID. A total of 10 hydrants will then become temporarily unusable of which 2 are already depressurised for the Neste NMA project. By rolling out fire hoses from hydrants that are in operation, we mitigate the risks.
Request to the Guard to confirm commencement on the day of execution 19 June by email citing occurrence no. 1153955 to meldkamer@dcmr.nl cc rick.mimpen@dcmr.nl and to inform the joint fire brigade.
Involved in the creation of the notification and this message: Ronald van der Hoeven, Machiel Naber.
On the day (19 June), Mark Prook sent e-mail confirmation with further explanation to DCMR, VRR and GB.
On 22 July, PMC repeated the notification because the work on 19 June did not go ahead because the wrong materials had been delivered. On 25 July, following notification from FAC that the work had been successfully completed, PMC cancelled.

TITLE: HRSG Blowdown , step change in noise and steam release.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During start up #97, HOT rates, 0700 Sync.
It was noted during the start up ( ongoing issue with Premix TSOV), a step change in noise was observed during the start, plant was at 30MW.
The noise was above the start up noise ie hogger/bypass etc.

A quick investigation led to observing that the noise came from the blowdown vessel area, increased steam release noted with noise.

Info when the superheater drains were closed, the noise reduced as well as the steam release., vice versa with those drains opened.

GT was tripped at 0714 30MW.

Restricted access to the Turbine hall.

Pressure in drums maintained for investigation purposes.

Exec and Mech TL aware.

See attachments videos attached.

Under a MO/FWI and HP Drum pressure at 9.0 Bar, Mech Eng carried out an non intrusive visual inspection.

Initial findings were that the pipework from the top of the tank which swans neck downwards to feed a local pressure gauge, the top section has fractured from the vessel .
Picture attached.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Plant was shut down/Tripped.

Restricted access in turbine hall.

Maintain Boiler pressure.

Awaiting Mech Engineer

TITLE: Steam Turbine delay to run up due to a ET200 power supply fault.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: ST Would not run up to warming speed. There was a standing ET200 power supply fault which would not clear activated the previous evening. Various boiler Temp And pressure signals had been lost, most appeared to be 2oo3 channels, and unit ran oK  with the fault the previous evening. However ST was missing the S/HTG RHT AHD TURB >30K criteria to  release the ST. This was due to signal 10LBB50CP004 being the only channel used to calculate the superheating and was currently a bad signal. This was simulated to replicate CP002/003 at 22 bar to release the ST.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: It was later found that thermocouple 10LBB50CT006 had suffered heat damage and was the cause of the ET200 trip. Once this was disconnected the ET200 reset OK.

TITLE: Black smoke from PKM pipe 24
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Totalis reports black smoke entering the boiler from burner nozzle 24 (photos added). Totalis is carrying out work, immediately next door, on burner 23. Wait went to the scene and also saw the black smoke. It comes out slowly, at the bottom of the boiler, and falls slowly down the wall, some of it rising/diffusing.

Cause is from cutting fire work PKM20 bends. After stopping this work (and partly opening pipework), it can be seen that smoke is still forming from this duct. See photos/video.

Subsequent inspection (photos added) shows that fuel is present in the pipes, this is pulverised coal. The pipe always contains several millimetres of dust, but in many places centimetres thick. The cutting burners give open fire to this fuel + liquid metal on the fuel.

The licence does not mention presence of fuel, working in ATEX zone, and specific measures to mitigate this.
HSE revision spoken to. They will discuss this further within revision team.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Boiler cleared. PKM20 operations halted.
Fire-fighting equipment put on standby on site.
Conducted further inspection and consultation with HSE man this evening: Add to TRA that combustible material is present, ATEX zone active. And discuss what measures are needed. For example, grinding or cutting instead of cutting fire, open section, clean pipe, then cut fire, or use inert gas in ductwork.
This is taken to revision team.

TITLE: PO activities need not be performed because systems are (would be) off.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The contractor who came to perform the legally required monthly maintenance tasks on the fire alarm system was told in the morning that several systems (systems by name) did not need to be performed because they were de-energised. However, this is undesirable for several reasons.

* It is a legal requirement.
* There is a contract with the contractor to have it done.
* The logbook simply has to be filled with facts.

But the contractor could not do anything because there was no voltage present i.e. the overhaul!

The contractor could have simply fulfilled its obligation. Visually inspecting such a fire alarm system, making sure the components present were accessible, possibly cleaning the BMC and last but not least, filling in the logbook that the system was off, possibly due to the overhaul.

Not having the legal task performed unexpectedly bites us in the tail in the future because we will simply have a hole in the logbook and will not be able to prove why we did not perform our legal tasks.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Legal, monitoring and reporting (Non-compliance of obligations)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Told the contractor who came to announce this that we will not allow this and just do his work with what we contracted to do, only if he/she finds that the work cannot be done properly (in accordance with proper law/regulations) under the contract manager wants to hear about it, until then just do the work and record the facts of a BMC in the logbook. The contractor went back a working day later as usual.

Recommendation:
If one does not know what is contractually regulated and legally required, one should inform the subject expertise and jointly make sound decisions.

TITLE: Overheated heater carrier air + dangerous reset
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Due to I/O card failure, discharge valve closed and carrier fan stood by against a closed valve with heater standing by.
There is an air temperature monitor, it was not addressed.
The element monitor 30ETP20AC021/2/3 of the heater was later addressed.
After repair card, the heater's E-casts had to be reset.

The following risks were present and need further discussion:
- Locally, the plant overheated. As a result, melted "plastic" could be seen and a smoke cloud could be seen. Deployment of FAFS was not necessary.
What melted/smoked here and was there a fire hazard? Should element guards intervene earlier.
- The cabinet was mounted horizontally. As a result, there is a lot of fly ash on the cabinet and has to be removed first to prevent VLAS on E-elements. This creates a short-circuit risk and fire hazard
- Performing the reset on the cabinet is not safe to do. An MOC was supposedly written for it 3 years ago which was rejected. What is the status of the MOC / reason for rejection?
- How can we (until there is a MOC solution) perform a safe reset? Now a mechanical reset has to be given with a poorly isolated tool. This is not safe.
- The cabinets are not easily accessible. There is no proper ladder, at least not properly secured, to safely access the cabinets.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Reset was performed with risk.
Installation is back at.

200 metres upstream of the bridge, the river still lies on the right bank and swings

This means that the greater part of the runoff and therefore the current flows through the left-hand bridge span and the river bed scours out below it.

The bridge axis is at 2442.646. This profile is unchanged compared to the last soundings.
This also applies to the following profiles up to approx. 40 metres below the bridge. Here (2442.606), a well 2 metres deep
a 2 m deep, approximately 15 m wide channel towards the underwater.
The profile 50 m downstream of the bridge (2442.596) also shows this scour channel, albeit scoured out by the flood by about 1.5 m in depth and width.
The last profile at 2442.546 is also deepened by approx. 0.5 m by the flood. Here, however, the current line is already in the centre of the river and swings to the right.

The almost vertical left slope of the channel is conspicuous, which was also seen in earlier soundings. This is only plausible under the assumption of a Flinz location on the former left valley slope. However, this is not completely stable against erosion; in profile 2442.596, an erosion of approx.

TITLE: Restriction dewatering pipe serving pipe section between HD turbine quick release valve and HD turbine control valve mechanically barred.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the start-up phase of MPP3 after outage 2024, it was observed that the pressure between HD control valve and HD quick release valve (left --> 30 MAA11) remained pressurised.
Following the observed, order 30004652095 was created and a dewatering valve 30MAL40AA111 was opened for investigation.
 
Due to maintenance and OPS, nothing strange was observed at the dewatering valve taken on site. However, it was observed that ttv of
dismantling v/h pipework, the pipework was still full of condensate while it should have a free run to the vacuum collector. This could possibly
cause due to a possible blocked restriction further up in the pipework.
the pipe according to PID. KKS 30MAL40BP010

After boroscope examination, the restrictor was found to be almost 100% clogged with a piece of metal which significantly reduced the dewatering of the pipe section between the HD quick release valve and and HD control valve.

Later this week, the dewatering pipe will be "cut" as the restriction is welded into the pipework. Only after the trimming/striking through will further specific investigations be possible and perhaps the origin of the metal encountered still be identified.

Failure or a lesser dewatering function could mean that possibly at the first opening of the HD quick release valve and HD control valve ttv a start-up water/condensate goes to the HD turbine !  

Possibly, depends on where this piece of metal comes from / came from this could also have gone through the HD turbine....
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
SAP orders 30004652095 & 30004652510
Later this week, the dewatering pipe will be "cut" as the restriction is welded into the pipework. Only after the cutting/striking through will further specific investigation be possible and perhaps the origin of the metal encountered can still be identified.

TITLE: Main Water Treatment Plant Stream 1 Cation & Anion.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the committed work program for Friday (1st March), there was a request to isolate both the Anion & Cation on Stream 1.  Stream 1 has not been in service for many years and the request was to unbox the vessels and pump out the resin in preparation for decommissioning the stream.  Stream 1 has sat isolated for at least 10 years.  Overnight the keys were retrieved from the CPO's key safe and all the isolation points were checked, and the old E-on caution labels were replaced with Uniper labels.  As the vessels had been isolated for so long, and there is no external indication of level, it was an unknown as to the level within the vessels.  The Anion and Cation drains to the effluent sump were opened, and a flow was heard immediately.  Also the tell tale drains and vents to atmosphere were opened.  I would estimate that the vessels were at least half full prior to starting draining.  As the vessels were draining there was a pungent smell noted,  we remained in the WTP as the vessels drained and continued to apply further isolations to the acid & caustic dilution tanks in preparation for future de-commissioning.  The smell appeared to us to dissipate fairly quickly, so once the vessels were fully drained, the drain valves were locked shut to complete the isolation.  We returned to the Permit office to prepare the PFW.  When passing through the control room there was several comments made about a foul strong smell, and it was quickly realised it was emanating from our skin, overalls and clothing.  I returned to the WTP to assess the odour, and on re-entering the WTP the smell was extremely strong.  But again within a few minutes I became accustomed to the smell. 

Due to the pungency of the odour, I stated (in the further precautions on the PFW) that a selected person should attend the unboxing of the vessels and carry out an atmosphere check prior to starting work.

I understand that prior to the unboxing, discussions between the selected person and duty control person resulted in the PFW being withdrawn until the source of the smell could be identified, and to ascertain if it was in anyway harmful to health.  I was asked to input a Synergy tonight (2nd March).
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Hazardous substance, which is non-toxic, non-CMR substance (carcinogenic, mutagenic, reproduction toxic)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Email was sent to Selected persons asking for assistance prior to unboxing of vessels.
effluent sumps were pumped out and flushed to dilute the effluent.
Selected person took samples of effluent.

Selected person to carry out investigation into the source of the odour.

TITLE: Main Water Treatment Plant Stream 1 Cation & Anion.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the committed work program for Friday (1st March), there was a request to isolate both the Anion & Cation on Stream 1.  Stream 1 has not been in service for many years and the request was to unbox the vessels and pump out the resin in preparation for decommissioning the stream.  Stream 1 has sat isolated for at least 10 years.  Overnight the keys were retrieved from the CPO's key safe and all the isolation points were checked, and the old E-on caution labels were replaced with Uniper labels.  As the vessels had been isolated for so long, and there is no external indication of level, it was an unknown as to the level within the vessels.  The Anion and Cation drains to the effluent sump were opened, and a flow was heard immediately.  Also the tell tale drains and vents to atmosphere were opened.  I would estimate that the vessels were at least half full prior to starting draining.  As the vessels were draining there was a pungent smell noted,  we remained in the WTP as the vessels drained and continued to apply further isolations to the acid & caustic dilution tanks in preparation for future de-commissioning.  The smell appeared to us to dissipate fairly quickly, so once the vessels were fully drained, the drain valves were locked shut to complete the isolation.  We returned to the Permit office to prepare the PFW.  When passing through the control room there was several comments made about a foul strong smell, and it was quickly realised it was emanating from our skin, overalls and clothing.  I returned to the WTP to assess the odour, and on re-entering the WTP the smell was extremely strong.  But again within a few minutes I became accustomed to the smell. 

Due to the pungency of the odour, I stated (in the further precautions on the PFW) that a selected person should attend the unboxing of the vessels and carry out an atmosphere check prior to starting work.

I understand that prior to the unboxing, discussions between the selected person and duty control person resulted in the PFW being withdrawn until the source of the smell could be identified, and to ascertain if it was in anyway harmful to health.  I was asked to input a Synergy tonight (2nd March).
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Hazardous substance, which is non-toxic, non-CMR substance (carcinogenic, mutagenic, reproduction toxic)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Email was sent to Selected persons asking for assistance prior to unboxing of vessels.
effluent sumps were pumped out and flushed to dilute the effluent.
Selected person took samples of effluent.

Selected person to carry out investigation into the source of the odour.

TITLE: Water (with fim layer light oil) spill UHA 16, 0 and -6 mtr (leakage at burner 11)
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At burner 11, the bellows of the blow-through steam valve 30HJR11AA302 is leaking. This is a 3-way valve that separates atomising steam and light oil during burner shutdown by setting the discharge towards the light leakage oil tank.
This is so on all 36 burners.

Now in some burners, the 3-way valve is broken and it allows atomisation steam to pass through to the leak oil system. The leak oil tank cannot withstand high temperature, for this the drain valve from the burners to the leak oil tank is closed. As a result, the leak oil system from the burners condenses full and is under atomising steam pressure of 8 bar.

Because the bellows is leaking from the blow-through steam valve 30HJR11AA302, a considerable amount of water with light oil is coming out (from the leak oil system) from the tell-tale hole. This partly collected in the drip tray but then overflowed onto the floor and then to the 0 metre and basement. There is now a sizeable puddle of water with a film of light oil there. See attachments
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Slip / Trip / Fall (at the same floor level and on stairs)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
- Environment switched off
- Atomiser system depressurised by closing supply valve of auxiliary steam bar 30LBG02AA101
- Leak oil system drained to leak oil tank
- SAP notification made for clearance of spill 300010640262
 An order was already in place for the leaking valve of burner 11 30004641788

Recommendations:
- Asap repair all permeable atomising steam valves.
(Now a valve is occasionally replaced but due to the full condensation of the leaking oil system, water hammer occasionally occurs when starting an oil burner, causing 3-way valves to fail again)

TITLE: There are two containers for collecting old lithium batteries in the mailbox area near the photocopier
CASE_DESCRIPTION: AV building part A-OG area mailboxes near the photocopier: In this area there are two containers for collecting old lithium batteries. Empty batteries and rechargeable batteries in a collection box can also cause fires with considerable consequences. There is also an additional fire load here with the post boxes and the storage location for photocopier paper!
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
-> All types of batteries, i.e. 9 volt block batteries, Li ion batteries, 3A batteries, button cells etc. are collected in a container. Whether the container is closed, open, non-flammable or flammable is secondary. What is primarily important is that the poles do not touch each other and thus the remaining residual voltages are added together. If you now accidentally throw in a few paper clips, which cause short circuits, then it is only a matter of time before smoke appears and a fire breaks out. The solution - as is so often the case in fire protection - consists of various measures that together make sense and promise success: These include masking both poles with an adhesive film, disposing of the old batteries regularly and storing them in a place in the company where a fire can cause rather minor damage (e.g. rubbish room). This should be a room where people are not at risk if a fire does occur. And finally, it is important that everyone in the company is made aware of this requirement and these collection points.

->Only set up a small, non-combustible bin; do not place it in the area of fire loads; fire extinguishers should be placed in the immediate vicinity, have the bin emptied at regular intervals (do not collect batteries that are months old); instruct employees to have the poles taped; do not throw any other (metallic) objects into the collection bin!!!!

Done!

TITLE: Damage to external pipe house connection, Gla-Rentfort Woorthstraße 1
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The partner company's employees were busy excavating a pit for the installation of house connections. Instead of digging the pit manually, they decided to use an excavator.
The excavator operator had the plans from the relevant utility company for the low-pressure gas pipes that had been laid. The actual position of the pipes was slightly different than expected and a T-piece was sticking out of the pipe. When trying to excavate the pit, the excavator damaged the T-piece. There was no gas leak.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Work was stopped immediately and the area was cordoned off for safety reasons. The employees informed their superiors and the latter informed the responsible supplier EVNG. The house connection was replaced with a new fitting.
Uniper was informed of the incident two hours later.

Recommendations for sensitisation:
- Review of the AVO issue
- Approach to pipe location
- Compliance with GB manual excavation near the pipeline
- Instruction of partner company employees/documentation

Subsequently, a German workshop was used to raise awareness. All employees of the partner company, UWG project and construction management and UWG HSSE took part (content: topics listed above).

Furthermore, additional budget was made available for a project SIEKO with 100% FTE provided by UWG. The project SIGEKO commissioned until then only had a 40% FTE assignment and was due to expire at the end of March, as a SIGEKO is only required by law for the BPGH project. The Rentfort project is being carried out by a general contractor and will run until around the end of the year.

TITLE: UCML Chlorine dosing valves Pump1 closed causing no dosing (= were open, there was dosing, but had to be adjusted)
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The fa. H2O Biofouling Solutions does biweekly measurements for Uniper on chlorine bleach leach dosage in all cooling water systems and checks the biomonitors for fouling.
On 30 May, it was found that on the Lyondell side (Pump1, chlorine measurement 60PAD01CQ001), hardly any chlorine was measured. There was very high deposition of biofouling on the coupons (attached photos). On the MPP3 side (pump2, chlorine measurement 60PAD13CQ001), free chlorine was measured, but lower than desired. No deposition of biofouling could be seen on the coupons. Following this, the chlorine dosage was increased to the summer dosage of around 230 l/h.
Because the online chlorine measurements showed almost no reaction to the increase, manual measurements were carried out for control purposes. No free chlorine was measured on the Lyondell side, while free chlorine was measured on the MPP3 side. After investigation, both dosing valves of cooling water pump 1 on the Lyondell side (60PBQ41/42 AA101) proved to be closed. These were then opened, after which free chlorine was measured on the Lyondell side. This was also immediately visible on the online measurement 60PAD01CQ001.
At the last H2O measurement session on 16 May, free chlorine was still measured, so between 16 and 31 May, the valves were closed for a period of time.

Addition Iwan van der Kraats:
Investigation conducted and recorded in SOG report: Conclusion is that the hand valves were in the same operational position as the entire previous month. So they were open and CBL was dosed. Based on information BioFouling adjusted the setting.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: After investigation, both dosing valves of cooling water pump 1 on the Lyondell side were found to be closed (60PBQ41/42 AA101). These were then opened, after which free chlorine was measured on the Lyondell side. This was also immediately visible on the online measurement 60PAD01CQ001.

TITLE: Black smoke from PKM pipe 24
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Totalis reports black smoke entering the boiler from burner nozzle 24 (photos added). Totalis is carrying out work, immediately next door, on burner 23. Wait went to the scene and also saw the black smoke. It comes out slowly, at the bottom of the boiler, and falls slowly down the wall, some of it rising/diffusing.

Subsequent inspection (photos added) shows that fuel is present in the pipes, this is pulverised coal. The pipe always contains several millimetres of dust, but in many places centimetres thick. The cutting burners give open fire to this fuel + liquid metal on the fuel.

The licence does not mention presence of fuel, working in ATEX zone, and specific measures to mitigate this.
HSE revision spoken to. They will discuss this further within revision team.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Boiler cleared. PKM20 operations halted.
Fire-fighting equipment put on standby on site.
Conducted further inspection and consultation with HSE man this evening: Add to TRA that combustible material is present, ATEX zone active. And discuss what measures are needed. For example, grinding or cutting instead of cutting fire, open section, clean pipe, then cut fire, or use inert gas in ductwork.
This is taken to revision team.

TITLE: Product warning for GT V93: Possible component failure of the compressor vane carriers
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
We have received a service bulletin with the following information from Siemens via unofficial channels:

Experience with mature gas turbine frames and engineering evaluations have shown that compressor vane carriers made of GJL-250 (GG25) are at risk of cracking, which could lead to rapid, large-scale component failure. Such a failure could not only cause significant damage to the components, but could also eject high energy debris, posing a potential hazard to personnel, including serious injury or death.

Technical Information
Gas turbines of frame V93.x are equipped with compressor vane carriers 1 and 2 (CVC1 + CVC2) made of EN-GJL-250 (GG-25). Due to the brittle material behaviour of GG-25, there is a possibility of rapid, large-scale component failure driven by low cycle fatigue caused by start/stop cycles and rapid load changes. In the event of such a failure, parts of the stationary compressor vane carriers could come into contact with moving parts of the rotor and cause considerable damage. It cannot be ruled out that debris may be ejected with high energy and pose a potential hazard to personnel, especially in the area of the air intake duct, as the machines are not protected by an additional outer casing in this area.

TITLE: Passing valve fills acid measuring tank - Linked SL # 46684
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 00:47 High and High High level alarms were received on the Sulphuric acid measuring tank.
Pulling up the trend showed that the level had risen gradually from 26% starting at  approx 21:00. 
The air isolation valve for the Suplhuric acid dosing system had been isolated at around this time.
Sited was attended immediately to try to work out what had happened, the acid measuring tank filling valves were checked first.... both valves found to be closed.
When looking around the Acid Measuring tank it was noticed that the tank was very hot and on inspection it was found the the Acid ejector motive water valve fails open when the air is isolated... this should not be a problem as there are other valves that remain closed in the system.
It is suspected that one of the Acid Ejector suction valves 90GCN30AA010 or 90GCN30AA012 is passing allowing motive water to leak back to the Acid measuring tank when the air was isolated and the Motive water valve failed open.
Acid Measuring tank was left boxed.
During the night the tank level started dropping.
On investigation the flanged joint on the lower inspection point was found to be leaking and the stainless inlet pipe at the bottom of the tank was also found to be holed.
All acid that leaked was contained within the bund and associated chemical waste sump.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Hazardous substance, which is non-toxic, non-CMR substance (carcinogenic, mutagenic, reproduction toxic)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Reason for tank filling investigated.
Motive water hand isolator 90GCN30AA013 shut to completely isolate the tank.
Acid dosing skid barriered off.

TITLE: Düsseldorf - T2401 0543 - Fl, A1 lift to bridge crossing - general soiling - Near Miss with SiFa report
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The situation happened on my way out of the elevator on the first floor in Float, so 1B.  I was making my way from the elevators towards the bridge, so i could get to Capricorn, and before reaching the bridge i felt my foot slipping on the floor. I could regain balance and did not fall. But it happened twice (from elevator towards bridge in the morning, and from bridge towards elevator in the afternoon, as i was coming back).
Today i experienced it again (i take the same route every day).

The parket there seems to be used very often and has become slippery.
Knowing that we had a colleague who got hurt in the same area in the past, i believe we need to take this seriously. However, i saw the answer from the facility management team on the Ticket that my assistant raised and they say „there is no problem“. How can this be?
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Slip / Trip / Fall (at the same floor level and on stairs)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Near miss: Report the incident via the IP secretariat / ticket T2401 0543 to Fac. -Mgmt. with request to check the cleaning situation of the floor at the scene of the accident

Request for incident investigation by Anne Miarka REM/FM

Measures SiFa, A. Böhmer:
- Invitation of the IP by email to an on-site meeting
    Unfortunately not feasible in terms of time until the report is prepared (01.02. 15:40h)
- Email with the request for a description of the process --> see above, case description
- eMail with friendly enquiry about the footwear worn

Comment on the IP
- No injuries
- Incident occurred repeatedly in the area in question during further walks at various times. times
- Statement from the IP: Floor is probably slippery due to heavy use, please check

On-site assessment: 01 FEB 2024, 12:30h, Andreas Böhmer, SiFa
- Floor shines in front of the bridge in contrast to the wide passage area due to the concentration of pedestrians at the entrance to the bridge. In the less frequented area, the floor is matt
- Simplified friction coefficient measurements (mobile phone with rubber tape, pulled) did not provide any significant indication of particular slipperiness of the area compared to the overall surface
(despite the gloss of the surface)
- A tripping hazard could not be recognised.
- It was established with the cleaning service provider that the area had undergone basic cleaning and clearly completed resealing in the previous week (Wed to Sat) (statement)
- Dirt and moisture can be ruled out, at least in the overall context, as the weather conditions do not suggest any entry into the building since the basic cleaning. Dry cleaning is carried out daily.
- Spot soiling ("coffee stain" issue) can be ruled out as a cause, as the event occurred at different times according to the IPs.
- The question about the footwear worn could not be answered.

Conclusion: Ultimately, the cause remains unclear. Further investigation is not possible on the basis of the available data.
A.Böhmer, SiFa - REM/FM, 01 FEB 2024

TITLE: Failed Trip Test on control Transmitters of Fuel Gas Heater Stream A
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
While completing fuel gas stream A underperformance investigation and rectification, it was discovered that the fuel gas heater failed to trip when the transmitter is placed in open loop. 

This means that any failure of this nature would not be detected and the control room has no visibility  of the transmitter. Therefore, if the control transmitters (EKC20ZT006 or EKC20ZT008) were to open circuit it would drive the heaters to 100% output!
(The control and trip transmitters utilise the same cabling so have a massive common cause failure).

This could lead to disabling of the protection layer, as the control system drives energy into the heaters.

Perform clearance measurements.

TITLE: Ops Loss - U2 Outlet dust high due to 'C' Precip pass performance.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Following U2 RTS on Tuesday 25th June, the unit had to be MEL'd to 350MW from approx 18:00 to 21:00 to recover the daily dust position.  The MEL was raised to 400MW from approx 21:00.  MEL has remained at 400MW due to 'C' Precip pass being shut away.

The Unit had several milling plant issues on RTS, and the inlet dust to FGD was high, especially on the 'B' side.  The FGD outlet dust (on unit desk back left overview) was however reading ~14mg, which is within daily limits and was not in alarm.  The cause of the high inlet dust was presumed to be combustion led, but the inlet dust remained high despite trying numerous mill configurations.  

It became apparent that the outlet dust reading on the unit back panel was incorrect (still reading ~14mg), and the actual outlet dust (CDAS) reading was 3x higher than displayed on the overview.  The Centre desk was receiving the correct data and the daily average was exceeding the 18mg limit.  On the unit desk Air CEMS screen the Outlet dust was reading 14mg with a magenta box around the reading.  The CDAS outlet dust was reading 30mg+.

C3 Precip zone will not go in service (keeps tripping), and on interrogating the data it became apparent that the C1 & C2 passes were working extremely hard.  The conclusion was that the high 'B' side inlet dust was due to 'C' Precip pass not coping with the dust burden.

The MEL was reduced to 350MW to allow the 'C' Precip inlet damper to be shut.  
As the damper closed the 'B' side dust immediately reduced.  The MEL was later increased to 400MW once the daily dust position was recovered.  The MEL will remain at 400MW due to only 4 Precip passes being I/S.

C Pass has been box rapped several times after the unit came off load.  On the next RTS of Unit 2, C pass should be introduced incrementally and dust burden monitored closely.

Defects have been raised for C3 precip - keeps tripping (21525966), C2 Negative rapping U/S (21525967) & for Unit 2 outlet dust displaying wrong reading on the unit overview panel.  Strangely once the dust burden reduced, the Outlet dust started to read the correct values again and matched the CDAS reading!
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Dust (Inc. complaints, technical breaches or affecting ecosystems)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Load reduced to 350MW
'C' Precip inlet damper closed
Load kept at 350MW until Daily dust position recovered.
MEL increased to 400MW and proven OK with only 4 passes I/S.
'C' Precip pass boxed rapped several times overnight once unit was off load.

Refer C3 tripping issues to Elec team.  
Attempt to re-introduce 'C' pass on next run while monitoring inlet / outlet dust
Investigate Unit desk overview panel dust reading displaying incorrect value and not alerting the Unit operator to the high outlet dust.

TITLE: Unusually high temperatures Wet vapour in the shaft entrance
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During a period of heavy rainfall, the escaping wet vapour is unusually hot at the level of a manhole entrance. Temperatures of up to 72° were measured at the level of the manhole cover. The manhole has to be pumped daily due to the heavy ingress of rainwater. The fitter does not have to enter the shaft for this. However, when pulling out the pump, the fitter stands above the shaft entrance and gets more or less wet vapour in his face depending on the wind conditions. The protective clothing offers appropriate protection. One weak point is the helmet with protective visor. This is primarily intended for protection when drilling. In the body position when pulling out the pump, the visor offers too much downward contact surface for the rising wet vapour.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Inspection by HSSE after notification of unsafe situation by fitter.

Readjustment of the situation and measurement of the wet vapour temperatures.

Additional sensitisation of employees due to the heavy rainfall phase and the associated extremely high effort required to pump out manholes and the danger discussed.

Procurement of better PPE. A more suitable protective visor must be researched, tested and made available.

Note 7.2.24:
Test visors ordered for wear test.

So I didn't get to do any of my outdoor work today.

Attached is the route where I walked and where I was attacked.

TITLE: Sheet piling water basin Neste project thv junction BPT Lyondellhek broken
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Last night around 02:45, it was reported by our outside man UCML ( Peter Unger) that a sheet pile of a water basin Neste project t.h.v. the junction (the road to) BPT and Lyondell had broken through.
The dam wall had broken through in the corner of the basin. See images attached. On google maps image, a red circle indicates the location of the basin.
This would have happened after 01:00 am. Because around 01:00, our colleague was working at the reducers and nothing had happened yet. Peter immediately shovelled the hole closed. After this, there was still +/- 10 cm of water in the basin.
Initial content of the basin is not known. The drained water/mud ran across the road towards BPT/ reducing stations and towards Lyondell fence. Wet tracks within the deposit along the sheet piling are also visible.
In consultation with Marty (calamity watch), an SL report was made. No further reports to competent authority. We also do not know exactly what kind of water has been in the basin. The basins where polluted water is stored are fitted with a special foil. This basin does not. According to Marty, this could be a clean water basin.
Like to pick up and discuss things with the project during day shift hours.

Update Marty 4-10-2024 13:00: It appears to be an infiltration basin with clean water. The analysis shows that the total PFOS concentration of this water is 17 ng/l so far below the 60 ng/l as required by the DCMR.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Water (Inc. excess volume, lack of, uncontrolled release or excess use)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The hole in the dam closed.
Calamity manager M vd lock informed....

14-01-2025 FO: The slope has now been supplemented and reinforced, no further followup needed in Synergi.

Got the comment here again (this gave me the impression that I was not the first but well, hearing that you would think that everything should be in order here).
Asked him how the preparation for this job had gone and whether there had been a start/work meeting before the job and whether the risks had been explained to each other.
He replied to me that this had happened, to which I asked him how this had gone and whether this was also recorded (which was discussed verbally)
The work permit was complete and the necessary documents had been signed off including the handover.

Tip:
That I gave him is to write out the start/work discussion to discuss and have the attendee sign off as being a Toolbox and add this behind the work permit.
This gives an insight (to the inspector) into how this work has been prepared and you can draw attention here in advance to using the right PPE/equipment to complete the job properly and safely.


Addressed the keeper on the above observations and received as feedback
- Safety goggles taken off because the lenses were fogged up and he forgot to put them back on (he did put them on when he saw me coming)
- Special cutting gloves were not worn because the person peeling did not have a good feeling when peeling and had a lot of experience with cutting (They were ready at work).
- When I asked why the work area was not cordoned off, the answer I got was that there was no hoisting, even though there were cordon signs and the crane engine was running.

Discussed with the holder:
- The risks of not wearing the safety glasses and pointed out the dangers there were within his working area
- The risks of peeling the tyre without using the appropriate cutting glove and pointed out to him that cutting with knives is a common accident.
- Road closures immediately put in place on site.

I also inquired about the crane's certification and reviewed the crane book:
- Talked to crane operator about his start work measurement whether he had had it, he told me that work had been discussed with him before starting job
- Asked whether the crane book had been checked by security on arrival
- Checked certifications and inspections
All this appeared to be in good order.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
- Barrier was put in place immediately after finding it missing
- Safety glasses were immediately put back on
-Cutting gloves were to be used
- preparatory tips discussed on site

TITLE: Excavation works
CASE_DESCRIPTION: An excavation was being completed to expose electrical cables as part of the decommissioning works. On inspection there were aspects of the excavation which could be improved such as the access into the excavation and the angle of response for the battering and stepping.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Work was stopped and a review was completed and an action plan implemented to allow the works to proceed.

Response to Excavation Inspection Findings:

During the excavation to expose electrical cables as part of the decommissioning works, several areas for improvement were identified, specifically regarding access into the excavation and the angle of response for the battering and stepping.

Access to the Excavation:
Safe access and egress from an excavation are critical for worker safety. The current access should be assessed to ensure compliance with safety regulations. 

Recommendations include:
Installing proper ladders or steps to provide stable and safe access points.
Ensuring that the access route is free from obstructions and is clearly marked.
Evaluating whether the current access meets the required slope and angle guidelines to prevent slips, trips, or falls.

Angle of Response for Battering and Stepping:
The angle of the batter (slope) should be reviewed to ensure that it is adequate to prevent soil collapse. If the excavation is too steep, it increases the risk of collapse and makes it more difficult for workers to move around safely. Suggestions include:

Adjusting the slope to meet the recommended safety angles based on the soil type, depth, and stability.

Implementing proper benching and stepping techniques to reduce the risk of soil failure.

Regularly inspecting the slope to account for any changes in ground conditions during the excavation process.

Recommendations include:
Risk Assessment: A thorough risk assessment should be conducted to identify and mitigate any additional hazards associated with the excavation, ensuring compliance with all relevant regulations and best practices.

Training: Ensure all personnel working in and around the excavation have received the necessary training on excavation safety, including proper access methods and the importance of maintaining correct angles for the battering and stepping.

By addressing these points, the excavation process can be made safer, reducing the risk of injury and ensuring a compliant work environment.

TITLE: Unit 6 Steam Turbine High Vibrations on Run-Up.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
From Enerlytics alert dated 22/03/2023 @ 14:38
During routine OLVMS monitoring, UTG noticed higher than normal levels of vibration along the ST shaft line during the run up on 16th March. The highest levels were seen on the IP/LP Eccentricities where levels peaked at 290 um pk-pk with the unit at 842 rpm, during a normal run up a typical amplitude at this speed would be 25-50 um pk-pk. The change in vibration was 1/rev driven suggesting the unit had run up with a temporary bend.

A review of the barring file prior to this run up shows that the turbine remained stationary for approximately 1 hour following the previous run down on the evening of 15th March. The barring file shows the rotor straightening across the barring period, however the elevated vibration levels had not fully subsided before the start of the run up. If the unit was had remained on barring for a few more hours the rotor may had been able to fully straighten prior to starting.

Once the machine reached full speed and was loaded up, the vibration levels subsided as the machine straighten. Subsequent run ups and run downs have passed by without incident, comparing well to previous and giving no cause for concern.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Investigate the reasons for the turning gear not engaging at the correct time.

TITLE: Increased VL temperature STEAG delivery
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Between 0:15 and approx. 3:00, the VL temperature rises sharply to approx. 140 °C to just below the temperature cut-out. In the past, a lowering of the first temperature limit was actually agreed
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Consultation with STEAG: At min. load, it became apparent that the VL temperature was not being maintained during operation. Cause: There is a minimum quantity of primary heating water, which was matched to the minimum quantity characteristic curve of the primary pumps. The reason for this is that there was no minimum flow rate line for the primary pumps before the last conversion.
 
As this min-quantity line now exists, the primary heating water was reduced to 40 kg/s for this min-quantity; the remaining quantity now goes via the min-quantity line in order to remain in the pump characteristic curve.
 
This enabled the desired Uniper flow temperature to be set.
 
There is currently still a fluctuation of +- 3K in the flow; three controls are now in use here (pump speed, pressure maintenance point pump, minimum flow rate pump), which may need to be adjusted.

A process update has been installed. The analyses are in progress.

Note 08.03.2023: Optimisation is underway as part of IBN Herne 6. Fundamental change cannot be implemented due to timely closure of Herne 4.

TITLE: Environmental incident: Complaint about dark exhaust plume auxiliary boiler
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Environmental event
Description: The Heyden power plant is currently operating at full capacity (420 MW).
There was a technical fault at a flow meter (burner 21) on the auxiliary boiler.
The auxiliary boiler is important for the start-up and shut-down process of the power plant.
The power operation of unit 04 provided a time window for trial operation of the auxiliary boiler.

10:00 a.m. After repair work on the flow meter on burner 21 (auxiliary boiler), a trial run was carried out at around 10:00 a.m.. This showed that the fuel/air mixing ratio was still faulty.
The trial operation lasted a maximum of 2 minutes.

Situation: The altered mixing ratio resulted in soot formation in the flue gas flow of the auxiliary boiler, which was visible outside. Trial operation was cancelled immediately.

10:15 A concerned citizen complained about the dark exhaust gas flow.
The concerned citizen was informed of the situation by telephone by the shift supervisor.
10:30 The police went to the site to find out what had happened.  
The power plant management was informed.
The police were put through to the shift supervisor by telephone and informed of the facts in a telephone conversation with the shift supervisor. This did not result in any further action by the police.

11:00 Consultation with production: The telephone calls with the concerned citizen and the police were conducted in a calm and objective manner.
Maintenance: Limit values (half-hourly averages) were not exceeded
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Dust (Inc. complaints, technical breaches or affecting ecosystems)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The trial operation was cancelled immediately.

TITLE: Service provider's workshop lorry drives into stream collector
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the outward journey on a dirt track at Moos 103, the employee drove off the road in the service vehicle without any other occupants due to the softened verge and the distraction of a telephone call. Visibility was limited due to the rain. As can be seen in the pictures, the vehicle overturned into the stream collector running parallel to the Isar Canal and the Birkenhof pond estate. The employee was able to leave the vehicle unharmed through the window of the driver's door after unfastening his seatbelt.
The employee stated that he was able to switch off the engine immediately and that no oil, diesel or other substances escaped from the vehicle. The doors and windows - with the exception of the upward-facing driver's window, which was used to exit the vehicle - were locked.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Wurzer Umwelt GmbH and Werkstatt GmbH immediately installed oil barriers (see appendix) to prevent the possible spread of contamination. Two walking excavators, a crane and two cable winches were used to recover the vehicle. The employees on site were instructed to constantly monitor possible fluid leaks during the recovery operation and to report them immediately if they were spotted - however, no fluids or other environmentally harmful substances escaped at any time.

TITLE: Oil pollution in the BAA
CASE_DESCRIPTION: In the course of emptying and cleaning the CCS plant, washing liquid containing NaOH had to be transported to the industrial wastewater treatment plant (BAA). A Buchen vacuum truck was used for this purpose. The vacuum truck had previously been used in the area of the HER tank (HER = heating oil substitute fuel). Obviously there were still traces of HER in the vacuum truck (approx. 0.5 litres), but this was only noticed after draining into the sump of the BAA (odour and oil leaches on the surface of the water in the BAA). No water contaminated with oil was released into the environment. The BAA is only emptied into the Jade after the water quality has been checked.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
All circulation pumps have been taken out of operation so that the water in the basins can calm down and the oil can settle at the top. It is collected there with oil cloths.
The remaining water is closely analysed for oil content and only released if it falls below the limit values.
Batches that are above the limit value are disposed of properly.
Once the tanks have been emptied, they are cleaned before being put back into operation.

TITLE: Excavation above 33kV feeders
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Came across an unsupervised and unauthorised excavation carried out above our 33kV feeders, just as it was finishing (on public property by third party organisation).

The contractors read our marker posts around October time last year and using number on marker posts called the control room, they provided Engineering Manager's number and someone from their organisation contacted them.
A SAP was sent down to meet them and they described to them their plans. Our SAP instructed them to contact Engineering Manager with details on what they intended to do near our feeders and when.

They sent an email, but with what appears to have unfortunately been to the wrong email address. Therefore it was never identified by any Uniper personnel, so they never received a reply.

It appears that they took that as a green light to carry on with the work with no input from Uniper.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Discussions are ongoing with the contractor and their client as to how this occurred.

From initial discussions appears that the contractor followed safe working practices, but don't know at this stage if these align to Uniper standards.

There was no risk to Uniper personnel. The risk was to third party workers and also causing loss of power to site.

The process is we would issue a safety document for any work over or close to our feeders, which would include Uniper supervision. This did not happen in this instance.

Despite repeated efforts to contact contractor they have not responded. Action to be send letter via legal.

TITLE: WTP Effluent Tank Leak in to Bund.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Shift team received a radio message from Kaefer at approx. 15:00 11/10/21 reporting a very high level in WTP Effluent Tanks bund. Shift team immediately investigated and confirmed high level. No evidence to suggest the leak had breached the bund and no evidence of any release to ground. Effluent systems made unavailable and pumps electrically isolated. Area was then barriered off to restrict access. Potential leak source from flanged joint on 09SDATK080 identified, tank level  below level this joint at time of issue and leakage had stopped . Contents of bund sampled and were approx. 11pH. 09SXSUV001 and 002 closed as a precaution. Shift Team called Veolia Emergency response to arrange for tanker to empty bund contents. Shift team continuously monitored bund level using CCR cameras and carried out regular inspections of location to ensure no increase in level or leakage from bund until Ancorra attended site 10:30 12/10/21 to empty bund contents. Bund emptied of contents by 14:00 12/10/21.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Hazardous substance, which is non-toxic, non-CMR substance (carcinogenic, mutagenic, reproduction toxic)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Actions Taken:
- Effluent System isolated to ensure no further leakage in to bund.
- Area barriered off to restrict access to persons and continuously monitored.
- 09SXSUV001 and UV002 (Site road drains) shut as a precaution.
- Emergency response contractor contacted to arrange for tanker to remove contents.
Recommended Further actions:
- Investigate, confirm and understand failure mechanism that has allowed effluent to leak in to bund and mitigate. 
- Maintain continuous monitoring of area until failure understood.
- Review Veolia contract and expected performance as other contractor had to provide tanker.
- Provide high level alarm for Effluent bund.

TITLE: Testing of HV cables associated with SC10 SFC
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The tests were conducted by ICS who had installed, glanded & terminated the cables on behalf of EMI.

The agreed test was a VLF test for 15 minutes at 19kV RMS (27kV peak) on three conductors simultaneously.

People present:-

Uniper – Dave Rowlands (SFT)
Siemens – Louis Bucholsky
ICS – Graham Sloan (Test Engineer)
ICS – John More

Sequence of events:-

•	C/O Panel – Fuse Panel & C/O Panel – SFC Panel cables tested successfully
•	SFC Transformer - SFC Panel (10CJN91) cables (9 off) confirmed disconnected both ends
•	Continuity test of all 9 cables completed
•	Transformer cable ends all well clear 
•	U1 cable ends (3 off) in SFC panel connected together and insulated boots positioned between cable lugs and busbar
•	V1 cable ends (3 off) in SFC panel connected together and to earth and booted
•	W1 cable ends (3 off) in SFC panel connected together and to earth
•	1kV DC insulation resistance test conducted successfully on U1 cables 
•	19kV VLF test started on U1 cables
•	Flashover was heard 2 maybe 3 times in quick succession before the test was terminated. It is assumed the flashover occurred between one of the U1 cable ends and the U1 busbar.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Following an inspection and review it was determined the root cause, was ICS didn’t place sufficient temporary insulation round the cable ends. 

To avoid any further issues the subsequent tests were conducted successfully from the transformer with SFC end booted & shrouded and SFC busbars earthed.

The plant was inspected to prove there was no plant oil leaks.  Any fugitive oil must have already been in the oil heater bunds / house.

TITLE: PSO - U3 HP Shaft Position Indication Found Reading Off Scale
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The EC&I team were Investigating an oil leak on U3 HP Shaft position Differential Expansion probe.  It is standard practice to look at the current reading and note any standing alarms before any work is done.  The module was reading -1.25mm hard off scale.  There were no plant alarms standing.  Trending the value on the Ovation DCS revealed that the HP Shaft position had been reading off scale since 22/10/2021, just over 1 year.  Since this date, the generating unit has run many times with no accurate visibility of the turbine shaft position.  It was found that the alarms were not enabled in the measurement module.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The HP shaft position recalibrated and returned to service.
Module alarms have been re-instated.

TITLE: GRU 30 incomplete combustion event and reboiler low pressure trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the 28th February noticed puffs of black smoke being emitted from GRU 30 stack, not long after the Rich TEG feed had been introduced and on the following day the unit tripped on low reboiler pressure, again as the Rich TEG feed was being established.

The PI trend for the low pressure trip on the 1st March follows a very similar pattern to the trips observed in February & March 2020 and at the time wetter than normal Rich TEG was put forward as a possible explanation for a large spike in the reboiler pressure. However, the upstream GDU moisture analyser EKC10CQ001 wasn’t operating at the time which made this quite speculative.

One possible explanation for this could be the residual wetter than normal TEG held up in the contactors (approximately 14 m3) which would be transferred to the Rich Buffer tank in the subsequent withdrawals during which time it would be made partially drier by the incoming TEG although this would still have quite a high moisture content.

While the wet TEG theory remains far from conclusive it now has more credibility and GRU 30 was operated on the 2nd March with a Rich TEG feed which probably contained a more normal moisture content and no operating issues were observed.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Synergi 9408 from 30th March 2020 was last time we saw a similar trip. At the time there was one main theory that the trip was caused by high moisture levels in the gas. The plant was currently being operated in dual feed mode when moisture levels are high to double amount of glycol and therefore reduce moisture content of the gas. Since operating like this there had been no reoccurrences of the trip. 

Believed that the best course of action is to revert to dual feed mode on the contactors if the water content of the gas leaving the caverns increases significantly above the norm.

TITLE: Pressure increase in eastern network during pump switchover Herne4
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Switching the secondary pumps from the small to the large pump in Herne4 or RZR.
- The heat supply from RZR was too low for the consumer situation
- HWS switches to load case 4 (island operation, F-pumps RE go into operation)
- At this moment, the FH network is supplied by the RZR pumps and the HWS-RE-FH pumps.
- The HWS pumps switch off or on depending on the supply.
- The pressure in the FH system (RE) rises.
- The pressure protection for the FH network Wanne and Datteln takes effect.
- The process engineering path is blocked, the pressure in the UAS system cannot be reduced.
- Only when the UAS pressure is lowered can the normal UAS supply take place.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
2 proposed solutions are being examined by Da4:
a. The Herne 4 pumps should have a pressure limitation at the moment of activation.
b. Reprogramming of HW Shamrock to prevent pressure blocking

TITLE: Furnace Trip due to Naphtha KOD tank overfilled.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
First Incident:  4/12/2021
CPU 1 was undergoing start up after SW 30 shutdown. Almost at the end of start-up activity the following happened:
1. At 0110hrs received Furnace Non Urgent Alarm in DCS.
2. On checking at furnace BMS panel by operator, found Naphtha KOD level was around 10% and continuously dropping, but instead of appearing LAL-1711 and LALL-1711, the displayed alarm was LAH-1711 and LAHH-1711.
3. Furnace firing was stopped immediately from DCS and Field Operator (FO) was rushed to field to check for any leak.
4. Checked physically at site and found the naphtha KOD was full.
Action Taken
1. Vessel drained and reduced the level to reset LAH-1711 and LAHH-1711
2. Drained LIT-1711 and LIT-1713 LP and HP impulse lines
3. Reset the alarm in BMS panel and restarted the furnace
4. Observed the KOD vessel level control cut-in and cut-off working well.
Second Incident: 4/12/2021
1. At 1615 hrs Non urgent alarm appeared on SCADA.
2. 1615 hrs checked in Furnace PLC for alarm details, it was showing LAL-1711 (13 %) and continued going down trend.
3. At that point of time Naphtha flow to furnace was 1.2 TPH and P-004 to KOD was 1.9 TPH (KOD level control XV open and close function was ok throughout shift).
4. KOD level continue decreasing, informed FO to increased flow to KOD to prevent furnace Naphtha pump tripping on LAL-1711. (16:19 to 16:21 hrs).
5. At 1621 hrs LALL-1711 appear in PLC and furnace Naphtha pump got tripped on LL but furnace not tripped and continue firing with 250Kg/hr flow rate.
6. Furnace temperature continued to go down, so unit kept on long circulation at 1630 hrs and later kept on short circulation.
7. Informed FO to check KOD physically, FO found KOD was over filled.
8. Stop Naphtha feeding to KOD by closing XV-322.
9. KOD emptied out.
Similar third and fourth incident happened on 6/12/2021 at 0145 hrs and on 14/12/2021 at 1152 hrs respectively
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
1. Vessel drained and reduced the level to reset LAH-1711 and LAHH-1711
2. Drained LIT-1711 and LIT-1713 LP and HP impulse lines
3. Reset the alarm in BMS panel and restarted the furnace
4. Observed the KOD vessel level control cut-in and cut-off working well.

TITLE: U1 Return to service from Outage - Spray pump hand isolating valves found in incorrect position.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the morning of the return of U1 from main outage, it was noted that superheat spray flow was not sufficient as load increased.  The duty AUO was despatched to investigate the issue, helped by the commissioning lead operator.  They found the spray pump hand isolating valves in the closed position.  The valves could not have been 100% closed as there was sufficient flow to achieve ~5kg/sec of flow at the sprays.

These valves are very large hand isolating valves that are not routinely operated (2 man job to open / close) and are not part of any outage isolations as they are left available for maintenance during the outage.  

The work lists from the PFW's show that the valves were worked on during the outage, and we suspect they were operated by the maintenance team to prove operation following maintenance, and hence left in the closed position.

The valves should have been picked up as closed during the initial commissioning phase, and then again on the pre start checks prior to RTS of the pump.

This is the first Main outage RTS since the change to the outage procedure of filling the DA with FFA and forward filling of the feed system with the SSFP's.  With the introduction of the new boiler filling dosing skid, it means we no longer carry out the above step.  Instead we hold the feed water at the HP heater outlets and then fill the boiler using the filling pump with pre dosed water.  Then during the boiler Hydraulic, we back fill the steam circuits through the spray bypass line.  This meant that during our commissioning phase the Spray pump system got missed and highlighted a gap in the new procedure.

The pre start checks were carried out by the duty AUO.  On interviewing the AUO he stated that he had carried out a pre-start check, but only checked the electric valves as per usual for a normal return from a 2-shift.  This was a relatively inexperienced AUO who had never seen the hand isolators operated before.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Valves returned to normal working position to provide sufficient spray flows.
The new outage filling procedure has been updated to include back filling & priming of the spray system to re-capture the entire spray system.
Inexperienced AUO has been briefed on the extra checks required when returning a unit from outage compared to a normal 2 shift.
Outage return to service checklist will be updated to include visual checks on any hand isolators that have been worked on during the outage period.  This will be based on the returned WAL's (Work Attachment Lists), and valve lists provided by the teams.
Maintenance teams to record (on the WAL's) the position hand isolators are left in following overhaul.

TITLE: Bl.2 GT emergency oil pump started up independently.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
From the shift report:

Malfunctions at 18:05.
The GT emergency oil pump was armed and off. It switched on automatically (T3000). An attempt was made to switch off the emergency oil pump.
When switched off, the emergency oil pump switched on again.
As a result, the turbine oil tank was lowered by approx. 6.8 %. The turbine oil is in the nacelle GT -2m (run down).
I was unable to get the emergency oil pump to stop using simulations.
Had to switch off the DC emergency oil pump at the plug-in unit and switch it off.

Mr Stark places empty oil drums (0 m GT room). Approx. 1100 litres of oil have leaked out. Night shift please pump out oil - 2 m into the oil drums. Drum pump is in the control room.
Bearing relief pump still gets enough oil to make the remaining
adjustment by Sulzer.
Hot work licence for the AA 76056131 VG 010 has been withdrawn.
No welding work may be carried out on the GT. Only after
 consultation with Mr Stark. STM 50147274 created due to frequent switching cycles (emergency oil pump GT 0351 02QC10D021-M01-EMO).
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
T3000 simulations were unsuccessful. Had to switch off the plug-in unit on site.
Recommendation:
Check the motor and slide-in unit due to the high switching backlash
Visually indicate to T3000 that the switching command comes from the fuse section.
Discuss the situation with the shift supervisors.

TITLE: Contractor found vaping @ 19m level of HRSG unit 3.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Statement from shift TL:
On arriving via Unit 4’s DA’s approach I noted one member of the scaffold team Vaping; I made note of him by sight and confirmed him by noting a sweet vape type smell on his breath during a brief chat with him; other’s in the team had minor PPE infringements, so  I decided to stop the job and speak to them all outside the boiler house where hearing protection isn’t mandatory. I confirmed that everybody had signed on the GSAF and reminded everyone of their obligations upon signing on. I went through the aspects of wearing the appropriate PPE and adhering to the mandatory standards.
I then challenged the individual who had been vaping and I had witnessed doing so. He denied the fact he been vaping at the 19 Metre level and was he hadn’t been contravening our site rules. 

With the CP, we agreed that the best thing was that the team should go back to the amenities as it was clear that the discussion wasn’t being open and honest. (19:40)

After discussions and many ample times for the individual to admit his breaking of site rules, I was left in a position whereby I could not trust him to work within the guidance and standards we set for ‘smoking and vaping’ in the designated areas safely on the site and additionally to the terms of  the GSAF. He became very agitated and confused, back tracking on his sequence of events.
With this in mind I requested that he should leave site for tonight, because not only did he chose to break our rules, but he had become confrontational to Kev and me during our discussions.
At 20:16 he left site and returned his fob to the gatehouse pending a discussion / investigation through Kaefer and CQ.

TITLE: H2 leakage at generator exciter unit 2
CASE_DESCRIPTION: As part of a pre-outage inspection on the generator and generator exciter unit 2, a hydrogen concentration at the level of the LEL was measured at the shaft opening of the generator exciter diode housing. This was caused by a hydrogen leak in the generator filled with H2, which had spread from the generator via the hollow shaft and coupling bushing to the diode contacts in the diode housing via several defective sealing elements. The hydrogen was able to mix with atmospheric oxygen in the diode housing and form an explosive mixture. The electrical components of the excitation diode are not designed for explosion protection.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Forced ventilation of the noise protection enclosure Generator exciter
Dismantling the noise protection enclosure
Logging off the power station unit
Flushing the generator with inert gas

TITLE: Poor electrical installation
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During commissioning work for the Ambient Air Injection project, the drawings supplied by Schneider for the two new HMC1172 6.6kV VCB control panels were found to be roughly 75% accurate. There was also a suspicion that the motor heaters were remaining live, despite the fuses being pulled from the circuit. Work was put together, to validate the drawings and produce an as built drawing. During this work, it was found that the outgoing heater connections for both the new 6.6kV motors had been linked together, and then fed from the next closest HMC panel with motor heater connections. This meant that, if any of the three panels heater fuses were in place, all three motor heater circuits would be live.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Link cables were removed from all three outgoing heater connections. Heater circuits for each panel were proved for correct operation.

TITLE: Activation of GPP EDP system
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Routine preventative maintenance on Motor Control Centers in the Holford LV Switch Room caused an unexpected coms error in the installation's Safety Instrumented System (SIS).  Upon detection of the coms error (and in line with its design), the SIS automatically activated a controlled de-pressurization of the Gas Processing Plant through the site vent stack.  Following identification of the cause of the coms error, the de-pressurization process was aborted within approximately five minutes. The vent stack is designed and located to ensure the safety of all personnel during venting.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
- The site team followed our existing emergency response procedures - ensuring that key parties were informed and actions and decisions were logged.
- The site team attempted to replicate the faults through a repeat of the preventative maintenance work completed prior to the coms issue.  The coms issue could not be replicated.
- There were no standing SIS faults on the Alarm log 
- The GPP process was assessed for areas of potential risk in returning to service. The 
majority of the plant did not see large pressure swings with the exception of the 
compressors whose pressure reduced to 0.5barg. 
- The installation was balanced and re-pressurized in a controlled manner, using agreed methods.
- MCC inspections were put on hold pending further investigation of the root cause
- While the root cause of  the coms issue had not been completely understood, the plant was considered safe for RTS based on the work above, the low likelihood of reoccurrence and the knowledge that the installation would fail safe as designed.
- Full investigation of the incident will follow

TITLE: Lambda DFB2 has been < 1 several times.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
When the biopropane composition changes (or the Wobbe measurement fails), the lambda of DFB2 may drop below 1 (underoichimetric). The boiler protection system does not detect this and should already trip the boiler at a lambda <1.05.
There is then unburned hydrogen gas in the boiler.
Boiler engineers have experience that a "thud" can be caught with natural gas and the energy dissipated through the chimney.
Hydrogen gas is much more explosive and has a more powerful shock wave. How the boiler can absorb that is unprecedented.

This occurred on 18 June 2020 where an SOG report was prepared and an investigation team was set up.
More recently, this occurred on 20 April 2023 and 3 June 2023. An SOG of both was prepared. After 3 June, the biopropane composition was changed twice more, which was met manually by the WTK.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: On Friday 21 June 2023, the measure was promulgated to stop entering the boiler (for inspection rounds) and no work at DFB2.

TITLE: Review management of work system between Ops and Engineering and between the 5 Ops Shift Teams, with the aim of achieving consistency across the shift teams when assessing MO's and preparation of documents. In addition, investigate how to achieve a consistent standard of MO presented by engineering before placing on the weekly plan.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The following is an example of detail found on an MO and is an example that should never be allowed to happen: -

"While going through the plan today I noticed the above MO number already had a SAP decision on it, looking in enhancement it also had a Permit assigned to it – 2020/00406. 

As it looked like an older number I checked nisoft and this permit was “Not Issued” on 15/05/2020. 

I am concerned that we have received a MO on the plan that already has a safety decision applied along with a permit that is not ‘live’. I think the possibility of being able to re-using old MO’s needs investigating. I thought this was not possible. If it is then this has potentially serious consequences.

In this case the system has stopped any potential accidents as the MO could not be used with a cancelled/not issued document, however, If the original safety decision was at lower level such as a FWI and that MO was regurgitated but the plant/apparatus condition has since changed (therefore requiring precautions) it could prove to be more serious. As SAP’s we do not and can not check through every SAP decision that has already been made, some don’t even see this as they use GWOZ and only look at MO’s on the plan that are set to SRDR."

Questions I feel need answering are:
1. Who is capturing the volume of gaps in the standard of MO as there is no log book or day SAP in position.
2. What was captured in previous audits, regarding SAP MO's and documents, were any actions identified and carried out?
3. Discussion surrounding who and when a Safety Decision should be made to a MO and when is it suitable to place a document in 'mod' is being held across members of the Ops Team - should there be clarity from the management team so there is consistency?

TITLE: PSNH - U1 C16 Oil Burner hose leak
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
@ Approx 07:30 Sunday morning 04/12/22, a fuel oil leak was discovered on Unit 1 Burner Front.  The source of the leak was C16 oil burner inlet hose which had developed a leak.  The leak appears to be at the rear of the hose where it was touching the steel work.   The spray from the Leak was localised to C16 / C17 burner, but the excess has tracked down the pipework and steel work to the boiler basement.

It is unclear at what time the leak developed, but was not identified by the end of Saturday Day shift when the burner front was checked at approx 15:00hrs. 
The fuel oil had ran down the lower levels of the burner front, into the snake pit and Into the boiler basement adjacent 'C' pa fan.   As soon as the leak was discovered, the drain between 'C' PA fan and the ash hopper was plugged, and dresser dry applied to the immediate area.  Dresser dry was then applied to the higher levels where ever the oil had pooled.  Air heater wash sump, ash fines pits and ash crusher pits have showed no signs of oil as of 09:30 04/12/22.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Dresser dry applied to all pooled areas, and drain blocked off.
Services contacted to arrange clean-up crew to attend site.
Unit firing delayed until clean up completed and assessment can be made of lagging requirements.
Prior to firing unit, fire-fighting equipment to be set up and regular fire watch to be organised.

TITLE: Earth fault during commissioning Low-voltage main distribution of the gas pressure reducing station
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Together with a partner, Uniper has installed a CHP plant for an external customer. Recently, a damage pattern (traces of smoke on the slide-in unit) was noticed, which is apparently due to commissioning activities in September 2022.
The corresponding investigations have shown that effective technical measures did not jeopardise the safety of employees or the system at any time.
Nevertheless, such a procedure should be avoided at all costs and a repetition should be ruled out.

During the initial commissioning of the on-site gas pressure reducing station in September 2022, a short circuit was generated during measurements by the customer with a ZIP measuring device, which immediately tripped the compact circuit breaker in the feeding point 70BHA03.H01. When it was switched on again, the circuit-breaker could no longer be switched mechanically. As a result, the identical withdrawable unit from the reserve bay 70BHA06.H01 was used and the gas station was put into operation in order to ensure the availability and operation of the entire system.
The low-voltage switchgear 70BHA supplied by Janssen is of withdrawable design. The moulded-case circuit-breaker was removed from the withdrawable unit and sent to the manufacturer Siemens for damage assessment.
The slide-in module 70BHA03.H01 was inserted into the spare shaft 70HA06.H01 without circuit-breaker and pushed in until it was mechanically locked. The front door was closed and the connection to the busbar was established using a hand crank. As the moulded-case circuit-breaker had been removed and the internal connecting cable ends (cable lugs) of the withdrawable module for connecting the circuit-breaker were uninsulated in the withdrawable module, an earth fault occurred when the withdrawable module was retracted.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The NSHV is a type-tested switchgear. As the earth fault occurred within the closed enclosure of the system and did not leave the withdrawable unit/switchgear, there was no risk to employees at any time.

In order to put the system in a safe condition, the withdrawable unit was covered with a rubber mat and the contacts of the internal connecting cables were insulated accordingly. This prevented the system from being retracted again.

The following measures were taken to prevent such errors in the future:

Instruction of qualified electricians
Qualified electricians must familiarise themselves with the functionality of the switchgear and, in particular, know and take into account specific features.

It must be prevented that non-operational plug-in units are installed in switchgear panels; non-operational plug-in units must be clearly labelled as "Attention not ready for operation".

Only complete units may be inserted into the withdrawable units.
If a withdrawable module is removed for repair purposes in the future, this opening must be closed with a withdrawable module cover.
