TITLE: PSNH  - U3 re-heater Intercept valve tripping leading to r/htr safety valve 166 to lift.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On unit 3 run-up A1 Re-heater Intercept valve tripped and went undetected. The unit was synchronised and proceeded to load up, at approx. 440MW Hot Re-heater safety valve 166 lifted as a result of the intercept valve being tripped. Although the HP exhaust pressure was only 40 bar, indicating the safety valve had lifted “light” (there are also 4 other R/htr safety valves passing on this unit).
The unit load was reduced to 230MW initially thus reducing R/htr pressure and enable a gag to be installed, unsuccessful the load had to be reduced further to 20MW allowing successful fitting of the gag. Unit load was then returned back to full capacity. 
The problem of the tripping intercept valves on fast (5 minute) run-ups has been highlighted several times in the past and a previous OIT raised. Also, the turbine valve tripping isn’t highlighted significantly enough, meaning operators can miss this crucial problem.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Unit load reduction to reduce r/htr pressure which allowed a gag to be fitted.
A plant SIM as been introduced from 19/01/2021 to "soften" to change over of turbine valves from ESV to governor thus preventing the tripping of the intercept valves. 

All turbine valve mal-function alarms should be transferred to the emergency alarm system on the unit.

All hot & cold r/htr safety valves should be inspected due to the amount that are passing on this unit and 166 lifting at a lower pressure.

TITLE: Maxum Hazardous Area Classification Pressurization / Purge
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Purge system on the analyser- the pressure gauge on the front of the analyser Purge air has always read “0”- confirmed by site documentation dating back to 2011. 

The Hazardous area code on the analyser contains a  “p” for pressurisation.

The Purge air regulator is connected directly into a monitoring system inside the analyser electronics enclosure ( this system is currently disabled) 

The analyser is installed in a zone 2 area. 

So the equipment has been operating in a zone 2 area without the protection system operational.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The idea of the purge monitoring system is to maintain a positive pressure differential inside the electrical enclosure as it is full of uncertified electrical equipment, such as valves, power supplies etc. 

The protection concept for this appears to be “p” (pressurisation)  and is stated in the Siemens manual as being a requirement if the analyser is installed in a zone 1 or zone 2 area. (it is in a zone 2) 

The regulator has been set at 5 psi for now, for the short term until we can commission the protection system, (if it is found that this should be enabled).

TITLE: Cable damage during excavation work
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Several underground cables were damaged in the area south of the decarbonisation plant during civil engineering work as part of the construction of the 220 kV cable route. In addition to control and telecommunications cables, a medium-voltage cable was also damaged. The damage was caused by an excavator.

The construction site is the responsibility of the new construction project. The AvO informed the responsible site manager, who informed the contact person at the power plant directly. The latter inspected the damage site together with the responsible AnlV E and the deputy VEFK.

The damaged area (in the area of the damaged insulation) was checked to ensure that there was no voltage. During the subsequent inspection, it was initially established that only the outer cable insulation and the sheathing shield were damaged in all of the damaged cables. Damage to active conductors could apparently be ruled out.

As it was not possible to check the assignment of the medium-voltage cable with the means available on site, the damaged area was initially cordoned off. The following day, the assignment was checked and the repair measures were subsequently determined and carried out. The cable is feed 2 of the sewage treatment plant (10BD09 -> 64CT52)

The incident did not result in any direct danger to persons or restrictions in plant operation.

The approvals for the work were available in full. At the site of the damage, the cable and pipework plan deviated from the actual installation of the pipes, meaning that the presence of the cables could not be recognised in advance.

TITLE: Tailgate entry to site - poor attitude
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A Transit connect approached the site gate, buzzed the control room and after a conversation with the shift operator it was concluded that the person was at the wrong site and should be next door at the cement factory.

5 min later the Transit Connect appeared and parked to the side of the main gate. After approx 10 mins a contractor who is erecting a new fence arrived at site and drove to the barrier to card in. Uniper colleague approached the driver to ask who they were, why they'd tailgated through and who they were here to see.

They told me their Manager had told them to do it. Asked who their manager was and who they were here to see. They didn't know either but said they were here to wok with the fencing contractor. The person was extremely aggressive and confrontational. They were asked to remain in their van whilst Uniper colleague spoke to the contractor. It transpired the individual was here to work with them and was an agency temp. Due to the poor attitude displayed from arriving at site when engaged and the security breach. Requested that the contract company removed the individual from site.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Contract company contacted and contractor prevented from commencing work.

Further investigation with the contract company will be sort.

TITLE: H2 leakage at generator exciter unit 2
CASE_DESCRIPTION: As part of a pre-outage inspection on the generator and generator exciter unit 2, a hydrogen concentration at the level of the LEL was measured at the shaft opening of the generator exciter diode housing. This was caused by a hydrogen leak in the generator filled with H2, which had spread from the generator via the hollow shaft and coupling bushing to the diode contacts in the diode housing via several defective sealing elements. The hydrogen was able to mix with atmospheric oxygen in the diode housing and form an explosive mixture. The electrical components of the excitation diode are not designed for explosion protection.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Forced ventilation of the noise protection enclosure Generator exciter
Dismantling the noise protection enclosure
Logging off the power station unit
Flushing the generator with inert gas

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

TITLE: Failure of level transmitter during test
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During routine testing of the liquid level still chamber.
The “Control” level transmitter was found to have values entered the upper and lower ranges, that were different to the identical safety transmitter and identical control level transmitters on the two other identical vessels. 

It was also observed that the amplitude of the waveform seemed to be significantly lower than on the same device at other positions. 

The still well was filled with water and the level increase – immediately an issue with the “0” position was obvious the water level continued to be increased and no response was given from the transmitter.

The correct parameters were entered, and the waveform threshold retuned. 
The liquid level test then recommenced. 
The transmitter performed as expected at 
0 ,25,50,75,100% points. 

As the still well drained, the Transmitter registered the 75% point, however after that the reading froze despite the still chamber being totally empty. 

Should this have happened in normal operation the control valve could have opened despite the liquid level not being present. 

This would have likely put a demand on the SIF responsible for this protection.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
•	Survey and test remaining level transmitters on site and form a database of expected settings. 
•	Review stock holdings as replacement parts on site are not correct. 
•	Temporary MOC to cover isolation of transmitter for vessel RTS – TRA scheduled 26/10/23.

Ultimately the test was to see if level was working. It was not and action has been taken.

TITLE: Wrongly prioritised alarm
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
An alarm was discovered on unit 6 DCS linked to the Tantronic gas detection system. We often receive a lot of nuisance annunciations of this particular alarm due to low sample flows. On this occasion it was investigated and the same alarm was showing that there was a fault on the system (sample pump failure). This meant that there was no EV or SEV combustion ring gas detection and the alarm received was the same priority 3 alarm that you would receive for a low sample flow on one sample point.
A failure of a part of the gas detection system should give a more significant alarm.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
P1 notification raised and fault fixed immediately.
Alarm prioritisation for gas detection system needs to be looked at to make more robust.

CASE_DESCRIPTION: A fault on a separate CB required the 61BFB board to be switched out of service. This required changing the 61BMA board over from BFB board supply to BFA board supply. We were then just assessing what further actions were required on the BFB board, when the BFB / BMA circuit breaker closed automatically when it shouldn't have. TITLE: Overheated starting resistance of a DC drive
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Machine unit 1 was depressurised and flushed with nitrogen due to inspection units. The pressure was approx. 0.9 bar. The presumably higher outside temperature caused a slight increase in pressure in the machine to approx. 1 bar. One bar is the switch-on point of the air blower (emergency air blower). No hysteresis was set on the limit value module of the PLC. As a result, the drive was repeatedly switched on and off by a slightly fluctuating pressure. As a result, the starting resistors of the DC motor overheated considerably. The control centre driver noticed the switching on and off, whereupon he informed the fault clearance service/standby team. The overheating was then detected on site.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Enabling the actuator and setting a hysteresis on the limit value module in the PLC. Check the hysteresis on all limit value modules of the ME1-3 that are associated with switching on a drive.

TITLE: Door lock with panic function, offline card reader, door lock without panic function
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
In an office building with 6 floors, the Uniper companies have rented the 4 - 6 floors.
This area was sealed off from the other tenants in the building in 01/2023 using offline card readers on the doors.
In the direction of escape, all doors can only be opened without the card reader by pressing the door handle.
Some of the locking cylinders with the card readers were installed in existing door locks.
Door locks had to be retrofitted to some doors.
The existing door locks do not have a panic function. This made it possible to lock the doors. They could not be opened in the direction of escape using the handle.
When ordering and installing the new door locks, attention was paid to the panic function.
The panic function was not tested on the existing door locks. However, this function was not present.
The door locks with or without panic function are externally identical.
It was not considered and therefore not tested that the doors can not only be opened but also locked via the card readers if no panic lock was installed.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Incorrect posture or insufficient work environment
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The locks without panic function were removed immediately and new locks with panic function were ordered. The lock was cancelled during the delivery period.

TITLE: PSNH - U3 A SSFP started unexpectedly
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Whilst de-earthing / de-isolating U3 A SSFP, the pump started unexpectedly. The 11kv breaker was first removed from earth by tripping the breaker mechanically. The 11kv breaker was then removed from earth position, de-isolated and placed back in the cubicle and racked into the service position. The breaker selector was then switched from the OFF position to the REMOTE position. The mechanical and LV isolations were de-isolated and pre start checks carried out. The liquid reg Lram was raised and lowered to ensure control, at the same time the oil pump was turned to remote in the switchroom and the oil pump started straight away. The operative made their way round to the A SSFP to leak check the oil system. When the operative got to the oil pump he found the SSFP was running and fully in service. Contact was made with the control room to find out who had started the pump, the reply was nobody. The pump was then taken out of service immediately. EC&I and Turbine team were both made aware so the cause of the unexpected start could be investigated.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
SSFP taken out of service. On Initial investigations by EC&I and Turbine teams it appears that there was a latched start command within the plc from 5 weeks previous when the 11Kv SSFP breaker was isolated and closed remotely to circuit earth position. Even though on de-isolation and de-earthing the breaker was tripped mechanically, this did not override the latched start command.  

EC&I to carry out 11Kv breaker interlock tests to confirm initial findings. (Planned 22/09)
A SSFP to be test run with Turbine Team in attendance following EC&I interlock checks.
Ops to review breaker isolation / de-isolation procedure based on EC&I findings.
EC&I to review breaker start latched command, to understand reason for start command duration.

TITLE: Steam Turbine Safety System Transmitter changed without Modification Process Followed
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
One of the condenser level transmitters has been changed to a different make and model without the modification process being followed. 
This transmitter is part of the Steam Turbine SIL rated (Safety Integrity Level)  protection functions. 
The modification process should ensure the new transmitters meet the reliability calculations required of the attached Safety Manual and therefore maintain the integrity of the protective function.
There is a risk that the integrity of the safety system has been compromised without due diligence.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Immediate Action
1. Reported situation to C&I Strategy Engineer who wasn't aware of change and agreed to raise modification.
2. Discussed situation with C&I Delivery Engineers to ascertain awareness of SIS system.

Recommendations:
1. Raise modification to cover the change.
2. Seek advice from Ansaldo / GE / ABB as to a suitable replacement transmitter to meet the requirement of the protection system.
3. Plan & Deliver Safety Instrument Systems awareness training to all engineers and operators.
4. Decide the best way to physically identify on plant all components of each Safety Related System so that people are aware at the point of work.

Note - Further actions covered in subsequent A1 41002143 SL Case. 49019 - Can be found in connected cases section.

TITLE: Measures when opening an asbestos-containing fibre cement pipe after pipe damage.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
23.12.1924
An above-average steam leak was reported from a shaft in the UWG district heating network. As there was no immediate danger, it was decided to only continue monitoring the damaged area over the holidays.
24.12.2024
Finding that the vapour leakage was increasing.
The first measures taken were to surround the leakage shafts with fencing, traffic safety measures, daily pumping of the affected shafts and further monitoring of the damage.
27.12.2024
Direct inspection of the shaft was not possible due to the heat and vapour generated, even with intensive machine-assisted ventilation.  It was therefore not possible to localise the damage precisely. Daily inspection continues.
30.12.2024
Planning and initiation of localisation and repair. It was discovered that the protective pipe is made of fibre cement containing asbestos. Therefore, the unavoidable opening of the protective pipe must be carried out by a company certified according to TRGS 519.
02.01.2025
Construction site equipment.
03.01.2025
Briefing on the circumstances of the civil engineering company's employees. Carrying out civil engineering work. Exposure of the pipe strings at the suspected damage point. Weather: Overcast and damp.
06.01.2025
Opening of the exposed pipelines by specialist company (inspection of certificates), not possible due to vapour development.
07.01.2025
Decommissioning of the pipework. After the pipes had cooled down accordingly, it was decided to cut out the protective pipe. Protective measures:
Technical: Water-cooled hand-operated circular stone saw (dust binding), keep the surrounding area moist.
Personal: Protective suits with bonnet, respiratory protection (FFP3), eye protection (visor).
Organisational: max. 2 employees at the work site, max. work duration 4h, safety distance for bystanders and neighbours 5m. Disposal of the asbestos-containing cuttings by a specialised company.
08.01.2025
Carrying out the cutting work on the DSC pipe by a specialised company. Checking the specified safety measures during the work. Cleaning of the interfaces on the pipe.
Approval of the repair site for further work by the specialised company.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Cordoning off the damage site, informing the departments, determining further protective measures (see text)

TITLE: MUW DCS RIO Panel Wiring Discrepancies
CASE_DESCRIPTION: When reviewing loop diagram 755-TEL-XX-XX-DR-E-0215 for PAB80AA151 in comparison to the physical wiring inside the MUW DCS RIO panel, it became clear that there are multiple occurrences of disparity between the drawing and the actual wiring configuration within the panel. For example, the drawing states on terminal block X33 wiring should be X33-13 - Brown, X33-14 - Black, X33-15 - Blue, X33-16 - Green, but in reality it is X33-13 - Blue, X33-14 - Green, X33-15 - Brown, X33-16 - Black, and the wiring into AO card 1:5:0 should be wire 316 into terminal 3, 317 into terminal 6, but the reality is 317 into terminal 3 and 316 into terminal 6. These are just a couple of examples but several other discrepancies have been found (including in other drawings) suggesting the drawings cannot be relied upon to reflect the actual wiring configuration of the equipment.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: No immediate action taken. Recommend a full review of the entire wiring installation in comparison with the supplied drawings may be required as a limited review has already uncovered a significant number of errors.

TITLE: U1 A SSFP Oil Filter vent valve found slightly open.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
U1 A SSFP was being prepared for RTS ready for a test run, followed by pressure testing of HP heaters.

The SSFP was de-isolated & pre start checked by the commissioning operator.  The oil pump was put into service and the oil system checked for correct pressures, and checked over for leaks.  No leaks were observed following the oil pump going into service.  The Operator then walked the HP feed system to ensure a route was available for the SSFP's and de-isolated the remaining plant.  The Operator called the Authorised Person over the radio to make the HV breaker available for service.  As the AP was heading to the switchroom the Operator returned to the pump ready for the start; a period of approx 30 mins had passed.   On returning to the pump he observed a large pool of oil under the A SSFP oil filters.  On closer inspection the vent on the filter was found to be slightly open with a stream of oil running from it.  The filter vent was closed immediately to stop the flow.   The AP was called on the radio to divert straight to the pump.  Dresser Dry was deployed to dam the oil and to prevent entry to any turbine hall drains.   There is a 3" hole in the turbine hall floor adjacent to the A SSFP, and some of the oil had flowed down the hole which leads directly to the sub- basement.  Dresser dry was deployed in the sub-basement around the oil & the spill contained.

The oil mop in the reject tunnel was immediately put into service as a precautionary measure.  There was a very slight film of oil on the water before the weir, but nothing observed after the weir, or at either the station drains sump or Ash Fines Pit.

The filter vent is not operated as part of the RTS procedure,  and is only used to prove the filter off pressure during a filter change.  I suspect that at some point during U1 outage the vent cock handle has been knocked slightly, causing the vent to pass when the oil pump went into service which was missed on the initial inspection.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Oil (Inc. contamination of land or water)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The oil mop in the reject tunnel was put into service. 
Dresser dry was applied to all areas of the spill.
Altrad boiler ops were called to assist in the clean up operation.  All dresser dry was cleaned up and bagged, both adjacent to the feed pump and in the sub basement.
A defect card was raised to top up A SSFP oil tank.

Services team will be informed on Monday (10/07) to highlight the dresser dry used from spill kits

Consider filling in the Hole in the turbine hall floor  (expanding foam would suffice).

TITLE: LNG vapour leakage after damage to the breakaway coupling by a truck driver without full PPE
CASE_DESCRIPTION: A Vlantana lorry registered in Lithuania (registration number GO 052) drove onto our filling station in Rosengarten at around 10:41 a.m. on 19/01/2022 to fill up with LNG using the DKV card. The lorry was too far away from the dispenser so that the LNG hose could not be connected to the lorry. However, the lorry driver did not drive closer to the dispenser, but pulled hard on the LNG hose until he managed to connect the lorry to the dispenser. By pulling the hose so hard, the customer damaged the breakaway coupling on the dispenser so that the lorry could not be filled. The lorry driver saw the damaged breakaway coupling and tried to fill the lorry anyway. During the entire process, the lorry driver did not wear any safety gloves or face protection, contrary to the applicable safety regulations. During the attempt to fill the lorry, vaporised LNG flowed out of the damaged breakaway coupling, some of which touched the lorry driver without PPE equipment for approximately one second. The driver then uncoupled the lorry from the LNG hose and fled the LNG filling station without reporting the damage he had caused or securing the damaged area.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Notification of a DKV customer's violation of usage and safety regulations
Report to petrol station manufacturer to analyse and take safety measures and update system operation so that personal injury can be prevented.
Damaged breakaway coupling was replaced and its function checked and confirmed by the on-site technician.

TITLE: Lambda DFB2 has been < 1 several times.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
When the biopropane composition changes (or the Wobbe measurement fails), the lambda of DFB2 may drop below 1 (underoichimetric). The boiler protection system does not detect this and should already trip the boiler at a lambda <1.05.
There is then unburned hydrogen gas in the boiler.
Boiler engineers have experience that a "thud" can be caught with natural gas and the energy dissipated through the chimney.
Hydrogen gas is much more explosive and has a more powerful shock wave. How the boiler can absorb that is unprecedented.

This occurred on 18 June 2020 where an SOG report was prepared and an investigation team was set up.
More recently, this occurred on 20 April 2023 and 3 June 2023. An SOG of both was prepared. After 3 June, the biopropane composition was changed twice more, which was met manually by the WTK.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: On Friday 21 June 2023, the measure was promulgated to stop entering the boiler (for inspection rounds) and no work at DFB2.

TITLE: Earth fault during commissioning Low-voltage main distribution of the gas pressure reducing station
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Together with a partner, Uniper has installed a CHP plant for an external customer. Recently, a damage pattern (traces of smoke on the slide-in unit) was noticed, which is apparently due to commissioning activities in September 2022.
The corresponding investigations have shown that effective technical measures did not jeopardise the safety of employees or the system at any time.
Nevertheless, such a procedure should be avoided at all costs and a repetition should be ruled out.

During the initial commissioning of the on-site gas pressure reducing station in September 2022, a short circuit was generated during measurements by the customer with a ZIP measuring device, which immediately tripped the compact circuit breaker in the feeding point 70BHA03.H01. When it was switched on again, the circuit-breaker could no longer be switched mechanically. As a result, the identical withdrawable unit from the reserve bay 70BHA06.H01 was used and the gas station was put into operation in order to ensure the availability and operation of the entire system.
The low-voltage switchgear 70BHA supplied by Janssen is of withdrawable design. The moulded-case circuit-breaker was removed from the withdrawable unit and sent to the manufacturer Siemens for damage assessment.
The withdrawable module 70BHA03.H01 was inserted into the spare shaft 70HA06.H01 without circuit-breaker and pushed in until it was mechanically locked. The front door was closed and the connection to the busbar was established using a hand crank. As the moulded-case circuit-breaker had been removed and the internal connecting cable ends (cable lugs) of the withdrawable module for connecting the circuit-breaker were uninsulated in the withdrawable module, an earth fault occurred when the withdrawable module was retracted.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The NSHV is a type-tested switchgear. As the earth fault occurred within the closed enclosure of the system and did not leave the withdrawable unit/switchgear, there was no risk to employees at any time.

In order to put the system in a safe condition, the withdrawable unit was covered with a rubber mat and the contacts of the internal connecting cables were insulated accordingly. This prevented the system from being retracted again.

The following measures were taken to prevent such errors in the future:

Instruction of qualified electricians
Qualified electricians must familiarise themselves with the functionality of the switchgear and, in particular, know and take into account specific features.

It must be prevented that non-operational plug-in units are installed in switchgear panels; non-operational plug-in units must be clearly labelled as "Attention not ready for operation".

Only complete units may be inserted into the withdrawable units.
If a withdrawable module is removed for repair purposes in the future, this opening must be closed with a withdrawable module cover.

TITLE: Oil leakage in the oil pump house

The on-site inspection revealed a large accumulation of oil at the bottom of the oil pump house.
The drain 02PE00S305 was open, as was the vent 02PE00S354. The oil had escaped from these two positions. The personnel on site estimated that approx. 150 litres had escaped. The valves were in the "OPEN" position due to disconnections. Oil binding agent (perlite) was available on site, but oil binding cloths were not available. As a result, the oil that had run into cable ducts could only be removed after 2 days. There was no danger to the environment.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The tank shut-offs were closed immediately and the drain and vent were sealed. The auxiliary steam generator was then started. The oil in the oil pump house was skimmed off and bound with oil binding agent. The oil pump house was then cleaned. Oil binding cloths were ordered.

Work was carried out on the standby system and whilst the analyser was warming/booting up, work was started on the duty system. After work was completed on the duty system, a QAL3 was carried out on the the standby unit, which subsequently failed. cbiss left site with the duty system operational and were instructed to return the following day to continue fault finding on the standby system. TITLE: Recycling/discharge of off-spec R-net water due to non-flowing quality measurements
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
For some time, the R-net discharged off-spec water to the process water tank and also temporarily to the surface water for a while as the quality measurements were not flowing through. In trend, we discovered that the line of quality measurements had been writing straight for some time. Checked measurement on site on this and then found that the pH and conductivity measurement had no flow. See trend in appendix, blue and pink line write a straight line until flow was restored.

So with the current set-up of the system, it is possible to drain off-spec water to the process water tank. Water (which is outside the permit requirements) can also be discharged to the syphon well.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Water (Inc. excess volume, lack of, uncontrolled release or excess use)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
made sure the measurements were flowing again

Recommendation:
Placing a flow meter at each measurement ( 01GUA14CQ001/ 002/ 003)
integrate flow measurements into DCS so that the R-net system automatically stops discharging to the syphon well or BMW tank and starts circulating until the measurements are provided with flow again.  This creates proper protection and prevents off-spec water from being piloted.

This was also implemented in the case of the steam/water loop sampling.

TITLE: SIS trip GRU20 reboiler high pressure QCA20ZP004
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Regen 20 was up and running and the cooling air pressure to the combustion chamber (QCA20ZP004) had started to drop off. 
Caused by ice forming over the cooling fan vent mesh which requires removal by technician. 

On this occasion though, it was an unusually freezing cold wet night and when technician went to remove the ice from the mesh they inadvertently made it worse as they wiped water across the mesh and it instantly froze blocking off all the air flow which resulted in the trip.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
This last occurred in January 2019 (Synergi: 3211).

The main action taken was to raise an MoC (235) to add a ‘smart’ DCS low pressure pre-alarm to QCA20ZP004 and QCA30ZP004 on GRU 20 and GRU 30 cooling air streams. 

To avoid the generation of nuisance or standing alarms this alarm will only be enabled after the associated cooling air fan running signal has been active for 300 seconds and the alarm will be disabled as soon as the fan running signal is lost.

This worked in this instance to allow the site team to respond, unfortunately the response exacerbated the issue in this instance.

TITLE: Control air system EFM00/01/02 not in order (not inspected) and not redundant
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The control air compressors in the basement of MPP2 have not been serviced since the closure of MPP1 and 2. It was decided at the time to start using the compressor of the MBM system for MPP1/2, O system and UCML condensate system. It was also decided not to install a redundant compressor in case the current compressor fails.

The only option left then is to start an old control air compressor
The old control air compressors are piston compressors that have leaky head gaskets and this can cause water hammer and cause eea to burst.  This can lead to a dangerous situation.

Also, this can lead to a trip of MPP2 and UCML condensate system and the entire 0 system.

There are also several components in the control air system that are past their inspection date (drums and safety devices).
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
- asap component retesting (SAP 30004591888)
- provide a redundant solution
- decommissioning old control air compressors (cutting cables)

TITLE: During unloading of 12 tonnes of hydrochloric acid demi old side, counterflow occurred under tanks A & B from tank A to tank B - 0UZ21B031
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During unloading of 12 tonnes of hydrochloric acid demi old side, backflow occurred under tanks A & B from tank A to tank B - 0UZ21B031. An MOC to replace the control panel old demi to control from DCS is currently underway. This MOC was partially implemented in December 2021. In the old situation - via the panel - only 1 tank can be controlled open at a time. Currently with operation partly in DCS - and no longer controllable on the old panel - all valves under the tanks can be steered open at the same time. Because level measurements in DCS are still missing, this is how it has been in recent weeks. However, the situation then arises that when hydrochloric acid was unloaded - tank A was empty - both tanks started levelling through the PVC piping and through the valves under the tanks. This created counterflow from tank A to tank B. This is not by design, nor is it known whether the valves and valves are suitable for this. An unknown pressure is also created in the PVC piping.

The pressure level in the entire system has been reduced and the risk of recurrence is very, very low.

The situation is analysed in detail after an actual near-crisis situation (dynamic network simulation etc. required)

TITLE: Odour nuisance due to styrene spindle at Lyondell
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

No trucks via access MPP3 for the time being.   Fuel supply informed no trucks via port MPP3
- 16:30 : Port office cleared, all work halted due to odour nuisance.
- 17:30 : div measurements taken, peak value 92 ppm benzene-like substances.
- 18:35 : FS to go home.
- 19:30 : div measurements taken, peak value 232 ppm Well started cleaning port
- 22:00 Lyondell called; harbour cleaning is done according to TL (boat still sailing around)
- 22:10 our measurement gives same values, dirt is now in dead corners against the shore. Stench is still the same. After consultation with B v D no more actions needed tonight. Mirjam discussed it with her who will call several companies and see how it is tomorrow morning.  
- Night shift stench is no longer present.

TITLE: Specific hand fire alarm in Heavy's containers is not included in the cause and effect list of Heavy's hazards
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
In the heavy container in EH3, specific hand-held fire detectors have been installed. Due to the danger of the fuel in combination with incipient fire, it is stipulated in the UPD that the heavy's installations should be controlled by the fire alarm system to terminate the fuel supply to the unit.

This is achieved by a 2-detector dependency whereby 2 automatic detectors in alarm the fire alarm system signals the DCS that this condition is active and DCS then controls function blocks to stop the fuel supply to the unit and go into bypass operation outside near the heavy tank.

Because the definition of hand-held fire alarms is that they can only be operated by a human action, within the NEN2535 (fire alarm standard) a hand-held fire alarm has been put on the same level as 2-alarm dependency or verified fire alarm.

 Because these hand-held fire detectors are fitted in the containers, it is
 desirable/necessary that these hand-held fire detectors ALSO signal to the DCS that a verified fire alarm is present.

Now the situation is that you as an employee are working in the container and a fire breaks out and you press the manual fire detector but the fuel supply is not stopped, unfortunately you have to wait a while until the fire has reached sufficient size that 2 automatic detectors have been activated and then the fuel supply is terminated.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
We will write an SA for the modification of the fire alarm system software.

Project teams do not communicate fully and too often the right expertise from within Uniper Benelux is not brought in. The project teams then disappear, leaving behind systems that do not work properly without proper documentation (as-built) and proper commissioning.

The recommendation is therefore that project teams should be assisted by expertise from UBX and the monitoring of proper AS-BUILT revision should be better secured from UBX and certainly not left to the project teams.

TITLE: Leakage of control oil in oil compartment HT
CASE_DESCRIPTION: On 21 June 2022, there was an oil leak in the HT oil compartment of unit 1. The floor of the oil compartment was flooded with oil and the oil flowed into the drain, triggering the "HT oil compartment" message. At the same time, an employee from the mechanical workshop was on site and noticed the oil leak. The pressure gauge 01SU16P504 was not fitted and the shut-off valve of this pressure gauge was open. The oil leaked out at this point. Approx. 300 litres of oil escaped. This was deliberately drained into barrels, so there was no adverse effect on the environment.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: See incident report dated 21/06/2022. It was ensured that the spray flood system was not triggered by the oil leak. A shift employee then shut off the shut-off valve upstream of the missing pressure gauge. The pumps were secured against starting up. An electrical engineering employee assessed a possible electrical risk. At the same time, the oil drain was secured and the oil was collected in drums. This prevented the oil from escaping into the environment. The oil compartment was then cleaned with oil binding agents. Sufficient oil binding agents were available.

TITLE: Activation of GPP EDP system
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Routine preventative maintenance on Motor Control Centers in the Holford LV Switch Room caused an unexpected coms error in the installation's Safety Instrumented System (SIS).  Upon detection of the coms error (and in line with its design), the SIS automatically activated a controlled de-pressurization of the Gas Processing Plant through the site vent stack.  Following identification of the cause of the coms error, the de-pressurization process was aborted within approximately five minutes. The vent stack is designed and located to ensure the safety of all personnel during venting.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
- The site team followed our existing emergency response procedures - ensuring that key parties were informed and actions and decisions were logged.
- The site team attempted to replicate the faults through a repeat of the preventative maintenance work completed prior to the coms issue.  The coms issue could not be replicated.
- There were no standing SIS faults on the Alarm log 
- The GPP process was assessed for areas of potential risk in returning to service. The 
majority of the plant did not see large pressure swings with the exception of the 
compressors whose pressure reduced to 0.5barg. 
- The installation was balanced and re-pressurized in a controlled manner, using agreed methods.
- MCC inspections were put on hold pending further investigation of the root cause
- While the root cause of  the coms issue had not been completely understood, the plant was considered safe for RTS based on the work above, the low likelihood of reoccurrence and the knowledge that the installation would fail safe as designed.
- Full investigation of the incident will follow

TITLE: 81BFT20 415V circuit breaker not opening on command
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Overnight, the duty operations shift were requested to change over the duty 415V unit auxilliary transformer in preparation for the engineering department to change some protection settings the following day. 81BFT10 11kv breaker was closed prior so that the transformer could soak. The BFA-BFB breaker was opened and the BFT10 415V breaker closed to supply the BFA board from the BFT10 transformer. This worked correctly. The BFB to BMA board breaker was opened starting the standby diesel generator which took the load on the BMA board. A back synch to BFA board was selected which functioned correctly. The BFA board / BFT10 transformer was then supplying the power to the BMA board. This was correct. An attempt was made to open the 81BFT20 415V incomer CB to BFB board. An open feedback failure alarm was received and the current on the breaker did not drop. BFT20 transformer remains supplying the BFB board awaiting engineering assistance.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Remains in a safe condition, in service. If a fault were to occur, the 11kV VCB protection would open to clear the fault.

TITLE: PSNH - Common ammonia plant toxic gas trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The Ammonia Plant South West Perimeter LOS (Line-of-Sight) toxic gas detected alarm was received and release of the deluge system operated. This was coincidental  with collection of the waste ammonia solution IBCs for environmental disposal. One possible cause being diesel engine emissions from the Services JCB all-terrain FLT.  The driver was in close proximity to the LOS beam at the west end of the offloading bay when the LOS gas detection was triggered. Another possible cause could have been ammonia vapour emanating from the IBCs themselves, however these have not caused a problem in the last 3-4 weeks that they have been stored in the offloading bay. On this occasion there was no generation taking place, hence no operational loss. However there is the potential for operational units to suffer immediate non-abatement due to loss of NH3 injection so a repeat scenario should be avoided.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Communicate event to (Services, Boiler Team, Doosan, C&I Team, Env and Chem Team)
•When carrying out FLT operations in close proximity to the ammonia plant LOS beams, avoid the use of the ‘older’ JCB all-terrain FLT and substitute for either a newer diesel or propane powered FLT.
•When planning the delivery or collection of any IBCs to consider scheduling when the Units are not running if feasible.

TITLE: Storm damage Tree on power line, Schimmelsheider Park, Recklinghausen
CASE_DESCRIPTION: A leak has occurred in shaft 19 due to water penetrating through a leaking butt joint in the shaft ceiling. The fallen tree damaged parts of the overhead line and the manhole entrances with the protective pipes.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The repair requires:
> the tree must be removed.
> approx. 15 metres of overhead line must be renewed
> the protective pipes incl. core pipes at the shaft inlet and outlet must be renewed
> the shaft must be re-piped (various sections of the line are already corroded)
> Depending on the corrosion or condition of the pipe, the road crossing (approx. 12 metres) may also need to be renewed.
> For the repair, the shaft ceiling must be lifted, parts of the shaft walls dismantled and the route excavated a few metres in front of and behind the shaft.
> the insulation has to be dismantled and replaced in several places.

TITLE: Drain valve incorrectly connected Feedwater pumps DFB2
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Investigation revealed that all 5 feedwater pumps of DFB2 have the drain valves connected to the wrong chamber.
These are supposed to be connected to the pump housings, but turn out to be on the cooling water chambers of the mechanical seal covers.
So when one thinks one is draining the feedwater pumps, in reality the Cogen intercooling water is being drained.
During the last overhaul DFB2, draining all 5 pumps caused the Cogen cooling to go down so dangerously that a trip of the cooling water was narrowly avoided.
On the Cogen intercooling water hangs the entire UCML plant including Lyondell and Neste.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
From feedwater pump 5, the drain valves have been widened and the stub blinded, as this pump is already under maintenance.
From the other pumps, these are yet to be removed, the valves are blocked with a chain and lock.

TITLE: Fuel Gas Fiscal metering system failure.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: At approx. 14:00 on 02/06/2021 the fuel gas metering system at the Enfield AGI stopped recording gas flow data. The failure was noticed by the onsite engineer at approx. 17:30. The failure means that no gas flow data was recorded or transmitted to the Control Room or NGC for either fiscal or UK-ETS purposes during this period. There was no automatic alarm raised to notify operators of the failure and prompt them to change over to the redundant stream.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Legal, monitoring and reporting (Non-compliance of obligations)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Upon noting that the flow computer had stopped running the Control room was contacted to confirm that the data flow had stopped. The flow computer control panel was unresponsive, so the unit was power cycled and rebooted, at which point the Flow Computer started operating again.
The Senior Environmental Adviser and Uniper Gas desk were both notified so that back up methodology for UK-ETS and Fiscal data could be put in place. The Flow computer was close monitored for 1 hour without any further issue, and remote monitored through the evening and overnight.

TITLE: CODE tank
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Sequence of event on April 21st
1. 23:35hrs CPU-1&2 taken on long circulation.
2. 01:45hrs Feed tank changed over from T-302 to T-303.
3. Non urgent alarm received in SCADA, related to CPU-1 Furnace. Firing did not stop
4. Operators checked in Furnace BMS PLC and found Naphtha KOD (knock Out Drum) Level low low alarm. Level indication found 0.
5. Furnace stopped from SCADA immediately at 02:07hrs.

Found LCV-1712 is open. On checking in field found KOD level is very High. Drained more than 10 buckets of Naphtha and level brought down less than the low pressure impulse line of the Level Transmitter. Level Transmitter low pressure impulse line drained and indication restored in PLC. Alarm reset done in PLC and furnace started at 03:45 hrs.

The suspected root cause is a momentary malfunction of LCV-1712 or LT-1711 the reason for this is under analysis. LCV-1712 - Level control valve maintain a constant level of NAPHTHA supply to KOD. LT-1711 controls the level of Naphtha in KOD and sends signal to LCV-1712 to open/ close the LCV-1712 valve for supply of Nphtha based on set values.

TITLE: Water surge into Oil interceptor pits after heavy storm.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During an heavy storm the GT oil interceptor pit high level alarm was received. The sudden surge in water had filled the adjacent overflow sump. The alarm then cleared but an oily scum was seen in final chamber of the interceptor pit. A slight sheen was  also observed on the surface of rain water pit. The Rain water pumps were immediately switched off and the outlet valve closed.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Oil (Inc. contamination of land or water)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Rain water pit pumps switched off and outlet valve closed. Adler & Allen our external environmental company contacted and a tanker arranged to visit site on Thursday. CDC to be point of contact overnight.
11/5/23 SW: Adler & Allen attended site and skimmed off 12000 litres of oily water from the interceptor pit, mainly from the final chamber. While an initial inspection of the rain water pit in the morning suggested a sheen was present, by 11 am this had disappeared and the consensus from A&A was that the sheen was from a very small amount of oil which had evaporated in the sun and there was nothing for them to skim off, with the penstock valve being safe to open. The rain pit was monitored by CDCPK personnel during discharge to ensure no visible oil was present. Arrangements made by ops for a larger tanker to attend site 12/5 to continue clean out of the interceptor pits & overflow.

TITLE:
Old control room
The Smoke Corner on the control room in the DWZ does not fulfil the requirements for non-smoker protection.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Smoking in the workplace has been prohibited in Germany since the Non-Smoker Protection Act came into force.  

Ordinance on Workplaces (Workplace Ordinance - ArbStättV)§ 5 Non-smoker protection

(1) The employer shall take the necessary measures to ensure that non-smoking employees in workplaces are effectively protected from the health hazards of tobacco smoke. Where necessary, the employer shall impose a general smoking ban or one that is limited to individual areas of the workplace.

(2) In workplaces open to the public, the employer shall take technical or organisational measures in accordance with paragraph 1 to protect non-smoking employees when setting up and operating workrooms in accordance with the nature of the business and the type of employment.  

Requirements for smoking cabins:

Complete capture and retention of tobacco smoke

No escape of smoke, not even when air is moved by people passing by. No increase in the concentration of pollutants in the installation room.

The Smoke Corner on the control room in the DWZ does not fulfil the above requirements.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Incorrect posture or insufficient work environment
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
It is therefore strongly recommended that a new smoking cabin be purchased if space permits and there is a need. In addition, a smoking area should be created outside for our own employees and partner companies.
Done!

TITLE: Make-Up Water Redundant Pipe Removal
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
This Synergi has been raised on behalf of EDF by Asset Support & Outage Excellence UK 

Decommissioning of the CDC MUW supply pipework to include removal of the pipework, 10-PAR-20-CF001 flow meter and 10-PAR-20-AA151 Actuated Control valve.

Prior to the Safety document being written the SAP and the Uniper Project Engineer visited the point of work to discuss the exact works. The SAP had opened the drain valve on the redundant  MUW pipework and air could be heard rushing in there was no water from the drain proving the isolation of 10-PAS-72-AA002 of which separated the new MUW system form the old MUW system thus proving the integrity of the valve. A further discussion between the SAP and Uniper Project Engineer took place reference the status of the MUW pump booster station reference the HV cable disconnection and that he MUW booster pumps could not run as there was no power present.

A Safety document was issued by the Uniper SAP for the decommissioning works to proceed and at approximately 12:30 p.m., the Uniper Project Engineer received a phone call from Trant Works Manager responsible for the works to ask if an isolation had been applied at the EDF end of the MUW supply pipe to CDC.

An email was received at  12:37 from EDF Site Separation Lead Mechanical Engineer Decommissioning as follows:

I have just been to see the Trant guys doing the make up decommissioning work on CDC, I did a spot check on the safety document, and subsequently asked Nathan Pearson to stop works.
 
The only mechanical isolation in place is on valve 10-PAS-72-AA002, this valve separates the old system from the new system.
It appears no valves have been isolated upstream from the booster station end.
 
If EDF were to start one of it’s make up pumps, this could potentially feed water all the way to the CDC site, either causing harm when flanges are split, or flooding the CDC
 
Nathan is going to speak to Steve Nelson and the Ops team, could you please raise a Uniper synergy case for this.
 
The booster station may be electrically disconnected, but there is nothing to stop valves from being opened
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Work stopped immediately and SAP informed by Trant Engineering. Safety document  cancelled and locks and chains applied to the MUW booster pumps discharge manual isolation valves 10PAR11AA003 and 10PAR12AA003. New safety document issued and work completed.

TITLE: Unit 6 Steam Turbine High Vibrations on Run-Up.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
From Enerlytics alert dated 22/03/2023 @ 14:38
During routine OLVMS monitoring, UTG noticed higher than normal levels of vibration along the ST shaft line during the run up on 16th March. The highest levels were seen on the IP/LP Eccentricities where levels peaked at 290 um pk-pk with the unit at 842 rpm, during a normal run up a typical amplitude at this speed would be 25-50 um pk-pk. The change in vibration was 1/rev driven suggesting the unit had run up with a temporary bend.

A review of the barring file prior to this run up shows that the turbine remained stationary for approximately 1 hour following the previous run down on the evening of 15th March. The barring file shows the rotor straightening across the barring period, however the elevated vibration levels had not fully subsided before the start of the run up. If the unit was had remained on barring for a few more hours the rotor may had been able to fully straighten prior to starting.

Once the machine reached full speed and was loaded up, the vibration levels subsided as the machine straighten. Subsequent run ups and run downs have passed by without incident, comparing well to previous and giving no cause for concern.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Investigate the reasons for the turning gear not engaging at the correct time.

TITLE: Failure to monitor water discharges during cooling water discharge
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Following breakdown of the water sampling pump in the environmental, the system was isolated for repair at around 14:00 on the 13/7. However, the bypass system to allow a continued flow to the analysers was not opened and so flow in the sampling system was reduced and monitoring was incomplete. Purging of cooling water continued during this time, with the monitors upstream of the environment kiosk demonstrating temperature, pH and chlorine remained steady and within permit limits during this period. No discharge of process water from the UGX pit was undertaken, and so no release of ammonia is expected during the period. The issue with the low flow and bypass valve was identified at shift change at 20:00, at which point the purge valve was closed. The bypass valve was then checked and opened to allow sufficient flow to the environmental kiosk monitors prior to the purge valve reopening.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Legal, monitoring and reporting (Non-compliance of obligations)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Once issue was identified, purging was stopped and only restarted once the bypass valve was open and monitoring resumed

TITLE: Service provider's workshop lorry drives into stream collector
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the outward journey on a dirt track at Moos 103, the employee drove off the road in the service vehicle without any other occupants due to the softened verge and the distraction of a telephone call. Visibility was limited due to the rain. As can be seen in the pictures, the vehicle overturned into the stream collector running parallel to the Isar Canal and the Birkenhof pond estate. The employee was able to leave the vehicle unharmed through the window of the driver's door after unfastening his seatbelt.
The employee stated that he was able to switch off the engine immediately and that no oil, diesel or other substances escaped from the vehicle. The doors and windows - with the exception of the upward-facing driver's window, which was used to exit the vehicle - were locked.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Wurzer Umwelt GmbH and Werkstatt GmbH immediately installed oil barriers (see appendix) to prevent the possible spread of contamination. Two walking excavators, a crane and two cable winches were used to recover the vehicle. The employees on site were instructed to constantly monitor possible fluid leaks during the recovery operation and to report them immediately if they were spotted - however, no fluids or other environmentally harmful substances escaped at any time.

TITLE: Black soot plume when starting Irsching 3
CASE_DESCRIPTION: When Irsching 3 was started due to a grid operator request, Irsching 3 drew a black plume of soot for approx. 45 minutes. This soot plume cannot be avoided during a cold start of Irsching 3, as the atomiser steam generated from the unit is normally 12 bar. At start-up, the block is not yet self-sufficient and auxiliary vapour at a pressure of 8 bar must be used. This leads to incomplete combustion with a corresponding soot plume. This cannot be avoided. Due to the fact that the weather at the start was beautiful on Sunday, many neighbours noticed this. Some then complained to the power station about the "environmental pollution". The shift foreman, plant management and production management telephoned the neighbours. In addition, a corresponding newspaper article was published in the local paper.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Dust (Inc. complaints, technical breaches or affecting ecosystems)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Optimised driving style as best as possible and wrote newspaper articles for clarification; continued to speak calmly and objectively with the callers.

TITLE: Supply failure in Datteln municipal grid due to telecontrol transmission fault
CASE_DESCRIPTION: On Friday there were problems with the telecontrol transmissions at UWG (presumably due to the thunderstorm), in Wanne and Bochum the controllers jumped to substitute values due to the faults and were thus maintained. In the Datteln municipal network, the control system on Höttingstrasse was set to 1.5 bar. A delta P of 1.7 bar was displayed. There were no reports of telecontrol faults in Datteln. After a short time, it was noticed that although a dP of 1.7 bar was displayed via Höttingstrasse, only approx. 60 m³/h was being delivered by the Datteln feed pump. CASE_DESCRIPTION: A Permit For Work was cleared by the CP with nil exceptions recorded in section 5 of the safety document, the associated worklist was not completed, there were  jobs still outstanding and no exceptions recorded for the current state of plant within the worklist. The person involved is very experienced and knowledgeable of the process. I have reiterated the importance of ensuring that when documents are cleared, even for a rehash, that the exceptions must be clearly identified and recorded.

CASE_DESCRIPTION: : On 12.1.21 Hot work permit(21561) issued for unloading chemical drums in CPU-1/2 by using fork lift from chemical carrying vehicle ,at 11:15 hrs fork lift operator arrived at site, he is from Al saleh transport company. TITLE: PSNH - Common ammonia plant toxic gas trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The Ammonia Plant South West Perimeter LOS (Line-of-Sight) toxic gas detected alarm was received and release of the deluge system operated. This was coincidental  with collection of the waste ammonia solution IBCs for environmental disposal. One possible cause being diesel engine emissions from the Services JCB all-terrain FLT.  The driver was in close proximity to the LOS beam at the west end of the offloading bay when the LOS gas detection was triggered. Another possible cause could have been ammonia vapour emanating from the IBCs themselves, however these have not caused a problem in the last 3-4 weeks that they have been stored in the offloading bay. On this occasion there was no generation taking place, hence no operational loss. However there is the potential for operational units to suffer immediate non-abatement due to loss of NH3 injection so a repeat scenario should be avoided.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Communicate event to (Services, Boiler Team, Doosan, C&I Team, Env and Chem Team)
•When carrying out FLT operations in close proximity to the ammonia plant LOS beams, avoid the use of the ‘older’ JCB all-terrain FLT and substitute for either a newer diesel or propane powered FLT.
•When planning the delivery or collection of any IBCs to consider scheduling when the Units are not running if feasible.

Batches that are above the limit value are disposed of properly.
Once the tanks have been emptied, they are cleaned before being put back into operation.

TITLE: Increased COD values in the scrubber and waste water
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
COD is the "chemical oxygen demand" of the FGD wastewater; according to the water rights permit, there is a limit value of 80 mg/l plus the preload from the Main.
In FGD unit 5, COD values are in a high range.

Due to technical problems with the wastewater pump of the FGD unit 5 absorber, we were only able to discharge 4m³/d from the plant for some time and thus temporarily increased the thickening of the absorbate. As a result, we detected a COD value of 93 mg/l in the 24-hour mixed sample of the FGD wastewater from 18 August 2022. The authority was informed about this on 23.8.22
We have now stored part of the FGD unit 5 in the former absorber of unit 3 to dilute the FGD unit 5.
However, we currently have the problem that the medium in FGD unit 5 is also foaming up. This may be due to the increased temperatures of the FGD due to e.g. MAIN water with a higher temperature or algae formation or also due to the increased COD value.
The unburnt material during incineration and the particle size are unremarkable.
From 1400 degrees during combustion, COD is no longer formed. This can therefore actually be ruled out as the cause of an increased COD. The cause is therefore currently unclear. A chemical reaction in the scrubber is suspected.
12.9.22 The cause is probably the additional water basin which had no water flow during the 4-week shutdown of unit 5 at very high outside temperatures and thus had accumulated a very high COD. Block 5 is fed with approx. 2400m³ per day at full load from this basin. This proportion of COD now had to be removed from the FGD by various measures. This proportion of COD now had to be removed from the FGD system using various measures. The basin was also cleaned over a weekend. Since this cleaning, we have been able to continuously reduce the values in the FGD and wastewater.
19.9.22 - we are currently able to reduce the values in the FGD and waste water with all measures (see appendix). Since last week 16.9.22 we have fallen below the limit values again in the waste water
21.9.22 - The wastewater values are below 70mg/l so that with the pre-load from the Main we are then at less than 60mg/l - limit value with pre-load is 90mg/l.
The final step is to move the AEB back to REA 5 as a temporary storage facility in the coming weeks. We are currently assuming that there will be no further limit violations here.
The RP Darmstadt authority will be kept up to date until complete emptying
The AEB tank was diluted several times and completely emptied by the beginning of December.
FGD scrubber:
1m AEB was run to FGD 5 - 29.9.22
1m AEB was transported to FGD 5 - 10.10.22
1m AEB was driven to FGD 5 - 12.10.22
1m AEB was driven to REA 5 - 14.10.22
1m AEB was driven to REA 5 - 19.10.22
1m AEB was driven to REA 5 - 06.11.22
7.11.22 the AEB was filled up by 1m and then 1m was driven back into REA 5 so we are now at approx. 4.3m AEB (less than 4m the agitator stops)
15.11.22 AEB was filled with 3m, COD is now 128
Now please lower AEB to 4.3m again after block 5
Then top up again by 3m
18.11.22 COD current AEB 90
End of November: AEB has now been completely moved to REA 5.
12.12.22
The COD values in the scrubber as well as in the waste water are good. The authorities were regularly informed and the issue is now officially closed

FGD block 5 lowered and filled with make-up water

Further support from Scholven, Heyden, UTG has been requested
At the same time, an attempt is being made to find a means of reducing foaming
A test was run through the shift at the weekend to understand the issue of foaming
Today on 29.8.22 a coordination with experts will take place as described above

TITLE: PSNH - Gypsum slurry overflowing from U1/U2 FGD absorber sump, sump pumps and agitator tripped
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Around 9am, it was reported by Ops to the FGD team that the U1/U2 absorber sump had filled to 100% level, was overflowing and the agitator and sump pumps had both tripped and could not be started. On investigation into what was causing the sump to continually overflow, it appeared to be a drain valve that was open on 'B' Gypsum extraction pump, even though this was the standby pump ('A' was in-service although was actually tripped by accident when trying to locally operate valves to ensure their position). The loss of the absorber sump (sump pumps and sump agitator unavailable) means there was no start permissive on U1 or U2 FGD therefore this immediately became a P1 notification.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Work was immediately progressed to pump out and unbog the sump agitator. The sump was returned to service by c. 4pm.
Recommendations for further actions:
A) Regardless of reason, whenever the sump is filled to 100%, the agitator and sump pumps trip and cannot be restarted until the sump level becomes within 'operable range' i.e. there needs to be manual intervention by using a temporary pump to pump out contents of the sump. This is a detriment and a plant mod should be considered that would allow the pumps and agitator to remain operable, even if the sump becomes 100% full and/or overflows. (FGD team)
B) The cause of the sump getting overwhelmed and hence overflowing needs to be investigated by the Operations team. First investigations into the probable cause of continual overflowing on the morning of 29/06 suggest the 'B' Gypsum extraction pump (was the standby pump) drain valve was open and slurry was flowing at high rate from this drain. When this valve was closed by the operator, the sump ceased to overflow.

TITLE: Danger to an employee when backfilling a pit with an excavator
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
english see appendix: 2023_04_04 of incident_CCGT_DE_KWI_33518_EN

An excavation pit measuring approx. 5 by 5 metres was backfilled on the power plant site after a cold condensate pipe repair. The pit had a shallow embankment on the east side for getting in and out. On the north and south sides, the pit was correctly embanked with a slope of approx. 60° (1.2 m by 2 m) in accordance with DGUV-R 101-604.
The western side was covered by a smoothly cut asphalt surface approx. 20 cm thick. This side was not sloped, but the wall was vertical.

The soil was compacted in the entire area of the pit and beyond.

An employee of a partner company was working inside the approx. 2 metre deep pit with a vibratory plate. Another employee of the construction company was standing outside the pit.

At the same time, an excavator operator was adding backfill material to the pit with the excavator shovel.


1. in the opinion of an inspection team, the stability of the western vertical pit wall did not meet the requirements of the applicable building regulations DGUV-V 38 and DGUV-R 101-604.
 

A risk of (partial) burial for the person in the pit was suspected.

2. the employee in the pit was close to the moving excavator shovel and could in principle be hit by the shovel. He was focussed on the compaction work. Therefore, he did not have a permanent view of the moving excavator shovel. This was an acute risk.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Immediate measures:
The work was stopped. A safety meeting was held with the excavator operator and the employees on site. The excavator operator discussed whether the western pit wall was stable or whether the employee could be endangered by any sliding wall material. The excavator operator's assessment differed from that of the safety inspection team.
Furthermore, the concern was expressed that the employee could be hit and injured by an unplanned movement of the nearby excavator shovel, e.g. in the event that the excavator shovel could move uncontrollably due to a sudden health problem of the excavator operator. The construction team was asked to minimise this risk by increasing the distance to the moving excavator bucket as much as possible. The work was completed without accident.
Further measures: Safety dialogue with the excavator operator on 13.4.2023
- Clarification of the stability of the pit
- Clarification of the technical safety measures on the excavator: How is it ensured that the excavator does not make any uncontrolled movements, e.g. if hydraulic lines fail?
Result: All hydraulic parts of the excavator are protected by shut-off valves (safe closed). In the event of a sudden drop in pressure, the affected part is "frozen" in the last position. Work would be stopped immediately.
How and at what intervals are the safety devices checked?
Before starting any excavator work, the mechanical functions of the excavator are checked by activating them. The safety functions are checked annually by an external authorised person. (Protocol of the last inspection in accordance with BetrSichV has been submitted)
- Refresher on the occupational safety policy and objectives of Uniper and the Irsching power plant for the partner company: Safe work and no accidents
- Discussion of the acute risk to employees from the excavator shovel moving nearby.
Result: The pit was large enough. The work inside the pit and the excavator work could have been carried out at a sufficient distance from each other. After the safety stop, the work was continued at a sufficient distance and completed without any accidents.
A position below the excavator shovel - even for a short time - must always be ruled out!  When working in special conditions, e.g. manual excavation with excavator support, work in the pit must be interrupted during excavation and constant visual contact must be maintained in both directions.
- A work permit was available. A risk assessment was available on site (dyn. II). The construction team had completed the initial instruction and had been briefed at the work site by the power plant's contact person.
- The personal protective equipment was worn correctly in accordance with the power plant standard and the risk assessment. In addition to the standard PPE, hearing protection was worn due to the noise hazard caused by the vibration work.
- Management system factor: A few years ago, Uniper still had a construction expert who visited the southern sites on a daily basis and as required. He supported the construction measures with his expertise and labour capacity or took over their execution. The on-site presence was particularly helpful for the sites. This service was discontinued. An architectural firm is currently in charge of construction projects. However, the support focuses on the planning and documentation of comparatively complex measures. An on-site presence is very rare. It should be examined whether a construction expert could be employed to support the Uniper sites in the south (power plants, hydropower, storage facilities).

TITLE: DCMR-Company notification detection CBL in double wall of underground transport pipeline, intention to place mobile tank (incident no.1068656)
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Following the invocation of detection on CBL in the double pipe wall, dosing at UCML has been interrupted, and soil and pipe investigations have been commissioned to determine whether soil contamination may have occurred, and to find and repair the pipe break. This investigation is currently taking place.
However, any interruption in CBL dosing is at the expense of fouling. Therefore, Uniper plans to have a standard temporary mobile storage tank (approx. 21 m3) installed by fa. Logisticon with dosing system, which will be set to the regular pulse chlorination dosing programme. This will ensure that the maximum total volume of stored CBL is not exceeded. This temporary mobile system serves to bridge the gap until repair and restoration of the old functionalities. (Uniper has previously had good experience with this in about 2010.) It is estimated that this will take about 8 weeks in total.

Chlorine bleach lye (CBL) has been licensed to Uniper Maasvlakte for use as an antifouling agent in cooling water. For this purpose, CBL (150 g/l) is stored in bulk in two above-ground storage tanks with a combined maximum storage volume of 125 m3 (cf. environmental change dd 12.12.2018).
From tank 12/A, CBL is fed via underground double-walled pipes to 2 cooling water intake systems (UCML and EFM1/2). From tank 15, CBL is supplied to the cooling water intake system of MPP3 via underground double-wall pipes.
The present report concerns the piping system from tank 12/A to UCML.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Legal, monitoring and reporting (Non-compliance of obligations)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Supply to UCML stopped. Investigation started into pipe burst and whether soil contamination occurred.

Oil barriers were set up at the Ickinger weir, at the Mühltal power station and in Großhesselohe.

Flow velocity at Pullach power station reduced.
Dredger replaced.

Failure of the inverters doesn't cause a direct issue, but means the wellhead is on mains bypass with no backup.

TITLE: U6 IP Bypass system Safety Valves Lifting
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
U6 PN off time 23:59hrs. At 23:57hrs the IP bypass Function Group deactivated (event message received), IP bypass SOV & CV and Warming Line V/v all Shut and Process Safety interlock activated. 
IP steam system Safety Valves lifted. (ST out of service, HP bypass valve Open).
At the DCS the IP bypass system spray water Valve recorded 90% Open but with little or no flow. 
At -3MW Generated Load a GT Trip was initiated from the Unit Desk.
The IP Safety Valves closed almost immediately.
On investigation it was determined the Condenser neck temperature had recorded a >Max 2 Temperature, which had deactivated the IP Bypass Function Group. At the IP bypass system spraywater Valve, the valve / positioner linkage was found not set correctly, the linkage cone was not in the correct position. The positioner output was asking for 90% but the valve was physically shut. The linkage cone was refitted, the valve was stroked from the CCR to confirm correct operation.
A notification was raised to check valve positioner linkage at next opportunity.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Environmental noise & vibration (Inc. complaints, technical breaches or affecting ecosystems)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: see case description above

TITLE: External damage due to burst pipe Gelsenwasser pipe to FW-Ltg. Recklinghausen Tannenstraße
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On-site appointment with Mr Schimmelpfennig (Provinzial expert).
The damage site of Gelsenwasser AG in the Tannenstr./Tannenhof area was inspected. The directly neighbouring shaft of Uniper Wärme was opened during the on-site visit and the situation was presented. Significant quantities of water had been washed into the neighbouring shaft from the Gelsenwasser damage area over a long period of time, which had also introduced massive amounts of sand and sludge into the shaft.
From there, the water and sand entered the neighbouring shafts via the jacket pipes of the district heating pipeline. Initial drying attempts over several days were unsuccessful. The extent of the damage was still easily recognisable at the time of the inspection.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
At the construction site, vacuum drying was quickly rejected as an option for technical reasons and it was jointly determined that repairs could only be carried out using the open construction method.
A second shaft was opened and inspected to substantiate the extent of the damage.

UWG will draw up a repair concept in the next few days and calculate the costs based on the currently valid contract with the framework contract partners.
These will be forwarded to Mr Schimmelpfennig shortly, including the personnel and deployment costs incurred to date.

TITLE:
Enfield issued with an SIR from National Grid. 
UTG & ABB concluding technical investigation EXTENDED 28/02/2022
CASE_DESCRIPTION: An incident occurred during the transformer testing which led to a huge MVAR swing of +160 to -78. This caused the grid voltage to drop from 136KV to 122KV. National Grid have now issued us with a Significant Incident Report to investigate and provide information on what happened and what went wrong.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
On the 18th November 2021 while carrying out Grid Code Compliance testing and with the unit operating at approximately 410MW and +220MVAr (lagging region) at the generator terminals (400MW and 120Mvar at the connection point) it was unexpectedly found during these planned tests, while the unit was settling after a tap of the the generator step up transformer was performed from taps 3 to 2, the Stator Current Limiter (SIL) within ABB Unitrol P excitation system became active and pulled the reactive power back to 0MVAr with a subsequent overshoot into the leading region (up until -70MVAr as shown as the orange signal in the below high speed recording). The reasoning for the large overshot is thought to be because of the high gain control of the SIL function. 

As a resultant of the SIL activation the effect unfortunately reduced both generator terminal and station board voltages by approximately 13% of nominal ( i.e. 21kV) and consequently reduced the 132kV system network voltage suddenly from 137kV down to 122kV. To counter act the effect of the SIL, the generator step up transformer was progressively tapped via controlled instructions from myself to our control room from taps 2 to 5 to increase the voltage back to as close to nominal and thus removing the unit from the SIL operating action. 

This counter action brought both the generator terminal and station board voltages relatively close nominal voltage and brought the 132kV system network voltage steadily back to 136kV, and the unit was left at position after NG Central Control Room (CCR) instructed Enfield not to carry out any further tapings. We inform NG CCR at this point that we would like to tap the unit back further towards unity power factor (i.e. tap 5 to 13) as there was a concern that the SIL could operate again if the system voltage were to alter thus moving the position of the reactive power at the generator terminals back towards the lagging region, however we were informed by NG CCR not to do this until all customers had been contacted and therefore the unit was left and no further tapping performed again until approximately 1 and half hours later.
