TITLE: Safety round by invitation of project team member (Chrome6)
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Following invitation from project team member last week to walk a safety round together on the DFB1 project.
Walked round alone because project team member was stuck in a meeting that ran out (so walked round alone).
(New appointment to follow)

Observations below:

- On arrival me via central storage plate work permits checked which activities were going on. (All permit folders were empty while which activities were going on at the construction site)
- Scaffold construction was at work
- Mourik civil was at work
- Newes was at work
- Miller was at work
- The construction site was well enclosed with building fences. Everyone working used the correct PPE's and the necessary extra harnesses.
- Then I went to Newes' welding tent and found people not wearing the right protective equipment. What stood out and immediate actions:
- That people were welding and grinding on stainless steel in the room without using proper protection
- In addition, there were about four people walking in this room completely without protection.
- Had work stopped for a while to get an overview of exactly which ancillary activities were taking place here and why in the tent.
- First asked whether they were aware of the dangers/substances released during welding and grinding of stainless steel
- Whether they had thought about this beforehand (work plan/toolbox/risk assessment) was not the case.
- I briefly reminded them of the dangers and that it is not desirable to have more people in the tent than just those directly involved in the welding and grinding activities.
- I then asked why so many people were working in the tent while grinding and welding stainless steel.
- Answer I got was that in this area was the rack with bolts nuts and flanges and that they were busy greasing bolts and nuts.
- I replied that this is not the right place to do this at the same time, especially if no protection is worn.
- I then agreed to fetch our chromium6 protocol and the necessary toolboxes we have on this subject and hand them over to the foreman so that he can share this toolbox with his people and hand them in to Johanna de Hoop as done by means of a checklist (which was attached).
- Overall impression of the building site is cluttered because here and there is dirt on the site that has been loosely dumped or just put away here a fixed point storage of construction waste would be a good solution.


You can use the link below to access the procedure.


Health and Safety : S09. Chromium 6 activities and measures (16)
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Toxic substance or CMR substance (carcinogenic, mutagenic, reproduction toxic)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
- Called people together and asked if they were aware of the dangers involved in grinding and/or welding stainless steel. and not using or not using the correct PPE.
- Highlighted and issued the Uniper chrome 6 procedure and toolbox with instructions that the foreman give this toolbox.
Informed project team member of this immediately and also emailed this procedure and documents.

TITLE: Water treatment plant  - Failure of effluent dosing pipework
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Whilst dealing with an analyser problem in the WTP it was noticed that there was water spraying from somewhere approximately 3 metres above ground level.  Further investigation identified that it was from the dosing pipework for effluent system 2 which was in service and in the process of neutralising the effluent tank.  I immediately went to local control room and stopped effluent system 2 and made it unavailable. The leak was from plastic pipework that travels over the top from the pumps to the ejector skid.  This pipework fails regularly as a result of movement when the pumps stop/start or a dose of either caustic or HCL is applied.  At the time of the leak the PH of the tank was 13 so it was dosing with HCL.  The leak would have been a mixture of HCL and motive water.  The area is always barriered off due to the regular failings off the plastic pipework used on this system. Notification raised for repair to be carried out.  Improvements to the plastic pipework need to be made as this is a regular occurrence.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Toxic substance or CMR substance (carcinogenic, mutagenic, reproduction toxic)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: System made unavailable.  Redesign of pipework to mitigate this issue happening again

TITLE: Employee complaining of back pain.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
See description from attending first aider:
13:02 -  I was requested by James lang to attend the 3rd floor
13:05 - When attending IP he explained that he could not move position, he was sitting very still in his chair stating that he feels like his back has gone.

•	Initial questions asked: 
•	Where is the pain? - Strip around the middle of the back
•	Any tingling in arms and legs? - No
•	Can you move arms and legs? - Yes
•	What other pains or symptoms do you have? - Back area hurts when breathing
•	Any medial history? - Asthma 
•	Do you have inhaler with you? - Yes
•	Have you carried out any unusual activity or lifting today? - No

13:08 - Call was made to 111 to establish what was the best course of action which was initiated by IP. 
13:13 - IP administrated his own paracetamol to ease the pain
13:18 - IP was helped to his feet to see if there was any issues with walking, this seemed to help and loosen of what seemed like a muscle spasm. 
13:39 - Decided to be taken to hospital which a member of Uniper personnel escorted IP to A+E department of Chester hospital.

Also see following report from Line Manager:
-	At approx. 13:00 on Tuesday 18th Feb, the IP raised concerns to the team that he was having some difficulty in his chair and that his back was seizing up.
-	He was showing signs of discomfort and pain so a station first aider attended. Following discussions that the IP stated that was having pain when breathing but was walking around, the decision was made to take the IP to Hospital. A colleague drove the IP and stayed with him to ensure he was settled and OK.
-	Later in the day the IP informed me that he had been assessed by a doctor and had an Xray which was clear and so the doctor had suggested he has a deep muscle strain and should apply heat and cooling.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: See case description. No further actions.

inspection around the Uniper coal fields. The inspector was picked up by yours truly and together we made a tour of
the coal fields.

Discussed;
Supply regime, this starts almost every week on Thursday or Friday and then continues into the weekend (Average 50 kt)
Pulp regime.
Upcoming supply which starts Thursday to the A field.
Cleaning regime approach roads, currently a Sagro sweeper truck drove around.
C field, this will be excavated differently compared to the A and B field, excavation from the top side compared to the side of A and B field and so the top side will not be pulped (anymore).
is not (anymore) bepulpted.  Current test operation with excavator C took place.

During the tour, the inspector drew my attention several times to the fact that outside the unannounced inspections, they do more inspections from a distance,
i.e. from outside the Uniper site and using binoculars.

Showing;
Coal fields,
A1 with co-firing heaps.
C field, also showing we had a brewing spot earlier today which had since been dug out.

15:30 F. de Croon dropped off at porter's lodge.

Hoping to have informed everyone sufficiently with this.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
High rainfall going into the catalysts, resulting in contamination from the plates.

Follow up with mechanical team- the catalysts are to be moved to the REU warehouse pending disposal.
Ops carried out extra checks throughout the day.

TITLE: Field fire not far from ESCH B 5
CASE_DESCRIPTION: A grain field caught fire not far from the ESCH B 5. It was caused by a combine harvester during the harvest. The fire was 5 metres from the fence and approx. 20 metres from the borehole.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Fire / Explosion (affecting local inhabitants ,ecosystems or surrounding environment)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The fire brigade was alerted by a third party and immediately began extinguishing the fire with the support of the farmers (slurry tankers with water); an OGE employee also noticed the fire and drove to ESCH B 5 and coordinated the fire protection for the drilling site.

TITLE: Risk of crushing / cutting when operating fittings
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During a tour of the station, a group of fittings was discovered in / under an improper insulation / sheet metal enclosure. These do not allow the hand levers to be operated as the first valve cannot generally be operated and the second valve would cause cuts to the sheet metal when operated. Dryer 2 Station Bierwang.

IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Employees informed

TITLE: Damage to transmitter box
CASE_DESCRIPTION: When reversing with the workshop vehicle and a condensate trailer, the right-hand wing mirror of the vehicle caught on the transmitter box. The mirror was broken and the transmitter box was also slightly damaged. The pressure of the transmitter in the cabinet was 125 bar, there was no gas leakage.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: After the damage had occurred, the workshop vehicle was driven out of the area and the damaged area was checked for leaks using leak spray. The broken box was secured and reported to the company. The incident was discussed with the people involved and they were made aware of their duty of care when reversing. Furthermore, the incident was discussed with the employees in the company and the source of danger was pointed out.

TITLE: Fire brigade operation in Huntorf
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The fire service control centre was informed of suspicious smoke above the power plant by a passing motorist. The power plant was in compressor operation at the time and the smoke was water vapour from the recooling system.
The sequence of events was as follows:
15:18 hrs Call from Mr Schwarting (Oldenburg control centre) that smoke had been sighted.
-> The fire brigade had already been alerted at this time and was on its way to Huntorf.
15:20 The standby ( T. Entrup ) was informed.
15:21 The fire brigade called to check whether the power station was in operation.
15:24 The AGN standby ( O. Kuhlmann ) was informed.
15:44 Feedback from Mr T. Entrup that it was again steam from the cooling water system, but that this was completely normal.
15:56 O. Kuhlmann, who was already in Huntorf at this time, was informed.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The fire brigade control centre is once again made aware of reports of suspicious smoke and advised to first ask the Etzel control centre about the status of the system.

TITLE: Delays in meeting PN sync time and further imbalance on run-up
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The unit had a PN sync time of 16:00 after the return to service from the CW pipe repair . The delay was remitted in half hour periods on 4 occasions until the decision was made to remit the sync time out to 20:00. Our trading colleagues pulled the PN and re-scheduled it for 20:00. Unit synchronised at 20:00 and ran up until a delay was incuured on the ST program, this was due to the seal steam pressure being at 2.9 bar as opposed to the required 3 bar in Step 8 of the ST program. The delay caused a temperature imbalance between the boiler and ST ESV/Control valves not usually present on a cold start holding the ESV's from opening as required.

TITLE: Unit 6 HP Bypass Water Injection Control Valve logic modification fault.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Unit 6 HP Bypass Water Injection Control Valve logic was requested to be changed to match Unit 7's, that has been on trial. 
The logic is designed in such a way there is a test facility (a switch to turn the modified logic on/off). This was in place so that the logic could be switched on when DCS engineers where on site, during a run up, to monitor it and tune it if required. 
With the test bit off, the new logic would not be active and the control would not be changed. 
The logic was copied, but an error was made and the test facility was accidently left on. During Unit 6's run up after its outage, the spray valve wasn't operating. This is when the 'test' logic was still realised to be on. The test facility was turned off and that allowed the spray to function, stopping the unit from tripping on high temperatures.

TITLE: Possible, impermissible pressure increase in burner oil supply
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Block 5 is currently being commissioned with oil levels 20 and 30. The oil supply for each level remains in operation until the respective coal mills are at operating temperature. The oil burners on the respective level then go out of operation.
The coal mill on level 40 is then put into operation without an oil fire. Finally, the coal mill on level 10 goes into operation. The oil firing is required again for this.
As long as the main oil supply (block 0) including the booster pumps (block 5) are in operation, there is a controlled oil pressure of 17 bar before each oil level.
If an oil burner level is now out of operation, the oil control valve upstream of the oil burner level closes in the last programme step. If this is now completely closed, as is currently the case at level 30, the cold oil is trapped in the oil pipe between the oil control valve and the respective quick-acting oil shut-off valves of the individual burners (approx. 80 m pipe, DN 100). This cold oil then heats up due to the radiating heat from the boiler and begins to expand. This causes the pressure to rise to >40 bar (design pressure of the oil system).
If damage occurs in this area, the oil can escape in an uncontrolled manner. Since in this case the mechanically controlled start-up control valve, which is installed in the bypass of the electronically controlled main control valve, regulates an oil pressure of 5.5 bar, it will always allow oil to flow in the event of damage.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Hazardous substance, which is non-toxic, non-CMR substance (carcinogenic, mutagenic, reproduction toxic)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Immediate measure:
Pay attention to the oil pressure in the levels. This rises to >20 bar due to the tight-closing oil control valve caused by heat radiation, so that the oil pressure >max. warning appears on the signalling monitor.
Action: after oil fire OFF, move the oil control valve to a 5% OPEN position on the levels so that the oil pressure in the main oil system can relax.
When starting the oil burner via the function group, the oil control valve automatically moves back to the CLOSED position in the first step.

Further measures:
Extensive conversion in accordance with TÄM 50117218 / Asset Improvement PN55190

TITLE: Like for like actuator issue
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Up until 2014 site had a problem in the Winter with the wellheads tripping on low temperature when the wellhead flow control valve was closed, usually when the DCS Stop or Adjustable Setpoint were reached at Pmin or Pmax. 

This trapped the gas between the wellhead and the control valve stopping the normal convection flows of warmer gas between the caverns. 

If the ambient temperature was below zero this static gas would cool to 0 degrees and activate the low temperature wellhead trip which is only intended to prevent low gas temperatures in the cavern and production tubing caused by a large, prolonged withdrawal.

To remedy this problem the trip was made ‘smart’ and was only activated if the flow control valve was open and it was deactivated when the valve was closed and no withdrawal could be occurring but this required a closed limit indication adding to the actuators. (see attached)

Since then 8 replacement actuator controllers were ordered that don’t come with the limits as standard and they have been in the stores for some time until one was fitted on H403 and were identified that the limits (there may have been an open limit fitted too) were missing.

The absence of the closed limit switch would not create a hazard and it would just generate the potential for an unnecessary trip.

This has been recorded as it is a case of a like for like replacement that isn’t.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Replacement actuator controllers ordered with correct limits set.

The slide was opened (or was still open) with a brick so that the water drained away from the box 5 floor. The floor of box 5 had been sprayed on.

TITLE: Unanticipated effect from altered Operator set point
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
An initial problem was detected with the GRUs where they were quickly dumping >6m3 hour of cold teg into the regen units on start up, which if wet could lead to a pressure trip. A modification was prepared for tuning out some poor control on the flow limiter on the stripping column.  However, it was not implemented because on closer inspection, the Rich TEG buffer vessel level Operator-adjustable set point was sitting at a low level.  Increasing the set point from 380 mm to 500 mm smoothed the start up process and prevented the pressure trips.

After a period of time, Operators detected that during the shut down of the GRUs, the TEG HP pumps were repeatedly turning on and off.  Investigation identified that this was because the auto-changeover setpoint of 1m3/hr was now being matched by the flow of Rich TEG from the buffer tank due to the changed setpoint (as described above).

There was no safety consequence to the pumps repeatedly changing over.  However, there was a potential plant damage risk.  Hence, this observation has been raised to determine any additional learning relating to the sites control of modification set points, including operator adjustable set points.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: No further immediate action required.  Further investigation of the installations control of set point modifications will be conducted by the Lead Process Engineer, DCS Engineer and Production Manager.

TITLE: Three-pole short circuit at 6kV transformer station block 6 after inserting the earthing switch
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The 6kV transformer station for the site power supply unit 6 was to be commissioned on 9 June 2021 at 10:00 a.m. The work permit (SAP number 76059441 process 50) and flow chart (see appendix flow chart IBN transformer) for commissioning were available to the power plant operator.

In order to better understand the near-accident, it should be mentioned in advance that we were working at an interface between the operator KWIR and the new Block 6 construction project. On the operator side, two new NATUS switchgear units 00BBN07 & 00BBM07 were installed in the PCC container/switchgear unit Block 4 (two for redundancy) with temporary cable labelling. Switchgear 00BBN07 was tested and commissioned by a specialised company approx. 5 weeks ago.

The construction site transformer block 6 was scheduled to be put into operation on 09/06/2021. Switchgear panel 1 (in the site transformer building Block 6) is fed via the NATUS switchgear (in the PCC container Block 4) 00BBN07 and are connected to each other with the cable with the temporary cable number 16. The switchgear in the site transformer building Block 6 has temporary labelling.
The commissioning of the 6kV building site transformer was successful as such.

An E-master and the VEFK were present in the PCC container on the part of KW Irsching. The opposite side of this interface was coordinated/accompanied by the E+L site management for Block 6.

However, what we realised during commissioning is that there is a special condition that harbours a high hazard potential. The NATUS switchgear has a terminal contact which is responsible for the mutual interlocking. This interlocking does not yet exist because the original target address for switchgear 60BBA has de facto not yet been installed. 00BBN07 is initially to be used for the construction current and will be used regularly at a later date.

In order to guarantee the function, the contact was bridged with the following risk.
If the switchgear 00BBN07 is switched on and the earthing switch on switch panel 1 in the site power supply building block 6 is active, an earth fault or short circuit is triggered.

The VEFK informed the site management (Block 6) about this critical condition. As the measure could not be solved technically, an organisational measure was requested in the form of written switching instructions, including naming the group of people who are authorised to switch in the transformer building. In addition, the transformer (switch panel 2) was to be switched off again. It should be switched off at around 3 pm.

At around 2.45 p.m., the team met again on site and the switching operation was discussed.

The site management was in the site transformer building block 6, while our electrician in the control room took the switching call via mobile phone.

The procedure was agreed as follows:

- Switch panel 2 (transformer) OFF
- Switch panel 1 OFF
- Switchgear 00BBN07 remote command wait OFF
- Feed switch 00BBN07 in test position

The near-accident occurred because switch panel 1 was switched off and the earthing switch of switch panel 1 was switched on immediately afterwards without first checking that there was no voltage. This resulted in a three-pole short circuit to earth. Instead of giving the feedback in the switching dialogue after switching off switch panel 1 and having the next switching operation carried out via the control room, an incorrect operation was carried out (see appendix Circuit diagram 09.06.21).

Nobody was injured. Various faults were triggered on the operator side due to undervoltage. The faults were rectified very quickly by the shift.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Decommissioning of site transformer block 6

TITLE: U4 Kue grit blast waste, failure to segregate waste as per agreed method resulting in additional work to properly segregate waste.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Kue a sub contractor to Doosan undertook grit blast of the primary and secondary platens in U4 boiler. Agreed method was to sweep and bag waste and transport to 'duct bags' on pallets to be segregated on site, this was part of method statement and confirmed again just prior to work. Work was undertaken from Friday 20/5/22 to Sunday 22/5/22. Altrad provided resource to collect the waste on pallets and to remove and store onsite. The work area was inspected at the end of the job, the main focus was the prep, however it was noted that the scaffold was clean, free of waste grit and the when asked if the plastic sheeting had been removed we were told "yes" Kue also made a point to say that the Altrad resource had been very helpful, as the Altrad resource had been set up specifically to remove the waste it was assumed that this therefore had gone well. TITLE: Ratcliffe 2020 EU ETS Gas Turbine Oil CO2 error
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Following submission of the 2020 verified Annual Emissions Report on 23rd March 2021 to the Environment Agency, an error was identified on the report. The error relates to the permitted fuel, F7 Gas Oil.  Activity data is taken from the turbine flow measurement system (GO FM1 and FM2) recording gas oil consumption to each gas turbine. The units of measure are recorded  in gallons, gallons are then subsequently converted to litres and finally converted to tonnes.  For the 2020 annual submission on 23rd March 2021 the  conversion factor of 4.54609 from gallons to litres was omitted from the calculation.  This resulted in an un-intentional under report of 664.04 tonnes of CO2.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The Annual Emissions Report was corrected, returned to the verifier for re-verification and subsequently submitted to the Environment Agency on 28th April 2021 (in advance of the deadline - 30th April 2021).  The additional EU Allowances were transferred to the registry account.  The additional EU Allowances were surrendered by the deadline of 30th April 2021.

To prevent a re-occurrence of an inaccurate gas turbine oil CO2 calculation, the spreadsheet used for calculating CO2 at Ratcliffe was revised to make the calculation steps of gas turbine oil more transparent and automated by avoiding the need for manual entry.

TITLE: Runtime error with process gas SAV of machine 1 and 2
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During the quarterly SAV maintenance, it was determined that the running time (closing time) of the process gas SAV was longer than the prescribed 2 seconds. If the time was exceeded, it would be possible for the pressure to switch from the pressure side to the suction side.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: As a result of this finding, identical SAVs were also analysed and tested. The runtime error was detected in several SAVs. The quick exhaust valves were removed and the cylinders of the SAV were filled directly via the EO line, thus ruling out the possibility that the fault was in the SAV. Another reason for the long running time is the long line path. By installing a second quick exhaust valve directly on the switching block of the valve, the running time could be maintained again. As a result of this realisation, all the affected valves were modified.

TITLE: Specific hand fire alarm in Heavy's containers is not included in the cause and effect list of Heavy's hazards
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
In the heavy container in EH3, specific hand-held fire detectors have been installed. Due to the danger of the fuel in combination with incipient fire, it is stipulated in the UPD that the heavy's installations should be controlled by the fire alarm system to terminate the fuel supply to the unit.

This is achieved by a 2-detector dependency whereby 2 automatic detectors in alarm the fire alarm system signals the DCS that this condition is active and DCS then controls function blocks to stop the fuel supply to the unit and go into bypass operation outside near the heavy tank.

Because the definition of hand-held fire alarms is that they can only be operated by a human action, within the NEN2535 (fire alarm standard) a hand-held fire alarm has been put on the same level as 2-alarm dependency or verified fire alarm.

 Because these hand-held fire detectors are fitted in the containers, it is
 desirable/necessary that these hand-held fire detectors ALSO signal to the DCS that a verified fire alarm is present.

Now the situation is that you as an employee are working in the container and a fire breaks out and you press the manual fire detector but the fuel supply is not stopped, unfortunately you have to wait a while until the fire has reached sufficient size that 2 automatic detectors have been activated and then the fuel supply is terminated.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
We will write an SA for the modification of the fire alarm system software.

Project teams do not communicate fully and too often the right expertise from within Uniper Benelux is not brought in. The project teams then disappear, leaving behind systems that do not work properly without proper documentation (as-built) and proper commissioning.

The recommendation is therefore that project teams should be assisted by expertise from UBX and the monitoring of proper AS-BUILT revision should be better secured from UBX and certainly not left to the project teams.

TITLE: Humber Oil Refinery (P66) Condensate Valve ESD Trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The pressure of the steam to the Uniper heat exchanger rose to 4 bar and this caused the condensate ESD valve trip to shutting off the return line to HOR. HOR provide the steam for this system.
The system is designed to protect the steam pipework from gas infiltration caused by a tube break in the heat exchanger. However due to system design the pressure monitoring is on the steam side of the heat exchanger and is set at 4 bar, the system normally runs at approx 3 .5 bar.
The issue would be cold gas to the refinery which should be supplied at above 0 Deg C  ,with the valve shutoff the gas temperature remained above that.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Temperature Extreme (Inc. Hot or cold surfaces, gases and environments)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The system was reset then it tripped again after 1/2 hr ,, therefore contact was made with HOR who provide the steam to our system and we advised them to lower the steam pressure. They looked at how this could be done but decided for there current process the benefits of a slightly higher LP steam pressure out weighed the negatives from colder gas.

TITLE: Class Break Valve Stroke Test Failure
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Class break valve stroke test issues over the weekend – further investigation at next opportunity JaR/CB. JaR / CB investigation – scaffold required.  RAMS prepped for Altrad.  With permit office, safety document yesterday -scaffold built.  SIS digital output card card replaced yesterday – tested fine thereafter (further testing today).  Going into fault when solenoid deenergised – Theory: no reverse diode or diode in card failed – self check of card picking up EMF from solenoid being de-energised and incorrectly thinking open circuit.  Potential to add a redundant card to allow auto-switchover in the vent of card failures.  Loop delivers self-check rather than SIF.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Issue no.1 - Initiation of the partial stoke test command from the DCS caused an immediate channel fault on the card when the solenoid holding EKG50AA193 was de-energised roughly 1 in 5 times. This caused the partial stroke test to fail and cancelled the test.

Root cause – age related electronics failure, more detail on the likely electronic failure mode in attachment.

The card did its job by detecting a fault and generating an alarm, and causing the partial stroke check to fail. 

Repair – Replaced the SIS card. This has been tested 20+ times now with no channel fault. 

Issue no. 2 – The partial stroke test was initiated and the valve started its partial stroke test travel. The partial stroke test reached the partial limit switch and started to return to the fully open position as designed. The partial stroke test failed before the open limit switch was reached. 

Root cause – The DCS has timers set to meet the partial limit switch and timer to fully complete the test. The return to fully open was occasionally not being reached in the correct time. Trending the event logs, this has been an issue, and is a plant wide issue with incorrectly configured valve movement supervision timings. They are nearly all on their default values. There are no SRS requirements for opening the valve, and no signs of increasing movement duration over time.

TITLE: PSO - Common ammonia plant forwarding manifold high pressure
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During shutdown of unit 3 (last unit) NH3 forwarding pump discharge pressure high alarms received (CP014 & CP015.  Tank pressure and accumulator pressures both steady. Local plant checks conducted and local pressure indications aligned with Ovation readings. No evidence of plant distress or any HRV's having operated. Over the following 1.5 hrs the pressures on the forwarding manifold restored to normal at around NH3 tank pressure before the erratic swings started again with no ammonia flow
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Monitor plant condition, investigate cause. Unable to draw conclusions as to the reason. Open up to a wider investigation

TITLE: PSO - U2 Seal Oil System pipework swinging during test
CASE_DESCRIPTION: When carrying out the turbine lub and seal oil cut-in tests it was reported that the pipework was swinging and noisy
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Violent noise and knocking reported shortly after starting to conduct the routine Saturday turbine oil pump tests on Unit 2. DC seal oil pump had but run for approx 15 seconds before being armed and starting the tests. Aux POP was in service and the unit operator was unable to arm the AC seal oil pump without it cutting back into service. Pipework around the main lub oil tank was knocking loudly and seal oil pipework was shaking violently throughout the system (see attached video) although the H2 seal oil diff and seal oil pressure appeared steady. Running either the aux POP or AC seal oil pumps either in isolation or together made any difference. Knocking appeared most severe at either spill valve 367A or DC Seal oil pump discharge NRV 357B. Able to take turbine off barring and take o/s lub oil pumps, so eliminated knocking as being due to main oil system. As soon as the DC seal oil pump was started the distress in the system stopped. The DC pump was left in for a few minutes before being stopped. Once out of service the system remained 'normal'. Suspect the the cause of the distress was possibly 'hammer' from air in the section of seal oil pipework associated with the DC discharge pipework before teeing into the seal oil cooler to seal pipework? Or possibly the DC pump NRV 357B passing back (although it can be confirmed that no seal oil pumps were reverse rotating when out of service.

TITLE: Maxum Hazardous Area Classification Pressurization / Purge
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Purge system on the analyser- the pressure gauge on the front of the analyser Purge air has always read “0”- confirmed by site documentation dating back to 2011. 

The Hazardous area code on the analyser contains a  “p” for pressurisation.

The Purge air regulator is connected directly into a monitoring system inside the analyser electronics enclosure ( this system is currently disabled) 

The analyser is installed in a zone 2 area. 

So the equipment has been operating in a zone 2 area without the protection system operational.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The idea of the purge monitoring system is to maintain a positive pressure differential inside the electrical enclosure as it is full of uncertified electrical equipment, such as valves, power supplies etc. 

The protection concept for this appears to be “p” (pressurisation)  and is stated in the Siemens manual as being a requirement if the analyser is installed in a zone 1 or zone 2 area. (it is in a zone 2) 

The regulator has been set at 5 psi for now, for the short term until we can commission the protection system, (if it is found that this should be enabled).

TITLE: Oil leakage in the track bearing oil circuit at turbine 6 in Kachlet
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

Approximately 30 litres of oil escaped. The cause was a leaking metal pipe fitting.
Finally, an internal inspection of the earthed generator was carried out and no oil contamination was found. There was no environmental pollution on the outside (especially in the water)

TITLE: Oil leakage Irsching 4
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The generator in Irsching 4 is currently being repaired. To align the shaft in the course of this repair work, it was necessary to commission both the lifting oil and the bearing lubricating oil. The commissioning of the bearing oil was carried out in consultation with the Siemens generator technicians on site, who also arranged for this partial commissioning. The bearing oil was switched on with the upper bearing shield of the bearings still open.
After the bearing oil was switched on, a check was made to see whether oil was leaking or not (both by Siemens and the shift). The oil remained in operation to warm up the components. After approx. 10 minutes, the external runner of the shift checked the area again and realised that oil was now spraying out of the open bearing.
This was a splash of approx. 20-30 litres of lubricating oil.
Oil binder was immediately applied to the wetted areas (foundations) and cleaning began. The bearing oil was switched off for this process
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Switch off the bearing oil and apply oil binder. Furthermore, the leakage occurred in the ""oil-proof part"" of the block - i.e. if the leakage had been significantly larger, the oil would ultimately have run to the oil separator.

TITLE: Block 5 Drip leakage Flange connection HDU10
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During ongoing operation of unit 5, a leakage was detected at the flange connection from the motive steam line to HDU10 during a shift inspection, similar to the leakage at HDU20 on 13 November 2019 (see SynergiLife case 6778).
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
In consultation with the ZÜS, the block was taken out of service at the weekend and the defective flange seal and the expansion bolts on the HDU10 and, as a precaution, on the HDU20 were replaced by W&T.

The damage was presumably favoured by the frequent response of the HPU as a result of the vibration problems on the turbine after the 2021 overhaul.

As all expansion bolts were replaced during the 2020 shutdown due to presumably insufficient bolt tension on both HDUs as a result of SynergyLife case no. 6778, it was decided together with W&T to use a different type of seal and other expansion bolts with a higher torque (700Nm instead of 640Nm).

Due to the short-term availability of spare parts, the original seal and bolt type from stock was used on the HDU20 (without current damage). The conversion to the new type will take place during the 2022 shutdown.

A learning will be created.

The HDUs will continue to be monitored using a thermal imaging camera and displayed on the heat control centre.

TITLE:
Near-miss radiographic testing

Lucy Pipeline: RT testing (radiographic testing: X-ray or gamma radiation) in Scholven
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
As part of pipe construction work on the Lucy Pipeline, Evonik, as the operator of LIW, had to install a valve. Parts of the work to be carried out were outsourced to another subcontractor by Evonik (cutting, grinding and welding work, as well as testing of the non-destructive weld seams using RT testing (radiographic testing: X-ray or gamma radiation).

The work permits and necessary instructions required by Evonik were issued by West 1 as the site owner.

The incident occurred during the RT inspection: two parallel inspections by two different companies happened to be carried out simultaneously in a neighbouring area during the day. One client was Evonik, the other client was near the Sener/UTG works.

The neighbouring inspection by the GuD PIII project was registered and took place exclusively on the construction site. The colleagues from Evonik were informed shortly before the test, the radiation area of 20m was outside the workplace and outside the area cordoned off from the inspector.

The second test by the Evonik subcontractor was then carried out at around 14:00. Barriers were set up with flutter tape, although the road was not allowed to be cordoned off according to the company carrying out the work. According to the inspector of the GuD PIII project, there was an increased radiation exposure and it must be checked whether the work arrangements were properly coordinated and the danger zones clearly defined. Personal injury may have occurred. This requires information on the radiation source and the activity of the radiation source.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The health and safety coordinator for the PIII gas and steam turbine project consulted with the companies carrying out the work and pointed out the barriers.

TITLE: Service provider's workshop lorry drives into stream collector
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the outward journey on a dirt track at Moos 103, the employee drove off the road in the service vehicle without any other occupants due to the softened verge and the distraction of a telephone call. Visibility was limited due to the rain. As can be seen in the pictures, the vehicle overturned into the stream collector running parallel to the Isar Canal and the Birkenhof pond estate. The employee was able to leave the vehicle unharmed through the window of the driver's door after unfastening his seatbelt.
The employee stated that he was able to switch off the engine immediately and that no oil, diesel or other substances escaped from the vehicle. The doors and windows - with the exception of the upward-facing driver's window, which was used to exit the vehicle - were locked.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Wurzer Umwelt GmbH and Werkstatt GmbH immediately installed oil barriers (see appendix) to prevent the possible spread of contamination. Two walking excavators, a crane and two cable winches were used to recover the vehicle. The employees on site were instructed to constantly monitor possible fluid leaks during the recovery operation and to report them immediately if they were spotted - however, no fluids or other environmentally harmful substances escaped at any time.

TITLE: Main turbine hall waste oil tank
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The turbine waste oil tank high level alarm initiated at approx 1500hrs. The AUO was dispatched to check the level in the tank and he confirmed that the level was high but no chance of overflowing.
Considered transferring oil over the waste oil purification tank, however this tank was already full. 
Contacted Altrad to inform and check whether they were aware that the tank was full and needed emptying. Person responsible had left site but message was left for the following morning.
The wider shift team conducted further checks of the waste oil recovery tank systems to confirm that there was nothing draining such as oil cooler / coalescers etc. Nothing concerning was found across the four units.
At approx. 1930hrs it was observed that the turbine waste oil tank was overflowing.
Immediate action was taken to contain the oil within the local area and prevent ingress into the drains.
Altrad Boiler Ops were contacted to provide support with cleaning and responded quickly with a gulper. The oil spill and spill-dri was cleared.
The source of the problem was identified as a steam / water leak on  Unit 4 spray water booster pump which was causing the turbine waste oil tank to fill with water. This was balancing into the MBFP waste oil recovery tank, which in turn was being pumped into the turbine waste oil tank.
The unit 4 turbine waste oil tank was in a barriered area (associated with the leak causing the problem) and was consequently not checked as part of the operational check associated with the high level.
The turbine waste oil tank was covered with a tarpaulin to prevent further water ingress.
The site services team were contacted to arrange further support to assist the night shift with the follow up cleaning and lowering of the waste oil tank level below the high level alarm and monitoring / gulping of the main reject tunnel station water drainage of any carry over oil which was completed.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
U4 turbine waste oil tank covered with tarpaulin
Oil spill cleaned up and waste oil tank level lowered below high level alarm
Consider covering over the associated unit turbine waste oil tanks with some kind of liftable cover to prevent recurrence. The waste oil system is a supervised system for recovering oil when draining coolers and coalescers etc not for continually pumping leakage from other sources.
Consider some kind of bund arund around the main turbine hall waste oil tank and any options on alarms ie hi and hihi and bund alarm although this may not be feasable.

TITLE: PSNH - Station Mulsifyre Detection Air System
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The mulsifyre detection air systems depressurised resulting in the operation of most of road 4 mulsifyre water systems and very nearly all of road 3 generator transformer associated fire systems, however operation of those systems was averted in this incident. The incident occurred following the release of and isolation of station general service air compressor no.2 which had been supplying the back-up alternative air supply to all three main station mulsifyre systems. The standby general service air system had not been started and this resulted in the GS air system and in turn the mulsifyre air detection system depressurising which caused the operation of road 4 mulsifye systems. The root cause of the incident being that the three individual mulsifyre detection air top up compressors are all unavailable through breakdown. The top-up compressors run excessively due to detection air system leakage. We have consequently been reliant on the alternative air provided by the GS air system to maintain pressure in the mulsifyre detection air systems, however this is not the primary purpose of the GS air system.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
GS air system re-instated and mulsifyre detection air systems re-pressurised. Road 3 mulsifyre deluge water isolating valves shut off. Mulsifyre pressure tank taken off line on refilled. Report to station fire PA to reset road 3 fire systems.
Recommendations to reinstate the the three separate mulsifyre top-up compressors and identify and repair the most significant air detection system leaks across the site to minimise wear and tear on the top-up compressors. Return the air detection systems to normal stand alone operation and become less reliant on the alternative back-up GS air supply.

TITLE: Damage to customer station with hot water leakage (customer side)
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Site manager report:
While on call, I received a call from the Recklinghausen fire brigade that water vapour was escaping from the cellar of a house on Bochumer Straße in Recklinghausen. This vapour was hitting the power connection box (400V). The entire street was then de-energised by the responsible energy supplier RWE in order to rule out any danger from electricity in the basement of the property. It was then established that the damaged DN 15 copper pipe had been wilfully damaged by a third party. I was also able to establish that this pipe
does not fall within the area of responsibility of Uniper Wärme GmbH. This pipe is located on the side of the building and has no connection to the UWG pipe network. The building is supplied with hot drinking water via this pipe. The pipe was permanently heated in conjunction with a 500 litre water heater and a storage charging unit, which are heated with district heating. To prevent any further hot water escaping from this leak, our customer service team and I switched off our district heating station completely. This was explained to the building's contact person on site by myself and the fire brigade. After this shutdown, the power supply to the entire street and the property was restored. A child who needed to be ventilated in a house in the street was attended to by the fire brigade. There were no problems in this regard. The power outage lasted about 60 minutes. Thanks to the prudent actions of everyone involved, there was no danger to people during the entire operation.
The district heating station will be put back into operation as soon as the customer has repaired the damage.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Temporary decommissioning of the FW supply for the customer in consultation with the fire brigade.

Customer system is currently blocked. Contractual partner has been informed. It will be put back into operation when the customer contacts us.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During a walk about it was noticed that diesel was visible on the floor around the temporary make up pump installation. Maintenance Delivery and operations team were informed of the leak and investigated. There had been a delivery of diesel that day and as no leaks were found at that time it was assumed there was a small spill of diesel from the delivery.

On investigation and running of the diesel generator, a leak was spotted on one of the supply hoses inside the generator cover. The leak should have been contained in the bund, but a flange on the bund sump was found to be loose and the contents was leaking out of there. There was no indication that the diesel had reached the site drains, but a cover was put over the drain as a precaution and the spill cleaned up. The hose has been repaired and is not in a safe condition for use.

TITLE: Removal of Waste from CDC site non-compliance
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Re-power project Trant Engineering additional work scope on behalf of EDF to remove old transformer bunds BHT03 and BHT05 waste.
EDF via email 24/03/2023 issued waste collection note to Uniper project team as documentary evidence to be added to project handover documentation of which was in addition to Hitachi (main contractor work scope).
On review of information project team had a meeting on the 04/04/2023 CDC Environmental officer to determine that project teams understanding was correct, the process had not been followed and that the documentation was non compliant for the reasons given below prior to issuing response to EDF.

Waste collection note issued is non-compliant for the following reasons: 
•	The collection and delivery addresses are to be in full including post codes
•	SIC code 3511 is missing
•	Producer (Uniper) has not signed the document and the declaration which has been ticked should be a declaration for the producer (Uniper) to sign (Appears that waste has been removed from CDC site without signed authorisation from Uniper representative as per agreed process).
•	Tonnage is not acceptable as 1 load as there are 2 EWC codes 17.01.01 and 17.05.04 in which Uniper require separate tonnage per code 

In addition Uniper have checked the waste carrier license 401 5100 30 and confirm license is still valid. Prior to waste being removed from Uniper CDC site Uniper should of received completed waste classification forms (WM3 assessments) for the 2 different wastes. As the EWC codes are mirror codes and have been deemed as non-hazardous by Trant Uniper require analysis data i.e. copy of test results to demonstrate non-hazardous waste. This information should have been provided to Uniper for review and acceptance prior to any waste being removed from site as per agreed process, this does not appear to have happened and a synergi case has been raised.

Response sent to EDF 04/04/2023 to provide the correct documentation and carry out an investigation with Trant Engineering and to provide an update to enable Uniper to complete the investigation.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Response sent to EDF 04/04/2023 to provide the correct documentation and carry out an investigation with Trant Engineering and to provide an update to enable Uniper to complete the investigation.

TITLE: Lambda DFB2 has been < 1 several times.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
When the biopropane composition changes (or the Wobbe measurement fails), the lambda of DFB2 may drop below 1 (underoichimetric). The boiler protection system does not detect this and should already trip the boiler at a lambda <1.05.
There is then unburned hydrogen gas in the boiler.
Boiler engineers have experience that a "thud" can be caught with natural gas and the energy dissipated through the chimney.
Hydrogen gas is much more explosive and has a more powerful shock wave. How the boiler can absorb that is unprecedented.

This occurred on 18 June 2020 where an SOG report was prepared and an investigation team was set up.
More recently, this occurred on 20 April 2023 and 3 June 2023. An SOG of both was prepared. After 3 June, the biopropane composition was changed twice more, which was met manually by the WTK.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: On Friday 21 June 2023, the measure was promulgated to stop entering the boiler (for inspection rounds) and no work at DFB2.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

The automatic extinguishing of the BAT and BBT transformers did not start during the test simulating a live situation, because the high pressure drop of the air supporting the valves did not occur during the live test due to the rupture of the air network reducers due to inadequate material separation. The built-in restrictors were made of Klingerin.

The system was tested after the installation of the new restrictors and performed its function properly.

TITLE: External processor measures slightly elevated radiation in regular discarded boiler material
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Processor drew our attention to notification requirements regarding disposed boiler pipe parts with ZAC liner, as they were found to have slight radioactivity in them. This had not been noticed by us. A suitable other final destination should also be sought. The curious thing is that the material was most probably unused (spare parts from the warehouse) and therefore unbearing on accumulation by the process.
A "notification of detection of radioactive material" was still issued to regulator ANVS via Applus RTD.
A warning letter dated 15 May 2023 has been received from ANVS of alleged violation: scrap not disposed to authorised processor.
Instructions were received on 6 June 2023 from ANVS on how to deal with the present batch as well as similar boiler pipes left with us. In the meantime, we must leave those unremoved parts untouched (they are now in the environmental field).
Update 14 June 2023: Enlisted expert company Applus RTD has put out demand to see if this scrap can be deposited at Mineralz Maasvlakte. As soon as this can be done, a container will be sent to EFM for the remaining non-disposed boiler pipe, to be loaded into the container in the presence of Applus RTD.
Update 5 July 2023: On 27 June 2023, the radioactive scrap metal was removed from Uniper Maasvlakte under the supervision of Applus RTD.
The proof of transfer (attached) was received 3 July 2023 and mailed to ANVS on 5 July 2023 cf instructions.
Update 1 September 2023: there has been no further response from ANVS: dealt with.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Legal, monitoring and reporting (Non-compliance of obligations)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The Boundary Manager has taken this up with the external radiation expert. This has already coordinated with Competent Authority ANVS and is helping us with the appropriate follow-up. It has also been checked and found that more similar material is still present at the site (EFIs EFM1/2). Update 17 May: the analysis report received from Applus RTD (attached) shows that this material is subject to registration with ANVS. The procedure will be taken up with the external radiation expert.

TITLE: Recycling/discharge of off-spec R-net water due to non-flowing quality measurements
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
For some time, the R-net discharged off-spec water to the process water tank and also temporarily to the surface water for a while as the quality measurements were not flowing through. In trend, we discovered that the line of quality measurements had been writing straight for some time. Checked measurement on site on this and then found that the pH and conductivity measurement had no flow. See trend in appendix, blue and pink line write a straight line until flow was restored.

So with the current set-up of the system, it is possible to drain off-spec water to the process water tank. Water (which is outside the permit requirements) can also be discharged to the syphon well.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Water (Inc. excess volume, lack of, uncontrolled release or excess use)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
made sure the measurements were flowing again

Recommendation:
Placing a flow meter at each measurement ( 01GUA14CQ001/ 002/ 003)
integrate flow measurements into DCS so that the R-net system automatically stops discharging to the syphon well or BMW tank and starts circulating until the measurements are provided with flow again.  This creates proper protection and prevents off-spec water from being piloted.

This was also implemented in the case of the steam/water loop sampling.

TITLE: SC10/20 Generator Hydrogen Leak alarms.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
There have been multiple cases of low level hydrogen leaks detected on both SC10 and SC20 synchronous condensers during offline periods.

July 7th 2022

The synchronous condenser was shutdown due to the need for a Mod 2 400KV grid isolation for maintenance activities.

Whilst the SC20 Generator was at standstill a hydrogen leak alarm was received on the gas detector panel CYE01 in the Killingholme control room. Investigations at that time could not detect a genuine leak although the reading appeared to last for approximately 30 seconds and peaked at 20% LEL. This alarm was detected at both ends of the Generator on both HD005 and HD006. 

Later as the Hydrogen Purity Concentration procedure was being carried out these alarms were received again. This time a noticeable leak could be heard within the turbine hall also. These readings peaked at 40% LEL and the detection lasted for several minutes. 

To clarify the first alarm was received with the shaft at standstill and no work being carried out and the second alarm was received when the shaft was still at standstill but hydrogen filling was taking place.

A further leak alarm was detected when  SC20 was put on barring up to 200RPM using the oil system

Aug 21st 2022

Again a 400KV outage was required for maintenance activities on MOD1.

Again, Killingholme OPS took the opportunity to attempt to sweeten the generator hydrogen purity. There were similar leaks of hydrogen detected as there was on SC20 above but in slightly different.

* Whilst at standstill during the H2 sweetening process

* Whilst at standstill following completion of the sweetening process.

* Whilst on barring on the return to operation

19/12/2022

Leak alarms were once again raised when SC20 was stopped to carry out repairs on GT21 GCB.  Leaks stopped once the unit was put back on barring.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Gases / Fumes / Vapours (Release of SOx, NOx, SF6, NH3, CH4, CO and CO2 into the atmosphere)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Generator returned to barring and Purity procedure stopped.

TITLE: Lack of COVID protocols on Safety Passport training course
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
No COVID protocols were included with the joining instructions from the course provider Purple Cow Training. In answer to a request for this from me via the Engineering Academy, a COVID general information sheet v1.0 dated May 2020 was provided.

On arriving at the venue (Clock Warehouse, Derby) I enquired about the risk assessment for the training room and was told by the trainer that he did not have one, but had been assured by the provider that the room was adequate. He was expecting five delegates but there were already more than this in the room. I made a dynamic risk assessment of the room (small, low ceiling), number of people (about eight with possibly more to come, no face coverings),  their proximity (two to a desk, desk rows quite close), ventilation (small window at one end, partly opened) and duration of course (seven hours plus) and decided it was not in line with current Public Health England guidance on ventilation of indoor spaces or the current protocols for working indoors at a Uniper UK site.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: I informed the trainer of my name and organisation and that I would not be staying. I left the venue and travelled home.

TITLE: Employee stuck in the lift for 2 hours. Incorrect message in the signalling chain and thus delayed rescue
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
employee took the lift on the first floor in the C area of the Capricorn at 08:00 to get to the 4th floor. The doors did not open there.
MA pressed the alarm button and reported the situation via the intercom.
At around 08:30, the lift took the employee to the mezzanine floor.
At 09:15, the employee is still stuck in the lift and presses the alarm again. He is told that a technician had been on site but that there was no one in the lift. The employee corrects this and reports that he is still in the lift. He calls his colleagues, who also ask at the Capricorn reception desk whether the situation is known and help is on the way, which is confirmed.

The employee is told over the intercom that a technician will be on site in about 15 minutes. An in-house technician is at the lift door and speaks to the employee.

In the meantime, the employee has tried to unlock the lift with the access card and select a new floor, but this was not successful until 09:50. At 09:50, the lift opened from the inside so that the employee was able to free himself. The door opened by chance as the technician was not on site at the time.  
The technician then arrives and reports that he was only informed 15 minutes ago that there was a person in the lift.

The voice connection from the lift was extremely poor.
The signalling chain was not working properly.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Incorrect posture or insufficient work environment
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Established and maintained telephone contact between employees and colleagues.

Recommendation: Clear check of the signalling chain and acoustics of the alarm telephone in the lift with strong fan noises. Loudspeaker crackled. Suggestion: Report directly to Capricorn reception so that a clear report and support is possible.

TITLE:

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the first Steam Turbine run up the cold re-heat NRV failed to open, on investigation it was found that the actuator and valve keyway had been assembled 90 degrees out.
The actuator, instead of releasing the valve plate to open on flow was trying to lift the valve plate open, this was held back by the steam pressure difference.
Under normal operation the actuator would remove the closing action and allow the plate to lift open when the pressure difference across the valve was sufficient.
In this state, had the actuator been powerful enough to force the NRV open, with positive DP down stream the flow would have reversed back to the HP turbine Exhaust.

Latest release of Flow Computer communication software obtained and installed.

Quotes requested for replacement memory modules for Flow Computers.

Data recovered from Flow Computer and memory cleansed.  

Flow computer data now under observation to gather performance data for OEM

Pi tags relating to FC flow and CV restored. 

Conference call to OEM to take place to ensure that recommended memory upgrade will resolve this issue. 

B stream validation to be carried out asap so that redundancy is restored.

TITLE:
Enfield issued with an SIR from National Grid. 
UTG & ABB concluding technical investigation EXTENDED 28/02/2022
CASE_DESCRIPTION: An incident occurred during the transformer testing which led to a huge MVAR swing of +160 to -78. This caused the grid voltage to drop from 136KV to 122KV. National Grid have now issued us with a Significant Incident Report to investigate and provide information on what happened and what went wrong.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
On the 18th November 2021 while carrying out Grid Code Compliance testing and with the unit operating at approximately 410MW and +220MVAr (lagging region) at the generator terminals (400MW and 120Mvar at the connection point) it was unexpectedly found during these planned tests, while the unit was settling after a tap of the the generator step up transformer was performed from taps 3 to 2, the Stator Current Limiter (SIL) within ABB Unitrol P excitation system became active and pulled the reactive power back to 0MVAr with a subsequent overshoot into the leading region (up until -70MVAr as shown as the orange signal in the below high speed recording). The reasoning for the large overshot is thought to be because of the high gain control of the SIL function. 

As a resultant of the SIL activation the effect unfortunately reduced both generator terminal and station board voltages by approximately 13% of nominal ( i.e. 21kV) and consequently reduced the 132kV system network voltage suddenly from 137kV down to 122kV. To counter act the effect of the SIL, the generator step up transformer was progressively tapped via controlled instructions from myself to our control room from taps 2 to 5 to increase the voltage back to as close to nominal and thus removing the unit from the SIL operating action. 

This counter action brought both the generator terminal and station board voltages relatively close nominal voltage and brought the 132kV system network voltage steadily back to 136kV, and the unit was left at position after NG Central Control Room (CCR) instructed Enfield not to carry out any further tapings. We inform NG CCR at this point that we would like to tap the unit back further towards unity power factor (i.e. tap 5 to 13) as there was a concern that the SIL could operate again if the system voltage were to alter thus moving the position of the reactive power at the generator terminals back towards the lagging region, however we were informed by NG CCR not to do this until all customers had been contacted and therefore the unit was left and no further tapping performed again until approximately 1 and half hours later.

TITLE: Potential for Duplicate Swipe Card Numbers to be allocated with different Access Control Cards
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Recently at Ratcliffe we've taken delivery of 600 new HID access control cards.  As of last month our previously issued E.On access control cards ran out and we started issuing from the new batch.

After a few days a couple of users informed us that when setting up SecurePrint on their new cards, when scanning in on the printers instead of taking them through the registration process it logged them in as another user.

We believe that this is due to the stored numbers on the two active people's different cards being the same, and/or SecurePrint not using the site code portion of the access control cards.

This is a data protection risk as there is a chance that these users with duplicate card numbers could print sensitieve personal data off the SecurePrint queue from that account that they are incorrectly logged into.

I've attached a flow diagram to explain the problem.

Fundamentally we believe that the fragmented way that Access Control cards are issued across the company and having a company wide access control card swipe system for the printers is why the risk of duplicate numbers on Access control cards is a data protection risk.

There is also a potential that these duplicate cards could allow someone access to another site that they are not authorised, but we don't believe this risk is high as the access control systems should use the site codes as well, but this will need investigating.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
An MS Form has gone out to the UK sites to gather basic information about their Access Control Systems and ID cards to ascertain what level of risk each site has.  (see links)

IT Security, Printer Management and Data Protection have been informed and I've requested a call.

For the two users that this has occured with, we have re-issued them with new access control cards.

An IT incident ticket has been raised (INC1028153)

TITLE: U4 main coalescer vent found open causing small (10-20L) oil spill.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: On Friday morning, a report was received to the outage office that there was oil dripping from the Coalescer drain separator vessel.  On investigation it was found that the Coalescer vent valve had been opened slightly.  The oil issuing into the Coalscer drain had eventually overcome the drains separator, and spilled a small amount of oil onto the basement floor.  The vent was closed immediately upon discovery.  It is not known how long, when or for what reason the vent was opened, but it is presumed it had been unintentionally knocked by a person or object at some point that morning.  There was no operational reason to operate or move the valve, and no-one was in the vicinity of the Coalscer when the open vent was discovered and closed.   The jacking oil pumps, oil tank and Coalescer were all available for normal service and at NWP.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Oil (Inc. contamination of land or water)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The Vent was returned to its normal operational position of fully closed.
Dresser Dry was placed on the area in the basement and subbasement immediately below the separator vessel, and a notification raised for the clean up.
Operatives in the surrounding area were asked if they had seen anyone in the immediate vicinity of the Coalescer that morning, but no-one had been seen working in the area.

TITLE: Grinding rollers dropped during cleaning wzh in PKM50
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Order: 30004578225
VSA: 13100990
VSL: 657117

Work permit was issued on August 26 in the morning.
Prior to the PO work, the mill will be cleaned.
For this, employees of the Rohre company enter the grinding table to vacuum out the coal residue left on the grinding bed.

This work started on Friday 26 August and continued again after the weekend from Monday 29 August around 11:00 am.
These works were scheduled to be completed today (Monday 29 Aug).

During the removal of the coal residues, the grinding rollers n.a.w. reset themselves, causing them to sink a few cm (between 2-3 cm). This while cleaners from Rohre were inside the mill.
Understandably, they were hugely shocked. None of the workers sustained any injuries from this, nor did any entrapment take place.
No requests for temporary standardisation for the hydraulic system have taken place since the safety clearance.

The licence has been taken.

To complete the clean-up work, the rollers will be secured with the appropriate clamps so that movement of the rollers is no longer possible.
Once this securing is added to the safeguarding, work can continue.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Actions taken;
Licence taken
Grinding rollers secured in high position by placement of appropriate clamps.
Securing adjusted

Proposed actions:
In case of cleaning before PO (i.e. while entering grinding room), always secure the grinding rollers. Include this in the standard safeguards. If this safeguarding is then not necessary, it can be set inactive in SAP. This way, it cannot be forgotten and skipping this "extra" safeguarding is a conscious action.

Actions:
Standard VSL has been updated. Locking clamps have been added to the VSL, preventing the grinding rollers from lowering. E.e.g. was additionally communicated by e-mail. See attachment.

TITLE: Open measuring block with cap removed
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The manual shut-off was open on the measuring block of the 52LBA10CP501 high throughput live steam measurement. In addition, the safety cap of the measuring block had been unscrewed.  Boiler house 52 had been shut off for the start-up of boiler 52. After start-up, flow noises indicated a leak. When searching for the leak with the thermal imaging camera, the leaking measuring connection was discovered.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The boiler house was not allowed to be entered anyway. The decision was made not to start the leak detection until the boiler 52 was shut down and the live steam pressure was less than 50% of the normal operating pressure. The leak search was carried out with the aid of a thermal imaging camera, as FD leaks are not visible. Once the leak had been found, an attempt was made to close the manual valve on the valve block. The measure was successful and the FD leak was thus eliminated. The valve block was presumably opened during welding work (both the fitting and the blind cap) in order to be able to form via this connection. The operating personnel were not informed about this. The open valve block was not noticed during the inspection before recommissioning.

TITLE: Lambda DFB2 has been < 1 several times.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
When the biopropane composition changes (or the Wobbe measurement fails), the lambda of DFB2 may drop below 1 (underoichimetric). The boiler protection system does not detect this and should already trip the boiler at a lambda <1.05.
There is then unburned hydrogen gas in the boiler.
Boiler engineers have experience that a "thud" can be caught with natural gas and the energy dissipated through the chimney.
Hydrogen gas is much more explosive and has a more powerful shock wave. How the boiler can absorb that is unprecedented.

This occurred on 18 June 2020 where an SOG report was prepared and an investigation team was set up.
More recently, this occurred on 20 April 2023 and 3 June 2023. An SOG of both was prepared. After 3 June, the biopropane composition was changed twice more, which was met manually by the WTK.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: On Friday 21 June 2023, the measure was promulgated to stop entering the boiler (for inspection rounds) and no work at DFB2.

TITLE: Dust emission during fly ash loading
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During fly ash loading, it was observed that there was a very high release of fly ash. This was then reported to the shiftleader fuel supply on duty.
A video is attached.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Dust (Inc. complaints, technical breaches or affecting ecosystems)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Reported to shift leader fuel supply on duty.

Addition Iwan van der Kraats, dated 24 November 2023:
I spoke to the afternoon shift manager of Fuel Supply (the port).

My preliminary conclusion:
Such a dust cloud (with precipitation in the port) can occur several times during a wet fly ash loading and cannot be prevented by current means. If this is not environmentally permissible, it means that wet fly ash ships cannot be loaded. A new ship is scheduled to arrive next week.

Clarification:
Dry fly ash is transported towards the pier. Here, water is added (about 35%) with a hand valve, and continuous occupation of a port employee.
Too little water makes the fly ash too dry and can give the emission recorded in the SynergiLife report.
Too much water can quickly lead to a blockage of the loading arm.
Whether enough water is added can only be assessed at the exit point of the charging arm and the valve position can be adjusted.
The fly ash quantity varies. Therefore, if the fly ash is slightly too wet or too dry, the valve will not be adjusted immediately.
At start-up loading, "too dry" is always started to prevent clogging of the loading pipe.
When resuming loading, this is also the case. (After shifting the vessel.)
If loading is resumed the next day, often the top layer of the vessel has become drier and produces dust when touched by the fresh loading.
At the end of loading, the fly ash comes to the upper edge of cargo hold ship and the loading is more sensitive to the wind.

Wet fly ash is loaded because fly ash supply at Maasvlakte site is very full, and we have no space in the external dry fly ash storage. Discharge is made to Flushing, where we deliver wet fly ash.

I looked up the valid procedures. I found:
- MV-OPM-P04, Dust control for bulk goods.
- MV-OPM-P04-W01, How to deal with dust control in bulk goods.
This states that wet fly ash is no longer used at Maasvlakte.
So there are no valid procedures for loading wet fly ash or it is not allowed according to the procedures.
There is no guideline in terms of wind speeds. In principle, loading continues in all weather conditions.

Wet fly ash has not been loaded for several years. Last winter, this was resumed. Approximately in the months of November to January.
This is another of the first loadings since last winter.

The ship had been moored for three days. Due to a technical malfunction, loading could not be done earlier.
The loading rig was technically available at the time of loading and had no defects.
The loading trunk has correct height above the ship.

TITLE: Loss of power to U6 BFB board causing trip of condensate extract pump and other systems fed off BFB board.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
While carrying out fault investigation under MO - 1180967658 an unexpected operation of the BFA to BFB interconnector caused loss of power to the BFB board.

Breaker 61BFT20GT200 (BFB feeder) was placed in test position for the purposes of fault investigation.

Upon reaching step 5 of the MO "Operate breaker locally and observe operation." a peer check was carried out to ensure that the correct operation was being undertaken.

Once the ON(Test) button was depressed, breaker 61BFT20GT200 (BFB feeder) closed, this was the intended outcome. However with this, 61BFA15GS021 BFA to BFB interconnector opened, this caused loss of power on the BFB board. This caused condensate extract pump 2 to trip, fortunately pump 1 was available and swapped over without issue. Other systems impacted were as follows, MBH55 GT exhaust cooling fan, CMAS fan 2, vacuum breaker etc. The event list is attached.

In normal operation if the the BFA feeder was closed and the BFB feeder was to close the interconnector should open. However the collective understanding was that in the test position this logic would be void. 

Upon investigation of the logic it was found that this is not the case.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Immediate action - Shift team leader sent out email to all shift team leaders outlining what happened.

Recommended actions -  The logic be updated to take into account test position.

TITLE: Open condenser drain valve during operation
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During MPP3 start-up, a condenser drain valve was left open. During unit downtime, the condenser level rises, causing in some cases this drain valve to be partially opened to keep the level under control. During operation, this valve should be closed.
It was not, causing a relatively high vacuum in the condenser for a long time. The search for this vacuum has incurred costs. The unit failed to follow the PCC signal. This restriction has been registered under React number 2023-00934.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Valve closed after it was found to be this valve. The fact that this valve was open was not known and was not administered.

Recommendation: During a unit stop (commercial and technical), keep a list of which valves have a deviating position due to operational necessity (just like a hatch list, for example), or process this in the safety list in SAP. This depends on the valve in question and its operating frequency.

As a safety net, this valve will be included in the start-up protocol so that at each start-up, this checklist must be ticked off to indicate that the condenser's drain options are closed.

CASE_DESCRIPTION: During routine plant checks, operations technician observed leak from sulphuric acid bulk storage tank outlet pipe stub. Leak from pipe stub between tank and outlet isolation valve. Emergency leak management & clean-up contractor (Adler & Allen) contacted and informed of situation and requested to mobilise for clean-up process in daylight hours. TITLE: EPE L-Gas : REMIT notification
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
UST Dispatching shared information with UGC (customer) which has not been published before and which therefore can be classified as potential insider information according to REMIT.

Background: a published unavailability in UST’s storage facility Epe was not updated correctly on the respective portals/publication channels after it ended. Only in UST’s internal “Maßnahmenplan” (Maintenance Plan) is was cancelled. Based on the published information UGC did not fully nominate their capacity. In a phone call between UST and UGC, UST’s dispatcher who didn’t know that the unavailability was still published externally while it has be canceled internally in our “Maßnahmenplan” stated that the curtailment does not exist anymore. By that UGC was made aware of unpublished information. As a precautionary measure, UGC stopped its trading activities until the publication had been corrected.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Unintended disclosure of confidential / personal information
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Update of the unavailability message on the UST storage portal and on AGSI+.
