VSA 1340892 had been issued. To solve the reported leakage on the SAP order/report, the atomising steam valve with KKS MPP30-HJR15AA302 had to be dismantled
in order to fix the steam leakage.  However, while dismantling the atomisation steam blow-through valve, it was found to be still under steam pressure
and further action was halted. Relevant maintenance staff (Joop & Yuksel) therefore returned to Operations with the work permit.

After further investigation Operations found that the blow-through valve of burner 15 through the bottom, (3 way valve) the outlet to the leakage oil system was under steam pressure.
are under pressure. The passage of about 7 three-way atomising steam valves at other burners and the closure of the leak oil drain valve (30HFJ98AA301)
to the leak oil tank could thus allow this pressure build-up to take place.  (The 7 drains all come out at the same outlet to the leak oil tank and whose
the drain valve to the leakage oil tank was closed, making it a closed system).

Safeguarding for wzh to an oil burner is in principle always done this way, however due to a confluence of process circumstances, this
undesirable situation was able to occur.   

No physical injury occurred when opening an installation that was under steam pressure.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Future measures;
If in the future wzh may need to be performed again on the steam system of a burner, at all times the leak oil valve(30HFJ98AA301) to the
leak oil tank must be in the open position, and a physical check for pressurisation must be carried out at all times. (Action operations)

After consultation M van Eijl and B. Knoppert made an SL report, this with the aim of learning from the situation and preventing recurrence in the future.

TITLE: PSO - U2 tripped at 430MW on turbine trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION: U2 tripped at 430MW on turbine trip. This is believed to have been caused by the HSUs changing over & one of the oil supply pumps failing to cut in, however this has not proven yet.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The trip happened to the previous shift, they safely ran down the turbine / unit & changed over to station supplies. They contacted the turbine & electrical team
Around 18.30 our shift took over at this point the turbine was on barring with station electrical supplies established.
Ovation trends were analysed we concluded that for an unknown reason the HSUs had a changeover initiated & on this changeover the A side supply pump no2 failed to start, this caused a Non Urgent turbine trip.
After consultation with the turbine & electrical teams we decided to reset the turbine, run a number of HSU change overs & if successful put the unit back on.
We were unable to reset the turbine due to a ‘Valve combination trip’ standing after further help from the C&I team this was cleared & the turbine was reset. HSU change overs where initiated numerous times without fail & it was then decided to put the unit back on.  
The unit was back energised from the 400kV substation & whilst the unit was being prepare for a start-up, the control engineer out a start on No2 CW pump, as the pump started the Unit Transformer protection was initiated & the 400kV supply tripped thus losing unit supplies, this incident will be logged as a separate synergy.

TITLE: PSO - Ammonia plant trip after delivery

The ammonia plant was forwarding to U3 at the time of the trip and NOx injection was lost for c.40 minutes, until ammonia plant was re-established.
To clarify both the tanker chiksan arm and vapour return hose were off-pressure. The chiksan arm had been successfully disconnected. Conclusion is that there must of been a small amount of liquid ammonia within the vapour return hose that was not evident (zero pressure & no frosting), which gassed off during disconnection.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Toxic substance or CMR substance (carcinogenic, mutagenic, reproduction toxic)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
1. Ammonia Plant reset and returned to service.
2. Consider using steam lance or similar to heat tanker chiksan arm & vapour return hose to assist venting down prior to disconnection during cold ambient temperatures.

TITLE: 400kV Trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During works to replace the Gen CB drive unit on GT12 a 'breaker failure protection' trip was instigated because the gen CB lost its position. This in turn sent an intertrip to GT11 and tripped the GT11 6.6kV incomer, excitation and common services feed. It would've done the same on GT12 as well but the 6.6kv board incomer and excitation CB were already locked open as part of the isolation. This would've also tripped the GT11 BFE (415v) board but this was being fed from GT21 as part of the works.

A 400kV trip was instigated as part of this, the DCS received the relevant alarms, however the 400kV did not trip.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Further investigation with National Grid, site and UTG have suggested that because the GT12 disconnector (X1093B) was open as part of the isolation, this prevented the 400kV CB (X1090) from operating.

TITLE: No proper commissioning during project phase (SER)
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During a Bureau Veritas inspection, the TRIP signal of the biopropane plant should be demonstrated. Unfortunately, this was not entirely clear to us how this works because of unclear documents from the project team. Whereupon, before Bureau Veritas checks it, we want to understand the installation ourselves and test how it works and see that it all does what it is supposed to do so that we are not "fooled" during the actual certification of the fire alarm system.

During the internal test, it was found that the trip signal from the ss valve on MPP3 was not properly incorporated into the DCS at all and totally untested by the project team as to whether all function blocks were working correctly and completely.

The commissioning document was also never signed by the project team and no complete as-built overhaul drawings are available.

If it had gone wrong on MPP3 with a fire in the biopropane plant that would never have stopped the supply of the GAS while giving a TRIP. The ss close on the DCS works but was not included in the function block of the TRIP.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
By Maasvlakte field engineers immediately adjusted the function block without waiting for SA notification.

The recommendation has been made before.  Project teams usually do not complete the works till the end, often you are told the hours are up, and leave everything else to run its course. AS-BUILT overhaul and proper commissioning of installations is no longer carried out and delivered with all its consequences. (This is visible in several areas.) Have vakexpertise from Uniper Benelux nv accompany the delivery and assess whether everything is really in order.

TITLE: Foreign bodies of concrete in the delivered coal
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the unloading of the early train U1 on Wednesday 15 June 2022, the coaling employee on duty was notified of a large number of foreign objects in the unloaded coal. The report was made by the unloading personnel of the service provider HHPI.
This was noticed after the last wagons to be unloaded had been filled.
During the immediate on-site inspection, a large number of concrete-like lumps, some up to 60-70cm in size, were found. There were also pieces of concrete on the rubble grate that looked very similar to cast concrete mouldings. All chunks/concrete parts remaining on the rubble grate were removed manually and deposited separately in the area of coal stockpile 40. It cannot be ruled out that chunks/concrete parts that are/were smaller than the perforated grid of the rubble grate (approx. 20cm-25cm x 20cm-25cm) passed through it and were deposited in the coal stockpile 40.
On the U2 late train, which was unloaded on the same day, there were again foreign bodies in the coal, some of which were retained by the chute grid, but some of which may also have passed through it. The affected coal was also stored at coal stockpile 40.  In both cases, it was a coal mixture consisting of 80% Colombian hard coal by mass from the seagoing vessel "Ultra Courage" and 20% foundation coal by mass from the WHV power plant.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: As an immediate measure, further trains with the same coal mix were cancelled and switched to 100% Colombian coal by mass, as the foundation coal is suspected of carrying foreign bodies. Furthermore, it was decided not to remove any coal for power generation from the affected coal stockpile 40 for the time being.

TITLE: Dust emission during fly ash loading
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During fly ash loading, it was observed that there was a very high release of fly ash. This was then reported to the shiftleader fuel supply on duty.
A video is attached.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Dust (Inc. complaints, technical breaches or affecting ecosystems)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Reported to shift leader fuel supply on duty.

Addition Iwan van der Kraats, dated 24 November 2023:
I spoke to the afternoon shift manager of Fuel Supply (the port).

My preliminary conclusion:
Such a dust cloud (with precipitation in the port) can occur several times during a wet fly ash loading and cannot be prevented by current means. If this is not environmentally permissible, it means that wet fly ash ships cannot be loaded. A new ship is scheduled to arrive next week.

Clarification:
Dry fly ash is transported towards the pier. Here, water is added (about 35%) with a hand valve, and continuous occupation of a port employee.
Too little water makes the fly ash too dry and can give the emission recorded in the SynergiLife report.
Too much water can quickly lead to a blockage of the loading arm.
Whether enough water is added can only be assessed at the exit point of the charging arm and the valve position can be adjusted.
The fly ash quantity varies. Therefore, if the fly ash is slightly too wet or too dry, the valve will not be adjusted immediately.
At start-up loading, "too dry" is always started to prevent clogging of the loading pipe.
When resuming loading, this is also the case. (After shifting the vessel.)
If loading is resumed the next day, often the top layer of the vessel has become drier and produces dust when touched by the fresh loading.
At the end of loading, the fly ash comes to the upper edge of cargo hold ship and the loading is more sensitive to the wind.

Wet fly ash is loaded because fly ash supply at Maasvlakte site is very full, and we have no space in the external dry fly ash storage. Discharge is made to Flushing, where we deliver wet fly ash.

I looked up the valid procedures. I found:
- MV-OPM-P04, Dust control for bulk goods.
- MV-OPM-P04-W01, How to deal with dust control in bulk goods.
This states that wet fly ash is no longer used at Maasvlakte.
So there are no valid procedures for loading wet fly ash or it is not allowed according to the procedures.
There is no guideline in terms of wind speeds. In principle, loading continues in all weather conditions.

Wet fly ash has not been loaded for several years. Last winter, this was resumed. Approximately in the months of November to January.
This is another of the first loadings since last winter.

The ship had been moored for three days. Due to a technical malfunction, loading could not be done earlier.
The loading rig was technically available at the time of loading and had no defects.
The loading trunk has correct height above the ship.

TITLE: GT vibration trip setting
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During a run up to FSNL. 
21:22 Bearing 2 vib > max 1 alarm. DCS showed 20mm/s but this is the max of its range. GE suggested the GT should have tripped automatically but it didn't. 
21:23 GT reached FSNL and vibration has dropped

The reason for the GT not tripping on high vibration was investigated. The Bentley Nevada set points were checked and the trip levels are set at 14.7 when the GT trip matrix says they should be 11.8. With the 1.5x mulitplier on start up the 14.7 became 22.05 which was above the range of the instrument (20mm/s) so the GT did not trip. Once at FSNL the multipliers are not in effect so the trip limit was back to 14.7. 

Further investigation required.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: UTG contacted and they confirmed vibration had dropped to acceptable levels.

TITLE: Contractor found vaping @ 19m level of HRSG unit 3.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Statement from shift TL:
On arriving via Unit 4’s DA’s approach I noted one member of the scaffold team Vaping; I made note of him by sight and confirmed him by noting a sweet vape type smell on his breath during a brief chat with him; other’s in the team had minor PPE infringements, so  I decided to stop the job and speak to them all outside the boiler house where hearing protection isn’t mandatory. I requested the attendance of the Competent Person who was just entering the Boiler House as the working party descended the stairs (ie the CP  not being at the point of work but walking towards it.)
I confirmed that everybody had signed on the GSAF and reminded everyone of their obligations upon signing on. I went through the aspects of wearing the appropriate PPE and adhering to the mandatory standards.
I then challenged the individual who had been vaping and I had witnessed doing so. He denied the fact he been vaping at the 19 Metre level and was he hadn’t been contravening our site rules. 

With the CP, we agreed that the best thing was that the team should go back to the amenities as it was clear that the discussion wasn’t being open and honest. (19:40)

After discussions and many ample times for the individual to admit his breaking of site rules, I was left in a position whereby I could not trust him to work within the guidance and standards we set for ‘smoking and vaping’ in the designated areas safely on the site and additionally to the terms of  the GSAF. He became very agitated and confused, back tracking on his sequence of events.
With this in mind I requested that he should leave site for tonight, because not only did he chose to break our rules, but he had become confrontational to Kev and me during our discussions.
At 20:16 he left site and returned his fob to the gatehouse pending a discussion / investigation through Kaefer and CQ.

TITLE: Control air system EFM00/01/02 not in order (not inspected) and not redundant
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The control air compressors in the basement of MPP2 have not been serviced since the closure of MPP1 and 2. It was decided at the time to start using the compressor of the MBM system for MPP1/2, O system and UCML condensate system. It was also decided not to install a redundant compressor in case the current compressor fails.

The only option left then is to start an old control air compressor
The old control air compressors are piston compressors that have leaky head gaskets and this can cause water hammer and cause eea to burst.  This can lead to a dangerous situation.

Also, this can lead to a trip of MPP2 and UCML condensate system and the entire 0 system.

There are also several components in the control air system that are past their inspection date (drums and safety devices).
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
- asap component retesting (SAP 30004591888)
- provide a redundant solution
- decommissioning old control air compressors (cutting cables)

TITLE: Hire Car Loss of Acceleration when moving on to A1 carriageway with traffic
CASE_DESCRIPTION: While I was pulling out of a layby in a company provided hire car (supplied via Hertz) I attempted to accelerate to join the traffic in a safe manner.  I had waited for a suitable gap in the traffic and then proceeded to accelerate.  The car initially accelerated normally to 20mph and then accelerated at a significantly reduced level.  This was concerning as the gap in traffic I had moved out in to was OK for a car able to accelerate to 70mph normally but wasn't large enough to allow for reduced acceleration.  This caused the vehicle behind to brake hard to avoid colliding with my vehicle.  I was able to over come the issue by manually shifting the gears and slowly accelerating until the car reached normal road speeds; the car then appeared to recover from the error and was able to drive normally again.  I then left the dual carriageway at the next exit and altered my route home to avoid busy roads. The car was fully automatic petrol car and had been performing correctly up to his point.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: On collection I informed the hire company representative of what had occurred and advised them to get the car inspected before it was used again.

TITLE: Gas Pipework not vented or purged prior to safety valve works
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

The engineer had removed the vent flange but spotted the pressure before removing the bolts from the main flange.
The engineer reported back to the SAP that there was 36bar pressure in the line and work was stopped.
Upon investigation, the pipework was isolated on an IHC (2023/00208H) and therefore hadn't been de-pressurized and purged with the rest of the gas pipework.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
1. Work was stopped on the valve.
2. Issue was discussed with the maintenance team leader and it was decided to stop all works on the gas pipeline as the isolation and purging procedure hadn't been followed correctly.
3. All works on the pipeline were stopped and the relevant safety documents were suspended (2023/00692, 2023/01243, 2023/01230) while a decision was made how to vent and purge this section of pipe.
4. Method to de-pressurise and purge the remaining pipework agreed.

TITLE: Station and Unit Auxiliary steam header over pressurisation.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Unit 1 desync 2025hrs, Unit 4 sync 2207hrs, Unit 2 desync 2255hrs.
At 2254hrs Aux Boilers 210, 240 & 250 tripped due to a fleeting gas detector (Steam Generator 2 Gas Detector).
Until the Boiler system and gas slam shut valve could be reset the aux steam header was supplemented from Units 1 & 2, manually,  via SVAPCV019. This initially resulted in an momentary over pressurisation of the Auxiliary Steam Headers up to18Bar, (0*-SVA-025-PT).  Unit 3 Auxiliary Steam Header was isolated and depressurised for outage and so unaffected.
The Aux Steam header then dropped to 2 Bar before Aux Boilers 220 and 230 began loading enough to raise the pressure.
This resulted in the condenser pressures of Unit 1 reaching 165mBar and Unit 2 301mBar due to low gland steam pressures. Unit 4 vacuum was unaffected.
The Gas Treatment Plant was being started at the time of the trip, which required some venting of the compressor HP suction drum V403, and the wind was from the west (this may or may not relate to the gas detector trip).

The Unit Auxiliary Steam Header Safety Valves PSV003 are rated to lift at 18Bar according to the P&ID.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: - Auxiliary boilers reset and put back in service to control unit and station aux steam header pressure. Aux steam pressure controlling in Remote.

TITLE: BP Engineer unfamiliar with site and Uniper work practices allowed on site without host being contacted.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A repair request was raised with BP for EV charger number 2.  Syed Ishrat was given a name by BP for the person coming out to investigate.  The BP engineer was booked on site through VMS with Syed's contacts details as the host.

On arrival, he was booked in by security and directed to the power station.  Syed wasn't contacted by the gatehouse, so wasn't aware the engineer had arrived.

The engineer then went to the charger, reset it with the external reset button and was then spotted by myself as I went to my car.   No intrusive work other than pressing the reset button was carried out so the risk was minimal, but as a new person to site, the BP engineer would've been unaware of our safety and working practices.

I have found recently that I am rarely contacted by security when a visitor comes to site and the first that I hear of their arrival is when they arrive in reception and reception call me.  9 times out of 10 this isn't an issue, but if someone doesn't know to go straight to reception or is unfamiliar with site, they might end up somewhere they're not supposed to with no one site knowing that person is on site.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: No injury occurred, but potential for injury if unsupervised work was carried out.

TITLE: Operational Loss - U2 Gen TX  high HV winding temperature  resulting in load drop and Unit Mel to zero.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: High HV winding temperature alarm initiated at 12:42 @105oC , trip at 110oC. Load reduced at 14:07 to 300MW & O MVAR, temp reached 108oC. Load reduced to 230 MW @ 14:26 , temp peaked at 109oC. Unit MEL to 230 MW until 02:30 then O MW until 08:30. Electrical team investigated with the fault believed to be an instrument false reading however the instrument would initiate a unit trip. All 4 cooling fans put in service and attempt made to swap over the oil pumps. This resulted in both pumps stopping and neither would restart. Standby pump finally restarted some 30 minutes later. Temp now stable at 103oC.  Ovation schematic issue identified with Red phase labelled as 'A' phase ,  the Red phase at the TX is labelled 'C' phase.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Load reduced to 230 MW  , unit shutdown early by UGC . Unit Mel to zero until 08:30 resulting in loss of income on a high value day. Electrical team attending site at 06:00 to investigate fault. Further actions are: 1 - check remaining phase temperature indications. 2 -  Resolve oil pump changeover issues  3 - Resolve ovation schematic errors.

TITLE: PSO - U3 HP Shaft Position Indication Found Reading Off Scale
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The EC&I team were Investigating an oil leak on U3 HP Shaft position Differential Expansion probe.  It is standard practice to look at the current reading and note any standing alarms before any work is done.  The module was reading -1.25mm hard off scale.  There were no plant alarms standing.  Trending the value on the Ovation DCS revealed that the HP Shaft position had been reading off scale since 22/10/2021, just over 1 year.  Since this date, the generating unit has run many times with no accurate visibility of the turbine shaft position.  It was found that the alarms were not enabled in the measurement module.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The HP shaft position recalibrated and returned to service.
Module alarms have been re-instated.

TITLE: Foreign bodies in delivered coal
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
After unloading the early train U1 on Wednesday 09.08.2023, the coaling employee on duty reported a large number of foreign objects
were reported on the pouring grate. These were discovered during a routine inspection after the train had been unloaded.
All of the foreign objects were removed from the rubble grate and deposited in the wagon unloading area for further examination.
The foreign objects removed (see pictures in the appendix) range in size from 30 cm to 60 cm and vary in terms of material and hardness. Some of the foreign bodies found are very similar to the parts from the incident in June 2022. (SL case 26254)
 
The grid of holes in the rubble grate is 25cm x 20cm, which means that smaller foreign bodies slipped through the rubble grate and were deposited in the stockpile with the coal.

A visual inspection/inspection of the corresponding coal stockpiles has not yet revealed any further foreign bodies.

Furthermore, various ropes, tension belts, textile remnants and a rubbish bag with household rubbish were discovered on the rubble grate and removed.


The coal types delivered during the last unloading processes were a mixture of Kazakhstan coal/foundation coal from the WHV power plant or Colombian coal/foundation coal from the WHV power plant.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
All of the foreign objects on the pouring grate were removed.
People involved in the coal logistics process were informed about the incident.
It was agreed not to add any foundation coal from the WHV plant as a mixture until further notice, as this is again suspected of carrying the foreign bodies.

Data recovered from Flow Computer and memory cleansed.  

Flow computer data now under observation to gather performance data for OEM

Pi tags relating to FC flow and CV restored.

B stream validation to be carried out asap so that redundancy is restored.

. The cause was an unusually high pressure drop in the well water system
during operation of the site's demineralisation plant.
2. 02/05/2021, temporarily three wells in operation with 171 𝑚3/ℎ
. Due to damage to the boiler house 2 fire extinguishing pipe until the pipe was shut off
of the pipe and its repair.
3. 13 and 15 October 2021, temporarily four wells in operation with 231 𝑚3/ℎ
. Due to the trial operation of reserve block 3 in combination with the
operation of the demineralisation plant.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: In order to avoid the above-mentioned overruns in future, the operating personnel were sensitised to pay particular attention to the number of running well pumps when the demineralisation plant is running and to postpone the operation of the demineralisation plant to a time when there is lower consumption in the plant's water system in the event of a foreseeable drop in pressure.

TITLE: Compressor 30 loss of comms from the Siemens Anti-Surge control system to the ABB 800xA DCS
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Compressor suction and discharge pressure, temperature and flow values freeze. Compressor still running until 18/06/22 09:00 

Compressor is then started again at 18/06 10:30, values come back at 18/06 12:30 values freeze again at 18/6 20:30 and compressor continued to run until 23:00. The values do not come back.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The Siemens UCP (Anti-surge control) and USS (Compressor safety) both have CP341 cards that handle serial RS485 Modbus comms back to the DCS through an RS485 convertor to RS232. 

The card was checked and found to have failed. The first incident of freezing of data could have been an early sign it was failing, but too soon before total failure to have done any pro-active maintenance. 

This incident has highlighted an issue that the failure of comms did not warn the operator, put the readings into fault, or stop the compressor and this allowed them to continue running the compressor.

Requires a mod to loss of comms that makes the compressor unavailable and faults out any IO that is linked to it

TITLE: Gas leakage at the hydraulic system of the underground safety valve of the BW 58 well
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During the safety function test at assembly drilling site 5, a maintenance colleague noticed that there was "bubbling" in the hydraulic tank of the BW 58. IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The hydraulic line (control line) on the E cross of the BW 58 was immediately closed and secured via the needle valve, thus stopping the gas flow. The borehole was put into a safe condition and taken out of operation. Further measures: Repair of the UTSAV

TITLE: PGS 15 standards Fe(3)Cl several times exceeded
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Fe(3)Cl, ferric chloride or Ferry chloride is a highly corrosive substance to which metals are very poorly resistant. Due to an incident in 2024, this substance is temporarily stored differently.

At the time of writing, I count 3 different storage sites where at all three the PGS 15 standards are completely ignored.

1) Next to the R-net sedimentation basin
a badly labelled IBC stands above a clogged gutter made of metal
2) In the UGB building opposite the large thickener
two IBCs with residual 40% ferric chloride stand on a metal drip tray without leak protection
3) Chemical room UGB
three IBCs are on the ground. after comments, the drip tray is no longer used because it is made of metal

PGS 15 prescribes:
- Use chemical-resistant sump trays such as PE
- Drip tray capacity must be able to collect 110% of the contents
- Drip trays must be fitted with leak detection
- Use correct labelling and marking

IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:

TITLE: Increased pressure in the compressed air system of a drilling site during the commissioning phase
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A subcontractor detected increased pressure in the compressed air system.
Functional tests of fittings had been carried out the day before. The system was supplied externally with nitrogen for this purpose. The nitrogen bundle used for this purpose was not disconnected from the system afterwards and was not closed at the shut-off valve. Control valves are not considered to be leak-proof. This can also be assumed here. As the nitrogen bundle was integrated as an external, unplanned pressure source at the construction site, the installed safety valve could not be triggered.
The pressure in the system had risen to approx. 20 bar overnight, whereas the system is designed for a nominal pressure of 10 bar.
There is no risk of a pipe bursting at this pressure, but there is a risk of damage to the installed fittings. However, this also failed to materialise.
The source (nitrogen bundle) could have delivered a pressure of up to 200 bar. If the increase in pressure had not been noticed, a pipe rupture due to the further increase in pressure could no longer have been ruled out.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The system was immediately depressurised and the nitrogen bundle separated.

The system affected here will be retrofitted with a safety valve. This will prevent an unintentional increase in pressure, regardless of the cause.

So immediate danger has been removed but attention is needed.

TITLE: HDE NO2 exceedance
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The auxiliary boiler was restarted on Saturday 11 January 2025 after a boiler repair.
The boiler was cold and was started via the programme with the lance burner, fire on was at 11:58.
 
At 12:02, the short-term NO2 value (normalised) was 206 mg/Nm³. Research into the cause of the high NO2 values was initiated immediately. At 12.48 pm, burner 1 went into operation and the lance burner was shut down. As a result, the short-term NO2 value (normalised) improved to 109 mg/Nm³ at 12:54 and was again below the limit value. Due to the high NO2 values, there was an entry in class S01 > RGW (226.84 mg/Nm³) at 12.30 pm.
 
Two malfunctions were detected during the subsequent fault analysis.
1. at the end of pre-ventilation (before fire on), the rezi blower was switched off due to a signal overlap, causing the flap to close after the rezi blower.
2. when the lance burner is started, the "Feedback On" ReziFan is requested, but the damper after ReziFan is not opened.
 
Due to the closed damper after ReziBlower, the ReziGas control dampers remained closed and the lance burner was operated without ReziGas.
 
As the above-mentioned events were not a fault in the true sense of the word, but a malfunction, there were no corresponding alarm messages from the control system. This made it even more difficult to determine the cause of the high NO2 values.
 
The recognised faults in the control system were rectified and the missing signals were replicated.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Gases / Fumes / Vapours (Release of SOx, NOx, SF6, NH3, CH4, CO and CO2 into the atmosphere)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Coordination of continued operation with production manager
Incident investigation,
Information government of Middle Franconia on 14.01.2025

TITLE: BHV deployment at EBS - accident involving EBS employee and transported to hospital
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Deployment of FAFS at EBS (third party). Uniper provided the FAFS. The floating crane and barge is moored at a quay owned by Uniper. See report below.

1. On 8 March at 13:10, a call from Security on the SL phone that there was an accident at EBS. An employee was injured. It was indicated that an ambulance was required, this was called in advance by Security.
Once at the scene, it became clear that this was a serious incident where the victim was lying in the barge, was approachable, but could not/may not move, had cramp in legs and nausea. Once descended into the barge, there was continuous contract with the victim.
3 While (connecting/disconnecting) a slide of a bobcat (located in the barge), the victim was hit from above by the grapple. This suddenly dropped down while the victim was (un)connecting under the grab. The sudden lowering of the grab was naw caused by the crane operator grabbing a bottle of water and accidentally hitting the joystick, causing the grab to sink. At this, the operator immediately raised the grab and it was found that the victim had been hit and had fallen. There were no further witnesses to this accident; the 2 other colleagues were not in sight of the victim at the time.
4. It was soon clear that getting the victim out of the barge would be a challenge taking into account his possible back injury. To this end the fire brigade was called, they were on the scene at 13:30. The fire brigade scaled up to the port authority for assistance with a vessel equipped with a crane, which was on site by 13:45.
5. Ambulance personnel eventually descended into the barge and after examination, victim was carefully placed on the stretcher and hoisted out of the barge. The vessel was docked on the other side of the pier to hoist the victim to the quay and then transport him to the Hospital (St Franciscus).
6. Meanwhile, the police had also arrived. They interviewed those involved including the safety expert and foreman of EBS. There was also contact with the labour inspectorate. A request was made to Operations to send the available photographic material (done) and secure video material. Securing the video footage has been organised by Security.
7. The Labour Inspectorate will continue dealing with this accident on Monday, 10 March. On this basis, I have cleared the loading of timber for Sunday.
8. At 14:40, all emergency services (except police) had left the site.
9. Victim's name is known to security, Operations, police and foreman EBS.
10. At 15:50, the police had also left the site.

Details:
- There is no safe way to board the barge. Eventually, a gangway was used which was improvised and attached so that ambulance and fire service personnel with their equipment could enter the barge in a relatively safe manner. Such a gangway service to be standardly available on the quay of EBS. --> no contact details known to discuss the matter.
- When walking on the barge, the walking space between the barge and the water is about 50cm. Both fire and ambulance personnel have life jackets. Operations does not have these vests. These should be available (at least 4 of them) in the FAFS van. --> have been ordered via SAP-Ariba
- No phone number is known to Operations and Fuel planning department from EBS. Would like the SL to have an operational contact to communicate with in case of an (emergency) situation. The operational numbers Laurenshaven (06-22221546) and Europoort (06-51254955) cannot be reached. The queue I remains at "1", even after hanging on the line for 20 minutes. Who can provide an accessible number?
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Entering EBS premises, going on scene and calling emergency services
Care for victim
Coordination of emergency services
reporting

TITLE: Kop van Zuid - Measuring point CH4 too high (poor engineering and acceptance)
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
All measuring points (were) in the Kop van Zuid have been positioned so that they can do their job, and for the 1/2-year maintenance inspections, provisions have been made so that maintenance of the measuring probes can be carried out without unauthorised climbing and scrambling.

The measuring probes hang at about 2.5 - 3 metres in height and a connection point for maintenance/calibration of the measuring probes then hangs at about 1.5 - 1.8 metres in height.

The new measuring probe for the new Eneco boiler hangs at about 6 metres and the connection point for normal calibration of the measuring probe now hangs at 4.5 metres.

A copy was made of the steelwork of the current probes only they totally failed to understand why there is a connection lower than the probe.

This probe now requires scaffolding to be built at all times to calibrate the probe 1/2 yearly.

IMG_4320: New probe installed by AVR/Eneco project with the connection point for calibration at approximately 4.5 mtr height.

IMG_4321: Desired situation, measuring probe at height, calibration connection point at default working height.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Incorrect posture or insufficient work environment
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Unfortunately, no direct actions are possible.

Recommendation:
Involve good subject matter experts in changes. Would like to restore that the connection point for calibration is accessible 1/2 yearly to avoid the expensive repetitive cost of scaffolding.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

By aligning the Spool using a chain hoist, the tack welds gave way and the Spool came loose from the pipe.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Recommendation: This could have been avoided by communicating this so that it was known that this seam was bonded and not welded through and/or marking the weld on the pipe.

The replacement amplifier was hung on one string, wiring was not connected properly and parameters were entered incorrectly.
Result: Incorrect measurement values for invoicing to Eneco.

17-11-2022 : Uniper Head technician fixed the cabinet correctly, connected wiring correctly and set parameters correctly. The boiler has been started and signals checked during operation.

Recommendations for further actions:
Allow only Uniper people with sufficient knowledge of comptable heat measurements to work on the measurements.
Start training programme to increase the knowledge on this (Both in depth, and the amount of people) within DO.

TITLE: Cover plate for penetration through roof for manual torqueing STT EDH mounted in wrong place.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
After DCS failure and consequently trip STEG, it was necessary to manually torque the steam turbine to prevent it from getting stuck and therefore unavailable for several days in a row.
Unfortunately, the grommet in the roof of the STT casing had been sealed with a metal plate secured with pop rivets. The plate turned out to be mounted in the wrong place. It left open an old grommet that is no longer used today. The grommet is needed to put an extension through so that one can manually torque the turbine from the roof of the enclosure.
In all haste, the plate was literally torn off with brute force in order to start torquing the just-tripped, still very hot steam turbine as soon as possible. If this had taken too long the STT would have stalled and the STEG would have been unavailable for several days as a result.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
See above.
Tore off the misplaced plate and then started manually torquing the turbine as soon as possible

TITLE: Open exterior doors geothermal power plant
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Operations conducted a control round at AWC on 20/10/24

On site, it was found that the two doors - of the inner
and outer shell - near boiler 20 were wide open. In order not to get unwanted
visitors at AWC (with all its consequences), both doors were
doors closed again of which the inner shell door was locked.

The guard contacted Security Center Maasvlakte (SCM) to
ask questions about the doors at AWC that were open. The employee
at SCM was able to tell that both the door contacts and the
badge readers had been bridged for months.

The guard raised with SCM that this situation is highly undesirable as they
do not receive any door reports, they also do not know which persons
present/registered at the site. This is a security breach.
Think sabotage, theft, accident (fatal or injury), etc etc etc.

The guard escalated this further by presenting this problem
to the Site Leader on duty.

------------------------------------------------------------
Site Leader inquired with the security specialist whether this situation is known. The security specialist indicated that he was not aware of any information regarding bridging. However, he can inform that there was never a handover during the conversion project to HAL and the related responsibilities in alarm follow-up were made known. In doing so, it could be that since the start of the conversion (Eneco/Uniper) to (Eneco/Uniper/HAL), everything has been deactivated and never updated.

Site leader then enquired from the operators who made the rounds at AWC on 19/10/24 whether they (accidentally) left the doors open. Answer is no.

The only other party present on AWC at that time (19/10/24) was a technician from Aardyn. Aardyn technicians have access to this location.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Doors AWC closed. Reinstate door alarms and badge readers on AWC . (Advice sought from security specialist)

TITLE: Uitval WSG communicatie
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Communication RoCa vs substations was briefly lost around 01:00.
Although this recovered fairly quickly, communication with the SSC remained completely down for a longer period of time (at least 5 minutes). In the process, there was no visibility of parameters and no operation was possible!

This incident reveals several problems:

Due to communication failure, both Boszoom pumps regulate back to minimum rpm, resulting in a strong pressure increase in the grid (city).
This is highly undesirable; the pumps should be able to operate autonomously! Intervention (control) was not possible.

Alarms in the summary and journal list (history) are largely "crossed out"; the system (and the operator) cannot verify whether the alarm is "real" (or not).
Alarm times deviate enormously from system time; failure analysis is therefore impossible.

Communication failures, Forestzoom control and alarm issues are known (multiple incident reports). Risks of the above issues are high.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Investigate cause of communication failures.

Adjust response of Boszoom pump control such that the control operates autonomously or "freezes", when communication fails.

Ensure alarms mummary and event logging are functioning properly! There are now very many alarms, unclear texts and unsound alarm times in the system which makes the whole thing practically unworkable.

TITLE: Tech Centre HV Maintenance Findings (May 24)
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the Tech Centre HV Maintenance a number of age / condition related hazards were identified on the HV electrical equipment that have the potential to cause harm / business interruption:

1. Partial discharge (PD) activity was identified on the PTB transformer circuit cable termination at the 11kV Scientific & Tech Centre Switchboard.

2. Fixed earth contact on one phase sheared during maintenance operation of the Winking Hill 11kV Circuit Earth Switch at the 11kV Scientific & Tech Centre Switchboard.

3. PTA Transformer Buchholz gas detection relay did not operate when initially tested.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
1. Partial discharge activity - Cable split and additional installation material added over visible areas of discharge. Recommendations - Warning notice / access restriction to switch room and regular online PD monitoring to be performed and trended (to be included in a maintenance management system).

2. Broken earth contact - Temporary repair installed and returned to service (Ductor and IR tested). Recommendations - Temporary repair to be replaced with OEM part(s) or reverse engineered substitute. Operational restriction + associated warning notice to be applied to switchgear (all outgoing circuits). Plant simulation to be recorded on Ratcliffe PS temporary simulation register. TITLE: RoCa: Soda lye leakage from dosing vessel.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the rounds walked on Tuesday 12 November, it was noticed that there was a puddle of liquid near the RO units (demineralised water plant), this is not unusual because during the change of a raw water filter, water gets on the ground. So no further suspicion at that point.
On Wednesday, I walked into the plant and saw white marks and crystallisation on the ground everywhere. The scaffolders were removing material at that time and also had the forklift in use. This work immediately stopped the foreman told me it was probably caustic soda and said rinse shoes and throw away gloves. Asked the chemical department if they knew what had happened based on previous observations that the NaOH dosage in the district heating water (make-up SV) was not working. Something had been tried with the plant but they had no idea where leakage had come from. Asked to determine the pH of liquid pool and approximate concentration of NaOH. This showed that pH was pH12 and concentration about 0.8%. This corresponded nicely to the composition in the NaOH dosing vessel. Daniel sluymers asked the Maurik company to clean the floor with appropriate PPE by diluting the mixture with sufficient water and rinsing/draining the gutter.

After a long search, it turned out that the suction hose from the dosing tank of the SVW NaOH dosing pump (00GBN31AP001) had slipped off the compression fitting (directly on the suction) and the hose had fallen right next to the drip tray, causing half the dosing tank to spill onto the floor by siphoning. Level was 73% and after leakage 27%, so about 120 litres of 0.8% solution across the floor. The concentration was fortunately lower because NaOH dosing with creation of new vessel had not gone well.
Hose reattached properly to pump suction however pump is still not pumping. Further action needed.
Maurik cleaned everything well and did a good job.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Stopped work around the area of the leak and instructed the people involved to rinse their shoes and throw away gloves.
Daniel sluymers asked Maurik's company to clean the floor with proper PPE, by diluting the mixture with enough water and rinsing/pulling into the sump.
Suction hose reassembled and secured so that it cannot fall next to sump.
Informed the guard.

TITLE: Partial shutdown SSC by switching operation
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Due to an electrical switching operation, 1 rail briefly lost its control voltage. As a result, 2 feed water pumps tripped and 1 return water pump tripped.
In the absence, or incorrectly set protection devices, the remaining feedwater pump ran very far outside the pump curve for a long time with periodically very high vibrations (25 mm/s). Pumps that were later restarted also subsequently ran very far outside their curve and tripped several times at minimum suction pressure.
The limitation of the pumps appears to be at the trip value so the existing protection/control cannot work.
Pumps are not protected on operating far outside their operating range. A lot of noise and vibration was observed by present personnel at that time throughout the supply water system.
From AW pump B, presumably the non-return valve was damaged as physical backflow was observed on site.
The return water pump operated well outside its curve for a prolonged period and the second pump, which became available again after a local reset, would not voluntarily synchronise with the auxiliary pump. (total flow equally distributed between the ancillary pumps) This action had to be performed on hand.

Finally got WSG back in control by operating 2 pumps on HAND and resetting AVR.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: SAP notification made for changing control suction pressure protections supply water pumps.

TITLE: ELD: unauthorised modification of the fire alarm control unit
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
From Facilities ELD, a question had come to Facilities ALG as to whether it is possible to prevent the fire pump from being started when the fire alarm system is periodically tested. This causes water to enter the pipes. It is laborious to drain the pipes afterwards and the water causes pipe corrosion. The solution was found in incorporating a time delay between an alarm and the control of the fire pump.
This was implemented in an ad hoc manner by installing a time relay for control to the fire pump. See attached photos for the implementation.

The BMC administrator was informed of the modifications to the BMC by Siemens on 31-03-2025, during work on the BMC.

- The demand from Facilities ELD is legitimate and the problem had been noted earlier
   during inspections with Bilfinger.
- The modification was done (circa early March) during my designation as BMI
   administrator.
- The person who made the adjustments is aware that adjustments to
   fire safety installations are my responsibility (Henk Torenbeek).
- The BMI manager was not informed about the adjustments.
- The modification was done outside the Subcontractor (Siemens).
- No drawings were made of the modification. The adaptation is also not
   included in the BMC manual.
- The adaptation is not documented in the Siemens drawings.
- It is unknown whether the components used meet safety requirements.
- The adaptation is powered from a socket. This is not permitted from the Machinery Directive.

Consequences:
The adaptation may fail undetected, allowing the fire pump to start unintentionally without being noticed or, conversely, not start at times when it should. The integrity of safety devices is compromised.
Because the modification was done outside Siemens, this is not included in the maintenance regime and falls outside the impending replacement BMC.
Potential problems with the insurer due to unauthorised modifications having been made to the BMC.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Actions taken:
- Have Siemens return the installation to its original state

Further actions:
- With Facilities EDH, DO-E and Operations towards an alternative by adjusting in the procedures. (During testing BMC turn off fire pump's working switch. Include this in the work permit. Operators may secure the fire pump.

TITLE: Pole slip GT 3 huge stress on shaft and windings.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During GT3 start-up, the warning Poolslip occurs in the generator protections.

In short, the drive (gas turbine), due to the influence of rapid changes in power, tries to pull the magnetic field loose between the stator and rotor of the generator in a synchronous generator.
This phenomenon is dangerous for the plant, see below picture and explanatory text as an example.

The 30-07-2024 example shows that the warning pole slip occurs due to the rapid load change of >10MW/min.
Times between REG216 and the trend in TC7 are unfortunately not time-synchronised and differ by 1 minute 27 sec in this example.
2.19MW power increase in 11.8 sec, amounts to 11.1 MW/min increase (DWATT line is unfortunately not visible at this point)
Sample time trend is ca.15 msec
It appears that the maximum power gradient of 4MW /min which was set in the MarkV is not yet present TC7
Item 22 from the residual points list.
 

The 5-8-2024 example shows another much more extreme example.
Here the deviation between REG216 and TC7 is 1 minute and 10 sec
In about 4 sec, the power goes from 48MW to -4.8 MW (backwatt. Shaded green) and back to 55MW.
1 sec later pole slip occurs again.
You don't have to be a rocket scientist to understand, what a huge interplay of forces is taking place here and that there are actually going to be problems from it. Huge stress on the shaft and the windings.
Sampling time approx. 280msec.

Power fluctuations occur on and around switching to a different combustion mode of the GT.

TITLE: Open exterior doors geothermal power plant
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Operations conducted a control round at AWC on 20/10/24

On site, it was found that the two doors - of the inner
and outer shell - near boiler 20 were wide open. In order not to get unwanted
visitors at AWC (with all its consequences), both doors were
doors closed again of which the inner shell door was locked.

The guard contacted Security Center Maasvlakte (SCM) to
ask questions about the doors at AWC that were open. The employee
at SCM was able to tell that both the door contacts and the
badge readers had been bridged for months.

The guard raised with SCM that this situation is highly undesirable as they
do not receive any door reports, they also do not know which persons
present/registered at the site. This is a security breach.
Think sabotage, theft, accident (fatal or injury), etc etc etc.

The guard escalated this further by presenting this problem
to the Site Leader on duty.

------------------------------------------------------------
Site Leader inquired with the security specialist whether this situation is known. The security specialist indicated that he was not aware of any information regarding bridging. However, he can inform that there was never a handover during the conversion project to HAL and the related responsibilities in alarm follow-up were made known. In doing so, it could be that since the start of the conversion (Eneco/Uniper) to (Eneco/Uniper/HAL), everything has been deactivated and never updated.

Site leader then enquired from the operators who made the rounds at AWC on 19/10/24 whether they (accidentally) left the doors open. Answer is no.

The only other party present on AWC at that time (19/10/24) was a technician from Aardyn. Aardyn technicians have access to this location.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Doors AWC closed. Reinstate door alarms and badge readers on AWC . (Advice sought from security specialist)

TITLE: Damage to the FD line block 2
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
After the unit was disconnected from the grid on Tuesday to Wednesday night (15 to 16 April), it was dry-preserved again.
At around 1:04 a.m., both HPUs were opened to `15% to reduce the pressure in the high-pressure system from 70 to 25 bar.

TITLE: ELD: unauthorised modification of the fire alarm control unit
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
From Facilities ELD, a question had come to Facilities ALG as to whether it is possible to prevent the fire pump from being started when the fire alarm system is periodically tested. This causes water to enter the pipes. It is laborious to drain the pipes afterwards and the water causes pipe corrosion. The solution was found in incorporating a time delay between an alarm and the control of the fire pump.
This was implemented in an ad hoc manner by installing a time relay for control to the fire pump. See attached photos for the implementation.

The BMC administrator was informed of the modifications to the BMC by Siemens on 31-03-2025, during work on the BMC.

- The demand from Facilities ELD is legitimate and the problem had been noted earlier
   during inspections with Bilfinger.
- The modification was done (circa early March) during my designation as BMI
   administrator.
- The person who made the adjustments is aware that adjustments to
   fire safety installations are my responsibility (Henk Torenbeek).
- The BMI manager was not informed about the adjustments.
- The modification was done outside the Subcontractor (Siemens).
- No drawings were made of the modification. The adaptation is also not
   included in the BMC manual.
- The adaptation is not documented in the Siemens drawings.
- It is unknown whether the components used meet safety requirements.
- The adaptation is powered from a socket. This is not permitted from the Machinery Directive.

Consequences:
The adaptation may fail undetected, allowing the fire pump to start unintentionally without being noticed or, conversely, not start at times when it should. The integrity of safety devices is compromised.
Because the modification was done outside Siemens, this is not included in the maintenance regime and falls outside the impending replacement BMC.
Potential problems with the insurer due to unauthorised modifications having been made to the BMC.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Actions taken:
- Have Siemens return the installation to its original state

Further actions:
- With Facilities EDH, DO-E and Operations towards an alternative by adjusting in the procedures. (During testing BMC turn off fire pump's working switch. Include this in the work permit. Operators may secure the fire pump.

TITLE: Open exterior doors geothermal power plant
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Operations conducted a control round at AWC on 20/10/24

On site, it was found that the two doors - of the inner
and outer shell - near boiler 20 were wide open. In order not to get unwanted
visitors at AWC (with all its consequences), both doors were
doors closed again of which the inner shell door was locked.

The guard contacted Security Center Maasvlakte (SCM) to
ask questions about the doors at AWC that were open. The employee
at SCM was able to tell that both the door contacts and the
badge readers had been bridged for months.

The guard raised with SCM that this situation is highly undesirable as they
do not receive any door reports, they also do not know which persons
present/registered at the site. This is a security breach.
Think sabotage, theft, accident (fatal or injury), etc etc etc.

The guard escalated this further by presenting this problem
to the Site Leader on duty.

------------------------------------------------------------
Site Leader inquired with the security specialist whether this situation is known. The security specialist indicated that he was not aware of any information regarding bridging. However, he can inform that there was never a handover during the conversion project to HAL and the related responsibilities in alarm follow-up were made known. In doing so, it could be that since the start of the conversion (Eneco/Uniper) to (Eneco/Uniper/HAL), everything has been deactivated and never updated.

Site leader then enquired from the operators who made the rounds at AWC on 19/10/24 whether they (accidentally) left the doors open. Answer is no.

The only other party present on AWC at that time (19/10/24) was a technician from Aardyn. Aardyn technicians have access to this location.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Doors AWC closed. Reinstate door alarms and badge readers on AWC . (Advice sought from security specialist)

TITLE: AVR cannot maintain the supply water temperature.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: AVR sometimes cannot maintain the supply water temperature causing it to drop too much. Since the AVR regulates on power (Q=m*C*T), their pumps regulate up as soon as the temp drops to deliver the power. As a result, the feedwater pumps on the SSC also regulate up, causing the pressure on the bleacher line to become high. AVR has to manually regulate the pumps back to get this back under control.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Have suction bar of the feed water pumps controlled on buffers again.
Have AVR controlled on flow IPV power.

TITLE: Non-functioning start releases (safeguards) GT-3
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On 28-09 at about 14:00, RoCa-3 was commissioned. After start-up, the alarmsummary on TCS-7 showed that washer valve L33AE4 was not in the correct position (since 24-09 14:46).
This is strange, because to obtain start release, this valve should be in the correct position!

Following this observation, some additional random tests were carried out to determine whether start-up releases are coming through correctly.
A number of things stand out here:

Washer valve L33AE4 continuously gives an alarm, regardless of the position of the valve. Start release (L33AE_ALM) remains present.
A number of other washer valves generate an alarm when leaving the final contact, but even then start clearance does remain present.

The "wash water valves" also include the 4 hand valves of the anti-surge protection.
The two valves at the bottom (NS and highway side) give an alarm, but start clearance is maintained.
The two valves at the top (NS and highway side) do not generate any signal.

The start conditions also include the correct position of various fire valves.
When the valves of the generator compartment are closed, this also does not result in the loss of start enable (L33VG1_ALM).

Similarly, blocking the extinguishing system, both by means of the key switch on the casing, and the switches on the BMC in the server room, only results in an alarm; start enable remains present.

These tests are anything but comprehensive and only serve to substantiate the fact that the start releases are (partly) not functioning correctly.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The cause of the malfunction of the aforementioned start-up releases is as yet unclear. Although Mark-V was recently replaced by TCS-7, it is too short to conclude that there is a direct connection!
It cannot be ruled out that some issues may have already been present.

This report should therefore in no way be seen as a reproach to those directly involved in this project!
As an organisation you have to ask yourself whether it is responsible to keep the machine operational, given the long list of issues that is still open at the moment!

We have therefore decided to report RoCa-3 unavailable until 16:00 tomorrow afternoon. Please consult us tomorrow morning on how we can guarantee that the installation remains reliable and safe.

TITLE: High-temperature ISS-1 server room.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: ISS-1's space temperature has risen unacceptably high due to work on both air conditioners.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Preliminary conclusions (discuss further with stakeholders):

The work was not reported to production by the Holder and/or Executive at the end of the day.  
The status of the work was therefore unclear to the guard, but the high temperature was noticed. Insufficient action was taken on this.

At the end of the work, insufficient measures were taken by the executive to ensure the cooling of the room. Also, insufficient arrangements were probably made in advance regarding temporary measures.

The Holder of the work permit himself was not directly involved in the execution; this was done by an outside firm. It is unclear what agreements were made with him and whether this employee reported to the Holder of the work permit.
Formally, the executor is not a party to the permit; this is a problem because one can then always claim to have no knowledge of the agreements made.

Security was not aware of any work and also had no visibility of the current status of the room/air conditioning units. This issue also played out in 2015 where misinterpretation of alarms played a significant role. The recommendation to make alarms of key rooms transparent to production has not been followed up to date.

Very limited resources were available to arrange makeshift cooling. Spaces containing potentially necessary materials are not always accessible to production; locks have been replaced over the years. This limits the ability to take action quickly (and is also undesirable from a disaster perspective).


Recommendations:

- Discuss with those directly involved the importance of correctly cancelling work permits/activities (FAC).
- Make clear agreements on how to act when abnormal situations are detected (PROD).
- For this type of work, make proper agreements in advance; record additional measures in a work plan or TRA.
- Have the person carrying out the work sign as Holder on the work permit; not a delegate who is not directly involved in the work.
- Ensure clear failure-signalling of important systems on duty (DCS); follow the 2015 recommendations!
- Ensure that the guard has access to all areas even outside office hours.

TITLE: Unexpectedly high noise emissions during waste heat boiler operation
CASE_DESCRIPTION: When the gas turbine 31 was run up to over 50% e-load, the increased steam production in the waste heat boiler, which was run off via the roof, led to extremely high noise emissions. The gas turbine run was therefore cancelled. Due to the design, it then took approx. 10 minutes for the noise level to drop back to an acceptable level.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The boiler has been shut down and the cause is being analysed.

As it was not possible to find the exact position where the noise originated based on the measured sound frequency of 1490 Hz, the start-up valve was dismantled. However, no abnormalities were found.
The investigation into the cause has not yet been finalised.
Short-term tests were carried out in order to avoid the noise development. It was possible to find a driving style that immediately stops the noise. In future, it is assumed that the operational situation that leads to noise development can be safely avoided.
Should further research into the cause reveal anything else, the appropriate measures will be retrofitted if necessary.

TITLE: Pole slip GT 3 huge stress on shaft and windings.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During GT3 start-up, the warning Pool slip occurs in the generator protections.

In short, the drive (gas turbine), due to the influence of rapid changes in power, tries to pull the magnetic field loose between the stator and rotor of the generator in a synchronous generator.
This phenomenon is dangerous for the plant, see below picture and explanatory text as an example.

The 30-07-2024 example shows that the warning pole slip occurs due to the rapid load change of >10MW/min.
Times between REG216 and the trend in TC7 are unfortunately not time-synchronised and differ by 1 minute 27 sec in this example.
2.19MW power increase in 11.8 sec, amounts to 11.1 MW/min increase (DWATT line is unfortunately not visible at this point)
Sample time trend is ca.15 msec
It appears that the maximum power gradient of 4MW /min which was set in the MarkV is not yet present TC7
Item 22 from the residual points list.
 

The 5-8-2024 example shows another much more extreme example.
The deviation between REG216 and TC7 here is 1 minute and 10 sec
In about 4 sec, the power goes from 48MW to -4.8 MW (backwatt. Shaded green) and back to 55MW.
1 sec later pole slip occurs again.
You don't need to be a rocket scientist to understand, what a huge interplay of forces is taking place here and that it will actually cause problems. Huge stress on the shaft and the windings.
Sampling time approx. 280msec.

Power fluctuations occur on and around switching to a different combustion mode of the GT.

TITLE: Open exterior doors geothermal power plant
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Operations conducted a control round at AWC on 20/10/24

On site, it was found that the two doors - of the inner
and outer shell - near boiler 20 were wide open. In order not to get unwanted
visitors at AWC (with all its consequences), both doors were
doors closed again of which the inner shell door was locked.

The guard contacted Security Center Maasvlakte (SCM) to
ask questions about the doors at AWC that were open. The employee
at SCM was able to tell that both the door contacts and the
badge readers had been bridged for months.

The guard raised with SCM that this situation is highly undesirable as they
do not receive any door reports, they also do not know which persons
present/registered at the site. This is a security breach.
Think sabotage, theft, accident (fatal or injury), etc etc etc.

The guard escalated this further by presenting this problem
to the Site Leader on duty.

------------------------------------------------------------
Site Leader inquired with the security specialist whether this situation is known. The security specialist indicated that he was not aware of any information regarding bridging. However, he can inform that there was never a handover during the conversion project to HAL and the related responsibilities in alarm follow-up were made known. In doing so, it could be that since the start of the conversion (Eneco/Uniper) to (Eneco/Uniper/HAL), everything has been deactivated and never updated.

Site leader then enquired from the operators who made the rounds at AWC on 19/10/24 whether they (accidentally) left the doors open. Answer is no.

The only other party present on AWC at that time (19/10/24) was a technician from Aardyn. Aardyn technicians have access to this location.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Doors AWC closed. Reinstate door alarms and badge readers on AWC . (Advice sought from security specialist)

TITLE: Near fire in RoCa3 due to leaking gland gasket quick-release valve supplementary boiler
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Due to the fire in May 2023, the cylinder of the auxiliary boiler was damaged beyond repair and replaced with a new cylinder.
The steam valve operated by the cylinder was leaking steam past the gland gasket. Due to the heat, the seal of the rod seal of the hydraulic cylinder failed and started spraying oil. The oil leakage was detected before the leakage increased to such an extent that oil spilled onto the hot steam parts and ignited.
The steam valve was not addressed during the repair after the fire.

With the recent repair, it was found (info Thorsten), that insufficient gland gasket was applied in the steam valve.

Note 1:
The quick release valve was externally inspected during the repair after the fire. It had not suffered any damage during the fire. To the best of our knowledge, this valve was recently overhauled by Fortum.

Note 2:
Uniper was lucky that the delivery of the hydraulic cylinder was so delayed. If this cylinder had been delivered during the heating season, it would have been used for so many 'running' hours that another fire would have broken out irrevocably.

Note3:
The date and time of the case is based on the period when the oil spill was discovered.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Actions taken:
- Hydraulic cylinder repaired by supplier
- Quick release valve made steam-tight again. (gland packing)

Recommendation for further actions:
- Checking gland gasket other steam valves
- Installing a thermal separation on the cylinder rod so that it is no longer exposed to the heat of the steam valve.

TITLE: Stedin at work on GOS site, without notification
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Time and notification:

According to the employee, these mechanics had been let in by the Productions department, but he wondered whether they had reported correctly to security.

Findings:
Checking revealed that the mechanics had not reported to security and had not received access passes. At the time of reporting, security was busy registering contractors and issuing passes, so this had not been noticed earlier. The 2nd security was driving a round along the substations, this prevented security on site from splitting up between operations.

Action:
Around 11:45 am, security contacted Nick Jager to discuss the situation. Nick and a member of security walked up to the mechanics to verify their status. They were two persons, whose names were unknown. Enquiries revealed that they had not been registered correctly.

Nick Jager then stopped work and gave the mechanics the opportunity to still sign in. However, the mechanics indicated they would leave the site. Afterwards, they were not observed at the counter.

TITLE: Work halted due to danger of collapse
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Monday 3-2-25, preparations began at the WSG site towards carrying out the Destructive Testing of the concrete foundation in the soil.

The preparations that have taken place are:
- Clearing the carriageway of the area to be investigated.
- Making test trenches around the area to be excavated
- Putting well drilling around the area to be excavated so that groundwater could be extracted into the subsoil over the weekend.
The excavation of the well started yesterday, 10 February. After arriving at 2m, it became clear that the groundwater was present to the extent that the made embankments were going to collapse.
Since the excavation had to go to 4mtr that and the subsoil was getting wetter, it was decided to stop the activities for safety reasons.
This problem was discussed with the PMer of UTbv and the engineering firm IOB and it was decided to stop the destructive testing, and reinstate the excavation
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Operations halted until further notice

TITLE: Dust leakage in REA 3 with alerting of the fire brigade
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Dust escaped during the unloading of lime hydrate in REA 3. The fire brigades in Ingolstadt and Großmehring were informed when the smoke alarms were triggered. The fire brigades did not have to intervene. No damage to persons or plant.

Detailed description:

The fire alarm system (FAS) triggered as intended on 23.12.22 at 9:20:20 after two smoke detectors (234/2; 234/4) of loop 234 REA 3 north side 16m responded.
The triggering was caused by dust escaping during the unloading of lime hydrate in the RRA Block 3 by the laboratory.

As the first firefighter to arrive at the fire station, Mr Seelking went into FGD 3 to investigate after a brief consultation with the control room.
When opening the FGD access door at 16m at the transition from the south stair tower to FGD 4, a heavy build-up of dust was detected in FGD 3 16m north side, and ventilation measures were immediately initiated in FGD 3.

In the meantime, the BtF's day shift personnel arrived at the fire station and the external fire brigades (Ingolstadt fire brigade, Ingolstadt-Mailing fire brigade, Großmehring fire brigade and the KBR Mr Lackner) were welcomed at the gate by Mr Jürgen Schmid. The commander of the Großmehring fire brigade, Mr Florian Schneider, was accompanied to REA 3 by Mr Schmid. After a brief briefing, the external fire brigades left again.

As usual, the dedicated line to the Ingolstadt ILS was switched off at 7:13:56.
The first smoke detector 234/2 was triggered at 9:17:06, the second smoke detector 234/4 at 9:20:20.
The second smoke detector then caused the external fire brigade to be alerted.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The system was ventilated and the fire brigade informed. Measures for future prevention must be planned.

TITLE: Oil leakage during testing of oil system of generator 2 in Leiden, the Netherlands
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
From Report by SPIT:
Maintenance company SPIT carried out major maintenance on
An oil leakage occurred while testing the oil system after generator maintenance. The test was with a generator (not rotating, not electrically coupled) secured during maintenance and the test was part of the maintenance protocol as the generator bearings had been disassembled for maintenance and inspection.
The test had been coordinated with Uniper in advance and necessary precautions had been taken for any oil leakage by the presence of the project team (6p) for observation and possible action, absorbent cloths and pellets.
Shortly after the oil pumps were started, a large oil leakage occurred from the bearing on the turbine side of the generator.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Oil (Inc. contamination of land or water)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Below from report by SPIT
Action:
 By direct observation, the oil pumps were stopped immediately, absorption cloths were placed/added at the leakage and buckets were provided.
Most of the oil could be collected in buckets (about 30 litres), the remaining oil (about 10 litres) flowed out of the bearing into the cloths on the steel floor on which the bearing is anchored. There was no stress situation (prepared test) and there was never a dangerous situation (absorption cloths), neither for machine (no damage possible) nor for mechanics and persons present (no risk or chance of injury).
After draining the discharged oil and saturated absorption cloths, the spot was first thoroughly cleaned with cloths and degreasers (brake cleaner and glass cleaner). For this purpose, the cloths were deposited in plastic bags in available containers, the oil in the designated storage vessel.
The bearing was then disassembled to find the cause. The cause was found immediately. A remaining cloth obstructed the outlet of the oil in the bearing seat, causing the oil level in the bearing seat to keep rising and the oil to seep out through the labyrinths as soon as the oil level reached this level.
The cloth could be removed quite easily with a gripper, allowing the oil to visibly flow freely back into the oil tank.

Analysis:
The (grey) cloth had been pushed into the exhaust before/during the cleaning of the bearing seat to prevent debris or particles from entering the oil lines during cleaning. This was not taken out after cleaning and not noticed before the bearing was closed after assembly.
A final inspection by a third person before placing the cap back on the bearing seat is not explicitly included in the working procedure, it is part of the assembly routine of relevant mechanics.
Inspecting the bearing seat before resealing it was not included as a witness point of witness/hold in this project.
It is possible that the focus on disassembling turbine-side generator bearing was less sharp because of the strong focus on the generation-side generator bearing, which was known to have leakage beforehand and oil contamination found during maintenance/inspection was visible in the generator and lower area.
There is no risk of generator fouling or damage, because the shaft/rotor has not been rotating oil is not sucked into the generator or pulled up the shaft, but seeps down through the labyrinths past the bearing seat.

Prevention: Such leaks are highly undesirable, so should be prevented. It is an unpleasant mistake, which the entire project team and project management care about and assessed among themselves afterwards with terms like "careless", "stupid mistake", "incomprehensible" that this happened to us.
The following follow-up and improvement actions will be implemented by Spit:

- Slide bearing de-/mounting during toolbox meeting (awareness)
- Addition to work procedure to have bearings checked by a third party/supervisor/customer before closing (prevention)
- Addition to work procedure to compulsorily take a photo of internal bearing seat (self witnessing).

TITLE: Partial shutdown SSC by switching operation
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Due to an electrical switching operation, 1 rail briefly lost its control voltage. As a result, 2 feed water pumps tripped and 1 return water pump tripped.
In the absence, or incorrectly set protection devices, the remaining feedwater pump ran very far outside the pump curve for a long time with periodically very high vibrations (25 mm/s). Pumps that were later restarted also subsequently ran very far outside their curve and tripped several times at minimum suction pressure.
The limitation of the pumps appears to be at the trip value so the existing protection/control cannot work.
Pumps are not protected on operating far outside their operating range. A lot of noise and vibration was observed by present personnel at that time throughout the supply water system.
From AW pump B, presumably the non-return valve was damaged as physical backflow was observed on site.
The return water pump operated well outside its curve for a prolonged period and the second pump, which became available again after a local reset, would not voluntarily synchronise with the auxiliary pump. (total flow equally distributed between the ancillary pumps) This action had to be performed on hand.

Finally got WSG back in control by operating 2 pumps on HAND and resetting AVR.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: SAP notification made for changing control suction pressure protections supply water pumps.
