TITLE: Tech Centre HV Maintenance Findings (May 24)
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the Tech Centre HV Maintenance a number of age / condition related hazards were identified on the HV electrical equipment that have the potential to cause harm / business interruption:

1. Partial discharge (PD) activity was identified on the PTB transformer circuit cable termination at the 11kV Scientific & Tech Centre Switchboard.

2. Fixed earth contact on one phase sheared during maintenance operation of the Winking Hill 11kV Circuit Earth Switch at the 11kV Scientific & Tech Centre Switchboard.

3. PTA Transformer Buchholz gas detection relay did not operate when initially tested.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
1. Partial discharge activity - Cable split and additional installation material added over visible areas of discharge. Recommendations - Warning notice / access restriction to switch room and regular online PD monitoring to be performed and trended (to be included in a maintenance management system).

2. Broken earth contact - Temporary repair installed and returned to service (Ductor and IR tested). Recommendations - Temporary repair to be replaced with OEM part(s) or reverse engineered substitute. Operational restriction + associated warning notice to be applied to switchgear (all outgoing circuits). Plant simulation to be recorded on Ratcliffe PS temporary simulation register. Increased frequency of inspection / maintenance of 11kV switchgear (to be included in a maintenance management system).

3. Buchholz gas detection relay - Relay exercised and repeat tested. Increased frequency of inspection / maintenance of Buchholz relay (to be included in a maintenance management system).

TITLE: Pole slip GT 3 huge stress on shaft and windings.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During GT3 start-up, the warning Pool slip occurs in the generator protections.

In short, the drive (gas turbine), due to the influence of rapid changes in power, tries to pull the magnetic field loose between the stator and rotor of the generator in a synchronous generator.
This phenomenon is dangerous for the plant, see below picture and explanatory text as an example.

The 30-07-2024 example shows that the warning pole slip occurs due to the rapid load change of >10MW/min.
Times between REG216 and the trend in TC7 are unfortunately not time-synchronised and differ by 1 minute 27 sec in this example.
2.19MW power increase in 11.8 sec, amounts to 11.1 MW/min increase (DWATT line is unfortunately not visible at this point)
Sample time trend is ca.15 msec
It appears that the maximum power gradient of 4MW /min which was set in the MarkV is not yet present TC7
Item 22 from the residual points list.
 

The 5-8-2024 example shows another much more extreme example.
The deviation between REG216 and TC7 here is 1 minute and 10 sec
In about 4 sec, the power goes from 48MW to -4.8 MW (backwatt. Shaded green) and back to 55MW.
1 sec later pole slip occurs again.
You don't need to be a rocket scientist to understand, what a huge interplay of forces is taking place here and that there are actually going to be problems from it. Huge stress on the shaft and the windings.
Sampling time approx. 280msec.

Power fluctuations occur on and around switching to a different combustion mode of the GT.

TITLE: Fall from roof during container installation
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A container system is being erected to extend the existing accommodation for a partner company. During assembly work on the first layer, an employee slipped, presumably due to wetness, and fell from the roof of the container. He was wearing PPE against falls from a height and was attached to a fall arrester. He received emergency medical treatment and was taken to hospital for further examination.
Fortunately, he did not suffer any serious injuries but only bruises.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Fall from height (Eg. Vertical drops from above or to below ground)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The retractable type fall arrester used has been secured. The required test document is available.
It must be clarified whether the retractable type fall arrester has failed due to a technical defect, whether the retractable type fall arrester was not used correctly or whether there are other reasons why the system did not block. If a technical fault is the cause, further steps must be taken.
The cause of the fall could be slippery sheets due to wetness. The extent to which technical anti-slip measures or organisational measures (criteria for "bad weather") or other measures need to be taken must be checked.
Irrespective of this event, it must always be ensured that employees are trained in the correct use of PPE and that the equipment used is in perfect technical condition.

It turned out that the entire repeater was de-energised. In fact, at the rear, the plug had come loose from the panel.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Fire / Explosion (affecting local inhabitants ,ecosystems or surrounding environment)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Plugged in again, after which the repeater started rebooting and returned to normal operation.

As soon as the cabinet door in which the repeater is mounted is opened, there is a risk of the plug coming loose from the repeater due to limited cable length. Despite the emergency measure in the past to remove the handle from the cabinet door (to prevent unwanted opening), it still sometimes happens that someone does open the cabinet door and unintentionally/unnoticed the plug comes loose and the repeater fails.
We recommend extending the cable so that the plug can no longer be pulled out by opening the cupboard door.

TITLE: Oil leakage above hot steam parts
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
As a result of the fire damage, the cylinder of the middle pressure quick release valve steam turbine was overhauled. Due to the delivery time of original parts, not all parts have yet been replaced or customised. Some oil is now dripping down the outside onto the steam line.
MH-Hydraulics has been on site. It very likely concerns an internal leakage. Due to the temperature on site, it is difficult to carry out work on site. To make a proper diagnosis, the cylinder will have to be dismantled and opened.
Original parts have been ordered. Enquiries on 04-12-23 reveal that parts are still missing. The lead time for overhauling testing etc is about 5 days.
The delivery date of the cylinder for the supplementary boiler is set at week 9-2024. This takes away the option of exchanging the cylinder with that of the medium pressure quick release valve in the near future.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
After observation, MH-Hydraulics was on site.
As a work around frequent inspection and cleaning.
Once all parts are in, disassemble, overhaul, test and assemble the cylinder. During this period, RoCa3 will not be available.

TITLE: Foot fracture during excavator work (green area renovation) at the Recklinghausen heating plant
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

The accident victim was cutting up a felled tree in the excavator's travel area for removal with a chain saw. He was wearing hearing protection, among other things. TITLE: Finger injury during cleaning work (FAC)
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

Visit to the doctor

TITLE: Accident at LNG petrol station Ulm-Seligweiler
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The service provider (Schenk GmbH) of Liqvis GmbH had an accident at our LNG filling station in Ulm-Seligweiler while delivering LNG. The tanker driver had new tyres on his truck and was tightening the nuts on his tyres after his work at the filling station. This caused the tool and the nut to become jammed. The release of the tool had an uncontrolled acceleration, so that the tool hit his lower leg and caused an open wound. Another Schenk lorry driver was refuelling at the site and called an ambulance. The ambulance administered first aid to the injured tanker driver and took him to hospital. At the hospital, the wound was cleaned and then stitched up. The driver was then able to leave the hospital. The Operations on-call service learnt about the incident from the forecourt operator, who was also on site, and from the Supply on-call service, who was contacted by Schenk. The LNG filling station was then taken out of service and the on-site technical service provider was sent to the LNG filling station. After ensuring that the LNG filling station was technically in order, the LNG filling station was put back into operation.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Manual handling - Load (Weight, size, stability, etc.)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: As people were on site and had already contacted the ambulance, the LNG filling station was taken out of service for safety reasons. As the accident is not directly or indirectly related to the LNG refuelling station, no technical measures are being taken. However, investigations are being carried out to ensure that the camera systems cover the entire petrol station area and that there are no hidden areas. In addition, it will be investigated whether there are AI-based camera systems that react immediately in the event of an accident. Further measures include informing service providers about the house rules within our premises, in particular that no lorry maintenance activities are to be carried out on our premises.

TITLE: On turning goggle flange GT-2 still gas pressure present.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During opening of flange connection, unwanted gas was released and this gas flow did not diminish because the valve passed through.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Work temporarily halted to remove hazard (gas pressure) by depressurising entire system. After this, glasses flange reversed and system re-pressurised quietly.

Turning the goggle flange is performed very regularly and also for work where a physical blocking (cutting off pipe) does not bring any benefits at all and introduces the high risk that turning this flange entails.  Therefore, the recommendation is to turn the goggle flange only when really necessary and not out of habit.

According to industry standards, with 18 bar gas pressure and diameter 150 millimetres, the installation should not be keyed open behind 1 valve and certainly not on the flange connection of that block valve!!! Move the goggle flange recommendation to the second valve in line so that you can create a double block and bleed, thus minimising the risk of the goggle flange turning.

TITLE: Alarmmanagement
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Alarm management on the RoCa/RWC/WSG systems is not in order. On the various systems, large numbers of alarms are presented which are unjustified. The risk is that the operator acts (or does not act) on the basis of incorrect information. Also, the quantity of alarms can lead to them being overlooked, sometimes even for days. This has already occurred several times and led to several incidents.
The problems have been raised several times in the past, but never adequately addressed. Please take action soon!
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: This problem has been highlighted in various ways in recent years, but for various reasons has never been adequately addressed. The risks are undiminished.

TITLE: Perloc valves conservation HD turbine unlocked
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Some years ago, a modification was made to the HD steam turbine whereby it was fitted with a fixed pipeline for conservation purposes.
This pipe connects an air dryer to the HD turbine and is fitted with two gate valves. These valves are both equipped with a special locking mechanism; a so-called Perloc system.
The keys to this system are released only if the valves are closed and must therefore be on guard before the installation can be started.

By chance, it was now discovered that the keys were not in the control room, but in the valves. Both valves were closed but unlocked. Probably, after an earlier repair, the keys had been sitting here for weeks.
Despite this, the plant was commissioned several times, but the absence of the keys went unnoticed.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Both valves locked, keys removed and returned to the control room.
The arrival of a Traka cabinet is soon going to help ensure that these keys can no longer be absent unnoticed.

TITLE: Level of day tank NSA of WKR too low
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Distributors 7CB/8CB were fully secured on Monday morning tbv a survey action for new power switch for the incoming feeds and torque switch. While 7CB/8CB was secured, the 7DA/8DA prevention distribution boards were powered by the emergency power generator (NSA) WKR.
After a few hours, it was found that the day tank of the NSA was low and almost no diesel was being pumped from the storage tank to the day tank.
Fortunately, the survey work was completed in time and we were able to switch the electrical system back to normal.
However, in blackout situations, the NSA needs to keep the critical components energised and therefore needs to be operationally reliable when the situation calls for it.
The oil system should therefore function without any problems. Periodic maintenance can ensure this
This applies to all sites.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Diesel oil filters of the system to pump from the storage tank to the day tank were pulled and found to be heavily fouled. Most probably, the storage tank is also fouled.
Recommendations:
In the short term, clean system and create PO plans to check this periodically and/or repeat cleaning.
It was also found that at load trial operation, WKR's NSA is underloaded. Report made to make a connection to the NSA panel to conduct load trial operation once a year with a load resistor by Royal van Twist company

Based on the statement from the emergency response team and supplemented with information gathered in the golden hour:
In the night from June 3rd to 4th, an incident occurred (around 01:20h) during brushing work in the boiler (76m) of MPP3, where a contractor injured his finger.

The injured person (IP) was working in a space in the boiler (ovo1.1) where the workspace is particularly narrow (43 cm wide). The IP was working just above head height with his left hand on the handle of the machine. With the right hand, he held the machine with the contact button pressed on. The IP moved over and released the contact button. During the machine's run-down (which takes 2 seconds), the machine slipped from the right hand and dropped/tilted - probably due to the machine's weight - slightly and in doing so, hit the right hand with the rotating steel wire brush between the thumb and index finger. The IP arrived at the hospital on June 4th (around 02:25h) and left the hospital later in the morning. Two subcutaneous stitches and six above-skin stitches were placed.

The employee was onsite the same day (4-6-2024 16:30h) for an incident investigation interview. The full report of the emergency response team is included as an attachment.

TITLE: Electric shock
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Touched the fine-wire fuse with a small finger as the necessary protective cap was not present.
The appliance was immediately taken out of service.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The appliance was immediately taken out of circulation and blocked for further use.
New purchase with internal fuse.
The inspection of the fog machine revealed the following:

The appliance was in order at the time of the DGUV inspection on 04/05/2022.
On the day of the accident, the device and the extension cable were taken out of service and checked in the workshop. The test showed that the extension cable was in order. However, the fog machine itself is not in order, which is why it represents a hazard and must be taken out of service immediately. The cover of the fuse was no longer present, so that one contact end of the fuse was exposed and the risk of direct contact with 230VAC is very high.
The cover of the fuse was found on the floor in the storage location near the fog machine.

Mr Sammüller probably came into contact with the fuse cover when connecting the remote control to the neighbouring socket (with his left hand), which is very easy to remove. The cover fell to the floor and he then touched the phase directly in the form of an open contact of the fuse.

Kind regards
Zlatko Tomic

The RCD of the feeder in question was (additionally) checked after the accident. It was in order. The RCD was not triggered by the electric shock. The reason for this is probably that the dangerous current required to trip the circuit breaker (30 mA) was not reached. The person concerned had touched the protruding fuse with their little finger and received a "wipe". She was well electrically insulated by the protective footwear.

TITLE: Foot injury due to falling object
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The injured colleague (Siemens AG) was asked to make the eccentric pin of the lateral height adjustment workable by inserting the pin into the fit several times until it started to jam, then pulling the pin back again and reworking the surface.
This process was to be repeated until the pin was easily inserted into the fit.
Disassembly of the pin was not planned at this point. When pulling the pin out of the clamping point, the pin slipped back unexpectedly easily and thus completely out of the guide on the housing.

TITLE: ELD: unauthorised modification of the fire alarm control unit
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
From Facilities ELD, a question had come to Facilities ALG as to whether it is possible to prevent the fire pump from being started when the fire alarm system is periodically tested. This causes water to enter the pipes. It is laborious to drain the pipes afterwards and the water causes pipe corrosion. The solution was found in incorporating a time delay between an alarm and the control of the fire pump.
This was implemented in an ad hoc manner by installing a time relay for control to the fire pump. See attached photos for the implementation.

The BMC administrator was informed of the modifications to the BMC by Siemens on 31-03-2025, during work on the BMC.

- The demand from Facilities ELD is legitimate and the problem had been noted earlier
   during inspections with Bilfinger.
- The modification was done (circa early March) during my designation as BMI
   administrator.
- The person who made the adjustments is aware that adjustments to
   fire safety installations are my responsibility (Henk Torenbeek).
- The BMI manager was not informed about the adjustments.
- The modification was done outside the Subcontractor (Siemens).
- No drawings were made of the modification. The adaptation is also not
   included in the BMC manual.
- The adaptation is not documented in the Siemens drawings.
- It is unknown whether the components used meet safety requirements.
- The adaptation is powered from a socket. This is not permitted from the Machinery Directive.

Consequences:
The adaptation may fail undetected, allowing the fire pump to start unintentionally without being noticed or, conversely, not start at times when it should. The integrity of safety devices is compromised.
Because the modification was done outside Siemens, this is not included in the maintenance regime and falls outside the impending replacement BMC.
Potential problems with the insurer due to unauthorised modifications having been made to the BMC.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Actions taken:
- Have Siemens return the installation to its original state

Further actions:
- With Facilities EDH, DO-E and Operations towards an alternative by adjusting in the procedures. (During testing BMC turn off fire pump's working switch. Include this in the work permit. Operators may secure the fire pump.

IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:

TITLE: Burn on the left forearm
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
While trying to open a condensate trap, a partner company employee burnt his left forearm on a hot surface (drain funnel):
The aim of the repair work was to overhaul a steam trap located above a funnel with poor accessibility. At the time of disconnection, the auxiliary boiler and therefore also the 13 bar rail, which is supplied via it, was out of operation. Some of the drains and vents of the 13 bar system collect in the aforementioned funnel under the steam trap. When the shift carried out the disconnections, the systems were cold and no danger could be recognised. The isolation was carried out properly and according to current standards.
Shortly before the employees started the maintenance work, the auxiliary boiler and the 13 bar rail were put into operation for a leak test on the condenser of the pump turbine. When the employees arrived, the funnel was already warm due to a leaking limit valve, but not too hot. There was no sign that the hopper would heat up any further. Within a very short time, as the pressure of the HPE was increased, the hopper heated up to an unacceptable temperature. However, this was only noticed when the employee touched the hopper with his left arm, which was covered by a pullover approved by the partner company, and injured himself. According to the employee, the injury was barely noticeable, which is why an attempt was made to complete the maintenance work. Further fittings were closed to prevent the hopper from heating up further or to cool it down, and at the same time the hopper was covered with a welding blanket to prevent contact.
The hopper was successfully cooled down, but the neighbouring steam traps were also hot. The operation was cancelled.
During a conversation, the injury then came to light, which is why the first aid measures were initiated."

TITLE: Scalding of customer service employee during replacement supply FW-Netz Gladbeck
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During scheduled work on a mobile heating centre (Hotmobil), a customer service employee suffered a scalding on his right shin that was about the size of a €1 piece. The PPE worn prevented a more severe scald.

During commissioning of the Hotmobile, the safety valve installed in the Hotmobile tripped.

With the intention of achieving additional pressure relief, the employee involved in the accident opened a KMF tap on the return line of the Hotmobile.
A steel flex hose was fitted to both the supply and return lines of the Hotmobile for depressurisation work at a different time (see photos in the appendix). After opening the KMF tap (RL line), this steel flex hose moved out of the floor opening and started to hit and splash.

In order to catch the hose again, it was fixed with the foot, which caused the scalding.

The safety parameters of the safety valve were exceeded due to an incorrect sequence of switching operations on the FW network and Hotmobil.

The mains and Hotmobile were unplanned connected for a short time.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Temperature Extreme (Inc. Hot or cold surfaces, gases and environments)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Immediate interruption of the work and securing of the network by pushing off the system components involved.

After removing the protective work trousers, the slight scalding was immediately treated with cooling packs. As a precaution, the employee was promptly taken to hospital for assessment. A suitable ointment was
was applied.
The managers and HSSE were informed immediately.

Once the cause of the safety valve tripping had been rectified, the replacement supply work was resumed.

The basic RCA was initiated.

TITLE: AWC : Unwanted fire and gas alarms during operations.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Several alarms were received in the control room of CR from Geothermal Power Station belonging to HAL: Fire alarm, Gas alarm all from installations directly related to HAL. There were software modifications operation at locations (download activities) which resulted in these unwanted signals coming in on the CCGT and unnecessarily burdening Uniper operators with these signals. According to HAL, software downloads were taking place and will possibly be the cause.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Unfortunately, no immediate action possible.

Recommendation : Implement good alarm management so that follow-up on alarms can also be carried out correctly. Unnecessary/unwanted alarms create situations where alarms are no longer taken seriously and are pushed away.

A good UPD and clear SLA is the basis and minimum for this!

In PLC, the term downloading is just the opposite of the expectation, downloading means putting new software into the PLC.

Changing software involving fire protection installations should always be checked for correct operation after a change, and the advice is to check the fire protection installations completely on the part where a change has taken place.  TMOC procedure should also apply if HAL changes anything (however minimal) involving Uniper installations.

In this area, the inlet grating has been lowered considerably for better drainage of the road. This results in a depression of approx. 20 cm directly in front of the kerb. The accident victim overlooked the depression and missed the pavement. This may have been favoured by the fact that he was wearing mouth and nose protection and his "normal glasses" fogged up as a result.
He caught his right shoe on the kerb, lost his balance and fell forwards. He reflexively performed an anti-clockwise rotation and hit the ground with his right shoulder. There were no work-related causes for the accident. It has not yet been possible to speak to the casualty.

TITLE: Crane jumped out of crane runway
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
In order to lift off the discharge box of the generator discharge on the GT-51, the special circuit up to a max. load of 300kg was determined after expert examination and clarification with the manufacturer KoneCranes. load of 300kg was determined and set up.
For this purpose, the crane operator and the AvO were instructed and it was also stipulated that the lift may only be carried out in the presence of the Uniper crane supervisor.

Summary of the measures:
- Crane operator instructed
- Maximum load on the crane hook 300 kg
- Lift may only be carried out in the presence of the Uniper person responsible for the crane.

Error:
The agreement was not adhered to.
- The lift was carried out without the presence of the person responsible for Uniper
- It was not the discharge box of the discharge that was lifted with approx. 300 kg but
   the bearing plate of the generator on the TS side with approx. 4500 kg

Result:
The crane was lifted out of the crane position when travelling over the specified lifting range with the
the crane was lifted out of the crane runway by approx. 100 mm.
When the load was lowered, the travelling gear could no longer reach its intended position. The travelling gear was therefore blocked.

No persons were injured and no machine components on the crane were damaged.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Crane, locked immediately
Inspection and set-up of the crane by the manufacturer
Instruction and advice that the agreements must be strictly adhered to.

TITLE: Near hit pedestrian collision
CASE_DESCRIPTION: While travelling to the airport after attending a 3-day course in Dusseldorf, it was a rainy day, and the tarmac was wet. We were driving around 30 - 40 miles an hour on a busy road when a pedestrian walked across the road without warning. The pedestrian was wearing a coat with a hoodie, presumably to stop them from getting wet. I couldn't see the pedestrian's faces during the emergency stop, and I could imagine the hoodie was blocking their view of the road from the side we were driving from. My colleague Faser Ali was driving and had to carry out an emergency stop.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Attending a Defensive Driving training would be recommended in order to be able to anticipate situations like this and avoid emergency stops.

TITLE: Minor RTA
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Location = M25 J25 4 lane roundabout above M25 from Enfield.

Parked up on inside lane of roundabout with handbrake on waiting for lights to change.

Observed odd activity from girl in car behind during queuing for a while to get to my parked position.

Watched her in rear view mirror engaging with a passenger in the back seat of her car – she turned around throwing a coat or something, and, I can only assume, let her foot off the clutch and drove into the back of me, so no handbrake on.

She immediately held her hands to her face in shock.

I gestured to acknowledge I had felt it!

My back felt the impact in 3 places – coccyx area, below shoulder and neck – all is OK for now, but my coccyx does still feel like it has been impacted. I will monitor to see if it doesn’t resolve itself.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
I got out of the car to indicate for her to follow me to a safer area, rather than hold traffic up and risk cars hitting us – the traffic lights began to change at this time so no time to get details or reg.

She then backed up and shot across the 3 additional lanes and left the roundabout in a lane she wasn’t positioned to take – prompting lots of horns and an annoyed driver to chase after her.

I exited on to the M25 because I could not get across to pursue.

Car drove (and still does) OK and on Inspection showed no damage from the impact.

TITLE: Smoke from a partner company's office container
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On 12 April 2025, an employee noticed smoke coming from an office container. He immediately informed the control centre, which then alerted the fire brigade.
The AGT team was alerted by telephone by the control centre at 15:03.
The emergency response was smoke developing in a container at the rubbish tip!
The AGT team arrived at the scene at the same time as 2 other control centre employees at 15:05 and was greeted by a signaller.
The person informed the emergency services that after noticing the smoke and informing the control centre, he had immediately disconnected the container unit from the power supply.
After a brief investigation of the situation, a clear smoke development with low heat radiation was detected inside the container.
The AGT team then fully equipped themselves with breathing protection, while the two control centre employees set up a water supply from the nearest wall hydrant.
On entering the container, the AGT team found a smoky interior, directly to the right of the entrance door was a charred & already destroyed microwave (Fig. 4) on a hob (Fig. 2), on closer inspection the AGT team realised that the right-hand temperature regulator on the hob was switched to level 3. The microwave was immediately removed and taken outside.
All windows of the container were opened to remove smoke. No extinguishing agents had to be used.
Due to the rapid interruption of the power supply and the fact that all the windows in the container were closed, no real flame was able to develop, it was merely a "smouldering fire".
Finally, the inside of the container was checked with the thermal imaging camera; there were no more hidden embers or sources of ignition.
The operation ended at around 15:30, the AGT team remained on site as a fire watch until 16:00. At around 5.45 pm, the AGT team carried out another follow-up check.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Disconnect the power supply to the container.
Container cleared of smoke
Fire watch

TITLE: Scaffolding was erected near generator switch 51 when the unit was shut down, although this work is only planned during maintenance shutdowns.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Scaffolding will be required at generator switch 51 during the overhaul from 5 April 2025. The scaffolding company was given the go-ahead to work as unit 5 was not in operation on the morning of 4 May and began erecting the scaffolding. It was assumed that the unit would no longer be in operation in the evening. However, as the unit received a start-up order in the afternoon, the scaffolding was dismantled again as a precautionary measure. This is because the flow of current through the generator down conductor can lead to uncontrolled earthing currents if metal parts are close to or leaning against it.
Information: At no time was there any danger to people or the system!
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Scaffolding in the vicinity of the generator discharges is normally only erected and operated when the unit is switched off. Approval was given on the assumption that there would be no more unit operation on the evening before the inspection.
The event was discussed in all the teams concerned.

TITLE: BHC Incomer Monitoring Incorrect Fuse Ratings
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Engineering investigated a report from operations regarding BHC switchboard voltage monitoring reading 0V. Upon investigation, it was found that out of the three inline fuses feeding the switchboard monitoring equipment (one fuse per phase), two of the three had blown. It was also noted that the fuse ratings were incorrect and mismatched (2A on L1 phase, 4A on L2, and 16A on L3). The 16A fuse was still intact. The datasheet for the monitoring equipment specifies a maximum ampacity of 3A, suggesting that the 16A fuse was significantly over-rated, and this is likely why it did not blow at the same time as the other two fuses. Incorrect fuse ratings can lead to damage of downstream equipment and poses a potential fire risk in the event of an overcurrent fault.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: fuses replaced with correct rating and synergi raised

TITLE: Sync Comp 400kV Alarms
CASE_DESCRIPTION: At 00:11 on 28/7/24 we received a 400kV interposing relay 110V DC MCB Trip alarm. This was raised as a P1 notification and communicated via email, although it did not cause any issues with the sync comp but it was a worrying alarm when added to other alarms that had been standing. A further alarm, 400kV CP 1 relay inoperative initiated at 11:15 and at 12:26 all indication was lost on X490, X493A, X493B & X493C, this prompted a discussion with TNCC and a request was made for the on call NGET SAP to attend site. On arrival, as expected from a previous alarm, the 110v battery charger was in fault and the output volts had dropped to 50V DC. This was the reason for the faults and it transpired, we had lost the fast acting trip capability.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
After further investigation it was determined that the 110V stand-by supplies could be applied by the installation of links in the X490 supply pillar and inserting fuses into the stand-by fuse holders at the top of the battery charger. This immediately brought the output voltage up to >120V. The unit on the HV Connection panel rebooted and the indication was restored to the switchgear graphics on the DCS and the alarm cleared.
All alarms have cleared down except the original 110V battery fault and the 400kV CBU Fault recorder alarms. Further investigations will have to be carried out on the battery charger unit under NF 21528133.

TITLE: Commercial loss due delayed start.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: After suffering a GT trip during the start at 05:30 (separate synergie entered for this) the unit synchronised at 07:30. During the hold period it became evident that the Steam Turbine X5 criteria would not be achieved for a number of hours. GT load was held back at 60MW which is unusual as this load should be around the 90MW mark. GT exhaust temperature was 465 degrees C which seemed low for the required HP steam temperature to clear X5. Theory that some HOF settings may be interring with run up, so a decision was made to shut the unit down and start again. Second attempt HP bypass appeared to behave as expected i.e. in flow control vs pressure control on previous attempt and X5 criteria was clearing at a more accelerated rate. GT load was held the same causing a prolonged hold period of 1hr 10mins vs 40mins expected. Looking back at previous starts the GT load is being pegged back at 60MW vs 90MW expected.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Raised with ROMs

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

Installation physically separated by competent person. Insulation resistance of cable and motor measured for possible damage at commissioning. Licence holder informed. Toolbox prepared. (This will be shared via HSEQ asap).

TITLE: Oil leakage above hot steam parts
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
As a result of the fire damage, the cylinder of the middle pressure quick release valve steam turbine was overhauled. Due to the delivery time of original parts, not all parts have yet been replaced or customised. Some oil is now dripping down the outside onto the steam line.
MH-Hydraulics has been on site. It very likely concerns an internal leakage. Due to the temperature on site, it is difficult to carry out work on site. To make a proper diagnosis, the cylinder will have to be dismantled and opened.
Original parts have been ordered. Enquiries on 04-12-23 revealed that parts are still missing. The lead time for overhauling testing etc is about 5 days.
The delivery date of the cylinder for the supplementary boiler is set at week 9-2024. This takes away the option of exchanging the cylinder with that of the medium pressure quick release valve in the near future.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
After observation, MH-Hydraulics was on site.
As a work around frequent inspection and cleaning.
Once all parts are in, disassemble, overhaul, test and assemble the cylinder. During this period, RoCa3 will not be available.

TITLE: Map of Co2 detection ""deliberately"" disabled and not restored.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
There was malfunction of 1 measurement point Co2 in mid-May 2022. Several parts are no longer available, the card has apparently been disconnected so the malfunction is "no longer present" according to the system. Despite the fact that there may no longer be a Co2 hazard it concerns a deviation from the licence (licence to operate) and one cannot override a security installation by removing the card from the system and not allowing the system to operate fully.

The fault itself can be traced in the logbook but the action of disconnecting the card is not described in the installation logbook. There is absolutely no safeguard on this bridging of a security system.

E.g. was fed back by Dräger on the basis of the annual preventive maintenance.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
No action taken yet, it is difficult internally to prevent this kind of thing because the sense of a UPD is not there and work is done without any sense of importance regarding regulations/fire safety installations.

Disconnecting/removing a card is not the solution, it should be a TMOC in which all facets of this installation should be secured as to why we don't have that card replaced and with it the UPD, drawings and procedures.

TITLE: Stickers on safety helmet
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
More and more colleagues are wearing safety helmets with stickers on them. According to the Health and Safety Portal, site of the Ministry of Social Affairs and Employment, you should not put stickers on safety helmets. Stickers, according to the site, cause the ageing process to accelerate, see the following link: https://www.arboportaal.nl/onderwerpen/persoonlijke-beschermingsmiddelen/verschillende-soorten-persoonlijke-beschermingsmiddelen/hoofdbescherming .
Apparently, it has also become policy to put stickers on safety helmets, as they are required to be on them after certain training courses are completed. Example is the training course 'Uniper- Specific HSE regulations City Power Plants'.

TITLE: Failure of cooling water pump 1 during shutdown of block 4
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the registered test operation from Thursday 12pm to Saturday 4pm on Friday there was a fault with cooling water pump 2. In total we had 2 pumps in operation at this time.
The reason for the failure of pump 2 was the failure of a temperature measurement at the bearing at 22:50 on Friday 28 January 22. At this time we were able to ensure operation with one pump due to the block line, so that pump 2 was not operated any further.
This performance was planned until the shutdown on Saturday.

On Saturday, the load distributor wanted to keep the unit connected to the grid until 10 pm instead of 4 pm, but with a lower output.
When the output was reduced from 360MW to 230MW, the cooling water pump 1, which was still in operation, was switched off, causing a protective trip and the unit was shut down.
Due to the cooling water failure, the turbine expansion had now also triggered as a result, so that the unit could not have been restarted immediately The load distributor then rejected a restart

A new test operation is not necessary
Ppe 4.2 has already been checked and tested and is ready for operation
The LT will be adjusted promptly, otherwise we would switch Ppe 1 to manual operation in the event of short-term operation - so that it cannot fail again.


Cause:
It is stored in the control system that pump 2 is the start pump and when the system is switched off, pump 1 switches off from a lower live steam quantity and pump 2 runs alone until the machine is in the turning gear There is an error in the software here. Pump 1 must not be switched off via automatic mode if it is running alone

A new test operation is not necessary
Pump 4.2 has already been checked and tested and is ready for operation
The LT adjustment will be carried out promptly, otherwise we would switch Ppe 1 to manual mode in the event of short-term operation - so that it cannot fail again.

TITLE: Main Gas Valve would not open.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: A recent Gas detection panel fault had closed the sites main Gas valve 10EKG70AA001 on protection. During the unit start up 3 attempts were made to start the GT for it’s DP run scheduled for 15:00 – 21:00. Each attempt failed due to time out of the fuel gas program as a result of 10EKG70AA001 not opening in time. On the 3rd start attempt, the valve was locally observed to see what was happening. It became apparent that the valve was trying to run open but not moving more than a fraction. Numerous attempts were made to drive the valve open, both electrically from the DCS, locally and manually using the handwheel. It was concluded the valve was either mechanically jammed or pressure locked. TITLE: Heat transfer buffers ROCA old.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

The temperature from the buffer (return water) had risen to 83°C and this was not noticed because we are not alerted to this this alarm only comes in at 90°C. Also, the colouring of the heat buffers from blue to red does not happen because the supply water temperature is too low. Conversion takes place at 85°C and at the bottom of the buffer this temperature is not reached.
We went down with the heating lines this summer, but did not look at the operational consequences.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
To avoid this problem in the short term, we have raised the firing lines 2 degrees so that the colouring of the buffers does return.
For the long term, notification 300010620365 has been made to lower the alarm settings and colouring value so that we regain operational reliability.

TITLE: Level of day tank NSA of WKR too low
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Distributors 7CB/8CB were fully secured on Monday morning tbv a survey action for new power switch for the incoming feeds and torque switch. While 7CB/8CB was secured, the 7DA/8DA prevention distribution boards were powered by the emergency power generator (NSA) WKR.
After a few hours, it was found that the day tank of the NSA was low and almost no diesel was being pumped from the storage tank to the day tank.
Fortunately, the survey work was completed in time and we were able to switch the electrical system back to normal.
However, in blackout situations, the NSA needs to keep the critical components energised and therefore needs to be operationally reliable when the situation calls for it.
The oil system should therefore function without any problems. Periodic maintenance can ensure this
This applies to all sites.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Diesel oil filters of the system to pump from the storage tank to the day tank were pulled and found to be heavily fouled. Most probably, the storage tank is also fouled.
Recommendations:
In the short term, clean system and create PO plans to check this periodically and/or repeat cleaning.
It was also found that at load trial operation, WKR's NSA is underloaded. Report made to make a connection to the NSA panel to conduct load trial operation once a year with a load resistor by Royal van Twist company

TITLE: Oil leak UST storage facility Krummhörn
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Tuesday, 12 January 2020, the operator OGE pumped machine oil into the intermediate oil tank for repair work on the ME 1 gas transport compressor.
After the repair work was completed, the oil stored in the intermediate oil tank was to be pumped back into the ME 1 machine.
The dismantled Uniper ME5 and ME6 injection compressors and the OGE ME1 and ME2 machines share a machine oil pressure line in this context.
During the dismantling work in the storage compressor hall, the pipeline in the hall was disconnected and not resealed in a pressure-tight manner. The cut machine oil pipes were only provisionally sealed inside the supply shaft of the compressor hall.
As a result of the pumping process, the oil did not return to the ME1 as intended, but instead emptied through the open pressure line in the supply shaft of the compressor hall due to the lower resistance.
The shortfall in the ME1 was compensated for by the OGE employee carrying out the work with fresh oil.
It was not until Friday, 15 January 2020 that the shortfall was discovered during a regular gauging of the oil quantities in the tank. The person responsible for the plant was informed of the shortfall on Monday 18 January 2020.
Immediate measures to contain the damage were initiated without delay. The responsible authorities and the plant operator Uniper were informed and the immediate measures were supported by the Aurich district authority.
There was no oil contamination of outdoor areas or public waters.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Oil (Inc. contamination of land or water)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Securing the tank farm systems against recommissioning.
Carrying out extraction and cleaning measures for machine oil at the supply shafts, the surface drainage system up to the central oil separator system / rainwater retention basin.
Damage assessment in the presence of all the above-mentioned authorities and the environmental expert Dr Spange.
Determination of further expenses for damage elimination (cleaning, soil sampling, replacement of contaminated soil if necessary, paving).
During the damage assessment, the discharge point of surface water after the oil separator into the public watercourse (Erbsenbinderschloot) was also examined. There was no discharge of machine oils / hydrocarbons.

TITLE: Damage to press sleeve Heinrich-Pardon-Straße, Recklinghausen
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A make-up line for the Reflex system from the RL primary is installed in the heating centre. Two pressure reducers were installed for safety (see diagram). The compression sleeve after the pressure reducer is torn off (photo 4834). As a result, the heating centre was flooded with primary water. Uniper was informed because the centre was steaming. The make-up line could be closed. The water was able to drain outside. However, further damage was caused. The Reflex system is partially damaged (photo 4850) and 3 temperature sensors (FW Sec VL and Sec RL and AF, photo 4875) are damaged (or their supply lines in the control cabinet).

Cause of damage:
The cause of the damage is not yet clear. At the time of the damage, all lines were insulated except for the make-up line. In addition, all ventilation holes in the double garage were open. This could be why the pipework froze. Or only the two pressure reducers may have frozen or been damaged by the frost, resulting in excess pressure in the make-up line to the Reflex system.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The make-up line could be turned off. The water was able to drain outside.
The control system was provisionally put back into operation by setting a fixed value for the volume flow controller (60 %) and securing the STW at 45° (photo 4877). The Reflex system was provisionally put back into operation by allowing it to feed district heating water from an ibc tank (see photo 4885 and 4889). The primary pipe was stripped so that it can act as a "heater" for the double garage. A fan heater was also installed and all the ventilation holes were filled with insulating wool (photo 4873).

Open points:
 Clarify the exact cause of the damage (pressure reducer? frost in the heating centre?)
 Avoid damage in future (keep heating centre warmer and / or do without make-up from primary RL and only use the ibc tank)
 Repair the control unit
 Repair reflex system
 Replace pressure reducer if necessary. Clarify assumption of costs (UWG, insurance, external company, ...?)

TITLE: Milk of lime contamination Process water
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Lime milk contamination of process water: The possibility of a backfeed from the WAA lime milk supply has been proven. There must be three reasons for this:
1. the basis was the recommissioning of the lime milk pump.
2) There were various difficulties with the availability of the pneumatic residents.
3. in the end, this led to the situation that the two lime milk ring lines were connected while pump 2 was in operation (point 1).
Under these conditions, the two valves listed in the report, 01GDN61AA301 Kalkmilch Ringltg.1 and 00GBT61AA305 Spülarm, opened. Kalkmilch Ringltg.1 (point 2).
Under normal conditions, this would only have led to the introduction of flushing water into the ring line of pump 2. Unfortunately, the process water pumps were switched off at precisely this point by one of the various pressure peaks in the system due to fast-running butterfly valves (point 3). The pumps switch on again automatically when the process water pressure drops below 4 bar. Due to the position of the pressure measurement at 0.0m, the evaluation of all other pressures must be provided with a static component.
This means that the 3.8 bar limestone system pressure is offset by less than 4 bar residual process water pressure in the worst case. As the process water system remains active even when the pumps are switched off and is therefore not leak-proof in reverse, it was possible to carry out a backfeed.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
We will increase the reconnection of the process water pumps from 4 bar to 4.5 bar, i.e. the reconnection will take place earlier. A higher value is not possible, as the fast-running pneumatic valves repeatedly cause considerable pressure drops despite the frequency converter.
- Optimising the interlock for flushing connections with incorrect delta p is not realistic due to the large number of flushing points / programmes in the WAA system.
- In order to prevent the problem of sluggishness of valves, we are making a far-reaching modification to the switching of the lime milk ring lines in order to minimise the influence of the flushing programmes on the process during a change of lines. This has already been done in the preparation/storage area.

TITLE: Heavy release of ash following lorry loading Loading lane 1 new ash loading.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Following the successful loading of the lorry, the loading system went into the off-programme as planned. This resulted in a blockage of the dosing roller on loading line 1, presumably caused by a foreign object in the system.
Due to this blockage, the flow of ash towards the lorry could not be stopped. The employee of the partner company who was present then activated the emergency stop of loading line 1. After successfully simulating the position feedback of the dosing roller, the programme could then be cleanly transferred to the exhibition. The lorry was able to leave the loading area.
During the activation of the emergency stop, the loading of the neighbouring loading line 2 was in operation at the same time. This had to be put back into operation. Due to the fact that loading line 2 also drew the product from silo 1 (just like loading line 1), conveying air got under the dosing roller of loading line 1 (simulated), which was still in operation, causing a backward flow of ash via the ventilation of loading line 1.
This could only happen because the corresponding shut-off valve of the conveying air system in the direction of loading line 1 was leaking in the closed position. This resulted in the uncontrolled escape of ash via the corresponding ventilation of the loading chute on loading route 1.
The estimated amount of ash is approx. 5 tonnes of E-filter ash.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Upon noticing the ash leakage via the loading bay on route 1, the partner company's employee immediately activated the emergency stop again. TITLE: Environmental incident: Pollution due to release of heating oil S in the oil pump house
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
In the course of maintenance work (integration of a plug-in disc) on the old connecting pipe from the slop oil tank pump house to the old heating oil tank, an uncontrolled release of approx. 50 litres of heating oil S occurred. The release took place inside the oil pump house.

Sequence of events:

In the course of the work permit procedure, an activation was created and provided by the shift personnel. This activation prevents/prevents unintentional start-up of the slop oil pump during work on the open pipework system.

To prepare for the opening of the pipe system, the affected pipe had to be drained. This was done via a hose connection with a ball valve shut-off on the pressure side of the slop oil pump.
The removed oil was fed into the leakage oil tank via buckets, the outlet of which is connected to the slop oil tank.

The insert disc was successfully integrated into the existing pipe system.

On the afternoon of 28 September 2022 at around 15:30, a message was sent to the process operating system stating that the oil detection in the oil pump house had responded. An on-site inspection was carried out by the shift personnel present. The oil leakage of approx. 50 litres was noticed.
The oil had escaped from the opening of the oil leakage container into which the buckets had been emptied beforehand. The foreman in charge of supply and disposal and the production manager were also informed by the shift personnel. The following immediate measures were taken:

-Informing the above-mentioned persons
-Scattering the leaked oil using oil binding agents
-Shutting down the heavy oil pump that was still in operation
-Closing the connection line between the oil leakage container and the slop oil tank
-Check the oil pump house and outside area for further oil leaks.

No further leakage was detected.
The cause is still being investigated.

Update 12.10.2022:

The cause of the leakage oil tank overflowing was an unnoticed rise in the slop oil tank with the slop oil pump, which pumps the oil into the heating oil S tank, switched off at the same time. This activation was necessary in order to be able to integrate the above-mentioned plug-in disc.
After emptying the pressure line into the leakage oil tank using a bucket, the connecting slide valve to the slop oil tank remained in the off position (normal state).
Any slop oil that continued to accumulate during operation was regularly fed into the slop oil tank. This caused the slop oil tank to rise and eventually spill out of the leakage oil tank.

The following points can be derived as lessons learnt, which are also illustrated in the action associated with the case:

-Timely scheduling and coordination of the disconnection/order execution with the smallest possible time delay

-Immediate pumping out of the slop oil tank before activation

-Normalisation of the activation as quickly as possible after return of the work permit
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
-Information of the named persons
-Scattering the spilled oil using oil binding agents
-Commissioning of the heavy oil pump still in operation
-Closing the connection line between the leakage oil container and the slop oil tank
-Check the oil pump house and outside area for further oil leaks.

TITLE: Conductivity increase in deionised water tank 1&2 due to input of well water
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the night of 5 January 2024 to 6 January 2024, the shift supervisor on duty noticed an increase in the conductivity of the deionised water after deionised water pumps (measuring point GCA40FQ001). In order to rule out an incorrect measurement, a control measurement was carried out by the power plant laboratory on the morning of 6 January 2024, which confirmed the increased conductivity.
The subsequent determination of the cause revealed that well water had entered the deionised water system due to an incorrectly positioned fitting (well water for temperature control of the oxalate air) in the FGD system.

The background to this is that the oxi-air required for oxidation in the scrubber is regulated to a specified temperature with water. Normally, the medium used for temperature control is deionised water. In this case, however, the supply was temporarily switched to well water because a defective piece of pipework (deionised water) was replaced in the FGD (order 76132669). The activation required for this involved shutting off the deionised water pipe and switching on the well water pipe in order to be able to continue supplying the temperature control system with medium.
After the pipe was replaced, the deionised water pipe was made operational again during the corresponding normalisation, but the supply of well water was maintained in parallel.
Due to the higher system pressure in the well water system, well water was able to flow backwards into the deionised water tanks 1 & 2 via the normalised deionised water pipe.

In the event of no fault, the valve for supplying the system with deionised water should have been opened and the valve for the temporary supply of well water should have been closed. In this case, however, both remained in position.

The power plant was not in operation at the time of the incident, which prevented the contamination from spreading.


Update:

Technical measures have been implemented to prevent a recurrence.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
- The electrical conductivity measurement was checked/confirmed by a manual measurement.

- The scope of the contaminated deionised water was limited to the two deionised water tanks by preventing contaminated water from entering the cold condensate storage tanks (Kako). (There was no water transport from the deionised water tanks 1&2 into the two cacos).

- The valve responsible for the entry of well water was closed and secured with a chain.

- The two communicating deionised water tanks were separated

- Both deionised water tanks were emptied and flushed separately

- New deionised water was produced using VE sheets.

- Thematisation in the early round on 08.01.2024 incl. decision to implement a technical improvement to prevent a recurrence.

TITLE: GT Trip from PRS ESV’s closing
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

Scada system alarms showed ESD system operated due to PRS common hand switch operated, (PRS\ESD\UA4002) and ESD trip from CDC control room (PRS\ESD\HS4002C) receipt of this alarm would indicate that the operator himself had activated the PRS trip by pushing the emergency trip button in the plant MCR This cannot of been the cause of the PRS trip due to the operator not pressing the push button in the MCR, this was witnessed by gas operations as they were present in the control room when the ESD system tripped. whilst the gas pressure supply to CDC did fall the cause of the unit trip was from combustion instability (humming). it is recognised  that the low gas pressure would have tripped the GT by activation of the low gas pressure trip signals however on this occasion 'Humming' occurred operating the MAX 3 protection trip before the low gas pressure trip signals were received. The load at the time of the trip was 414MWgen (full load in 'OTC operation).
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: STL contacted to establish his condition and personal safety.  Generating systems made operationally safe (Boiler, Steam Turbine, Feed & condensate systems), Both GT & ST shafts brought to cooling turning speed. Engineering informed of incident.

TITLE: On turning goggle flange GT-2 still gas pressure present.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During opening of flange connection, unwanted gas was released and this gas flow did not diminish because the valve passed through.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Work temporarily halted to remove hazard (gas pressure) by depressurising entire system. After this, glasses flange reversed and system re-pressurised quietly.

Turning the goggle flange is performed very regularly and also for work where a physical blocking (cutting off pipe) does not bring any benefits at all and introduces the high risk that turning this flange entails.  Therefore, the recommendation is to turn the goggle flange only when really necessary and not out of habit.

According to industry standards, with 18 bar gas pressure and diameter 150 millimetres, the installation should not be keyed open behind 1 valve and certainly not on the flange connection of that block valve!!! Move the goggle flange recommendation to the second valve in line so that you can create a double block and bleed, thus minimising the risk of the goggle flange turning.

TITLE: Damage to switch 5 connecting railway Heyden power station
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On 8 September 2022, points 5 were damaged during shunting work at Lahde station when a HHPI traction unit travelling alone bluntly drove over the points from track 12. However, the points were in the straight ahead position and were therefore hit. In the process, the linkage connecting the bolt hand lock with the switch blades and the switch linkage or a clamp point lock were damaged.

An on-site investigation by the railway operations manager of the Heyden power station revealed that the points can still be carefully operated in the straight-ahead position. This means that the supply of coal and ammonia to the power station is ensured for the time being.
However, a different procedure for shunting activities on the part of HHPI must be taken into account. HHPI has been informed of the current status and the written instructions of the railway operations manager.

The DB dispatcher at Lahde station has also been informed of the incident by the railway commissioner.


Furthermore, it is being clarified which repairs/repairs need to be carried out in the area of signalling and track technology in order to restore unrestricted use of turnout 5.


Update:

Turnout 5 was repaired on 10/09/2022 in terms of both the superstructure and signalling technology. All operational regulations laid down on 8 September 2022 are therefore no longer necessary and the usual regulations can be applied again. The responsible DB dispatcher was informed, as was the responsible RU "HHPI".
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
- Assessment of the damage by KW staff and the railway officer responsible for the power station
   responsible for the power station
- Locking of switch 5 in the straight-ahead position to enable operation of the power station
  to enable operation of the power station
- Information to the DB dispatcher
- Information to the dispatcher at HHPI
- Contacting DB to rectify the damage

TITLE: Staudinger IBN block 4 and vaporisation of oil (control oil) from the insulation of the LPU.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

We were not informed in advance that this was a possible incident (leakage / leakage of control oil that had run into the insulation) during reassembly by GE.
GE was informed immediately and will also carry out an analysis.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The IBN was cancelled. All ventilation systems in the block were switched on and opened during the incident. Roller shutters were also opened. Access to the block was blocked and employees were informed.
On 14.11.22 the clean-up in this area will take place, i.e. the insulation will be completely removed and a sample taken, the area around the HDU will be cleaned
A leak test of the control oil is also carried out again.
An extraction system is installed as a precautionary measure for another IBN.
The employees directly affected were all informed about the incident on 11/11/22.
All employees who were on the control room, shift or in the block during the IBN were recorded and received a record sheet on 11/11/22 to register how long they had been working at the source (NDU) and at what intervals.
The operating instructions and the data sheet were also sent to the employees and managers. On Thursday 10.11.22, a consultation took place with the company doctor who offers a blood test for the employees concerned.
Important note. We do not see any danger to employees at this point - however, due to our duty of care, we have considered it important to inform employees in detail and also to offer this blood test.

TITLE: Water ingress into buildings
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Due to a local heavy rainfall event (approx. 35 litres/m² within 60 minutes), water ingress occurred in the area of the cable ducts and the EB system. This was detected by an earth fault in the fire alarm system, which led to a fault message "Object protection fault" in the ZEW. The control room operator on duty informed the on-call service. After a brief search for the fault, a massive ingress of water was recognised in the area of the EB system. After consultation with ZEW and the on-call supervisor, the local fire brigade was alerted. As soon as they arrived, they began pumping out the ingressed water in order to protect the EB system. While the fire brigade was still on duty, the standby and on-call supervisors checked the entire building for further water ingress and, at the same time, for the possible cause of the damage. The latter could not be determined at the time of the damage.
It was not until the following day that a rainwater inspection chamber in the immediate vicinity of the building, which showed signs of a massive backflow, could be identified. Several pipes drain into this shaft, some of which are no longer in operation and run in the above-mentioned cable ducts.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
As an immediate measure, in addition to pumping out the water, the entire surrounding area was checked for further water ingress and the electrical systems located there were inspected to rule out any possible danger.
Furthermore, the rainwater drain, which appears to be partially blocked, will be inspected and flushed in the short term (probably in week 22) in order to prevent similar backwater in the future. Furthermore, the deactivated pipes should be checked to see whether they can be dismantled or otherwise made safer.

TITLE: Water shot incident
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On May 14th at 21:45 hrs, Both CPUs were running from T-302 (crude mix: Doba 96.88%, Dar 1.21%, Nile 1.91%) and panel operator found feed pump discharge and column pressure increasing beyond control, both units forced to shut down suspecting water shot.

During above the operations team noticed increased levels on back pressure in the Flash column, which could lead to an activation of automatic trip sequence shutting down the crude feed pumps (P-1-001 & P-2-001), all other main equipment will follow to shut down after trip sequence. Due to this and to avoid further process and plant safety and potential H&S problems both units taken to shut down. There was a loss of production of 6 hours 45 minutes in CPU 1 and 7 hours 35 minutes in CPU 2.


The CPUs are prepared as per design to take up to 3% suspended water but not to process free water, this is perceived as the main risk for this type of events. Similar events had occurred on 3rd March 2021. One of them was automatic trip due higher P in the Flash column.

The most likely scenario in case of not addressing this situation in time is would be a pop up of the Pressure Safety Valve (PSV) in the Flask Column. In this case the affected unit will suffer unplanned unavailability for the reinstallation of the PSV. In case of additional failure of the PSV, the failure could lead to a malfunction in the Flash column potentially leading to release of vapours (depending on where within the flask columns the failure materializes it might lead to release of vapours, crude etc).
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Furnace stopped and feed flow minimized.

Units taken to shut down by stopping pumps P-1-001 and P-2-001

TITLE: Fire incident at the FGD raw gas flap in unit C
CASE_DESCRIPTION: In unit C, there was heavy smoke development in the area of the raw gas flap inside the FGD building. The fire brigade was called and the fire was quickly extinguished. No major fire damage was found. The cause of the fire was leaking hydraulic oil from the flue gas flap drive. The area was stripped as far as possible to localise the leakage. Despite moving the raw gas flap, no further oil leakage from the hydraulic system can be detected at present. The FGD is now being put back into operation and unit C will continue to operate. A fire watch will initially monitor the fire area around the clock until Monday. The shift operation regularly monitors whether oil is leaking again. Further investigations will take place on Monday to find and eliminate the leakage.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
- Securing the area
- Support from the fire brigade
- Heat imaging cameras for monitoring
- Cause analysis initiated
- Soaked insulating wool was generously removed, leaks were eliminated.

A loosened pipe bracket in the Ermeto pipework caused increased vibrations in the pipework. This was followed by a leak at a screw connection to the drive unit, which led to smoke developing in the hot flue gas duct due to the soaked insulation material. The insulation material was replaced over a large area in the area of the drive unit. The screw connection was retightened and all pipe supports were checked and repaired. These measures were also carried out in the identical Scholven B unit.
After the repairs, the area was checked by a fire watch for 48 hours. No further leaks or smoke development were detected. Regular checks will prevent recurrence.

TITLE: Slight oil leakage from heavy oil preheater 2 in the course of maintenance work.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The Heyden power plant has 2 heavy fuel oil preheaters arranged in parallel, one of which is on standby.
During the 2023 inspection, the pipe bundle of heavy fuel oil preheater 1 was to be pulled and replaced. At this time, the entire heavy fuel oil supply/preheating system was out of operation. The auxiliary steam rail required for preheating was depressurised.

The two preheaters were mixed up in the course of the activation and release procedure. As a result, although preheater 1 was correctly disconnected from production, the stripping work, including scaffolding, was carried out on preheater 2, which was incorrectly in an operational state.

In the late afternoon of 19 June 2023, preheater 2 was finally opened by the specialist company Veltec. The foreman discovered a drip leak after cutting the seal. This drip leakage was immediately contained using a saucer and oil binding agent.
It should be added that the total oil leakage was less than or equal to 10 litres and took place in the oil collection tray of the heavy oil preheater. There was therefore no spillage outside the drip tray.
Veltec's foreman immediately triggered the reporting chain and informed the power plant accordingly.
In order to prevent any further oil leakage, preheater 2 was immediately disconnected, drained and vented by the production department.

The maintenance department decided to replace the previously severed seal and then reseal the preheater so that it could be made available to production for normalisation.

The tube bundle of the heavy oil preheater 1 will be replaced at a later date. This meant that preheater 1 could also be normalised by production.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
- Provision of a saucer to collect the dripping oil
-binding the leaked oil with binding agent/fleece
-Triggering the reporting chain by informing the KW staff
-Creation of the affected preheater by the production department

TITLE: Open exterior doors geothermal power plant
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Operations conducted a control round at AWC on 20/10/24

On site, it was found that the two doors - of the inner
and outer shell - near boiler 20 were wide open. In order not to get unwanted
visitors at AWC (with all its consequences), both doors were
doors closed again of which the inner shell door was locked.

The guard contacted Security Center Maasvlakte (SCM) to
ask questions about the doors at AWC that were open. The employee
at SCM was able to tell that both the door contacts and the
badge readers had been bridged for months.

The guard raised with SCM that this situation is highly undesirable as they
do not receive any door reports, they also do not know which persons
present/registered at the site. This is a security breach.
Think sabotage, theft, accident (fatal or injury), etc etc etc.

The guard escalated this further by presenting this problem
to the Site Leader on duty.

------------------------------------------------------------
Site Leader inquired with the security specialist whether this situation is known. The security specialist indicated that he was not aware of any information regarding bridging. However, he can inform that there was never a handover during the conversion project to HAL and the related responsibilities in alarm follow-up were made known. In doing so, it could be that since the start of the conversion (Eneco/Uniper) to (Eneco/Uniper/HAL), everything has been deactivated and never updated.

Site leader then enquired from the operators who made the rounds at AWC on 19/10/24 whether they (accidentally) left the doors open. Answer is no.

The only other party present on AWC at that time (19/10/24) was a technician from Aardyn. Aardyn technicians have access to this location.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Doors AWC closed. Reinstate door alarms and badge readers on AWC . (Advice sought from security specialist)

TITLE: Near fire in RoCa3 due to leaking gland gasket quick-release valve supplementary boiler
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Due to the fire in May 2023, the cylinder of the auxiliary boiler was damaged beyond repair and replaced with a new cylinder.
The steam valve operated by the cylinder was leaking steam past the gland gasket. Due to the heat, the seal of the rod seal of the hydraulic cylinder failed and started spraying oil. The oil leakage was detected before the leakage increased to such an extent that oil spilled onto the hot steam parts and ignited.
The steam valve was not addressed during the repair after the fire.

With the recent repair, it was found (info Thorsten), that insufficient gland gasket was applied in the steam valve.

Note 1:
The quick release valve was externally inspected during the repair after the fire. It had not suffered any damage during the fire. To the best of our knowledge, this valve was recently overhauled by Fortum.

Note 2:
Uniper was lucky that the delivery of the hydraulic cylinder was so delayed. If this cylinder had been delivered during the heating season, it would have been used for so many 'running' hours that another fire would have broken out irrevocably.

Note3:
The date and time of the case is based on the period when the oil spill was discovered.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Actions taken:
- Hydraulic cylinder repaired by supplier
- Quick release valve made steam-tight again. (gland packing)

Recommendation for further actions:
- Checking gland gasket other steam valves
- Installing a thermal separation on the cylinder rod so that it is no longer exposed to the heat of the steam valve.

TITLE: Near fire in RoCa3 due to leaking gland gasket quick-release valve supplementary boiler
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Due to the fire in May 2023, the cylinder of the auxiliary boiler was damaged beyond repair and replaced with a new cylinder.
The steam valve operated by the cylinder was leaking steam past the gland gasket. Due to the heat, the seal of the rod seal of the hydraulic cylinder failed and started spraying oil. The oil leakage was detected before the leakage increased to such an extent that oil spilled onto the hot steam parts and ignited.
The steam valve was not addressed during the repair after the fire.

With the recent repair, it was found (info Thorsten), that insufficient gland gasket was applied in the steam valve.

Note 1:
The quick release valve was externally inspected during the repair after the fire. It had not suffered any damage during the fire. To the best of our knowledge, this valve was recently overhauled by Fortum.

Note 2:
Uniper was lucky that the delivery of the hydraulic cylinder was so delayed. If this cylinder had been delivered during the heating season, it would have been used for so many 'running' hours that another fire would have broken out irrevocably.

Note3:
The date and time of the case is based on the period when the oil spill was discovered.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Actions taken:
- Hydraulic cylinder repaired by supplier
- Quick release valve made steam-tight again. (gland packing)

Recommendation for further actions:
- Checking gland gasket other steam valves
- Installing a thermal separation on the cylinder rod so that it is no longer exposed to the heat of the steam valve.

TITLE: KWIr, unit 3; HEL leakage at burner level 5
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On 14 June 2022, a trial run of unit 3 was carried out from 4:00 am. The first burners were ignited with (extra light heating oil) HEL at 4 a.m. The grid was switched on shortly after 6 a.m.
The entire HEL route from tank 4 to the boiler house was monitored by the shift with regular inspection rounds. The last inspection round was completed by around 8.15 am. No abnormalities/leaks had been detected by then. At around 8.25 a.m., an employee noticed HEL leaking down to zero metres in boiler house 3. He immediately informed the control centre. An intensive search for the cause/leakage was carried out immediately. At the same time, the oil spill was stopped with oil binding agent.
The oil was escaping from a leaking three-way valve on burner 5.1. The burner was immediately taken out of operation and the oil supply stopped.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Water (Inc. excess volume, lack of, uncontrolled release or excess use)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
- Oil supply stopped by burner off
- Oil binding agent in the area of the oil pool to zero metres
- Opening of a floor drain, into which HEL had obviously penetrated, this leads into the boiler drain pit block 3
- Boiler drain pumps were secured in the "Off" position; no boiler drain water was pumped into the cooling water pipe leading to the Danube. A hazard to the water could thus be safely ruled out.
- Submersible pumps were set up to ensure stable plant operation and pumped into the substance-tight sinks.
- The pumped water, which is obviously slightly contaminated with HEL, is sampled. Environmentally friendly disposal is then arranged.

Thanks to the high level of experience and qualification of the shift workers (reinforced by two additional people for the trial operation), action was taken quickly and purposefully.
This prevented a fire and/or environmental damage to the Danube!
