TITLE: Incident during shunting activities on tracks 11 and 12 by HHPI
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Friday 12 April 2024, an incident occurred during shunting operations carried out by the RU Heavy Haul Power (HHPI). The train set parked in the Lahde transfer station forgot to remove a brake shoe before shunting work began. This is used to secure the parked train set against rolling away and should have been removed by the RU before shunting operations began. As a result of the shunting activities, the brake shoe was pulled along by a shunting unit and finally became wedged in switch two, which connects tracks 11 and 12.
The rail transport company was able to remove the wedged stop shoe from the affected switch. Furthermore, the points were checked by a DB InFraGo employee and declared passable. The power station has not received a corresponding report. It should also be noted that the power station was not informed of the planned shunting activities in advance.
The power station was only informed of the facts by the railway undertaking HHPI after the incident. After receiving the information, the power station called in the responsible railway operations manager, Mr Heinz Imgrund, and informed him of the incident. No significant damage to switch 2 was found, so that the switch was released by the railway operations manager as "fully operational".

A written report on the incident from the railway undertaking is still pending.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
-Contacting the railway operations manager (Mr Heinz Imgrund)
- On-site inspection of the points.

TITLE: NOX limit exceeded at the main steam generator
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The Durag evaluation system detected an exceedance of the daily average NOX value at the main vapour generator. 104.66 mg/Nm³.

Cause:
The time of the Durag computer is offset by one hour. The UTC time is used in the computer and not the UTC+1h time valid for us. This results in 12 half-hourly mean values for this journey and not 10, which means that no valid daily mean value can actually be calculated.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Adjusting the Denox start-up time

TITLE: Issue untested personal gas meters
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Some time ago, adhoc personal gas meters were introduced as unodorised natural gas was being used temporarily.
Afterwards (the gas has since been reodorised), discussion arose regarding permanent use (sense of insecurity) and it was decided to continue to mandate use and conduct additional research into the usefulness and necessity.

Gas meters are still issued daily, but:
- are no longer functionally tested; there is no bump testing.
- registration is completely neglected; a good number of meters are not present.
- the usefulness of the sensors present is debatable (especially CO and H2S).

No one now feels responsible for management; clear instructions and supervision are lacking.

Meanwhile, people who are given a meter feel protected, which may therefore be a sham.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The promised research has been a while in coming; we need clarity on the use, usefulness and necessity as soon as possible!
If we want to continue using personal meters, clear agreements need to be made, including with regard to issuing, testing and registration.

TITLE:
Unit 71 trip due to instantaneous increase in bearing vibration.
RB - EXTENDED 30/05/2022 Centre led investigation.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The unit was running through overnight at baseload. During a load change from approx. 380 MW to 400 MW, max 2 vibration levels were exceeded on both GT 1&2 channels resulting in an instantaneous full load trip.  It was also reported that a visible plume was seen emerging from the top of U71 stack.
The condition monitoring team at UTG were contacted by the STL and requested to analyse the plant data at the time of the incident, and to advice likely immediate causes and next steps. It was shortly reported back from UTG that early indications of the event were attributable to a likely loss of mass from the GT LPT stages.
UTG were mobilised to site to undertake a boroscope inspection which concluded liberation of blade and vane material across LPT stages 2-4.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Unit put onto forced cooling followed by planned shut down and isolation in readiness for boroscope inspection activities

TITLE: Pressure switch failure leading to oil release

Technician managed to shut away the pressure switch to stop the leak.  The pressure switch was replaced during the outage.  Upon closer inspection it was found that the rating on the side of the pressure switch was 12 bar or less.  The system it was fitted on runs at 120 bar.  The markings on the side of the pressure switch were very small and almost ineligible. After investigation it was found this indication was sensing pressure range and not max pressure. Switch was rated for system integrity wise.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Pressure switch isolated to stop leak.  Defect raised for a replacement of switch to correct specification.

TITLE: U7 Chimney Stack integrity failure (external RCA in progress - (EXTENDED 31/12/2022 Panel of Enquiry) 14/10
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 13.20 on Friday 18th February 2022 the integrity of Unit 7 Chimney Stack failed in high winds. The chimney stack collapsed and folded at a height of approx. 35-40m onto the corner of the HRSG roof, causing the top of the stack to collapse down the north side of the building in between Unit 7 and Unit 6.
Unit 7 GT Trip Push Button was initiated from the CCR at 13.21.
Unit was shut down as safely as possible with the GT & ST going On Barring. U61 was also shutdown in a controlled manner as a precaution, whilst U81 was already non operational due to Outage activities progressing.
A full site evacuation was ordered, with all site personnel and contractor workers being fully accounted for. There were no reported injuries or off site local impacts as a result of the collapse.

This incident occurred during storm Eunice, with a red weather warning Met Office alert having been issued earlier that day (having already been upgraded from an Amber alert issued the previous evening). Site had already implemented the high winds procedure which restricted any external work activities. This measure was agreed and communicated following the morning meeting performance dialogue. At approx. 12:00 hrs, as a further control measure all non essential works were ceased on site, with all contractor workers being stood down and returning to their respective office/messroom facilities.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Unit 7 was manually tripped and shut down safely - MEL'd to Zero until further notice pending investigation.
U61 was also shutdown in a controlled manner as a precaution, whilst U81 was already non operational due to Outage activities progressing.
A full site evacuation was ordered, with all site personnel and contractor workers being fully accounted for. There were no reported injuries or off site local impacts as a result of the collapse.

TITLE: Falkenhagen methanisation fire alarm
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On 20 May 2022, a fire alarm was triggered in the methanation system at the Power to Gas plant in Falkenhagen and the local fire brigade was sent to the plant by the Uniper dispatching team. The alarm in the methanisation plant turned out to be a false alarm.
The background to this false alarm is a planned maintenance measure by the grid operator in the neighbouring transformer 103 in Falkenhagen. Although the shutdown of the transformer should officially only affect the medium-voltage level 20kV, the shutdown apparently also leads to the shutdown of the domestic supply of the plant. When the transformer is switched on or off and, as a result, when the voltage to the control systems is interrupted, the alarms are set.
The network operator EDIS was contacted about the faulty communication of the switching release. A request was made to avoid this switching in the substation.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The fire brigade and emergency services of the Edis service provider were informed and sent to the plant (MGMT Dispatching UST incident).

TITLE: Water shot incident
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On March 3rd 05:45 hrs, right after the feed tank change over from T-303 (crude mix: Doba 40.69%, Dar 34.35%, Nile 24.95%) to T-301 (crude mix: Nile 22.28%, Doba 73.50%, Dar 4.24%) both units had to be shut down due to a water shot.  
 
Following the tank feed switching operation the operations team noticed increased levels on back pressure in the Flash column, which could lead to an activation of automatic trip sequence shutting down the crude feed pump (P-001), all other main equipment will follow to shut down after trip sequence. Due to this and to avoid further process and plant safety and potential H&S problems both units taken to shut down. There was no loss of production as it happened during start up process.
 

The CPUs are prepared as per design to take up to 3% suspended water but not to process free water, this is perceived as the main risk for this type of events. Similar events had occurred only 3 times in the asset lifetime, including this one. One of them was automatic trip due higher P in the Flash column.

The most likely scenario in case of not addressing this situation in time is would be a pop up of the Pressure Safety Valve (PSV) in the Flask Column. In this case the affected unit will suffer unplanned unavailability for the reinstallation of the PSV. In case of additional failure of the PSV, the failure could lead to a malfunction in the Flash column potentially leading to release of vapours (depending on where within the flask columns the failure materializes it might lead to release of vapours, crude etc).  

The crude feed tank that was being used , T-301, had been last operated by Uniper Ops team, on February 24th, due to vessel discharge operations was. In this case the available time for tank preparation was sufficient.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Furnace stopped and feed flow minimized.
Units taken to shut down by stopping pumps P-1-001 and P--001 (Crude in pumps ).

TITLE: Failure of transformer 10AT31 and customer interruption of steam supply
CASE_DESCRIPTION: A faulty trip caused by a defective protective relay on transformer 10 AT31 led to a disconnection of the 35 kV upper voltage side and consequently to a failure of the 5 kV busbar 10BA in Scholven SH2. This meant that essential components of the internal power supply were de-energised. As a chain reaction, air compressors, FH pumps, boiler 7 and components of the steam reduction station failed, which caused severe steam pressure and temperature fluctuations and thus led to the shutdown of the customer Ineos Phenol (45 bar steam). The Gladbeck district heating area of UWG and the 400 V station of BP were also affected.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: All equipment was checked to see if there was actually a short-circuit fault. After all of the equipment except for the transformer in question was found to be faultless, clutch 10BA/10BB was switched on at 3:47 and the affected busbar was supplied with power again. All components were then put back into operation step by step.

TITLE: Traffic accident in the area of the hot water pipeline of PTG/Methanierung Falkenhagen
CASE_DESCRIPTION: A lorry and trailer being loaded at the Pritzwalk veneer plant crashed into the methanation hot water pipe with the crane extended. The accident took place on a public road. The bridge that crosses this public area was completely torn over (45°). The accident was caused by the lorry reversing slowly with the loading crane (1.5 t) extended. Due to the heavy weight of the lorry and the slow speed, the lorry driver did not notice the contact with the bridge for a relatively long time and therefore pressed for a very long time.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The lorry driver and the neighbouring veneer factory have informed the police and recorded the damage. The accident number has yet to be ascertained. The police involved the Pritzwalk volunteer fire brigade.
After we received the accident, the service provider on site (E.DIS) was asked for assistance.
E.Dis also recorded an incident report for us in parallel with the police. Edis was also able to clarify the condition of the pipe (had been emptied and secured) with the fire brigade.
E.Dis is now involving its own service provider (pipeline construction) to separate the pipeline to the left and right of the road. The service provider has also organised a lifting platform for this purpose.
The veneer plant has offered to organise a crane that can lift and lower the bridge.
The recovery of the lorry and the bridge is expected to take place this afternoon.


Update from the afternoon of 21.07.2021

A brief summary of the current situation.

As summarised below by Edis colleagues, the accident site was cleared this afternoon. The Edis employees and the employees from the veneer factory were able to do this together with the appropriate technology. The local hire company for construction equipment was also able to provide the lifting platform at short notice. EDIS treated the incident as an official incident and charged us the costs as agreed. As always, the veneer factory supported us in a good neighbourly relationship.

TITLE: Failure 35kV
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
25.03.2024 00:26 Failure 35kV
The circuit breaker was to be disconnected for the switch overhaul on the 35KV LS UW Buer cable 1/2 in bay 10AG02D001 taking place on Monday 25 March 2024.
After notification and consultation with LIW, the door from Sh4 / 35KV was opened to relieve the pressure and waited outside the building for LIW to switch off the circuit breaker. LIW switched off the outgoing cable 1/2 before switching off the 35KV LS in UW Buer and no more current consumption was displayed. The switching noise of the 35KV LS in Sh4 was perfectly audible.
When switching the system isolator system 2 in bay 10AG02, a loud popping noise was heard and a strong flashing could be recognised through the glass panes from the upper system area (system isolator). An odour of burning was then detected.
In consultation with LIW, the upper system separator area was visually inspected through the glass pane. This revealed that the system isolator had opened and no visual damage was recognisable.
The 35KV circuit breaker signalled an out signal and was pulled out of the cell and de-energised. The switch is located in front of the cell on the switching gear.
When measuring the contacts (with a fluke/multimeter), a resistance of 32 ohms was measured between the upper and lower contact on phase L1 when the circuit breaker was open. This means that the switch on phase L1 did not open when it was switched off.            
Information LIW:
When the system disconnector was switched off, various protective excitations occurred and the 35KV system voltage increased.
Impact Scholven:
Failure of heating return pump Westerholt, pressure booster app. GBL7 and failure of DWZ boiler 2. Failure of various frequency converter pumps in the sewage treatment plant and ENK.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The contact persons here are LIW and Thomas Funke
There was no risk to persons present due to regulatory requirements.
The causes are still being clarified by LIW.
There were no significant customer restrictions.

LIW statement:
1. due to the age of the LS/disconnectors, such faults can be assumed. This is why the maintenance by the partner Engie was so important, as we know that the circuit breakers are susceptible, and the older they are, the more susceptible they are.
2nd impact LIW: None in addition to the "Scholven impact on the generation units" below. Voltage peaks, as in this case, cannot be ruled out. The protection systems worked as specified.
3. consequences: Unforeseeable grid disturbances can always occur in the superimposed 35kV grid, which is why the systems and connected components must be supplied with n-1 protection.

TITLE: Embers in the coal feeder 5.40
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A smouldering fire broke out in the area of coal feeder 5.40 this afternoon at around 2:10 pm.
It was detected in parallel by the on-site CO detector of the fire alarm system and by attentive employees of a partner company who were supposed to be carrying out work on this mill.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The assigned group leader of the plant fire brigade was able to detect a high concentration of carbon monoxide inside the coal feeder using a measuring device. Work on site was stopped immediately. The area around the feeder and the floors above were closed off. The boiler house is being ventilated. Until further notice, the boiler house may only be entered with a CO alarm.
Falling glowing coal particles could be detected inside. Using a thermal imaging camera, two pockets of embers were found in the area of the scraper belt. These areas cannot be reached from the outside to remove the coal.
Flooding the feeder with CO2 or water is not technically possible. Therefore, the embers cannot be extinguished. Attempts to clear the area via the moving belt have not led to any improvement.

TITLE: No AGI alarms to the DCS during UPS failure/ESD trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
There were no DCS alarms from the AGI to the CCR to draw the operator's attention to the evolving issue at the AGI. This resulted in 2 hours of confusion/investigation and ultimately led to the unit being shutdown when it otherwise may have been able to stay on had the problem been highlighted. 

Operations are blind to any issue at the AGI due to the lack of CCTV and CCR alarms. The ESD had tripped shut while the unit was on and the UPS power back up was not adequate during the power cut but at no point was there anything to alert someone at Enfield. This is a process and safety issue.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Gases / Fumes / Vapours (Release of SOx, NOx, SF6, NH3, CH4, CO and CO2 into the atmosphere)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Issue at the AGI was rectified and the ESD was re-opened.  The pipeline pressure was restored and all valves/alarms/trips returned to normal condition. Unit was shutdown and stabilised and due back on this morning.

Recommendations: Mechanical inspection of the turbine, bearings and generator before recommissioning. Check the cost of automation. Check the signalling paths.

TITLE: Derailment of bulk goods wagon type Falns
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
After the coal train had been unloaded at the Heyden power station site, an incident occurred at around 12:00 noon in which a shunting section (a wagon with a bogie) derailed.

After the unloading process, the team from the service provider HHPI attached two Falns wagons, which had been removed the previous day for repair work, to the existing train. The two wagons were located on a parallel track to the coal bunker (track 23) and underwent repair work by MKB this Friday morning. The two wagons were parked by the HHPI team on Thursday 28 September 2023. According to HHPI, a brake shoe was installed to prevent them from rolling away.
According to the shunting attendant, when the two repaired wagons were coupled to the existing train at around 12:00 today, they forgot to remove the brake shoe (installed the day before). As a result, the last wagon (Falns type) in the formation seen in the direction of travel derailed approx. 100 metres after the start with the leading bogie. According to the driver, an HHPI employee was two wagons ahead of the derailed wagon at the time of the derailment to accompany the shunting movement. This employee informed the driver of the derailment by radio, whereupon the driver initiated the braking process. The derailed wagon came to a halt approx. 100 metres after the derailment.

Immediately after the derailment, the HHPI foreman on duty for supply and disposal was informed of the incident.
An on-site assessment was carried out immediately, in which several people from the power plant and the responsible railway operations manager (Mr Imgrund) were involved.
The HHPI internal reporting chain was initiated in parallel by the HHPI team.

The derailment caused damage to various wooden sleepers in the points area and in the level crossing area; to various small pieces of iron (screws and fastenings); to the points linkage of the changeover device; to the points signal and to the asphalt in the level crossing area on the power station site.
There was no personal injury


As an initial measure, it was decided that the derailed wagon must be placed back on the track so that it can then be removed.
The planned rerailing is carried out by the Schlamann company using a mobile crane.
The rest of the train can then leave the power station site.
The power station has also contacted a track construction company in order to carry out the necessary repair work once the damage has been assessed.

As a further measure, an SH2 disc will be set up in the track in the area in front of the level crossing after recovery.

Obvious damage that has occurred was recorded by photo.

TITLE: 35 kV grid red ring: earth fault with subsequent short circuit
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The first to occur was an earth fault on phase L3 at the connection of the choke coil VK5. Approx. 40-60 ms later, another earth fault occurred on phase L1 at the connection of the Is limiter VK8. This second earth fault immediately turned into a three-pole short circuit via the housing. However, parts of the customer's system still failed due to the voltage dip. After the disconnection, the single-pole earth fault at VK5 remained. This was switched off manually after approx. 48 minutes.

TITLE: GT Fire suppression system activated
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Thursday 2021-07-08 around 19:00 a fire alarm was received from the GT tent and the Co2 system went out. The GT did not fall out and continued to operate. The GT was shut down by the operating staff for safety reasons.

In fact, there was no fire as firefighters arrived.

Minimax was notified around 22:30 they arrived and started to replace the cylinders and investigate the cause of the fire.

They investigated the incident and made the following determination:

- the first indication on the control panel was that the Co2 cylinder line had been activated - a signal from a switch
- Co2 extinguishing has started and Co2 has entered the tent.
- This caused the 2 flame detectors in the tent to be triggered this caused the fire alarm to be triggered on the central monitoring system and on the T3000.
- GT did not get trip as the Minimax logic states that one flame and one heat detector should trip simultaneously this will cause trip and initiate extinguishing 2 flame detectors will not trip and initiate extinguishing.
- The flame sensor is actually the inflow of Co2 detected as a flame.
- This left only manual start as an option but the starter bottle was completely intact and no gas was missing from it as measured. Thus, the normal process of manual extinguishing start could be excluded.
- The key release mechanism was also checked by a real test and worked well.
- The Minimax field technician found no reasonable explanation for the extinguishing malfunction, the system was restored to its original state and has been in operation since.
- The entry was made in the SBT logs.

Further information:
- for GT trip and start of extinguishing the following conditions are required: pressing any manual extinguishing start button will result in an immediate trip the Co2 gas inlet the presence of at least 2 closed end stops on the gas fittings. Or the activation of one piece of flame and one piece of heat detector will cause a trip and the extinguishing will be triggered after the closed end stop of the gas fittings.

2021.08.18.:

The immediate cause of the extinguishing start was the mechanical starter rupture that starts the extinguishing process.  The triggering system did not receive a command from the extinguisher cabinet.

An investigation/reporting of findings will continue in person with the specialist company that maintains the system in the coming weeks.

MJ: With the assistance of the specialty subcontractor (Minimax), the system was restored immediately. In addition, the investigation of the incident has been done in 2 steps: one immediately after the incident and the other during the maintenance on 25 October 2021. No technical fault was detected during the investigation. The possibility of intentional operation was raised, but there is no evidence of this. The system has been operating reliably since it was recommissioned. No further action is required at this stage. Case closed.

Tue 9/21/2021 4:59 PM
Fortunately, the 2nd round of investigation into the CO2 extinguishing system discrepancy with SBT. resulted in better news than first reported. It turns out that the problem that caused the incident we experienced has no effect on the tear out we used so it is safe to use and still achieve safety from the system.  In this respect, the following precautions can be lifted.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
1. Suppression system (CO2 gas bottles) have been replaced. (DONE)
2. Spare bottles are being procured. (ONGOING)
3. Actual severity determined: People: Near Hit (Process safety) Asset: replacement cost of empty bottles.
4. Potential severity is being evaluated (ONGOING)
2. Investigation started. (ONGOING)

TITLE: Ember nest in the coal wagon

Both wagons were unloaded onto a concreted surface; they could not be unloaded into the deep bunker.

The unloading process was supervised by the fire brigade and embers were successfully extinguished. The other wagons could be unloaded without any major problems.

The coal was separated and compacted, and regular monitoring is carried out.

TITLE: RoCa: Soda lye leakage from dosing vessel.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the rounds walked on Tuesday 12 November, it was noticed that there was a puddle of liquid near the RO units (demineralised water plant), this is not unusual because during the change of a raw water filter, water gets on the ground. So no further suspicion at that point.
On Wednesday, I walked into the plant and saw white marks and crystallisation on the ground everywhere. The scaffolders were removing material at that time and also had the forklift in use. This work immediately stopped the foreman told me it was probably caustic soda and said rinse shoes and throw away gloves. Asked the chemical department if they knew what had happened based on previous observations that the NaOH dosage in the district heating water (make-up SV) was not working. Something had been tried with the plant but they had no idea where leakage had come from. Asked to determine the pH of liquid pool and approximate concentration of NaOH. This showed that pH was pH12 and concentration about 0.8%. This corresponded nicely to the composition in the NaOH dosing vessel. Daniel sluymers asked the Maurik company to clean the floor with appropriate PPE by diluting the mixture with sufficient water and rinsing/draining the gutter.

After a long search, it turned out that the suction hose from the dosing tank of the SVW NaOH dosing pump (00GBN31AP001) had slipped off the compression fitting (directly on the suction) and the hose had fallen right next to the drip tray, causing half the dosing tank to spill onto the floor by siphoning. Level was 73% and after leakage 27%, so about 120 litres of 0.8% solution across the floor. The concentration was fortunately lower because NaOH dosing with creation of new vessel had not gone well.
Hose reattached properly to pump suction however pump is still not pumping. Further action needed.
Maurik cleaned everything well and did a good job.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Stopped work around the area of the leak and instructed the people involved to rinse their shoes and throw away gloves.
Daniel sluymers asked Maurik's company to clean the floor with proper PPE, by diluting the mixture with enough water and rinsing/pulling into the sump.
Suction hose reassembled and secured so that it cannot fall next to sump.
Informed the guard.

TITLE:
Oil spill to surface water due to overturned cube containing oil and flushing away due to process water leakage.

Oil spill to surface water due to a tipped over IBC with oil and the wash away due to a process water leakage.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Sequence 1
While moving a cubel (mounted on a undercarriage with wheels) on the forks of a forklift by a contractor employee, the cubel with undercarriage fell over while being set down. This allegedly happened because the tyres of the undercarriage of the cubel were too slack, making it unstable. After the cube with undercarriage fell over, +/- 300L of oil leaked from the cube through an unsealed opening at the top of the cube and spilled onto the tiled floor.

Actions taken immediately: immediate report to Uniper by contractor employees. Spill contained and covered with absorbent gravel. Also put the cube with undercarriage back upright.

Sequence 2 ( case 40361)
After the incident had occurred and was made safe, the contractor company resumed its operations (clearing the hall). While moving a pallet containing material, a contractor employee (while making a turn with his forklift) 30-60 min after sequence 1 hit and damaged an in-service process water pipe (7.5 bar). This involved a capped branch of a GRE process water pipe that protruded +/- 1.5 m straight up from the floor. This process water pipe transports process water from the Brielse Meer and is supplied by Evides.

Immediate actions taken: immediate report to Uniper by the contractor employees. The shift operators on duty blocked the process water pipe locally, stopping the leakage.

Sequence 3
Due to the large amount of water released from the process water pipe, the oil spill drifted away, ending up partly in an HWA gutter next to the hall. This HWA drain discharges via underground sewers directly into the Europa harbour.

Immediate actions taken: immediately placed floating oil beams in the harbour by Uniper employees, as a result of which the oil spill from the HWA sewer was contained as much as possible.

General note:
- Unclear whether work permit procedure was followed. The incident investigation should show whether it was applied.
- Unclear whether loss of process water could have caused Trip. The incident investigation should show what the possible consequences could have been.
- Current case 40353 will be used as the main case for cases below. Only this case will be filled after the investigation.

TITLE: Water input into the plant air system
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
In the course of the tank inspection as part of the recurring TÜV inspections (pressure test) of the SCA10BB001 plant air tank, water entered the plant air system, the origin of which cannot be determined with certainty at present. The cause is still being investigated.

Chronological sequence:
14.11.2021-> Activation & emptying of the plant air tank
17.11.2021-> Filling of the plant air tank with well water & manual operation of the Airleader.
18.11.2021-> Carrying out the pressure test & subsequent emptying and drying of the air receiver.
19.11.2021-> Normalisation of the air receiver & commissioning
25.11.2021-> Detection of water in subsystems of the plant air network


The water was most likely introduced backwards via the air dosing of the sediment in the AWA. The cause was most likely an incorrect system pressure (plant air). Switching on consumers within the plant air system caused a drop in pressure, which could not be registered by the plant air compressor in operation. As a result, the factory air pressure dropped below the level of the water column from the sediment.
No damage was caused.

When the system is tested again, a flexible connection of the pressure after the air receiver to the Airleader control system must be established.
In future, this procedure will be set out in writing as part of the order/activation process.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The affected subsystems of the plant air network were drained by employees of the power plant.

TITLE: Heavy release of ash following lorry loading Loading lane 1 new ash loading.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Following the successful loading of the lorry, the loading system went into the off-programme as planned. This resulted in a blockage of the dosing roller on loading line 1, presumably caused by a foreign object in the system.
Due to this blockage, the flow of ash towards the lorry could not be stopped. The employee of the partner company who was present then activated the emergency stop of loading line 1. After successfully simulating the position feedback of the dosing roller, the programme could then be cleanly transferred to the exhibition. The lorry was able to leave the loading area.
During the activation of the emergency stop, the loading of the neighbouring loading line 2 was in operation at the same time. This had to be put back into operation. Due to the fact that loading line 2 also drew the product from silo 1 (just like loading line 1), conveying air got under the dosing roller of loading line 1 (simulated), which was still in operation, causing a backward flow of ash via the ventilation of loading line 1.
This could only happen because the corresponding shut-off valve of the conveying air system in the direction of loading line 1 was leaking in the closed position. This resulted in the uncontrolled escape of ash via the corresponding ventilation of the loading chute on loading route 1.
The estimated quantity amounts to approx. 5 tonnes of E-filter ash.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Upon noticing the ash leakage via the loading bay on route 1, the partner company's employee immediately activated the emergency stop again. The lorry driver was able to escape unhindered into the open, the partner company's employee immediately went into the loading shed on loading route 2 and immediately informed the control room about the incident, as he was unable to escape into the open due to the poor visibility. The control centre immediately activated the alarm chain and activated firefighters with self-contained breathing apparatus to rescue the affected employee of the partner company. The employee of the partner company remained unharmed and was able to make his way outside under his own power. After the ash dust in the atmosphere had settled, rough cleaning was started immediately.
In consultation with the maintenance department, a concept was developed as to how to start identifying/rectifying the cause after the rough cleaning had been completed.
Actions were also drawn up for this case.

12:09hrs TST IP SV + CV Left FAIL 18MAB11EA121. Whereby, IP steam turbine governor valve closed fully, but the IP stop valve remained in intermediate mode (18MAB11AA001). Result was worsened vacuum >250mbar causing the steam turbine to trip (18MAX43EZ903_XU51). REMIT call submitted to Trading approximately 12:10hrs. Load dropped to SEL, drum levels controlled, air cooled condenser demin sprays put into service and sequencer selected to bypass. Grid were called to inform them of the situation.
By 12:17hrs, SEL was achieved. Due to standby to bypass being selected, gas turbine continued to deload.
At about 12:28hrs, Trading called requesting a REMIT update: 70MW from 12:30hrs to 13:30hrs. Then, between 13:30 and 13:43hrs increase load from 70 to 240MW. Remain at SEL until 15:00hrs.
Grid called and updated.
~ 13:34hrs programme device became disabled on the steam turbine and was manually given an ON command. Steam turbine became to ramp up from 70 to 240MW.
Steam turbine, at the time of writing is stable, and control valve stresses are improving (26 & 68% for HP and IP valves respectively.)

TITLE: Unintentional/unnoticed activation of the sprinkler system (fire extinguishing water) in the NH3 station.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the late shift on 5 June 2024, the sprinkler system (fire extinguishing water) in the NH3 station of the Heyden power plant was triggered unintentionally.
Due to an imminent internal test of the air receiver (see photo "Air receiver NH3 vaporiser station") for the HSX10 BB001 instrument air, it was activated by the late shift on duty. During this activation, the air receiver, which is fed by the plant air system, is shut off by corresponding ball valves and an associated bypass (see photo "Air receiver bypass fitting") is opened for continuous supply to the valves of the sprinkler system. During the disconnection measures, the bypass was neglected to be opened, as a result of which the fire extinguishing valves (see photo "Manifold valves for NH3 sprinkler system"), which were held in the CLOSED position by air support against the spring force, lost their CLOSED end position and fire extinguishing water was released. Due to the gradual drop in pressure in the system, the employee who had carried out the activation on site was unable to notice that the sprinkler system had been triggered. At around 19:00, a message was sent to the control centre via the PBS message sequence that the air pressure in the air vessel had dropped below a certain level. However, this is normal and desired in the course of activation, so there was no need to take any action as a result. There is no message via the process operating system (message sequence) about the opening of the fire extinguishing valves or the triggering of the sprinkler system.

The activation was finally noticed by an employee on the night shift at around midnight during a tour. The first thing he did after making sure that it was an unintentional activation was to close the upstream manual valve of the fire extinguishing water supply line. After the sprinkling ended, the previously mentioned bypass of the air receiver was also opened. Once the necessary system pressure (air) had been reached, the previously closed manual valve for the fire extinguishing water was opened again so that the sprinkler system was/is available again.

It can therefore be assumed that fire extinguishing water was released/sprayed from approx. 19:00 to approx. 24:00.
The following areas were sprinkled:
-evaporator station
-Waggon refuelling
-Tank 1 & Tank 2

The majority of the fire extinguishing water collected flowed through the channels provided into the HSQ00 BB001 collection tank provided for this purpose (see photo "HSQ00 BB001 collection tank"). The accumulated water was then pumped towards the neutralisation tank in the VE/KA system. This is neutralised at a sufficient level and pumped towards the precipitation tank.
However, as the capacity of the HSQ00 BB001 collection tank is limited,
the channels in the evaporator station area overflowed. The overflowed water reached the outside through the building doors and flowed into the gullies of the external drainage system. The water flowed into the rainwater retention basin via the existing drainage system. As a precautionary measure, the pumps of the rainwater retention basin were switched off electrically so that the water could not be pumped towards the overpumping station without prior sampling by the power station laboratory.

Parallel to the measures taken on site, the on-call manager of the Heyden power plant was informed of the incident by the shift supervisor on duty. The incident was also documented in the electronic shift log (SAP).

On 6 June 2024, the water in the rainwater retention basin was sampled by the power plant laboratory. An ammonia concentration of 0.3 mg/litre was detected, which is well below the limit value of 10 mg/litre. As a result, the collected water can be pumped towards the pumping station as usual, which led to the pump being switched off.

It should be noted that at no time was there a risk from the release of ammonia or any other hazardous energy in terms of process safety.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Immediate measures:

-temporary interruption of the fire extinguishing supply
-Restoration of the air system pressure
-activation of the rainwater retention basin pumps
-informing the on-call officer
-Documentation of the incident

Recommendations:

-Sensitisation of staff
-Check whether alarm signals can be retrofitted when the sprinkler system responds.

TITLE: Fuel Gas Pre-Heater shutdown / tripped causing GT Humming.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Valve 10EKT25AA101 FG P/HTR CIRC CTRL-V faulted with ‘Trouble Alarm’ and ‘Status Discrepancy Not Closed’. The valve had to be put in local operation at the Fuel Gas Pre-heater location and then manually operated in the open and closed  directions, the ‘fault re-set’ was then operated to clear the fault.  Multiple notifications under 21347109 are available to view valve fault history.  
During the valve fault the flow rate on the heating water side dropped and shut down the fuel gas preheater program.
 When the fuel gas preheater shuts down cooler natural gas flows to the GT burners. During this transition from Hot Gas to cooler gas the Gas turbine suffers combustion instability and combustion chamber rumble occurs causing GT Humming protection systems to operate.  
On the morning of 29-03-2021 the GT Humming protection operated as a direct result of cooler natural gas temperatures causing 0.2s to be added to the humming counter, there was a slight drop in load as the GT setpoint controller was switched off causing a slight imbalance during a load transient.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Gas turbine load transient rate decreased from 35MW/min to 6MW/min until heating restored to natural gas system ensuring no further combustion instabilities (humming)

TITLE: Smouldering fire in the coal outage shaft of mill HFC20
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the late shift at around 3.30 p.m., the shift on duty wanted to empty the HFC20 coal mill's drop-out box. As usual, the gate valve HFC20AA301 (see photo 1), which connects the discharge chute with the pyrite chamber of the coal mill in operation, was closed for this purpose. Without closing the aforementioned gate valve, it is not possible to open the discharge chute, as the two valves are hydraulically interlocked. This is necessary to ensure that no coal in the grinder and no air required for drying the grinder (temperature up to 290°C) can escape when the discharge chute is opened. After the gate valve had been closed (boiler house 0m), the shift workers went down to the cellar at -5m to the drop-out shaft. Once on site, the mechanical locking mechanism of the hatch of the discharge chute (see photo 2) was first loosened a little. The flap was then lifted to depressurise the manhole. The mechanical locking mechanism, which is not fully open, prevents the flap from swinging open in an uncontrolled manner. When the employees realised that the pressure relief was not successful, which suggests that the gate valve HFC20AA301 (see photo 1) was/is not tightly closing, they tried to close the drop-out box again. Unfortunately, this attempt was unsuccessful, as coal that had already escaped had lodged itself between the sealing surfaces of the outlet chute flap. In addition, air with a temperature of up to 290°C (normal operation of the mill) escaped from the gap into the open. The air flow ignited the coal in the discharge chute (smouldering fire), which triggered the fire alarm system. After communication between the shift personnel in the control room and the personnel on site, the shift supervisor decided to take the affected HFC20 coal mill out of operation.
This was done in the following order:
1. load sink to 600 MW initiated (16:08)
2. setting an NV in the REACT system
3. information to the load distributor
4. information to the person on standby (Mr Bredthauer)
5. mill out of operation (16:23)
6. mill inerted with steam
7. Slight vacuum in the HFC20 grinder retracted

At the same time, an attack team from the plant fire brigade equipped itself with self-contained breathing apparatus, CO measuring device and thermal imaging camera and moved out to -5m to the coal outage shaft.
Once an extinguishing water supply had been established and an overview of the overall situation had been obtained, the affected drop-out shaft was opened and the smouldering fire in the drop-out shaft was extinguished. In addition, the coal located in the drop-out shaft was rinsed out or cleared out and spread out on the ground and also extinguished/cooled.
After the extinguishing operation was completed, it was discovered that the seal of the hatch of the discharge chute was damaged. Maintenance was then informed by the on-call officer and fitted a new seal after arriving at the power station.
After the outage shaft was closed again and the coal mill was made operational again, the NV in the REACT was terminated and the load distributor was informed. After consultation with the load distributor, the HFC20 coal mill was then put back into operation (19:15).
Once the clean-up work had been completed, the fire brigade equipment attendant was also requested to ensure that the breathing apparatus used was ready for use again.

Update 17.01.2024

The issue/incident was discussed in the early meeting and measures for further action were determined (see Actions)
It was determined that the affected mill must be shut down until the cause has been remedied if the failure shaft needs to be emptied. Emptying will no longer take place during operation.
Furthermore, it has been determined that, until further notice, the breakdown chutes will be emptied at every block shutdown.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
-Load sink for decommissioning the HFC20 grinder
-Setting an unavailability in REACT
-Information to the load distributor
-Alerting the person on standby
-Formation of an attack team from the plant fire brigade
-Positioning of a reserve squad
-inertisation of the coal mill located outside
-Emptying and extinguishing of the coal outage shaft

TITLE: Gas Detection Panel failure.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At approximately 13.29 the G as panel in control room failed initiating a GT protection level 1 & 2 trip.
It was assumed that voltage fluctuations from the SFC had possibly caused a supply MCB to the panel to trip. (Running the SFC has been known to play havoc with some actuators on site, in particular ones associated with the aux boiler). Initial investigations revealed the power source for the gas panel (415v switchboard 10GMA06) had not tripped but further investigation within the gas panel were made which ascertained there was no 240v power to it’s internal power supply. A small fast blow anti surge fuse was found blown in the 240v supply line to the power supply unit. A new one was sourced and fitted. 240v power was now restored to the power supply unit, but there was no 27v DC output from the unit. Although the DC supply healthy light was lit on the front of the panel (from the back up batteries), there was no functionality from the gas panel at all.
Members of the Engineering team were called to site and the power supply unit was removed and dismantled to reveal it was badly burnt out inside. An alternative 24v DC power supply unit was obtained and temporarily installed which allowed the gas panel to be reinstated.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Temporary 24v power supply unit installed.

TITLE: EDH, Steam mixing vessel (EDH50-LBA01BB001): Possible instantaneous failure of the material mixing vessel due to graphitisation.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the overhaul, an inspection was carried out on the mneg vessel. Here, it was found that the mixing vessel contains signs of graphitisation. A section was ground out and re-welded.
The Inspection Group has advised that the mixing vessel should be replaced in 2022. This is because it cannot be ruled out that graphitisation has also taken place and is still taking place in other parts of mixing vessel. No damage due to graphitisation was apparently found during the inspection during the overhaul from the outside.
Graphitisation can lead to embrittlement and unannounced instantaneous failure of the material releasing steam at a pressure of 30 bars and 450 degrees Celsius.
(Above information from e-mail sent by M. de Jong on Tuesday 12-10-2021)

Now, an area has been cordoned off on the ground and 1st floors where people are not allowed to enter when the mixing vessel is under pressure (During operation). This assumes that the main steam valves at the mixing vessel and/or the OVO valves at the off-gas boilers close immediately because of trip off-gas boilers. That the volume of steam released is somewhat limited.
The question remains whether the off-gas boilers trip and the main steam valves at the mixing vessel still function at all. The OVO valves at the off-gas boilers are set "Local and Open" by default and do not go close to a trip of the off-gas boiler. Not even if they are set to "Remote and Automatic". In addition, the valves also have a run time of several minutes before they close.
So the volume of steam that can be released will be many times larger than first assumed. With all its consequences.

Should the mixing vessel fail during operation, the consequences could be as follows:
- Injuries and possible fatalities.
- Damage to the installation:
  * Damage to the off-gas boilers.
  * Damage to cables and pipes.
  * Damage due to moisture (steam condensing).
- Unable to meet the heat supply (Now with the winter season approaching) .
- Possible increased supervision by official bodies (also at other installations).
- Reputational damage.
- Unrest among residents in the neighbourhood/area/city.
- Impact on other projects planned at the site (Heat pumps, WOS WarmteLinq, Geothermal).
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Recommendations for further actions:
Several emails have been sent and some is told/explained verbally by management to different colleagues.
Now would like a unified written narrative from the management with at least the following topics:
- What is the probability that the mixing vessel can fail during operation.
- Plan of action for the period until replacement.
* How are we going to monitor the mixing vessel.
* How will we conduct operations.
* How will we deal with problems with plant parts within the deposit.
- Conduct Risk Inventory and Evaluation and pick up the resulting action points.

TITLE: Risk of severe injury or fatality due to different execution temperature sensors
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Temperature sensors are mounted in a pipe to measure the process temperature. The actual sensor is contained in a thermowell. This allows the sensor to be taken out without depressurising the pipe section.
There are two types of thermowells
- Weld-in thermowells
In this case, the thermowell is inextricably embedded in the pipework. The temperature sensor including housing is screwed onto the connection. When the sensor and housing are removed, the welded thermowell provides a seal.
-Screwed-in thermowells
Here, the housing of the temperature sensor flush with the thermowell. Once the housing is loosened, an opening is created in the pipe. In this case, there is a temperature of 160oC. The steam will squirt out of the opening with great force and injure the technicians or have fatal consequences.
It cannot be seen from the outside of the sensor which variant the technician is dealing with. A technician will have to know this through ready knowledge of the installation. With the current personnel policy of hired technicians, this knowledge is not present among technicians. This increases the risk of injury or fatality

Specifically refers to:
ELD03-MAW10CT010 - PAKKINGBUS - T-METING - temp.measurement TIC4671 stuffing box.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Temperature Extreme (Inc. Hot or cold surfaces, gases and environments)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
On behalf of the head technician, this notification was made to create awareness of this hazard.
It should be recommended to ensure that detachable thermowells are fixed so that they cannot be accidentally detached.

TITLE: Oil radiator fire
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 12:40 pm, smoke developed in the 110kV single-phase switchgear house WKW. The smoke was coming from a floor shaft between the circuit breaker cells and the office building.

The flap to the floor shaft was opened carefully and at a distance by the operating personnel. The smoke was thick and could not be assessed by the operating personnel, so the fire brigade had to be notified. The internal reporting chain was also triggered.  
When the emergency services arrived a short time later, they were informed and briefed by the plant personnel. The fire brigade then climbed into the floor shaft with breathing apparatus and brought an oil radiator outside through a window. It had leaked oil and was smoking heavily. A technical defect in the oil radiator was identified as the cause of the fire. The RCD on site tripped and switched off the oil radiator circuit. This presumably prevented greater damage.

An emergency doctor and the police were also on site. No persons were injured and the operation was over after approx. 1 hour.

This shaft and the room below it were not marked on the construction plans. This room had not been used in recent years.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Emergency call plan processed, then emergency call made.

TITLE: Crack in pipe fitting of the pressure connection of the drying glycol pump - P63541

The pump was immediately taken out of operation. The damaged area on the pipe fitting resulted in approx. 1200 litres of glycol escaping from the system. The escaped glycol ran into the safety device (WHG collecting basin). For this reason, there was no environmental damage. Based on the experience of the employees on site, this was a material fatigue failure.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The damaged area was repaired (welded) the following day and the leaked glycol was disposed of professionally. The WHG tank was then cleaned. The pipe fitting has been in use for several decades. Furthermore, comparatively identical screw connections were checked for damage from other drying systems in which glycol pumps are used. It is currently being examined whether it would be possible to switch from piston pumps to axial piston pumps, which cause less vibration, when replacing the glycol pumps.

TITLE: One-sided blackout in internal consumption at the 10 kV voltage level due to a faulty connection during normalisation work.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During normalisation work in the 10 kV self-balancing switchgear BBA on Thursday 24 October 2024, a circuit breaker malfunctioned on the BBT01 auxiliary transformer, which is earthed on the upper voltage side.

Background:
In the course of planned maintenance work in the 110 kV grid of Avacon (Bierde substation), the start-up transformer BCT 01 (power plant) was taken out of operation and disconnected for the duration of the maintenance work. In order to ensure the power station's own power supply, the two 10 kV busbars BBA and BBB were coupled and jointly supplied by the starting transformer BCT02 in operation. This is a normal, recurring procedure for carrying out maintenance work in the substation or on the starting transformer while ensuring the power supply to the site.

Location of the incident:
The starting transformer BCT01 normally supplies the busbar BBA (10 kV) via the two parallel-connected feed bays BBA06 and BBA07.
The two parallel-connected feed bays BBA04/05 for the EB transformer are located next to the feed bays of the starting transformer, but are permanently disconnected due to decommissioning. For these reasons, the auxiliary transformer BBT01 is disconnected and earthed on the overvoltage and undervoltage sides. The 10 kV switchgears BBA and BBB are fully enclosed switchgears equipped with SF6 gas circuit-breakers.


Chronology of the incident:

On 24 October 2024, Avacon reported the work at the Bierde substation as completed to the Heyden power plant. The shift supervisor on duty then arranged for the BBA switchgear to be normalised. This was carried out by the electrical engineering plant manager on duty (shift electrician with major switching authorisation).

1. before starting the normalisation work, the on-duty plant manager responsible for electrical engineering entered the FFFS switchgear and gained an overview of the work to be carried out (identification of the switch panels in accordance with the normalisation requirement). The tools required for the work (switch lever & crank) were taken by the plant manager from the cabinet at the other end of the switchgear for storage and placed ready for normalisation. The process of obtaining the tools meant that the person responsible for the system had to leave the previously correctly identified switchgear panels to retrieve the described tool. On his return, there was a mix-up and, as described in the following steps, the person responsible for the installation inserted a circuit breaker that did not belong to the normalisation request into the switchgear cubicle.

2. the first of the two circuit-breakers of the starting transformer BCT01 was retracted into the associated switch panel BBA06 and made ready for remote switching from the control room.

3. instead of retracting the second circuit-breaker BBA07 belonging to BCT01 and making it ready for switching, the neighbouring circuit-breaker BBA05 (belonging to the self-balancing transformer BBT01) was retracted into the switching cell and made ready for switching.

4 Immediately after retraction, the person responsible for electrical engineering realised that he had retracted the wrong switch. The message (drop-down flap relay) "Switch carriage locked" was displayed on the affected switch cell. After realising that the wrong switching cell had been fitted with an LS, the BBA05 switch could no longer be extended from the corresponding switching cell.

5 The person responsible for the system then called for assistance from an experienced colleague (with extensive switching authorisation) from the electrical engineering maintenance department.

6. after a joint telephone assessment of the situation, the decision was made to directly remove the mechanical interlock on the affected circuit-breaker, as this is the only way to open the breaker again, but first to complete the original normalisation of the starting transformer BCT01. For this purpose, the second (correct) circuit-breaker BBA07 associated with BCT01 was retracted into the corresponding switching cell and made ready for switching.

System status at this point in time:
10 kV busbar BBA and BBB supplied by the starting transformer BCT02.

7 Following normalisation, the electrical engineering system supervisor on duty, together with the colleague previously called in (step 5), wanted to reopen the circuit breaker BBA05, which had been incorrectly retracted in step 2, and set it to the normal "open" state.
To do this, the BBA05 switching cell was opened and the front panel of the retracted circuit-breaker was removed to gain access to the mechanism. Removing the front plate did not expose access to the live parts of the circuit-breaker or the associated busbar at any time.

9. the circuit breaker was switched on, which resulted in the permanently disconnected auxiliary transformer BBT01, which was earthed on the top voltage side, being switched to the energised 10 kV busbar BBA. The resulting short circuit caused the protective devices (EB protection) to trip. As a result, the BBA busbar was properly disconnected, which led to a one-sided blackout in the auxiliary supply.

Furthermore, the switchgear was able to conduct/discharge all currents occurring in accordance with its design and the corresponding protective devices transferred the system to a safe state. As a result, there was neither personal injury nor damage to the system.

11. the circuit-breaker BBA05, which had been connected by mistake, was opened when the 10 kV busbar BBA was de-energised and the auxiliary power supply was subsequently restored.

was applied.

TITLE: Rookgas leakage RoCa AK-3
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
In the waste gas boiler RoCa-3, there has been a considerable leakage near the injection water valve HD-Herovo for quite some time (occurring just after the last overhaul). Most likely, there is a crack in the boiler wall under the insulation, through which flue gases with a temperature close to 500 degrees are leaking. This is visible in the form of a large smoke. To limit the impact of the leakage on surrounding equipment, insulation blankets had already been installed against the boiler wall.

Last week (18-12), the injection water valve nevertheless failed and both the rubber diaphragm of the actuator and the positioner were found to be faulty. It is likely that these succumbed to the high temperatures.
As a result, RoCa-3 was not deployable for over three days which led to significant loss of revenue, according to information from PCC.

Although the malfunction of the injection water valve has been rectified, the same is not true of the leakage. Additional measures were taken to try to limit the direct impact of the leakage on the plant (installation of additional insulation blankets and a cooling fan), but the actual cause (the crack) was not repaired.

Besides the risks with regard to operational safety, extremely high flue gas temperatures as well as its composition (NOx, CO2) create safety risks for persons entering the boiler house.
The NO2 (part of total NOx) concentration has been determined to be 0.4 ppm; the CO2 concentration cannot be determined due to lack of appropriate equipment. However, based on previous incidents/measurements, it is likely that the limits of the permissible are approached or exceeded.

Conclusion:

There are (still) risks with regard to operational management which can have major consequences for the continuity of heat supply and can lead (and have already led) to loss of income.
There are safety risks regarding exposure to high temperatures and hazardous substances.
There is currently no concrete plan to remedy the cause of the leakage in the foreseeable future.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Opinion:

Take immediate additional measures to reduce security risks:
- Limit access to the installation to only the most essential.
- Communicate the risks clearly to those who must enter the installation.
- Monitor the current situation and take measurements at regular intervals regarding temperature development and the presence of harmful substances.
- Make measurement equipment available that makes smoke gas leaks easier to understand (*).

(*) Even if the limits of the MAC concentration are not immediately exceeded, such a leakage should not be accepted just like that! An increase in NOx and CO2 is abnormal and exposure should be prevented at all times.


Draw up a concrete plan to remedy (in the shortest possible time) the cause of the leakage and thereby ensure both safety and business continuity.
- Better map the problems, determine the actual damage.
- Provide a clear plan of action; get people and equipment ready to carry out the necessary repairs on call, as soon as the opportunity arises.
- Have Operations make all necessary preparations to have the plant secured immediately.

As an organisation, never accept the long-term persistence of such leaks!

TITLE: Emergency stop Boszoom activated
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On 08-01 around 10:30, the pressure picture in the SV network suddenly changes. The supply and return pressures on the RoCa side of the city rise and the transport capacity over the Boszoom drops sharply. The supply pump continuously falls into confinement due to low dP at the "equator" (BS3 selected, RoCa->city).

Cause is then unclear, but a physical restriction seems to have occurred, allowing much less power to be transmitted from RoCa towards the city.
Shortly before that, communication failures also occurred regarding a large number of dP measurements. It cannot be ruled out that this too might have an impact on the operation (regulation) of Boszoom.

Both the dP communication failure and the possible physical blockage are communicated both internally and with Eneco.
Despite many enquiries, searches and resetting of communications, no improvement occurs.

The next morning, "evidence" is found that a stepwise pressure increase occurred around 10:30 (08-01); this reinforces the suspicion of a physical blockage.
However, the dP failure has also not yet been resolved and cannot be ruled out as a cause.

Although no work is known, Eneco is checking the valves in the transmission lines after consultation.  
Around 13:30, feedback is received that no anomalies were found in the SV system either.

Since the suspicion remains that there is a restriction somewhere, an operator goes again to the Boszoom.
Locally, the central valves in the supply appear to be closed for about 90%...... the local emergency stop (supply) appears to have been activated!
Against the emergency stop is a megaphone (on a cabinet) which can be used on site during emergencies.

After the valve is reopened, the pressure image and transport capacity normalise.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Someone probably visited the Boszoom site around 08-01 at 10:30 am. No work had been reported as far as we know, but several parties had access to Boszoom.
It is likely that one, most likely unintentionally and possibly unconsciously, activated the emergency stop.


The emergency stops are meant to quickly create a physical separation between RoCa and city in case of emergencies.
It is likely (descriptions are lacking) that the valves are not supposed to close completely when activated; the last part must then be done manually.

Advice/action points:
- Secure local emergency stops against unintended activation by means of a protective cap or bracket (report made).
- Configure alarms on activation of the emergency stop and on the separation valves not being in open position (report made).
- Review the intended operation of the local emergency stops/valves. These emergency stops were added to the system later; the possible scenarios/risks that could occur may not have been sufficiently considered.

(The steam turbine was started without the watch being aware of the steam turbine shutdown).

Summary
Lee Beresford Dec 25, 2021, 9:49:35 AM UTC
UPDATE: after approximately 2hours of barring UTG advised a start could be attempted which passed without issue with the unit achieving full speed with vibration behaviour as previous.

UTG were called out this morning due to the steam turbine generator tripping on high vibration at approximately 1000rpm during a routine start-up, with increased vibration observed across the shaft-line. The vibration data indicated a temporary shaft bend had formed along the shaft-line and further analysis indicated that cranking (barring) had failed shortly after last nights shutdown. This resulted in a temporary thermal bend (hogging) forming in all rotors and creating a large temporary imbalance.

Recommendation
Lee Beresford Dec 25, 2021, 9:48:37 AM UTC
UTG recommends reviewing the DCS alarm configuration for the cranking/barring motor/system to help prevent a repeat as this situation could easily result in a shaft seizure.

After connecting the steam turbine generator to the grid, the generator switch (owner DSO Stedin) ended up in an unclear/incorrect position.
The overlying electrical safety system was triggered and removed the voltage from the installation. Engineering E and Maintenance E check the condition of our installation. There is an extensive list of checkpoints before we can go back into operation.
Maintenance M also checks the installation and replaces parts if necessary.

On 19 March at 15:30, the CMT for this incident was cancelled and the plant itself will continue to handle this case.

A return to service document has been drawn up.

TITLE: Auxiliary boilers Delftsevaart go out of operation without notification.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
In the morning shift at 06:40, HDV13 was started and after half an hour, to our surprise, we saw that the step programme went to step 53 flue gas valve close without us getting any alarms from it. Finally, the auxiliary boiler went out of operation completely and when it was in the final step, it went to step 90 (tripped) and only then did we receive the first alarm that the boiler 13 was tripped and thus not restartable from a distance! Locally, it turned out that the minimum flow protection had been triggered. Then we started HDV14 and to our surprise, exactly the same thing happened here. Locally, it turned out that a flame scanner had been triggered.
This is very undesirable in the moment of emergency and emergency action has to be taken to avoid leaving the city out in the cold! The moment the boiler is sent out due to a trip, we need to see this right away so we can act right away!
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Started an auxiliary boiler on ROCA and used the buffers to absorb heat loss.
Recommendation: find out why trip signal comes in delayed on RWC (DCS system substations) so that we can react immediately and avoid domino effect.
2nd recommendation is to resolve the trip track issues, these were reported a long time ago and have not been resolved to this day! HDV13 dP measurement (flow measurement) check and fix. HDV14 flame scanner check and fix cause.

TITLE: Asbestos incident
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the degasser tank (7th floor), a valve had to be deasbested. It was decided to use incubator bag technique to clean the flange surface of the lagging flange and pack the valve in its entirety and transport it to the asbestos container to further disassemble the valve and remove all asbestos.

While transporting the valve (double-wrapped asbestos warning bags), the bag ruptured and residual gasket got onto the floor (7 the floor next to the degasser tank).
This was noticed by GPW contractor and after this, Turkay (DTA Uniper) and Dennis (HSE) went to the site to have a look. Residual gasket was indeed present on the floor.
HAZARD_PHYSICAL_SECURITY_EVENT: Hazardous substance biological (Eg. naturally occurring respiratory and skin sensitisers / irritants / poisons)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
- Area cordoned off immediately (asbestos warning ribbon/sign)

- Immediately contacted an independent lab (Eurofins/Sanitas) to have a survey carried out

- To prevent emission, the DTA (Asbor) cleaned the cordoned-off area under asbestos conditions (hoover Hepa filter and wet wiped)

- Around 10:30 the Laboratory Technician arrived and started taking adhesive samples (total of 9 adhesive samples)

- After analysis by the accredited laboratory, the indicative adhesive samples taken showed no
asbestos fibres detected. No contamination is present in the relevant room (see annex asbestos report)

- The cooperation with the relevant DTA of the Asbor company was stopped due to several careless acts.

TITLE: Gas turbine trip due to 5 gas leaks at gas control valves
CASE_DESCRIPTION: On 29-11-2023, the gas detection at the gas control valves detected an excessive gas concentration. As a result, the gas turbine received an off command and unfortunately failed to come on the torn. After a prolonged search for the leaks, we found a total of 5 gas leaks. 1 leak on a swagelok coupling that was loose and 4 leaks on all 4 gas valves. The leaks on the gas control valves were all on the gland seal of the valve. The tightener of the gland seal which is adjusted with nuts were all loose. The cause could be that during commissioning there was not, or it was forgotten to check the valves for leaks. Also, the nuts were not secured in an environment where vibrations occur.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: All fastenings on and around the valves were checked to make sure everything was tight. This was repeated during start-up and during operation of the gas turbine.

TITLE:

IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The material extracted from the HVAC system pipes was sent by the FAC department to the Maasvlakte lab for analysis.

TITLE: Fire at unit 4, at the air duct, during the recommissioning of the plant, after a leak of light heating oil.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On 10 February 2024, a leak of light fuel oil occurred in the DENOX plant, unit 4. (Case number 42247) Unit 4 was not in operation at the time and the plant was cold. At a height of 15 metres at the duct burners, the oil escaped from a vent during maintenance work. As the drain pipe of the collecting tray below had been laid, the oil penetrated the insulation of the air and flue gas ducts. The insulation was removed and the ducts were cleaned.
After the ducts were insulated again, the plant was restarted on 11 March. A risk assessment was prepared for this and increased safety precautions were taken. At 18:09, the fire watch reported a spontaneous combustion. The system was out of operation again at this time and was shut down.

On 10.02.2024, a leak of light heating oil occurred in the DENOX plant, unit 4 (case number 42247). Unit 4 was not in operation at the time and the plant was cold. TITLE:
Olielekkage en vuur in GT omkasting tijdens bedrijf.

Oil leakage and flames out of framevent during trip in GT enclosure during operation.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Oil leak and fire in the casing of GT1 in Leiden on 09-02-2022

Around 11.45, I discovered a dense oil wash from the gas turbine casing ventilation exhaust duct (near the GOS). Upon inspection of the GT, I found that the hydraulic expansion vessel had a leak on its coupling, causing oil to be finely atomised under pressure, which was then distributed by the airflow throughout the casing and partly deposited on hot turbine parts.

To this end, the GT tripped in the HMI room. We then inspected the GT all around to find flames coming from the bulls horn of the combustion chamber on the other side of the GT (seen from the angle of the oil leakage). Immediately activated the extinguishing manually on the spot.

The watch was then called by the Haaglanden fire brigade to say that they had received a fire alarm and that the vehicles were already on their way.

NOTE: The security centre on the MV did not receive a report and only found out that something was wrong at the ELD location when the fire brigade had already arrived.

The extinguisher did its job, then the fire brigade arrived within minutes. I waited for these at the gate and directed them to the side of the GT building.

The commander did comment that it would be desirable to also be waited on site by someone from operations, explained that this is not possible with a 2-man crew (and may become even more difficult in the future)!

Together with the commander, we made a round around the equipment and discussed the situation and status quo.

Here we came to the conclusion that the situation could be considered controlled and completed, after which the fire brigade left the site.  

We then ventilated the building and the GT enclosure, after which the cleaners could get to work.

TITLE: HBS - RedCom - Third-party work with multiple anomalies
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
This morning following a fault report in the ICT domain of substation 2nd Blekerhof, I travelled to the substation in question.
The fault lay as the remote expectation suggested "voltage failure".

Although upon entering, it could not be missed in terms of noise (grinders/reciprocating saw), further investigation revealed that RedCom was fully engaged in activities not agreed upon in the preliminary discussions. It was so many anomalous/risky activities that I could not decide anything else to stop all work immediately.

1. Grinding activities (with grinding wheel) were carried out without spark collection, half-face mask, fire extinguishing facilities.
2. Old wardrobes were removed from the premises, which were thrown down through the window from the old business school room (2nd floor) in the hope that they would end up in the container. This did not go well with the first wardrobe, which ended up on the container and partly entered through Uniper's window frontage.
3. The agreed separations between RedCom and Uniper are not respected; a canteen/meeting area has been created in the Uniper area.
Persons regularly walk through the Uniper area for toilet visits and water taps for making coffee 4.
Electrical work has been carried out by a third party. This third party has switched groups on/off and cut various cables/have them cut in the area to be rebuilt. However, no agreements have yet been made by RedCom regarding electrical work. No instructions have been issued from Uniper as referred to in NEN50110/3140.

During one of these switching activities mentioned under point 5, an installation circuit breaker that supplies our ICT facility with voltage was probably touched by mistake.

As a result of the power failure, the pressure measurements in the SV grid were lost, which creates issues for our SLA with Eneco regarding our obligations. It is highly undesirable for this type of signal to be lost, especially during the winter period.

Work is and should remain suspended until further notice.


RedCom will not be allowed to resume until:
- obligations to the agreement are fulfilled and secured.
- work is carried out in accordance with the work plan.
o So physical separation has been realised including CCTV/reporting contacts
- Coordination with Competent Authority (=DCMR and not the Gem. Rdam) has been completed or taken up.
- Leo vd Vliet, William de Jong and undersigned agree on restart.

TITLE: KvZ gutted by laser beam smoke detector
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At KvZ, there are works to add an emergency boiler next to existing installation during these works, they dismantled (pulled away) a smoke detector that was in the way and in the process probably damaged the cabling, causing the fire alarm centre to be triggered and the alarm to go off and the 2 auxiliary boilers to be gutted, leaving south Rotterdam in the cold. There was no more dP to supply heat to the grid.
Operations went to take patrol and put the smoke detector out of action which allowed work to continue however the KvZ boilers had several malfunctions that had to be repaired with the necessary effort so it was not until 15:20 that they slowly returned to operation.

30/11 AH: On enquiry, it appears that the KvZ boilers were not tripped due to the removal of the said smoke detector. This smoke detector was not in operation and is an old one that was not connected. The boilers were tripped due to the AWP disturbing the beam of the smoke detector against the roof. The beam smoke detector was not switched off. Cause starts with poor preparation of the work. At the time, nothing had been arranged regarding the BMC. As of 29/11, this has been regulated.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Smoke detector isolated in the BMC and KvZ 11 and 12 restarted.
Recommendations:
1.When working on fire detection systems, discuss this with operations/Uniper first. Inform outside firms of the systems and automation of the plant they are working between.
2. Ensure that installations go into the heating season fault free. There are several failures and overrides on the boilers and also the BoE can only run at half power because of this!

TITLE: TGE A1 engine damage at the Audorf site
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
After one hour of power operation, there was a rapid shutdown with simultaneous noise development. Pending fault messages could not be acknowledged. During the search for the cause, loose insulation material was discovered in engine compartment A. In the course of further investigation, damage to the outer skin of engine A1 in the area of the turbine set was found. Metal parts were also found in the surrounding area. In addition, further broken material was found in the inner area of the NLT A power turbine.
The process of recording the damage and determining the cause was started.
The engines were last serviced in May 2023 (3-year interval)
There was no danger to persons at any time, as the engine rooms are locked during operation and no persons are present there.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Check the system after the rapid shutdown (establish safe state, initial cause determination)
System deregistered
Damage investigation process initiated
The defective drive unit was dismantled into individual parts in the workshop at the service provider's premises for diagnosis. The broken blade that caused the damage has been sent to a metallurgical laboratory for examination within Uniper UK.
There are currently repair offers for the power turbine, which are being analysed economically. A decision is still pending.
Various scenarios for further action are being considered and analysed.
UPDATE 05/05/2025: RCA analysis is in progress, report still pending.
